body:
Docs only. Pre-playtest fixes to `docs/playtest-2026-09.md` (160 -> 179 lines) and `docs/known-issues.md`: the between-sessions MM-profile trap, what a Hyrule crossing chest actually shows, a cheap-failure playtest order, and stale lines.

Refs #645, refs #310

## What changed

**`docs/playtest-2026-09.md`**
- **§2, boxed warning** after step 7: once a paired file exists, leave Combo > MM Randomizer / MM Tricks alone between sessions. An edit is accepted at load and refused at the next MM arrival. If you changed one, set it back exactly or recreate the file. The box now also covers Cross-Game Rules: a changed rule is refused at load on stderr only, the OoT file still opens, and nothing is saved to the pair.
- **§2 steps 5-6:** a paired Generate writes no spoiler. The spoiler is written at file creation (step 6). The old step 5 said it was written at Generate.
- **§3, "First session"** (new, at the top):
  1. Launch with stderr captured.
  2. Create one shipped-default file (or Closed Forest Off, the one named non-default).
  3. Cross at the Happy Mask Shop (after the Deku Tree on defaults) and check stderr for `arrival profile matches` and `HYDRATED`.
  4. Walk back and pick up one crossing in each direction.
  5. Play everything else, saving right before either final boss.
  6. Keep `stderr.txt`, `logs/` and the `.redsave`.
- **§3, "Working as designed"** (new): the confusion-list items from the analysis report that hold on main (see the premises section below for the ones that did not).
- **A4 rewritten.** It now says what each direction shows:
  - A Termina chest shows MM's cutscene and a textbox.
  - A Hyrule chest shows a corner toast only: nothing held overhead, no textbox, and its "Blue Rupee" stand-in is not given.
  - In both directions the item arrives at the next crossing into its home game, with a second toast.
- **B5:** notes that #763's Playtest section still names the retired "Combo > Windows > Toggle MM Randomizer Options". The current path is Combo > MM Tricks.
- **H3:** links the title-screen unlock to the §2 trap.
- **J:** notes that #761's Playtest text predates #766. The Cross-Game Spoiler window is no longer empty, and A2's counts supersede its "about 27-29".

**`docs/known-issues.md`**
- **New open entry** under "Save loss and corruption": "A changed MM option or Cross-Game Rule breaks the pair for the session". It links #564 and PR #570, gives the workaround, and names the load-time MM-profile compare as the fix to come. I did not file a new issue: the report leaves the compare to the operator (§7 decision 1).
- **"What does not ship yet":** the #438 bullet ("14 of 23 hook types remain") is replaced. Only "Majora Access: Remains" is drawn disabled, and it is retired on purpose.
- **"MM hook dispatch is still partial — #438"** is struck through as RESOLVED by PR #673.
- **"Some menu entries are stubs"** no longer claims live/partial/dormant/generation-only labels on the MM page.
- **C2 and §4 Attach** (guide): the Goal-change load refusal is stderr-only; refusal reports attach `stderr.txt`.

## Claims and their citations (all read on `origin/main` = `b95fc7d1`)

**1. The between-sessions trap**
- The freeze predicate is `gComboCtx.mmProfileDigest != 0`: `src/common/combo_mm_options_view.c:174-179`. Both pages gate on it: `src/common/combo_mm_options_page.c:48,67,83`.
- The digest is 0 on a fresh launch. `Context_Init` calls `ComboContext_Init`, which `memset`s `gComboCtx` (`src/common/context.cpp:264-265, 309-310`).
- The digest is dropped on return to title. `Context_InvalidateSessionOnReturnToTitle` calls `Context_InvalidateSessionState(RSBS_SEED_STAMP_DROP)` (`context.cpp:486-487`), and the digest survives only on KEEP (`context.cpp:346, 407-422`). The page's own note says so: "Return to the title screen to choose options for a new world." (`combo_mm_options_page.c:84-89`).
- Generate stamps the digest (`games/oot/soh/Enhancements/randomizer/3drando/playthrough.cpp:300`). That is why the rows turn grey right after Generate.
- LoadSlot compares Cross-Game Rules by field but does not recompute the MM profile:
  - `src/common/save.cpp:811-835` calls `Combo_ComboSettingsDivergenceFor(&combo.comboSettings, ..., combo.mmProfileDigest)`.
  - That function compares the combo record against the live `Combo_ResolveComboSettings` and recomputes the fingerprint from the stored digest (`src/common/foreign_items.c:521-540`).
  - No MM-profile recompute happens. The load then restores the stored digest (`save.cpp:838`, `memcpy(&gComboCtx, &combo, ...)`), so the pages lock again once the file is loaded.
- The MM arrival recomputes the digest and refuses on any difference:
  - `MM_Rando_GateCrossGameArrival` (`games/mm/2s2h/GameExports_SingleExe.cpp:4519`) compares `MM_Rando_ComputeProfileStamp()` against the stamp (`:4556-4557`).
  - On a mismatch it latches the slot (`RsbsSave_RefuseSlotIdentity`, `:4566`).
  - It emits the toast "Cross-game pairing REFUSED: ... Termina stays un-randomized and progress here will not be saved to the pair." with `remainingTime = 15.0f` (`:4568-4584`).
  - It returns 1, so the consume is skipped and MM plays the vanilla bootstrap (`:4696-4702`).
- The stamp covers tricks, excluded checks and starting items:
  - `games/mm/2s2h/Rando/Foreign.cpp:209-218, 638-639` (`ProfileIdentityString(values, tricks)`)
  - `src/common/combo_mm_options_view.h:250-252`

**2. The Hyrule chest hosting an MM item**
- `games/oot/soh/Enhancements/randomizer/hook_handlers.cpp:394-437`:
  - The foreign branch records the pickup (`OoT_Rando_Foreign_RecordPickup`).
  - Its only presentation is `Notification::Emit({"You found ", <article+name>})` (`:418-422`). The comment at `:397-403` reads "nothing is dropped or held overhead; the toast is the whole presentation" and "A toast rather than a blue textbox".
  - It marks the check collected, pops the queue and `return`s before the local give (`:437-438`).
- The physical stand-in is `kOoTForeignJunkCover = RG_BLUE_RUPEE` (`games/oot/soh/Enhancements/randomizer/ComboLogicEngineOoT.cpp:185`; comment `:2479-2482`).
- MM receives the item at the next arrival:
  - `MM_ConsumeSharedItems()` runs on the arrival path (`games/mm/src/code/z_play.c:2733`) and calls `MM_AwardSharedItem` (`games/mm/2s2h/GameExports_SingleExe.cpp:3352-3369`).
  - That calls `MM_ForeignItem_Give`, then `GiveNow`, which emits the arrival toast via `Notification::MM_Notify_Emit` (`games/mm/2s2h/Rando/ForeignItemsSingleExe.cpp:205-231`).
- The OoT-bound direction mirrors it: `OoT_ConsumeSharedItems` runs at `games/oot/src/code/z_play.c:587`, and its toast is at `games/oot/soh/GameExports_SingleExe.cpp:1196-1225`.

**3. Working-as-designed list**

- **"Majora's Mask is suspended; these options stay editable."** It shows whenever the profile is not frozen and the current game is not MM, which includes an MM that never ran: `combo_mm_options_page.c:100-109`.
- **No spoiler at Generate:**

body:
**05 · Lesson engine: gates, scoring, hints, progress, code runner, validators**

**Scope.**
- Pure core: `lesson/rules.ts` (§3.5 rules 1–7: 2-of-3 window and once pass, seeded fresh instances, hint ladder normal/puzzle, gaming → in-page fallback), `lesson/kinds` (§3.6 builders with sampleAnswer/mutate defaults, rollback helpers), `lesson/gateEngine.ts` (the single scoring path shared by the UI, `window.__course`, the guess bot and the CC learner; instances regenerate from persisted seeds, so a reload never rerolls; `hintHighlights` for L1 from the answered instance), `lesson/partNames.ts` (learner-facing names for every part id).
- Runtime: `progress.ts` (plain ProgressV1 JSON, corrupt/foreign/out-of-range values quarantined to `enigma.progress.corrupt` with a notice, memory fallback + banner), `chapterMachine.ts` (XState v5, flat scene states, NEXT guarded by canAdvance, BACK, GOTO ≤ reached, rebuilt from progress on every mount), ChapterPlayer/SceneFrame (route guards and redirects, scene setup, story cards with a static act clock, bets gating every first-time reveal in scene order, tasks, focus on entering a scene and after each bet), GateRunner (items one at a time, per-kind rollback views, L1 highlight / L2 worked example on a different instance / L3 reveal + fresh instance, setups applied and restored, focus management and one live region), `ui/focus.ts` (first usable control; locked keyboards skipped), recall scenes, the return-visit check (modal with focus trap), CourseMap/LockedPage and the Course, Chapter, GateLab and Fixture pages; `window.__course` + event log.

author: loganrenz
body:
## What

The generator side of the coding-standards deep dive (SPEC S1–S3, 2026-09-27). Companion to #1222 (`narduk-lint` `maxWarnings`).

### (a) Lint ceiling: S1
`apps/web/lint-budget.json` is now `{"strict": true, "maxWarnings": 10, "rules": {}}`. That means zero warnings normally and at most 10 recorded with `--accept-new-rules` in a pinch. The ceiling is enforced by `narduk-lint` from the eslint-config release that #1222 produces (2.6.0). An older `narduk-lint`, including the currently pinned 2.5.1, ignores the field and drops it the next time it rewrites the budget. So this PR must ship in the same release as #1222 or a later one. #1222 is merged, so the next release carries both. The eslint-config pin needs no hand bump: `sync-generator-package-versions.mjs` moves `PACKAGE_VERSIONS` when #1222's changeset versions the package, and #1222's changeset already lists `create-narduk-app: patch`.

### (b) Supply chain in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: S2
Checked against the pinned pnpm **10.33.4** (`PNPM_VERSION`), by reading its bundled source: `getOptionsFromPnpmSettings` maps `allowBuilds` true/false onto `onlyBuiltDependencies`/`ignoredBuiltDependencies`, and `createPackageVersionPolicy` parses `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` as name globs plus `name@version`.

- `minimumReleaseAge: 1440`, and `minimumReleaseAgeExclude: ['@narduk-enterprises/*']`. A comment names `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` as the path for an urgent security bump: add the exact `name@version`, then remove it once the release is a day old.
- **Why the estate scope is excluded (measured, not assumed).** `npm.nard.uk` serves publish times, so the cooldown applies to it. I generated an app with the exclusion removed and ran a fresh install. It failed with `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATURE_MATCHING_VERSION Version 0.4.5 (released 8 hours ago) of @narduk-enterprises/narduk-ai`. The release flow publishes the estate batch and then the generator pinned to it, minutes apart, so every new app would fail its first install for a day after every release, and so would every hand-made estate bump.
- **Build-script allowlist.** `allowBuilds` replaces the root `package.json` `pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies`. It is the form `pnpm approve-builds` writes in 10.33, and pnpm 11 keeps it. The allowlist now lists **exactly** the packages with install scripts in a generated tree. A fresh all-capability install with no allowlist reported exactly five: `core-js`, `esbuild`, `unrs-resolver`, `vue-demi`, `workerd`.
  - `esbuild`, `unrs-resolver`, `workerd`: `true`. Each script fetches or verifies a native binary.
  - `core-js`: `false`. Its script prints a banner.
  - `vue-demi`: `false`. Its script switches builds for Vue 2, but its default `lib/index.mjs` is byte-identical to `lib/v3/index.mjs` (checked).
  - `sharp` and `@parcel/watcher` are dropped. sharp 0.35.x is in the tree but has no install script, and nothing pulls in `@parcel/watcher`'s native build.
- Both files are seed (not in `MANAGED_TARGETS`), so existing apps are unaffected.

### (c) AGENTS.md quality bar: S3
The managed router region (`REGION_MARKERS.agentsRouter`) gains a **Quality bar** block of ten one-line rules. Each rule links its handbook chapter at `https://github.com/narduk-enterprises/coding-standards/blob/main/standards/<chapter>.md` (02, 03, 07; the file names were checked against coding-standards `origin/main`). The rules:

1. The S1 lint line, verbatim.
2. `defineUserMutation` (or the public/admin variants) with `withValidatedBody(schema.parse)`.
3. `/api/admin/**` requires admin and answers 401/403.
4. Loading, empty and error states say only what is verified.
5. 320 and 375 px widths: no horizontal scroll or clipped text.
6. SSR-safe time (`narduk/no-render-clock`, `useSsrNow`).
7. narduk-core nonce + `strict-dynamic` CSP, enforced and proven with `foundation:check:security-headers`.
8. `expectAccessible`.
9. `pnpm run performance-budget`.
10. A suite counts only if CI runs it.

I checked every helper named in the block against this repo: `defineUserMutation`, `withValidatedBody`, `defineAdminQuery`, `requireAdmin`, `useSsrNow`, `security.headers.enforce`, `expectAccessible`, and the generated `performance-budget` script. The social-previews line stays unchanged. `create-narduk-app upgrade` adds the block to an existing app's region, with a new upgrade test.

### Not done: `quality-level: standard` (workflows#158)
The generated `ci.yml` does not pass `quality-level: standard` yet. The generator pins `nuxt-cloudflare.yml@1513b2a`, and that commit does not declare the input: `quality-level` appears 0 times in its `nuxt-cloudflare.yml`. The head of workflows#158 is 28 commits ahead of it. A caller that passes an undeclared input to a reusable workflow fails at startup.

Commit 9529e04 therefore adds a TODO naming workflows#158 in `src/ci-workflow.ts`. The follow-up emits the input and the quality-bar line "CI: this app runs `quality-level: standard`; opting out of a check needs a written reason." once #158 merges and the pin moves.

## Proof: fresh generate + install
From this branch's built generator, all capabilities (`auth,seo,analytics,uploads,ai,mapkit`), outside any workspace, no lockfile:

| Step | Result | Time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile` | pass, no "Ignored build scripts" notice, `.modules.yaml` `ignoredBuilds` empty | 24 s (warm store; 146 s first run) |
| `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` | pass | 5 s |
| `pnpm run lint` (narduk-lint + Prettier over the generated `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `AGENTS.md`, `lint-budget.json`) | pass | 27 s |
| `pnpm run build:ci` (Nuxt/Nitro Cloudflare build: esbuild + workerd) | pass | 60 s |
| `pnpm run test:unit` | pass | 2 s |
| Same, with `@narduk-enterprises/*` removed from `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` | install **fails** `ERR_PNPM_NO_MATURE_MATCHING_VERSION` (as expected) | 3 s |

The allowlisted scripts did run: `esbuild/bin/esbuild` became the native Mach-O binary. With no allowlist it stays the JS shim.

## Checks run locally
| Command | Result | Time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter @narduk-enterprises/create-narduk-app run quality` (format, narduk-lint, typecheck, 249 tests) | pass (re-run on head 9529e04: 16 s) | 17 s |
| `pnpm run release-plan:check` | pass | 1 s |

The full preflight is deferred to CI: the diff does not touch `.github/`, CI scripts, the root `package.json` or the lockfile. CI's `packed-consumer-smoke` runs the same generated-app install with the cooldown in place.

## Interactions to know about
- **Dependabot.** A weekly Dependabot update to a third-party version under a day old will now fail resolution until that version matures (company-hq#737 is the related cooldown history). Estate packages are excluded, so internal updates are unaffected.
- **Generator pins.** A hand bump of a third-party pin in `PACKAGE_VERSIONS` to a release under a day old will make the packed consumer smoke fail until the release is a day old. That is the policy working, but it is a new way for the smoke to go red.
- **The one number Logan has not set** is the advisory patch window (SPEC S2, proposed 7 days). It is not part of this PR. It belongs to the baseline/handbook lane.

## Merge policy
Do not merge yet. This changes CI and lint tooling defaults, and the estate requires it to be verified. `pr-land` was not run (it has no `--no-arm` mode).

## Verify follow-up (967ff6d, rebased on #1222)

An Opus verify passed claims 1–4 and 7–8 and flagged these:
- **Release order.** Resolved by merging #1222 first. In a simulated merge and version bump, eslint-config went to 2.6.0, the generator pin to `2.6.0` and create-narduk-app to 0.15.0.
- **Three bar lines a fresh app didn't meet.** A new app has no enforced CSP, no `expectAccessible` spec, and no CI run of `performance-budget`. Those lines now say what to adopt and when, instead of claiming the gate exists. CI enforcement arrives with the shared workflow's `quality-level: standard` (narduk-enterprises/workflows#158) in a follow-up

## Summary

Backend half of specs/001 user story 6: explicit, withdrawable consent for a workout's title, location, notes and bodyweight (FR-029–FR-035). Tasks T085–T087, T089–T093, T096 and T097. The frontend follows in a separate PR (T088, T094, T095, T098).

Everything is behind `PRIVACY_LIFECYCLE_ENABLED`, which is off in production, so workout writes there behave exactly as before.

- **Schema (T090):** `users.optional_details_consent_version` / `optional_details_consented_at`, with a both-or-neither check. Nullable, no backfill: existing accounts start without consent (FR-035).
- **Statement (T089, T091):** real wording in `docs/privacy/consent/2026-09-28.json`, drafted at the owner's request. `OptionalDetailsConsentCatalog` embeds and validates it at startup, reusing the notice catalog's reader and validation. It has no announced successor (FR-034). The Dockerfile and its build-context allow-list now copy the folder.
- **Routes (T092):**
  - `GET /privacy/optional-details-statement`: public.
  - `PUT /account/privacy/optional-details-consent`: current version only, else 409 `consent_statement_changed`; idempotent.
  - `DELETE /account/privacy/optional-details-consent`: clears the pair, then every detail of the caller, and returns `clearedWorkouts`.
  - `GET /account/privacy` gains `optionalDetails { currentStatementVersion, consent, transitionPending }`.
- **Enforcement (T093):** with the flag on and no consent, `POST /workouts` and `PATCH /workouts/{id}` carrying a non-empty detail get 403 `optional_details_consent_required`, and nothing from the request is stored. Without consent, empty strings are stored as null, so "holds a detail" means "not null" everywhere.
- **Save vs. withdrawal:** both run under shared lifecycle access, so the users row orders them. A save reads the consent with `FOR SHARE`, and withdrawal updates the users row before the workouts. Details are in `OptionalDetails.cs`.
- **Export (T096):** `privacyRecords.optionalDetailsConsent` now comes from the row.
- **Transition clearing (T097):** the operator SQL and its zero-count check are in `docs/privacy/retention.md`. The dated step is in `docs/privacy/release-checklist.md`. Both files hold only this step until T071 and T078.

## Review notes

- `UsersTable_AfterAcknowledgement_HasNoConsentColumn` became `…_HasOnlyOptionalDetailsConsentColumns`. The amendment adds exactly this pair, and the notice acknowledgement still stores no consent.
- The statement refers to the privacy notice for providers and backup retention rather than repeating them, because the notice is still synthetic until T043. Its `reviewDate` is set once the owner approves.
- Not covered: SC-008's "withdrawal clears the reference notebook within 60 s" has no performance test yet.

## Test plan

- [x] `dotnet format backend/GymNotebook.sln --verify-no-changes`
- [x] `dotnet test backend/GymNotebook.sln`: 250 passed
- [x] Coordination tests checked by mutation: removing `FOR SHARE`, or swapping the withdrawal's statement order, each fails one test.
- [x] `TransitionClearingSqlTests` runs both SQL blocks from `retention.md` against a fresh migrated database.

author: joepetjr
body:
## Summary

Main's CI has one known red leg: the hold-tune check (`tests/characterization/songs-hold-tune.test.mjs`) sometimes hears no note at all. The cause is the test's stimulus, not the app.

- **What went wrong.** The old stimulus was a 90 ms-on / 40 ms-off pulse train. The songs mic tick reads the newest 4096-sample analyser frame (about 85 ms at 48 kHz), so no frame is ever silent between pulses. The onset detector (src/audio/onset.js) only fires on a rising edge, which means the first frame after it starts is the only chance to count a note. If that frame's pitch clarity is 0.7 or lower, nothing counts for the rest of the 20 s file.
- **Simulation.** A Node simulation drove the real onset, YIN, range and level modules over 60 phases. The old stimulus missed the note 16 times out of 60 at the normal 50 ms tick.
- **The fix.** The stimulus is now 0.61 s on / 1.92 s off, which missed 0 of 60 at 50, 300 and 500 ms ticks. 0.61 s is still well under this song's 1.44–3.6 s hold band, so the "hold each note longer" assertion is unchanged.
- **New test.** When the page's 50 ms mic tick runs 300 ms late, a short held note is still heard. It retimes only `setInterval(…, 50)`, the same narrow-match method as songs-loop-backing's LATE_SHORT_TIMERS.
- **Shared helper.** `attemptHoldTune()` is shared by both tests. On a miss it reports whether the mic was open, the notes-heard count and the elapsed ms, so the next failure explains itself.
- **Real tone.** A sustained 1 s tone is heard at both a 50 ms and a 300 ms tick (probe only, not shipped). No `src/` change.

Diff vs main e59aa54: 251 lines, test file only.

## Test plan

- [x] tests/characterization/songs-hold-tune.test.mjs: 2/2 pass three times (author) and twice more after main e59aa54 was merged forward (c9b6518).
- [ ] Full suite: this PR's GitHub CI.

Test-only change; no teaching content. Reviewed by: none yet.

body:
Blog initialization could render before metadata arrived, while database rebuild errors were passed into post rendering as rows. The loading overlay then disappeared after 15 seconds even when the page had not loaded.

Wait for metadata before routing and retry failed row queries with a bounded retry window. Preserve existing data during failures and offer Retry loading for a stalled initial load. Preserve identity and ownership fields across partial site-info events.

Restore direct xID selection and refresh site information after choosing an identity. Pending lookups cannot overwrite a newer identity or resume a cancelled posting action.

Validation: all 11 Node tests pass, including failures reproduced before the fixes. A browser fixture using the actual Blog page recovers after database errors, renders delayed metadata, and opens and completes xID selection without cached auth information.

Refs EpixZone/EpixNet#524. Existing published blogs need their owner to update and sign the changed files.

body:
Please fill in this template.

- [x] Use a meaningful title for the pull request. Include the name of the package modified.
- [x] Test the change in your own code. (Compile and run.)
- [x] [Add or edit tests](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/blob/master/README.md#my-package-teststs) to reflect the change.
- [x] Follow the advice from the [readme](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/blob/master/README.md#make-a-pull-request).
- [x] Avoid [common mistakes](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/blob/master/README.md#common-mistakes).
- [x] [Run `pnpm test <package to test>`](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/blob/master/README.md#running-tests).

Select one of these and delete the others:

If changing an existing definition:

- [x] Provide a URL to documentation or source code which provides context for the suggested changes:
  - plotly/plotly.js#8057
    - https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-function-reference/#plotlytoimage
    - https://plotly.com/javascript/configuration-options/#customize-download-plot-options
  - 
- [ ] If this PR brings the type definitions up to date with a new version of the JS library, update the version number in the `package.json`.

----
This PR fixes the following type definition problems around Plotly.js's image export features:

1. Lack of `"full-json"` literal type in `ToImageFormat` union type.
2. Lack of `setBackground` property in `ToImgopts` and `DownloadImgopts` interfaces
3. Lack of `imageDataOnly` property in `ToImgopts` interface.
4. Several properties in `ToImgopts` and `DownloadImgopts` wrongly set as required.
5. The second parameter of `downloadImage()` wrongly set as required.

Actually `full-json` format option has been available since [plotly.js v1.53.0](https://github.com/plotly/plotly.js/releases/tag/v1.53.0) released 5 years ago (see also plotly/plotly.js#4593) but until recently it was not documented (see plotly/graphing-library-docs#471). Documentation about `imageDataOnly` was also updated then but it seems the feature has been also available from old versions. Now the updated documentation is available in the official [Function Reference](https://plotly.com/javascript/plotlyjs-function-reference/#plotlytoimage) and [Configuration Options](https://plotly.com/javascript/configuration-options/#customize-download-plot-options) documentation pages.

I checked `full-json` and `imageDataOnly` change the exported data as expected on both Plotly.js v2.25.2 and v3.7.0. Also, I confirmed that the properties in `ToImgopts` and `DownloadImgopts` are actually optional (without providing them, no error is thrown) on both versions. I can't find documentation about `setBackground` and don't know when it was added. Anyway, type definitions of this property will not be harmful for existing code since it is optional.

Plotly.js v4 started to provide the type definitions by themselves. Reflecting the doc updates mentioned above, theier type definition was also updated (plotly/plotly.js#8066). What this PR updates are semantically very close to what their PR does. Plotly.js v4 currently only bundles the types with the main package. Therefore, for users of a partial package such as `plotly-basic-dist.min` the type definition here is still important. So is for version 3 users, of course.

In the process of fixing the problems listed above, the following code changes have been made:

- Create `SetBackground` and `ToImageFormat` types and `ToImageButtonOptions` interface, instead of directly defining them in fields of other types/interfaces.
- Inherit `ToImgopts` and `DownloadImgopts` from `ToImageButtonOptions`, instead of redundantly defining their properties.

body:
First slice of the redesign map's **PR 2 (shared web primitives)**. It covers the pieces the web mock specifies exactly and that render no artwork. No route uses the new primitives yet; Home (map PR 4) will. The `NavTabs` change does affect today's pill bars (Filler, Channel detail), and their baselines will move in CI.

## What's here
| primitive | from the mock | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `SectionHeader` + `SectionHeaderAction` | the 18 px title, the 12 px meta, and the quiet 13 px "Full guide →" link | `render` swaps the action to the router `Link` (same seam as `Button`). The arrow is `aria-hidden`. Wraps at narrow widths |
| `StatusStrip` + `StatusStripAction` | headline dot (10 px, 4 px ring at 20 %), 15 px title, divider, items with 6 px dots and 28 px buttons, trailing CTA | one `role="status"` region. The error state gets the `onair/40` border. The loading pulse reuses `onair-pulse` at the mock's 1.2 s, motion-safe |
| `ListGroup` + `ListRow` | On the way / Your requests rows: 8 px dot, 13/12 px title and sub, 160 px bar with a mono eta, or one outline action | a real `ul`/`li`. The row is never interactive, so its action is the only control (axe `nested-interactive`, 45 nodes in the mock) |
| `HighlightRow` | Tonight: 80 / 36 / fill / auto grid, mono time, amber channel number, show + muted episode, 12 px reason | goes in a `ListGroup`. The whole row is one control (`render` → router `Link`). The reason is a prop the client words from #1664's typed reason |
| `NavTabs` pills ("count tabs through NavTabs") | Requests / Filler counted pills | the pill variant now draws the `attention` tint (suggest while the count is above 0, and it outranks the active tab's colour, as mocked). Pills are 13 px and hover changes colour only |
| `StatusDot` tones | `attention` (suggest-300), `progress` (tune), `notice` (signal) | the colours the mock's rows use, named by what the row waits on |

All values map to existing tokens: `static-900/700/400`, `border-control` via `Button outline`, and radius `lg` = 12 / `md` = 8. No new tokens and no new CSS.

**One departure from the mock:** the last row doesn't draw its hairline. In the mock it doubles against the group's border.

## Not in this slice
I held these back rather than invent design. I've asked the supervisor about them:
- **Artwork fallback.** The mock never shows missing artwork. The map recommends a code-drawn fallback from the channel monogram and dominant hue, but its look isn't mocked.
- **WatchingCard / OnNowCard.** The map calls for "one card model" shared with native `ui/programme-card` (N7 moves the web guide to `ui/guide` via react-native-web). Whether the card lives in the web app or the shared package is an architecture call to settle first.
- **PosterRail, IdeaCard and the stretched-link card** all render posters or stills, so they wait on the artwork-fallback answer. The stretched-link pattern belongs with its first card rather than shipping alone.

## Checks (narrow, local)
The whole `src/components/ui` vitest suite (33 files, 153 tests) passes. So do the `NavTabs` callers' suites (filler, requests page: 183 tests), `tsc --noEmit`, and biome on the touched files. Visual baselines for the new stories come from CI (lane rule). Story data uses genre words only.

author: k1low
body:
## Summary

- `prerelease_for_tagpr` installed gocredits at `@latest` through `depsdev`, so the version writing CREDITS was whatever had been released last. v0.5.0 and older read the module list from go.sum, and v1.0.0 (2026-09-26) switched to `go list`.
- A `credits` target now installs gocredits pinned to v1.0.0 and appends `_EXTRA_CREDITS` (the claude-agent-sdk-python license added in #8), and `prerelease_for_tagpr` calls it. The `go mod download` step and the `depsdev` dependency go away. This follows k1LoW/octocov@c919651.
- `-skip-missing` is not used. The module has no dependencies, so gocredits finds nothing it cannot license, and a future dependency without a license will make `make credits` fail instead of being dropped silently. `make credits` reproduces the committed CREDITS byte for byte.
- `credits` is declared `.PHONY`. On a case-insensitive filesystem such as the default on macOS, make otherwise takes the `CREDITS` file as the target and prints "`credits' is up to date." without running anything.

author: rjhaikal11
body:
## What changes

Adds `karpenter_controller_iam_policy_statements` (default `[]`) to `aws-eks-karpenter` and passes it to the upstream `terraform-aws-eks//modules/karpenter` input `iam_policy_statements`.

## Why

Karpenter 1.7 and later need `iam:ListInstanceProfiles` on the controller role ([upgrade guide](https://karpenter.sh/docs/upgrading/upgrade-guide/)). The v20 controller policy that this module wraps (`v20.31.0`) does not include it, so callers had no way to add it.

## Impact

- Default is an empty list: existing callers render an identical policy and see no plan diff.
- A caller that sets statements gets them added to the controller policy as an extra statement.

Example:

```hcl
karpenter_controller_iam_policy_statements = [
  {
    sid       = "KarpenterControllerExtra"
    actions   = ["iam:ListInstanceProfiles", "ec2:DescribeInstanceTopology"]
    resources = ["*"]
  },
]
```

## Verify

- `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` pass on the module.
- After the release, a caller that leaves the variable unset shows no diff in `plan`.

## Rollback

Revert this commit; callers that did not set the variable are unaffected.

author: thiepdanghd82
body:
## Tóm tắt

Phần 4 của web MVP: bốn dịch vụ mà app Mac làm bằng hộp thoại hệ điều hành (chọn tệp, lưu về máy, mở tệp, in) giờ có bản chạy trên trình duyệt. Code màn hình chạy trên server, còn tệp nằm trên máy người dùng, nên tệp đi qua kết nối Blazor theo cả hai chiều (`wwwroot/js/web-files.js`).

Áp dụng cho các màn hiện có mà không phải viết lại: nhập CSV Work Center, nhập/xuất thư viện QC, nhập Spec từ Excel, tải lên và mở bản vẽ, hồ sơ PDF của IQC, xuất PDF/Excel tờ Spec, xuất nhật ký audit, và nút **In** của tờ Spec.

## Người dùng thấy gì trên web

| Thao tác | App Mac | Web |
|---|---|---|
| Chọn tệp | Hộp chọn tệp của macOS | Hộp chọn tệp của trình duyệt. Nút trong menu chuột phải (hồ sơ IQC) hiện thêm khung "Chọn tệp…" |
| Lưu về máy | Hộp "Save As" | Trình duyệt tải về. Thông báo: "đã lưu về thư mục Tải về của trình duyệt" |
| Mở tệp | Preview / app mặc định | PDF và ảnh mở ở tab mới. Loại khác, hoặc khi trình duyệt chặn cửa sổ bật lên, thì tải về |
| In | Bảng in của macOS | Hộp thoại in của trình duyệt, dùng đúng CSS `@media print`. Tên job thành tên file khi "Lưu thành PDF" |

## Các quyết định thiết kế

**Safari chỉ mở hộp chọn tệp TRONG cú bấm thật.** Ở Blazor Server, cú bấm đi lên server rồi server mới gọi xuống JS, lúc đó đã ra khỏi cú bấm nên Safari lặng lẽ bỏ qua. Cách xử lý:
- Nút bắt đầu chọn tệp mang `data-ccl-pick="pdf,png"`. `web-files.js` bắt cú bấm ở pha capture và mở hộp chọn tệp ngay lúc đó. Khi server gọi `pick()`, JS trả kết quả của chính hộp ấy. Tôi đã gắn 4 màn.
- Nơi không gắn được thuộc tính (menu chuột phải IQC dùng `RowContextMenu` chung) hiện khung "Chọn tệp…": thêm một lần bấm nhưng chạy được ở mọi trình duyệt.
- Test tĩnh `Every_screen_that_picks_a_file_marks_its_button_for_Safari` bắt màn mới nào quên gắn thuộc tính.

Hai phương án bị loại: gọi `input.click()` từ server (hỏng trên Safari), và lúc nào cũng hiện khung (luôn tốn hai lần bấm).

**Mỗi tab một thư mục tải về riêng trên server** (`WebDownloadArea`):
- Thư mục xoá khi tab đóng. Thư mục mồ côi quá 24 giờ bị dọn ở lần dùng đầu sau khi khởi động.
- Chỉ tệp nằm TRONG thư mục của tab mới được gửi xuống trình duyệt, để một đường dẫn lạc ra ngoài không thành lối tải tệp bất kỳ của server.
- Thư viện QC thôi ghi `/tmp/qc-library-<line>.csv`. Trên web mọi người dùng chung server, nên hai người xuất cùng lúc sẽ đè tệp của nhau. Màn này giờ dùng `IFileOpener.GetSafeDownloadDirectory()` như các màn khác. Trên Mac thư mục đó là `AppData/downloads`.

**Tệp tải lên được ghi ra đĩa trước khi giao cho màn hình.** Luồng tua được (Length, Seek) giống FileStream của Mac, và lượt tải lên API sau đó không phải chờ từng mảnh qua SignalR. Tệp tạm dùng `DeleteOnClose`. Giới hạn 64 MB (`WebFiles:MaxUploadBytes`); API vẫn giữ giới hạn riêng của nó.

**SVG/HTML luôn tải về, không mở inline.** Blob URL mang origin của trang MES, nên script trong một bản vẽ SVG do người dùng tải lên sẽ chạy với quyền của phiên đăng nhập. Chỉ PDF, PNG, JPEG, GIF và WebP được mở ở tab mới.

**Kết nối giữ 2 phút** (`ClientTimeoutInterval`). `window.print()` chặn JS của trang suốt lúc hộp thoại in mở. Với mặc định 30 giây, server sẽ cắt kết nối và trang hiện màn "đang kết nối lại".

## Sửa kèm

Test đỏ ngẫu nhiên của phần 2: `Valid_ticket_sets_an_HttpOnly_Strict_cookie_that_holds_no_token` kiểm tra cookie không chứa `"r1"`. Nhưng cookie mã hoá dài khoảng 150 ký tự ngẫu nhiên, và đo được nó tự chứa "r1" khoảng **3,3%** số lần. Refresh token giả giờ là một chuỗi mốc dài.

## Bằng chứng

- **Test:** Web 133/133 (29 test mới trong `WebFilesTests`) · Razor 674 · Client 774, 0 fail. Bộ test web xanh ở mọi lần chạy sau khi sửa test phiên (trước đó 4 lần liền xanh, 1 lần đỏ ngẫu nhiên — xem mục Sửa kèm).
- **Đột biến, 8/8 bị bắt:**
  - bỏ kiểm tra "trong thư mục tab" → 2 fail
  - cho SVG mở inline → 1
  - bỏ DeleteOnClose → 1
  - bỏ ClientTimeoutInterval → 1
  - bỏ `data-ccl-pick` ở NpiWorkCenters → 1
  - QcLibrary quay lại `/tmp` → 1
  - quên đăng ký `IFileSaver` web → 2
  - bỏ kiểm tra cỡ tệp → 1
- **Gate:** `gate-all.sh` 31/31 PASS.
- **Chạy thật** trên bản thử LAN `http://10.102.3.87:5200`:
  - `/js/web-files.js` trả 200 và trang host nạp nó.
  - Khung "Chọn tệp…" hiện đúng kiểu `modal-card` của app, focus vào nút "Chọn tệp…".
  - Esc và nút Huỷ đều trả về `null` và gỡ khung.
  - Không có lỗi console mới.

Mac không đổi: Razor chỉ thêm thuộc tính `data-ccl-pick` (vô hại vì app Mac không nạp `web-files.js`) và `@inject IFileOpener` cho QcLibrary.

## Cần thử trên iMac (phải đăng nhập — cả Safari lẫn Chrome nếu có)

- [ ] Thư viện QC → Nhập: hộp chọn tệp mở ngay khi bấm (Safari), nhập được tệp CSV/XLSX.
- [ ] Thư viện QC → Xuất: trình duyệt tải về `qc-library-*.csv`.
- [ ] Spec → Bản vẽ → Tải lên bản mới; mở bản vẽ PDF: mở ở tab mới.
- [ ] Spec → nút **In**: hộp thoại in của trình duyệt, xem trước đúng tờ Spec. Tên tệp gợi ý khi "Lưu thành PDF" là `SpecSheet_…`.
- [ ] Spec → Xuất PDF / Excel: tải về, thông báo "đã lưu về thư mục Tải về của trình duyệt".
- [ ] IQC → hồ sơ → chuột phải "Nhập tệp": hiện khung "Chọn tệp…", chọn được PDF.

author: cristim
body:
## Summary

Two gaps in the account scoping of purchase executions:

1. `approvePurchase`, `cancelPurchase`, `retryPurchase`, the session-authed branch of `revokeViaEmailToken`, and `revokeScheduledExecution` relied only on the `approve/cancel/retry/revoke-any/own` RBAC matrix and never consulted the session's `allowed_accounts`, unlike pause/resume/run/delete-planned, which call `requireExecutionAccess`. An operator scoped to one account but holding an `-any` permission could approve (firing the real SDK purchase), cancel, retry, or revoke an execution belonging to another account.
2. `requireExecutionAccess` itself scoped by plan-account intersection, not by the accounts the execution actually buys in. With an operator scoped to A and a plan spanning {A, B}, both a child execution for B and the plan-level parent (nil `CloudAccountID`, which fans out to A and B) passed the gate.

## Root cause

`requireExecutionAccess` (`internal/api/scoping.go`) was only wired into pause/resume/run/delete-planned, and it only asked "does any of the plan's accounts intersect the scope?", which is true for a multi-account plan even when the execution spends an out-of-scope account's money. For ad-hoc web purchases (`plan_id` NULL) it called `GetPlanAccounts("")`, which errors on the UUID column, so scoped users got a 500 on their own purchases.

## Fix

- One helper, `executionAccounts(exec)`, returns every cloud account an execution can buy in: its `CloudAccountID` when set; otherwise all of its plan's accounts (a plan-level parent fans out to every one, `purchase/execution.go`); otherwise, for an ad-hoc purchase, every recommendation's `CloudAccountID`, refusing the whole execution when any is nil or empty. `GetPlanAccounts` is never called with an empty plan ID.
- `requireExecutionAccess` / `requireExecutionInScope` require **every** account in that set to be in the session's scope (matched by ID or name). An empty set is a deny.
- The scope gate runs **first**, before RBAC and Constraints, on every session path: the approve, cancel and revoke dispatchers, `approvePurchaseViaSession` / `cancelPurchaseViaSession`, `tryRevokeViaSession`, `revokeScheduledExecution`, retry, and pause/resume/run-now/delete. Purchase details and the planned/upcoming lists now use the same rule instead of the plan-only check, so a B child row is neither readable nor listed for an A-scoped user.
- In the approve/cancel/revoke dispatchers a scope miss falls through to the email-token branch only when a token is present (`fallsThroughToToken(err, token)`). The `contact_email` token path stays unscoped, as the issue intends. Without a token an out-of-scope session gets the same 404 as a missing row, so the token/session branches' status guards (409/410/401) cannot confirm the execution exists or leak its status.
- The revoke status guard (`checkRevokableStatus`, 409) now runs only after authorization: in `tryRevokeViaSession` after the scope/RBAC and CSRF checks, and in the token path after `validateRevokeToken`. Before, it ran first, so an out-of-scope session or an unauthenticated caller got "still pending" / "cannot be revoked" for a non-completed execution. An authorized caller still gets the 409.
- Rebased onto main, keeping every guard from #375, #378, #392, #405, #406 and #409.

Also covers audit finding A16-009 (`TestAuthorizeSessionRevokeExecution_Matrix`): the `revoke-any` allow path, the `!hasOwn` 403 and both permission-lookup error paths of `authorizeSessionRevokeExecution` had no tests.

## Regression tests

`internal/api/execution_scope_test.go`, existing mocks only:

- `TestExecutionEndpoints_ScopeMatrix`: {plan-level parent with nil `CloudAccountID`, fan-out child, ad-hoc with `PlanID` ""} x {all accounts in scope: allow, partial scope: deny, no scope: deny} x {approve, cancel, retry, revoke completed via session, revoke scheduled, run now, pause, resume, delete, details}, 90 subtests. The caller holds admin plus every carved-out money verb, so only the scope gate can refuse. Deny cases assert the 404 and that none of the mutations (all four store methods and all three purchase-manager methods, literal names, full matcher arity) run; allow cases assert the mutation is reached. `GetPlanAccounts("")` errors in the mock, as Postgres does.
- `TestExecutionEndpoints_OutOfScopeNoTokenIs404`: an out-of-scope session with no token gets 404 on approve/cancel (wrong status) and on revoke of completed, pending, notified and failed executions, not 409/401. The pending/notified/failed revoke cases fail on `5907bb80` (409 from the status guard) and pass now.
- `TestRevoke_AuthorizedNonRevocableStatusIs409`: an authorized caller, via the session and via the email token, still gets 409 for pending/notified/failed and no mutation runs.
- `TestHandler_revokePurchase_PendingExecution` (existing) asserted the leak: a caller with no session got 409 for a pending execution. It now expects 401.
- `TestCancel_OutOfScopeSessionWithTokenUsesContactGate`: an out-of-scope session carrying a valid token reaches the token branch and succeeds as the account's contact email.
- `TestExecutionAccounts_AdHocUnattributedDenied`: nil and empty recommendation accounts deny.
- `TestPlannedPurchases_HidesPartiallyScopedParent`: the list hides a parent for a partially-scoped session and shows it when fully scoped.

Mutation proofs (helper replaced, tests re-run):

| Mutation | Failing tests |
|---|---|
| previous head's logic (plan intersection + `CloudAccountID`) | plan parent/partial (10), ad-hoc all/partial/none (30), the 3 no-token 404 cases, token fall-through, ad-hoc unattributed, planned-list |
| main's logic (plan intersection only) | the above plus fan-out child/partial (10) |
| `fallsThroughToToken` ignoring the token | all 3 no-token 404 cases |

The "no scope" deny cases for the parent and child also pass under the old logic, since plan intersection already refuses them; they are kept as matrix coverage.

## Verification

With `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6`:

- `go build ./internal/...`: clean
- `go test -race -short ./internal/api ./internal/server ./internal/mocks`: ok, ok, ok (includes `TestNoUnfailableMockAssertions`, which failed on `5907bb80` on the matrix's non-literal `AssertNotCalled` names and the unresolvable mock type returned by the helper; the test now constructs the mocks itself)
- `golangci-lint` v2.10.1 on `./internal/api/...`: 0 issues
- `gocyclo -over 10` on the changed files: no hits
- pre-commit hooks: passed

The previous head's Lint Code failure (`internal/scheduler` could not import `providers/azure`) was a proxy.golang.org `stream error ... INTERNAL_ERROR` while downloading `armcosmos/v2@v2.7.0`, not a code issue; Lint Code passes on main (`ca4b0b21`).

Docker is unavailable on this host, so testcontainers-based DB integration tests were not run locally; they run in CI.

## Related

Follow-ups found in review: #432 (approve's orphan-preflight 409 runs before any session or scope check), #433 (`AccountScope.Allows` matches display names, which are not unique).

Per-permission Constraints (`LeanerCloud/cloud-commitments-cli#1300`) is a different mechanism, handled separately.

Closes #92

## What

Documentation only (SPEC S3 / REPORT rec B, ch03). narduk-core's mutation wrappers and body helpers in `runtime/server/utils/mutation.ts` are auto-imported into every app, but the README never mentioned them. The deep dive found that 2 of 23 mutating routes in one app used them, and 0 in another.

A new README section, "Mutating routes: `defineUserMutation` and `withValidatedBody`", covers:
- an example: a Zod body with `withValidatedBody(schema.parse)` and a `defineRateLimitPolicy` limit
- the fixed order: rate limit, then auth, then body parse, then handler. An over-limit or anonymous caller is refused before the body is read
- a wrapper table: public, user, admin and cron mutations, plus user and admin queries, and what each handler receives
- the options: `rateLimit` is required; `parseBody`; `requiredScopes` applies to API-key callers only
- how failures are answered: a `ZodError` becomes the same 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` as `defineValidatedHandler`, an HTTP error passes through, anything else becomes 400 `Invalid request body`. Also `withOptionalValidatedBody` and `requireMutationBody`
- when to use `defineValidatedHandler` instead

No code changes. I checked every statement against `mutation.ts`, `mutationValidation.ts`, `auth.ts` (`requireAuthScopes`) and the generated Nitro auto-import list. The changeset is a patch for narduk-core plus `create-narduk-app: patch`, which `release-plan:check` requires because the generator pins core.

body:
Iteration 3 of `docs/agent-work/mobile-and-invites/GOAL.md`. The second adversarial round — fresh-context critics on the **shipped artifact** (races/ops and the invited friend) — found one P0 and a cluster of P1s. All fixed here, and the guard now **measures** each one instead of assuming it.

## The P0 and the P1s

- **P0 — the resume card's Join could never join.** `#room-code` was only prefilled for `?room=` links, so "Welcome back / Rejoin the arena" left the field empty and the button did nothing. Prefilled now (and the copy says *Rejoin*, not *Join*, for a returning pilot).
- **Takeover ran before the join was validated**, so a bad code kicked your own other device out of a live match. Takeover now happens after the room is resolved and admitted.
- **Held-empty rooms could exhaust `maxRooms`** (8 create+leave sequences → 5 minutes of `rooms_full` and a capacity alert at 0 players). At the cap the server now reaps a room with nobody in it first; `rooms_full` only when every room has a human.
- **The `/join` card advertised held-empty rooms as live** ("1 pilot · 5:00 left"). Liveness requires a human; an empty held room says "Waiting for players".
- **`invite-mode` was never removed**, so a failed join could leave the lobby without Quick Play. Removed on leave/failure. The transport error is human copy now, never `xhr poll error …`.
- **The weapon rail sat in the aim lane.** Measured: a single tap at (320, 320) swapped LASER → GRENADE, and the rail covered 17.8 % × 29.4 % of the fire surface. It lives in the top-right chrome corner now, under Menu, outside the resting thumb arc.
- **A kill rendered clipped behind the rail**, and **four wrapped chat lines painted over the kill feed** (guard measured `log.bottom 328 > feed.y 256`). Chat and kills are one stacked lane (`#feed-stack`; desktop keeps its own layout via `display: contents`), and the guard asserts `log.bottom + 8 ≤ feed.top` with four long messages *and* a kill on screen.

## HUD round 3 (two more adversaries) + your feedback

- **Smaller, balanced**: 44 px targets with an 8 px gap (HIG floor, ≈8.2 mm — the same physical target as Material's 48 dp), no container slab; the "smaller" comes from the paint. The **selected** weapon expands to name itself and its cost ("Laser · 25 energy"), which is what a first-timer needs to learn the rail.
- **Chat re-homed**: top-left on Menu's row (mirror-symmetric), out of the weapon rail's column, above the message lane it opens. Landscape puts it on the bar's single row.
- **Landscape**: compact rail (40 px) under `max-height: 480px`; the guard walks 740×360 and asserts no control collisions and the rail above the thumb arc.
- **Typing is not shooting**: an arena tap while composing no longer fires or wipes the draft.
- **Bots are opt-in** (your request): the "fill empty seats with bots" box defaults off, so an arena is humans unless you ask for bots.

## Evidence

```
npm test                                 → 293 tests / 293 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped
npm run test:browser                     → 19 PASS, no browser exceptions
node scripts/verification/invite-journey.cjs → PASS
   portrait: rail 119x148 @ x233 (right edge, below Menu), chat 44x44 @ (12,60) on Menu's row,
             message lane clears the kill feed, rail display-only while firing
   landscape 740x360: no control collisions, rail above the thumb arc, chat on the bar row
tests/invite-flow.test.js                → 5 pass
```

## Still open (the loop continues — iteration 4)

- Moderation minimum: room lock, block/mute, private report sink (the security critic's must-fix 5).
- The no-WebGL invite copy (an invited friend currently loses the card when the renderer cannot start).
- The composer-vs-keyboard assertion (needs a real device/soft keyboard).
- Vitals vs the thumb arc: hull/energy sit in the top-right dead space; moving them under the clock is a product call.

Dois retornos do teste no iPhone.

**PDF saía com uma página só.** O app vive dentro de uma área rolável — a `ScrollView` do React Native Web vira um `div` com rolagem — e o navegador imprime o que cabe na tela, não o que existe no documento. **Compartilhar mandava só os títulos.** A primeira versão mandava as três posições achando que o mapa inteiro não cabia numa mensagem. author: radawson
body:
## Why

Commit `5ebcbee92`, *"docs: generalise the operator note; this repo is public"*, cleaned one operator note and left the seed-estate survey tables directly beneath it — per-host RPC port layout, which configuration files were still the shipped example, and which host was unconfigured. The author knew the repository was public and still missed it, because "be careful about internal details" has no mechanical surface. This PR gives it one.

## The rule

`.cursor/rules/37-internal-information-boundary.mdc` (`alwaysApply`, placed beside `36-secret-locality` since that rule already answers "what lives where"). Three forbidden classes:

1. **Non-public Foundation host identities** — and the LAN addressing that reaches them.
2. **Per-host operational state** — reachability, RPC exposure, pristine-vs-edited configs, per-host peer limits. The dangerous class: a hostname alone is a naming convention; a hostname joined to *"its config is the unedited example file"* is a target.
3. **Local filesystem paths and personal identifiers.**

The guidance is to write the **role**, not the host — "the floor device" rather than a DNS name. That costs no precision: the role is the half a reader needs and the hostname is the half an attacker does. Evidence is never what gets removed; only identity and state.

**Seed identity is a carve-out, not an oversight.** A seed exists to be dialed by strangers — the addresses ship in every binary's `get_seed_nodes` and the onions are headed there, so publishing them discloses nothing an intending peer cannot already learn. Seed *operational state* is not carved out: "the seeds are at `A`…`F`" is shipped fact, "this one's config is the unedited example and its unrestricted RPC is on `:12030`" is an exposed admin surface.

The rule states what does **not** qualify as a carve-out: "it is useful" and "it is only a hostname".

## The gate

`scripts/ci/check_internal_information.py`, run by `docs-gates.yml`. **240 violations in 43 files → 0.**

It checks the two mechanically checkable classes and, on success, says plainly that it did not check the third — operational state is prose and no grep recognises it. A gate that stayed silent about its own blind spot would let a reviewer read a pass as "the rule is satisfied", which it does not say. Per `47-gate-subject-assertion.mdc` it also fails when it enumerates implausibly few files, so an empty pass cannot look like a clean one.

The allowlist carries a reason per entry, so adding one shows up in a diff.

## What moved, and the one item that mattered

Most of the 240 was `/home/<user>` pasted into benchmark captures 72 times by raw `cargo` output — embarrassing rather than dangerous.

One item was not. The public document stated that the seed hidden-service secret-key backup is a single copy on one machine, **and named that machine as the one also holding the genesis wallet** — one target for two unrelated compromises. Alongside it: which seed ran an unrestricted RPC listener on which port, and which seed's config was the unedited example.

Those, the 2026-08-11 estate probe table, and the per-host peer limits now live in `shekyl-dev`, `docs/Q12_D6A_SEED_ESTATE.md` (commit `e956ed5`). `Q12_D6A_PEER_DISCOVERY_RUN.md` keeps the run's reasoning, its rulings and every measurement it turns on; the custody *requirement* stays as the precondition that still gates Q12-R1, without the location.

## Judgment call left in

`SHEKYL_P2P_PROTOCOL.md:2553` still binds state to a seed. It is the **correction** recording that the August snapshot is stale and the host is now correctly configured — redacting it would make the correction meaningless while hiding nothing open.

## Verification

- `check_internal_information` — 3361 files, clean
- `check_doc_links`, `check_doc_headings`, `check_doc_status_banners`, `check_doc_fossils`, `check_followups_targets`, `check_followups_owners`, `check_followups_row_prose`, `check_index_table_shape`, `check_landed_rows_stamped` — pass
- `check_doc_claims` (baseline monotonic vs `origin/dev`), `check_doc_code_citations` (388 resolved) — pass
- `cargo fmt --check` clean; `shekyl-relay-privacy` and `shekyl-shard-visual` type-check
- `build.sh` and `gap7_pi4_gate.sh` parse; `consensus_constants.json` still valid JSON

## Out of scope

`dev` carries **195 commits with `Co-Authored-By: Claude` trailers**, against `90-commits.mdc`. Removing them means rewriting public history and is a separate decision, not folded in here. The rule and this PR's commits comply going forward.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Documentation, CI policy, and redaction of non-consensus prose; no runtime protocol or consensus constant value changes beyond comment wording.
> 
> **Overview**
> Establishes a **public-repo disclosure boundary** for `shekyl-core`: internal Foundation hostnames, LAN addresses, personal paths, and per-host operational detail belong in private `shekyl-dev`, while measurements and reasoning stay public under **role names** (e.g. “the floor device”, “the testnet miner”) instead of DNS names or `/home/…` paths.
> 
> Adds **`37-internal-information-boundary.mdc`** (three forbidden classes, seed-list carve-out, pointers to `shekyl-dev`) and **`scripts/ci/check_internal_information.py`**, wired into **`docs-gates.yml`**. The gate deny-by-default matches `skl-*`, `10.10.*` LAN, and non-generic `/home/` accounts, with an explicit allowlist; on success it states that **class 2 operational state is review-only**, not grep-enforced.
>

author: yeonjae1220
body:
## 문제

WATCH/MULTI/EXEC CAS(PR #21)는 **Redis에 유효 토큰 역인덱스가 하나만 남는 것**은 보장했지만, **같은 이전 토큰으로 시작한 재발급 중 하나만 성공한다**는 single-use 계약은 보장하지 못했다.

| # | 증상 | 원인 |
|---|------|------|
| 1 | 동시 재발급이 **둘 다 200**, 나중 저장만 유효 → 쿠키가 다른 쪽이면 조용히 로그아웃 | 제출 토큰과 저장 토큰을 비교하지 않음 (find → save 사이 TOCTOU) |
| 2 | refresh 와 경합한 **logout 이 취소됨** | `save()` 의 `putAll` 이 지워진 세션을 재생성 |
| 3 | 교체된 토큰이 다시 와도 기록 없음 | 재사용 감지 없음 |
| 4 | 서버 409(재시도 신호)에도 로그아웃 | `refreshAuth` 가 모든 실패에 `clearAuth()` |
| 5 | 같은 탭에서도 경합 | 선제 갱신 타이머가 raw axios 로 싱글톤 우회 |
| 6 | 여러 탭 동시 복원 시 경합 | single-flight 가 탭 단위 모듈 변수 |

## 변경

**서버** — `TokenStorePort.rotate(rotated, presentedToken)` → `RefreshRotationOutcome`, Lua 한 번으로 판정·쓰기

| 제출 토큰 | 조건 | 결과 |
|---|---|---|
| = 현재 | 세션 유효 | `ROTATED` 200 |
| = 직전 | 교체 후 10초 이내 | `CONCURRENT` **409 `AUTH_CONFLICT`** (Set-Cookie 없음) |
| = 직전 | 10초 이후 | `REUSED` 401 + `Refresh token reuse detected` 경고 로그 |
| 그 외 / 세션 없음 | | `INVALID` 401 (logout 경합 시 세션 재생성 안 함) |

- 재사용 감지는 **기록만** (세션 유지) — iOS WebView 쿠키 flush 오탐(GLOBAL-PIT-051)을 측정한 뒤 폐기 단계로 올린다.
- `save()` 는 신규 세션 전용으로 축소. 설계·대안: `docs/adr/0004-refresh-token-single-use.md`

**프론트** — 모든 재발급을 `refreshAuth()` 로 일원화
- `navigator.locks` 로 탭 사이 직렬화, 409 는 1회 재시도
- 400·401·403 만 로그아웃, 네트워크·5xx·429 는 재시도 후 throw 하고 인증 유지 (GLOBAL-PIT-012)
- 선제 갱신 타이머의 싱글톤 우회 제거, 죽은 코드(`authApi.refresh`, `pendingQueue`) 제거

> 서버·프론트는 **함께 배포해야 한다** — 구 프론트는 409 를 로그아웃으로 처리한다.
> 기존 Redis 세션은 마이그레이션 불필요 (`prevRefreshToken` 없으면 현재 토큰만 비교).

## 검증

- [x] `./gradlew test integrationTest` (JDK 21) — unit 396 · integration 32 전부 통과
- [x] `RedisTokenAdapterTest`: 같은 토큰 8스레드 × 15라운드 → 매 라운드 ROTATED 정확히 1, 나머지 CONCURRENT, 패자 토큰 미저장. Lua 에서 토큰 비교를 빼는 변이로 3개 테스트 실패 확인
- [x] `AuthRefreshApiTest`(실 보안 필터): 409 `AUTH_CONFLICT` + Set-Cookie 없음 / 401 / 200+쿠키
- [x] 로컬 실스택(Postgres·Redis 컨테이너 + Next prod build 프록시): 같은 쿠키 5개 동시 → **200×1, 409×4** · 직전 토큰 유예 내 409 → 유예 후 401 + reuse 로그 → 현재 토큰은 계속 200
- [x] 브라우저: 두 탭이 같은 순간 `/boards` 콜드 스타트 → 재발급이 Web Lock 으로 **겹치지 않고 순차 실행**(둘 다 200), 두 탭 모두 로그인 유지
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`, `next lint` 통과
- [ ] 미검증: Web Locks 미지원 환경에서 409 → 재시도 분기의 브라우저 실행 (서버 409 계약은 테스트로 고정)

author: felipemeriga
body:
## Epoch 3: I/O, CLI, and the acceptance oracle

The engine gets its edges: a streaming reader, the account writer, the CLI contract, and a fixture suite that encodes every documented behavior as an executable oracle.

### What's in here

- **`src/io.rs`** — `read_transactions` streams rows lazily (whitespace-trimmed, flexible field counts); structurally broken or invalid rows are logged to stderr with their line number and skipped — the stream never stops for a typo. `write_accounts` emits the `client,available,held,total,locked` CSV with four-decimal amounts. `run_sequential` ties reader to engine, logging domain rejections at warn level.
- **`src/main.rs`** — the exact CLI contract: `cargo run -- transactions.csv > accounts.csv`. stdout carries only the result CSV (verified empty on every failure path); all diagnostics go to stderr; missing argument or unopenable file exits non-zero.
- **`tests/cli.rs`** — binary-level tests via `CARGO_BIN_EXE`, including stdout-purity assertions on failure paths and collision-free temp files.
- **`tests/fixtures/` + `tests/acceptance.rs`** — nine minted scenarios, each paired with a hand-traced expected output: happy path, dispute→resolve (with re-dispute), chargeback locking (movements blocked, further verdicts processed), withdrawal disputes, the negative-balance fraud pattern, malformed-row resilience, partner-noise rejections, whitespace tolerance, and empty input. Comparison is order-insensitive and whitespace-normalized, mirroring how automated scoring treats output.

### Testing

38 tests total: 26 unit, 3 CLI binary, 9 acceptance. `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `fmt --check` clean. The full pipeline is now exercised end-to-end from file argument to stdout bytes.

### Next

Epoch 4 adds the deterministic big-CSV generator and multi-million-row stress verification.

author: purush2800
body:
## E-Sign Operational Closure

Closes the E-Sign → Core business loop as an **independent signing platform** (Independent-Digital-Signature-Platform Directive), reconciling the Operational Closure directive. Additive; DOC-1..DOC-6 not reopened.

### What lands
- **Backbone (B1–B9):** E-Sign durable outbox delivery (retry/backoff migration + generic lifecycle event with stable `event_id` = outbox row id + lease-guarded delivery service + lifecycle-managed worker, no `@nestjs/schedule`/Redis + HMAC+timestamp webhook publisher signing `${timestamp}.${raw body}`). Core-owned authenticated receiver `POST /v1/integrations/esign/events` (HMAC + timestamp-window verify, dedup, **in-process** write-back). `/v1/documents/esign-writeback` reclassified transitional. OpenAPI + Pact contract (esign-service → aramo-core; provider `requestFilter` re-sign, **test-only secret, no production tolerance change**).
- **OC-1** signer-request delivery (`SIGNATURE_REQUEST`; raw token never leaves E-Sign).
- **OC-4** nginx `depends_on` esign-service + env passthrough.
- **OC-5** RtrPanel mounted (status backend-derived). **OC-7** OfferLetterPanel mounted (evidence-only, dual-state; signing never transitions Offer). **OC-8** role-distinct executed vs execution-certificate access.
- **OC-6** RTR readiness **E2E through the real signed webhook** (Postgres 17): before → `SUBMITTAL_RTR_NOT_EXECUTED`; webhook → Document `EXECUTED` + readiness satisfied; wrong requisition → still denied; unsigned → `401`.

### Facts
- Migrations: **1** (esign outbox delivery-retry, additive). New error codes: **0**. New Pact interactions: **1** (E-Sign→Core webhook).
- Local: lint / vocab / OpenAPI / env-passthrough / typecheck all green; esign 6, esign-service 14, ats-web 13, api verifier 8, OC-6 2/2, pact consumer 3, provider `verify-esign` 1/1 + verify-api E-Sign interaction green.

### ⚠ Pre-existing Pact environment condition (NOT introduced by this branch)
The aramo-core provider wall shows **25 ats-web/portal interaction failures**. These:
- **reproduce identically on clean `origin/main`** (baselined),
- are **not introduced by this branch**,
- affect **ATS Web / portal** interactions only,
- do **not** affect the new E-Sign provider interaction,
- and the **new E-Sign Pact interaction is green**.

They are a separately-classified known environment condition and are **intentionally not fixed in this PR** (that would contaminate the closure scope).

### Deferred (separate increment, not this PR)
Mature reusable S2S auth for the internal Core→E-Sign **command** seam. The new E-Sign→Core **lifecycle webhook is authenticated** (HMAC + timestamp).

No PROD deployment performed.

author: martinsadir21
body:
## Qué se hizo
Se implementó la API de autenticación completa. Se crearon los endpoints de registro (`/register`) y login (`/login`) en el controlador de auth. Además, se integró `bcrypt` para el hasheo seguro de contraseñas y se implementó un middleware de seguridad usando `jsonwebtoken` (JWT) para proteger las rutas privadas.

## Por qué
Para cumplir con el requerimiento "Usuarios & Auth" de las funcionalidades nucleares del Sprint 2. Esto establece la base de seguridad necesaria para que más adelante los usuarios logueados puedan gestionar su carrito de compras y realizar pedidos.

Closes #36

## Vinculación obligatoria
- Issue / Tarjeta en GitHub Projects: `#36`
- Sprint: `Sprint 2`
- Rama: `feat/api-auth`

## Cómo probar
1. Descargar esta rama, asegurar que el archivo `.env` tenga la variable `JWT_SECRET` configurada (ver `.env.example`) y ejecutar `npm install` para instalar `bcrypt` y `jsonwebtoken`.
2. Levantar el servidor con `node server.js`.
3. En Postman, hacer un `POST` a `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/register` con un JSON en el body que contenga `email` y `password` para registrar un usuario (verificando el status `201`).
4. Hacer un `POST` a `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login` con las mismas credenciales y verificar que la API responda con el status `200` y devuelva el token JWT.

## Uso de IA
Se utilizó Gemini para estructurar la lógica del controlador de autenticación, implementar las mejores prácticas de hasheo con `bcrypt` (uso de salt) y configurar correctamente la firma y verificación del token en el middleware de JWT.

## Notas para el reviewer
- Se agregó `JWT_SECRET` como variable de entorno. Recuerden actualizar sus archivos `.env` locales basándose en el `.env.example` para poder probar el login.
- El token JWT está configurado actualmente para expirar en 2 horas.

author: andymac4182
body:
## Summary

**M4-53: the refresh schedule from docs/cluster.md.** This implements the owner-delegated decision.

- **Relay.** A stream refresh is now confirmed for the rest of its catalog snapshot: at most 5 s from the read's start. The bound is also enforced on the monotonic clock, from the challenge's receipt, so a wall-clock step cannot lengthen it. Cluster clock skew cannot lengthen it either, because the snapshot bound is computed in the relay's own frame. The 2 s `challenge_interval` now bounds only how late the relay may answer.
- **Connector.** It refreshes 2 s after the confirmed challenge started, or once 1.5 s is left if that comes first. A 2 s confirmation therefore keeps the old schedule; that covers the admission confirmation and older relays.

**M4-70: a lapse is retryable.**

- **New reset reason.** 4006 `AUTHORIZATION_STALE` marks a lapse, and the relay closes it 1011. An invalidation keeps 4001, which closes 1008.
- **Bounded retry.** An unanswered refresh is retried after 2 s with a fresh nonce. There are at most 3 challenges per refresh, and a retry never goes past the refresh's lapse deadline (first challenge + `grant_timeout_ms`, ≤ 5 s). Only the latest nonce is accepted.
- **Late relay reads.** If a read lands after the answer window and every bound is still valid, the stream still ends at once, so a suspended device fails closed (EC-055). It ends as "authorization stale" (`AUTHORIZATION_STALE`, a 1011 close) rather than as a 1008 revocation. The relay takes a replacement challenge only after the in-flight one's window has passed.
- **Unchanged.** A lapsed token, snapshot or credential still closes 1008.

## Measurements

Filesystem demo, one idle session held for 30 s, with a counting TLS front on the shared Redis:

| | refreshes/s per stream | refresh EVALs/s | all EVALs/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (`bfbd48cc`) | 2.0 (120/min) | 5.98 | 9.04 |
| after | 0.46 (28/min) | 1.42 | 4.53 |

**Revocation.** `revoke-grant` under a live session:

- Before this change the session closed 1008 in 214 and 111 ms.
- After it, the session closed 1008 in 1,071, 1,279 and 1,063 ms.
- `verify-m4-fs-real-path` measured 2,069 ms.

All of these are within the 5 s bound plus 1 s of tolerance.

## Gates and tests

- `verify-m4-fs-real-path` now bounds the renewals of an idle stream at 9 or fewer in its 12 s hold. It measured 6; the same hold gave 24 before this change. It also requires the revoked session to close within 6,000 ms.
- Each new connector and relay unit test goes red under a recorded mutation; there are 9 mutations in total.

## Review fixes (Opus review at `b66d44cb`)

**The connector no longer breaks the 5 s revocation bound.** Sending a refresh used to extend the stream's deadline to the refresh's start plus `grant_timeout_ms`. That let queued 9P requests and buffered HTTP chunks run about 7.1 s after the last authorizing read.

- **(a) The refresh's lapse deadline is capped.** It is now min(now + `grant_timeout_ms`, the previous confirmed deadline), which is cluster.md's rule. A confirmation is measured afresh from its own challenge's start.
- **(b) Defence in depth.** `StreamAuthority` now carries the confirmed deadline and reports stale once it has passed. `http_read` checks expiry while a refresh is in flight, and also against a separately held `confirmed_until`.

**Other fixes from the review:**

- An invalidation for a challenge that a retry retired is now honoured.
- The retry fires at 2.25 s instead of 2 s, so the relay does not ignore the replacement.
- An operation-deadline expiry now resets `ADAPTER_FAILURE` (4004) instead of `AUTHORIZATION_STALE`.
- An echo stream's held records now get `AUTHORIZATION_UNAVAILABLE` when a refresh read answers too late (a stale lapse), instead of `AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED`.
- The timing gate now requires `AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED` as the cause, and bounds its wait by the admission deadline it captured plus 250 ms.
- `protocol.md` now says that a receiver treats every reset reason except 4001, including an unknown one, as not about authorization, so the consumer gets 1011.
- Filed M4-75 (M4-72 was taken on main by #246): the relay does not abort a refresh read it has superseded.

**After merging main with #246 (`7e2e40b7`):** clippy passed; `cargo test --workspace` passed 2,836 with 0 failed; the M1, M4 and M7 credential-expiry and timing gates passed locally. The M4 harness renewed 6 times in its idle hold, and its revoked session closed 1008 in 2,099 ms.

**Tests.** Six new mutations (M10–M15) each turn their test red. The earlier M1–M9 were re-run and are still red.

**Re-measured at `0e1b3ae0`:**

- An idle stream refreshes 0.46 times a second, which is 1.39 refresh EVALs a second.
- After a revocation, live sessions closed 1008 in 1,469, 1,477 and 1,470 ms.
- The M4 harness renewed 5 times during its idle hold, and its revoked session closed 1008 in 2,055 ms.
- The M7 timing gate passed 3 of 3 runs, each with cause `AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED`.
- The workspace test run: 2,827 passed, 0 failed.

The fix narrows the stall tolerance to about 3 s. That value is still unmeasured, so M6-C87 stays open.

## Correction after the first hosted run

Hosted CI at `c6bd8e64` failed `verify-m7-timing-boundaries`, and the failure had two causes.

1. **The gate's timing assumption.** The gate assumed the old refresh schedule, so it now bounds the prior confirmation's end at 5 s from the refresh challenge's start.
2. **A real defect in the first M4-70 design.** That design kept a stream open when its refresh read landed late, which left a suspended device's stream open. The stream now fails closed, as stale. `01e4d9c3` passed every hosted job, M7 included.

## Verification (local, at the merged head's code)

All of the following passed:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast`: 2,821 passed, 0 failed, after merging main
- `scripts/m1-harness-verify.sh`
- `scripts/m4-harness-verify.sh`
- `verify-m7-credential-expiry-rotation`
- `scripts/m7-harness-verify.sh`, every gate except its Docker lane-restart gate. That gate hung in `docker run` because this host's Docker daemon is wedged; it did not fail.
- The tracker scripts
- `m6-release-checks.py --check secrets`

**Not claimed.** M6-C87's stall tolerance was not re-measured, and that row stays open.

body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
Closes #273

## Problem

`coach codesignal --baseline extra-positional-arg` exits 0 and prints a report. Go's `flag` package stops at the first non-flag token, so every flag after that positional is discarded. `coach codesignal --baseline extra-positional-arg --format json` returns text, exit 0, empty stderr. Suggest mode already rejects positionals with `project_config_suggestion_invalid_arguments` and exit 2. Issue: https://github.com/lousy-agents/coach/issues/273

## Change

The main scan path (`validateCodesignalFlags`) now receives `flags.Args()`. After the existing flag checks pass, a leftover token is a usage error: `codesignalUsage` plus `coach: unexpected positional argument %q` on stderr, nothing on stdout, exit 2. Suggest, check-project, and prepare-compiler validators are unchanged. `docs/cli-codesignal.md` states that contract. The living pilot evaluation archives the #273 claim.

## Scope
- [x] Single concern (no bundled drive-bys)
- Related PRs (open + closed search): #234 (suggest-mode positional rejection, merged), #306 (project-config exit contract, merged, explicitly out of scope here)
- Out of scope / deferred: `--project-config` failure exit/stream contract, unstable JSON key presence, `--build-target` toolchain requirement (#63), adding a positional operand form

## Architecture invariants
- [x] `pkg/semantics` does not import `pkg/githubingest` / `go-github` / `ghinstallation`
- [x] `pkg/githubingest` does not import `pkg/semantics`
- [x] Public JSON / error sentinels unchanged, or change is intentional and tested
- [x] Production HTTP clients keep a finite `Timeout` (no bare `http.DefaultClient`)
- [x] Store/dependency errors on protected paths fail closed (503 + stable envelope)
- [x] New comments follow AGENTS.md comment policy; existing comments left unless the task asks

No new comments. No HTTP, store, or package-boundary edits. Suggest-mode envelope code is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria → evidence

| Criterion | Where satisfied |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1. Main scan path with a positional: usage on stderr, empty stdout, exit 2 | `validateCodesignalFlags` in `cmd/coach/main.go`; `DescribeTable` "exits 2, writes nothing to stdout..." in `cmd/coach/positional_arguments_acceptance_test.go` |
| AC-2. A flag after a positional is rejected, not discarded | Same table entry "after --baseline when --format json follows the positional..." |
| AC-3. `--baseline extra-arg --format json` emits no report | That entry asserts exit 2 and empty stdout, not a JSON document |
| AC-4. Suggest mode keeps `project_config_suggestion_invalid_arguments` | No change to `validateSuggestProjectConfigFlags`; existing entry "combined with a positional argument" in `cmd/coach/project_config_suggestion_acceptance_test.go` still passed |
| AC-5. No positional: behavior unchanged | Positional check runs only after existing flag checks and only when `flags.Args()` is non-empty. Preservation specs still passed: "still includes it in a Repository Baseline", "--base resolves and there are commits since it", "explains they are mutually exclusive" |
| AC-6. Message quotes the offending argument; usage text; not the suggest envelope | `fmt.Sprintf("coach: unexpected positional argument %q", positional[0])` plus the existing `codesignalUsage` stderr path. Specs require `usage: coach codesignal`, the quoted token, and the absence of `project_config_suggestion_invalid_arguments`. Two positionals quote `"foo"` and not `"bar"` |
| AC-7. Living evaluation restamped | `docs/product/evaluations/codesignal-pilot-readiness.html`: #273 moved to the closed archive, path chip removed, Last reviewed 28 Sep 2026, HEAD `d4aa0b2`, 24th pass, `#282 · 9 / 24`. Verdict stays "Stay in pilot." |

## Acceptance-test-first
- Policy: failing acceptance test landed BEFORE production implementation
- Test file(s): `cmd/coach/positional_arguments_acceptance_test.go`
- Form: Ginkgo v2 `Describe`/`When`/`It` plus `DescribeTable` in `*_acceptance_test.go`, picked up by existing `TestCoachAcceptance`
- Red command + outcome:
```
go test -count=1 ./cmd/coach -run TestCoachAcceptance -ginkgo.focus="quotes the unexpected argument" -ginkgo.v
```
4 specs failed on the bug: exit code 0 and a non-empty report. The `--format json` case failed the same way, on a text report (`Repository Baseline for revision ...` / `No active CodeSignal findings.`), not because stdout was invalid JSON. `--base HEAD~1 bogus` failed with stdout `scope: production, filtered: 0, files analyzed: 1...` and exit 0. Ran 4 of 631 specs: 0 passed, 4 failed.
- Green command + outcome (same test):
```
go test -v -count=1 -run TestCoachAcceptance ./cmd/coach -ginkgo.focus 'quotes the unexpected argument' -ginkgo.fail-on-empty -ginkgo.no-color
```
`SUCCESS! -- 4 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 627 Skipped`
- [x] False-green check: test exercises the intended branch/failure mode (not a shared clock/fake making a different path look correct)

The red step ran the built `coach` binary. It does not call `parseCodesignalFlags` in process and does not use `runCoachSuggest`. The `--format json` assertion is rejection (exit 2, empty stdout), so honoring the trailing flag would not turn it green.

## Validation run

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go CI slice | `mise run ci` | not run. `/implement-issue` step 4 uses `mise run ci-fast`. The exhaustive gate is GitHub Actions. |
| Acceptance fast | `mise run test-acceptance-fast` | not invoked as that alias. The same `TestCoachAcceptance` suite ran inside `mise run ci-fast` (`go test -race ./...`, `cmd/coach` ok, 164.803s) and the focused green command above passed 4 specs. Preservation focus (suggest positional, baseline, `--base`, mutually exclusive) also passed 4 specs. |
| JS (if touched) | `mise run js-ci` | N/A for product JS. `ci-fast` did build the semantics sidecar and ran `workflow-test` (38 pass) and `opencode-plugin-test` (32 pass). |
| WASM (if tags/engine touched) | `mise run wasm-build` | N/A. Engine and build tags untouched. |
| Focused package | `go test -race ./cmd/coach -run TestCoachAcceptance` | pass, as part of `mise run ci-fast` (`ok github.com/lousy-agents/coach/cmd/coach 164.803s`) |

Extra verification: orchestrator `mise run ci-fast` exited 0 on this tree before commit (`gofmt`, `go-vet`, `acceptance-style-check`, sidecar build, `go test -race ./...`, workflow-test, opencode-plugin-test). The task reviewer and the integration reviewer each reported their own `mise run ci-fast` exit 0. Pass 24 re-ran four built-binary invocations (`--baseline extra-positional-arg`, the same plus `--format json`, `--base HEAD~1 bogus`, `--baseline foo bar --format json`): each exit 2, empty stdout, usage on stderr, quoting the first residual token. Not a corpus replay.

## Alternatives considered

Checking positionals before the other usage checks would change `coach codesignal extra` from today's "missing required --base" message to a quoted positional. The issue's reproductions all have otherwise-valid flags first, and AC-5 says no-positional behavior stays. The new check therefore runs only after those existing checks pass.

`rejectPositionalArgs` was not reused. It does not quote the token and it names a mode flag (`--suggest-project-config`, `--check-project`, `--prepare-compiler`). The main path quotes the first residual token instead.

## Risk / rollback

Invocations that passed a stray operand and exited 0 now exit 2 with empty stdout. That is the fix; scripts that depended on the silent report will fail at the CLI instead of downstream. Flag-only `--baseline` and `--base` invocations are unchanged. Suggest-mode stderr stays the structured envelope. Revert the branch to restore the previous exit 0.

## Review process
- Implementer/reviewer cycles: 1 × implement→review on T1 until PASS. No parallel tasks (one task; splitting would share `cmd/coach/main.go`). Integration review: 1 round, PASS. Plan self-check: no false para

author: k1low
body:
`prerelease_for_tagpr` installed gocredits at `@latest` through `depsdev`, so the version generating CREDITS was whatever had been released most recently. The v0.x releases read the module list from go.sum, so CREDITS also credits `github.com/google/go-cmp`, which only the tests import.

A `credits` target now installs gocredits pinned to v1.0.0 and `prerelease_for_tagpr` calls it. v1.0.0 collects modules with `go list` over every platform, so `prerelease_for_tagpr` no longer depends on `depsdev`. This follows k1LoW/octocov@c919651. With v1.0.0 the next release PR drops go-cmp from CREDITS.

Every module has a license gocredits can read, so `-skip-missing` is not used. A new dependency without one will make `make credits` fail instead of dropping out of CREDITS silently.
