author: brandon-fryslie
body:
The `race` job ran under `go test`'s default 10-minute per-package timeout. Under the detector `internal/cli` takes 446s median (79 CI runs to 2026-09-28). Runs 36312282343 and 36320546964 died at 600s in `internal/cli` with the running test 1–2s old, on runners that also took `internal/store` 1.4x its median. Nothing was hung; the binary was slow. The default timeout had become a second slowness alarm, and it fired before `tools/testbudget`, the check that is meant to catch slowness.

The job now passes `-timeout 30m`. The number is sized from the budget that binds, `internal/cli`'s 340s: ×2.6 under the detector (median race/non-race ratio across the same 79 paired runs) ×1.6 on a slow runner ≈ 24m. The next-largest budget, `internal/store`'s 210s, inflates to about 8m before any runner factor. The derivation lives once, in the ci.yml step comment. The spec's two descriptions of the race command and the changelog state only the lane's role.

Cost: a test that genuinely hangs now takes about 30 minutes to be reported instead of 10.

Measured margin: the 446s median is 25% of the timeout.

Review: `/code-review` high, medium and low. High's findings on scope ("every ceiling"), wording (the lane also fails on ordinary test failures), the slow-runner factor (store's applied to cli), duplication and anchoring are fixed in a82e06f3. Declined: making `internal/cli` cheaper under `-race`. Slowness is testbudget's single enforcer, and the race lane's floor moves only when cli's un-instrumented time does. Also declined: rewriting the header's dated 2026-08-26 figure (117s→242s), which is a historical measurement supporting a different point.

Before: в кампании можно было только переписываться в чате. Героев не было, а место ИИ-мастера молчало.

After: игрок собирает героя в комнате кампании (класс, раса, характеристики, навыки, снаряжение), и мастер его одобряет. ИИ-мастер отвечает на действия игроков: бросает проверки, проводит атаки, накладывает состояния, выдаёт предметы, выставляет существ и описывает итог. Числа считает только сервер. Модель подключается ключом Claude в `.env` или локально через LM Studio.

How:
- `app/tools/`: реестр инструментов (Pydantic-схема и обработчик). Допустимые id подставляются в схему на каждый ход. У вызовов есть идемпотентность и точка сохранения на каждый вызов. Журнал событий хранит кубики и обратную дельту.
- `app/core/world.py` и `app/rules/dnd5e/{character,modifiers}.py`: вычисляют листы, КД, атаки, модификаторы состояний, зоны дистанции и бюджет встречи.
- `app/agents/master.py`: очередь ходов по кампаниям и окно сбора реплик. Фаза решения: не больше 8 вызовов, контракт намерения с автоматическим отказом. Затем повествование без инструментов и аудитор разметки `[[id|текст]]`. Весь ход проходит одной транзакцией и откатывается при сбое. Каждый вызов модели учитывается в `llm_calls`, есть лимит расходов.
- `app/api/characters.py`: конструктор, броски 4d6 один раз, отправка героя на проверку, проверка живым или ИИ-мастером. Тайная предыстория видна только владельцу и мастеру.
- Базовый пакет 0.2.0: 334 существа, 12 классов и 9 рас из SRD (`tools/import_srd.py`), зелья, снаряжение и падение.
- Миграция 0002 проверена на PostgreSQL и SQLite, в том числе на уже существующей кампании. В SQLite включены настоящие SAVEPOINT: иначе откат хода не откатывал инструменты.
- Во временный клиент добавлены конструктор героя, лист, проверка героев мастером, статус мастера и выбор LM Studio.
- Тесты: 100 проходят на SQLite и PostgreSQL. Ход мастера проверяется на модели с заданными ответами.

В этот этап не вошли: `lookup_rules`, заклинания, самостоятельные ходы монстров и очередь инициативы (этап 4), сводки и память (этап 5).

author: tamassoltesz
body:
## Why

A call chain that holds one pooled connection (inside a `startTransaction`) and borrows a **second from the same pool** is the hold-and-wait exhaustion pattern behind the OAuth non-rotating-refresh regression and `WebAuthN.updateUserEmail`. Both reached the second connection through **helper indirection** (lambda → helper → borrowing call), which static analysis (ArchUnit's `callMethod`) can't catch without flooding false positives across the helpers' legitimate non-transactional callers. A runtime tripwire at the point of acquisition is precise and indirection-proof.

## What

- **In-memory `ConnectionPool`:** mirrors the guard added to the postgresql plugin (companion PR → `9.9`). Marks "in a transaction on pool P" in `startTransactionHelper` after it takes its own connection, and rejects a *new* same-pool borrow while that mark is set. Keyed per pool (cross-tenant borrows allowed); active only under `Start.isTesting` — no-op in production.
- **Regression test** (`NestedConnectionAcquisitionGuardTest`): opens a transaction and, inside it, borrows a second connection from the same pool; asserts the guard fires, that a clean transaction still works (positive control), and that per-thread state is cleaned up afterward.

## Notes

- Companion PR: supertokens-postgresql-plugin → `9.9` (the real pool). This one covers the in-memory pool and carries the test.
- **Draft:** the guard is a tripwire — CI may surface additional un-audited instances (that IS the guard working). Known: OAuth non-rotating refresh (being fixed on its own branch), `WebAuthN.updateUserEmail` (fixed, #1460). Verified locally: full clean multi-repo build compiles (main + test). The local test-runner was blocked by an unrelated pre-existing pg `jar` packaging quirk (duplicate `SchemaVerifier.class`), so CI is the authoritative test run.

author: makhnogk
body:
Phase 5a of the plugin/host migration. The daemon can now serve its
kernel on the network next to the unix socket, and a host can use a
remote kernel by URL. Postgres only. Nothing on the Mac is repointed.

- Listener: with MEMORY_RPC_LISTEN=host:port set, the daemon serves the
  same NDJSON JSON-RPC over TCP. The first frame must be
  `initialize {token}`. A missing, unknown or revoked token, or any
  other first frame, gets one -32001 error line, then the connection
  is closed. Frames sent before the verdict wait for it. A held
  connection is closed once its token is revoked. Only `initialize`,
  `health` and the call surface are served over TCP. The job queue and
  `status` stay on the unix socket, whose 0600 mode is their only
  guard.
- Principal from the token: Writer gains `principal`, set by the
  listener and never parsed from the wire. Policy, quotas, principal
  rows and event subscriptions all use it, and `meta.client` stays the
  session's client label. A pinned principal can only use its own
  sessions. subscribe_events is now stamped with the caller's
  principal. Through the daemon it used to subscribe the daemon's own
  unset identity.
- Tokens: `principal_tokens` (Postgres migration 001) keeps only the
  sha256 of each token. A revoke sets revoked_at and the row stays.
  PrincipalTokenService caches each verdict for 30 s and writes
  last_used_at at most once a minute. The SQLite adapter refuses, and
  on SQLite the daemon logs that the listener is not started.
- `cerebrium-service token issue --principal --label [--out]`, `list`,
  `revoke <id>`. Without --out, the token alone goes to stdout, so it
  can be piped to the client machine. It refuses a non-Postgres store
  before opening it.
- Client: rpc-client accepts tcp://host:port and a token. The handshake
  runs on every new socket, reconnects included, and a refused token
  (RpcAuthError) is never retried. MEMORY_KERNEL_URL and
  MEMORY_KERNEL_TOKEN_FILE name an explicit kernel. The MCP server then
  uses only that kernel: no local daemon, no ensureDaemon, no local
  fallback.
- compose: MEMORY_RPC_LISTEN=0.0.0.0:7433, published on the tailnet
  address only (CEREBRIUM_RPC_BIND, default 100.92.157.103).

Tests: the listener contract (no, bad or revoked token, meta spoofing
ignored, daemon methods refused), the TCP client (handshake, auth
refusal, reconnect re-presents the token, deadlines), explicit-kernel
config, principal pinning on both backends, the token service and CLI

author: abdallahelficky-wq
body:
This fixes two wrong payroll figures in the comprehensive monthly report (section C).

> **⚠ Merging changes figures for months already reported.** "Paid salaries" moves off zero, and "unpaid salaries" rises for past months as well as new ones, because it now includes the net pay sitting in employee sub-accounts. In both cases the correct number replaces a wrong one. But anyone holding an older copy of the report will see a difference for the same month.

## «رواتب مصروفة» — always showed 0
It read `overrides.netTotal` on posted payroll runs. Nothing ever writes that key.

It now shows what was **paid in the month**: debits on the salaries-payable accounts («رواتب مستحقة», matched by name) and on the employee sub-accounts, subject to three rules:
- The debit counts **only when the same entry pays out of a cash or bank account.** A reclassification between an employee account and «رواتب مستحقة», or any other adjustment that moves no cash, is not a payment.
- Payroll entries themselves are excluded.
- A payment reversed in the month is subtracted, using the same rule applied the other way round.

Leave-settlement payouts count as paid, because they go out of cash or bank.

### ⚠ Known limit: WPS / Mudad clearing accounts
A salary payment routed through a clearing account in a separate entry is not counted as paid:
- The entry that moves «رواتب مستحقة» to the clearing account moves no cash.
- The entry that pays the bank from the clearing account doesn't touch a payroll account.

The figure would then **under-report silently**. "Unpaid" stays correct.

This holds today because salaries are paid straight from the bank. Before payroll is routed through WPS or Mudad, the `paysCash` rule has to be extended to recognise that clearing account.

The limit is stated in three places:
- in the code, next to the rule;
- in `docs/reports/comprehensive-monthly.md` (new), which documents how every payroll figure in the report is computed;
- as a note under the payroll section of the report itself.

## «رواتب مستحقة غير مدفوعة» — missed legacy net pay
It read only the accounts named «رواتب مستحقة». Legacy payroll credits each employee's net pay to that employee's own sub-account, so none of it showed up.

It now adds the **credit balances of the employee sub-accounts at month end**, read directly from the ledger:
- **Old months are right too.** It doesn't depend on the switchover, and it doesn't wait for the balances to be paid down.
- **The sub-accounts are found from the chart of accounts:** the posting children of «ذمم الموظفين», and of any group that holds a current employee's account. They are not found from the current employee list. Deleting an employee keeps the account and its entries, so the balance stays in past months.
- An employee's debit balance (money the employee owes) doesn't reduce what is owed to others.
- Unpaid leave settlements booked to the same sub-accounts are included. They are dues owed to the employee, which matches the line's label.

## Mirror, reversal, and reversal-of-mirror path
- **Reversals:**
  - A reversed payment is netted out of "paid", and its balance comes back into "unpaid".
  - A reversal of a payroll entry isn't a payment. It reduces "unpaid" through the balance.
- **Mirrors:** a mirror is an entry in the other company. It counts in that company's report only if it posts to that company's own salaries-payable or employee accounts and pays out of that company's cash or bank. The figures are read per company.

## Tests
- The June legacy run shows 8,700 unpaid and 0 paid. Before this fix, unpaid was 0.
- The July totals month shows July's net plus June's balance still in the sub-accounts.
- An October cash payment counts as paid and reduces unpaid.
- A reclassification with no cash changes neither figure.
- Deleting an employee doesn't change June's unpaid figure.
- Reversing the payment restores unpaid, and paid goes back to 0.

author: blairham
body:
`D08cmdsubst.ztst` was strict 0/1 at **12 differing lines**. It had been a real result long before #4436's ranking and re-opened at #4988 — which was right to refuse what it now refuses. What was lost was one reading of the closing brace, not the option.

`ignoreclosebraces` takes the **reserved** reading of `}` away and leaves the **lexical** one standing: the brace still ends the word it ends, and is then an ordinary word rather than a group's closer. Reading the lexing off the reserved flag makes `a}` one word there — and a word is how an alias is looked up, so `alias CLOSE='};'` inside `$({ OPEN print bye; CLOSE})` stopped expanding and the substitution ran out of text at `)`.

Measured 2026-09-28 on `/opt/homebrew/bin/zsh` — `zsh 5.9.2 (aarch64-apple-darwin25.4.0)`, `go version -m` says *not a Go executable* for it — `-f` over a script file under `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin TERM=dumb` with a scratch `HOME`, the names moved on the line above:

```
                  neither  IB    ICB   both
  print a}        refused  a}    a }   a}
  print a }       refused  a }   a }   a }
  print }a        }a       }a    }a    }a
  print a}b       a}b      a}b   a}b   a}b
```

**The first row is the discriminator and refusal cannot see it.** `echo A}` takes under either name, which is why #4988's nine rows — every one graded on whether a line parses — were right and still left this standing. What separates the names here is how many words reach the command.

So the pair becomes three. `CloseBraceEndsAWord` is the lexical half, implied by `CloseBraceAlwaysReserved` and outliving it; the setter that owns the brace grammar writes all three at once. Every other dialect leaves it off, which is what it already was.

## Before / after

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `D08cmdsubst.ztst` strict | 0/1 | **1/1** |
| its differing lines | 12 | **0** |

The file itself was re-diffed, not the column's total. A forty-cell grid of the two option names over ten snippets agrees with the reference in every cell, after and not only before.

## Mutants

- the lexical reading made to follow the reserved one (`!ib && !icb`) — **2 tests fail**
- the lexer made to read only `CloseBraceAlwaysReserved` again — **the same 2 fail**
- the preset's own `CloseBraceEndsAWord = true` cleared — **survived everything in the package**, because the reserved reading masks it in the preset's own state. A row that reads all three readings back was added for it, and it fails.

Closes #5011

author: chenmingwei23
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** Fix two calibration defects in the wake judge: `owner_acted` cannot tell a read from a write, and a barely-confident `outcome` silently vetoes the owner's own `quiet`.

The label first. `owner_acted` answered True whenever the woken turn made at least one tool call, so a read scored the same as a write and 84 of 84 labelled verdicts came back True. One of those turns made a single read-only call and replied with a 124-character status line -- exactly the quiet cycle the label exists to name.

The mapping second. When the judge's `outcome` answered `needs_action` or `needs_human`, that answer overrode a `quiet` from `needs_owner` at any confidence at all. Because the outcome is chosen by argmax over its own options, it clears 0.5 by construction, so an outcome the judge was barely sure of could silence an owner-quiet the judge was much more sure of.

## Why it matters

The RFC tunes every threshold in the wake judge from the calibration log (`docs/request-for-change/rfc-wake-judge.md` section 3.1a), and a curve needs labels with variance. A constant-True label carries no information, so no threshold in that table can be tuned from the log the RFC says will tune it, and every over-wake the judge commits is invisible in the only reading that looks at it.

The two defects compound. The unconditional override is what produces the extra wakes; the broken label is why nobody could see them. Fixing the measurement is what makes the mapping defect visible, and what lets its fix be judged from data rather than argued.

## Not a goal

- No new threshold beyond `ACTION_OVERRIDE_MIN_P`. It ships at 0.6 as a first value, tunable from the log like every other constant in that table.
- No reader of the new `tool_names_known` field in this PR. It is recorded so a later threshold read can segment on it; reading the curve is separate work. The field is not near-constant -- it is False for every turn on a backend that dispatches without an identity channel, which `claude-agent-acp` and `opencode` both do.
- No change to the judge's prompt, its questions, or their option domains.
- No change to the reply-length or link fallbacks, which still decide a turn that reached the hook with no names.
- No probe or monitor wiring changes.
- No change to the RFC in this PR. The decision it needed is already recorded on main by #14678.

## What changed (motivation -> approach -> change)

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `src/kiro_crew/decisions/points/nudge_wake.py` | an action outcome overrode a quiet owner at any confidence | needs to out-rank that owner AND clear `ACTION_OVERRIDE_MIN_P` (0.6); below that, QUIET, with the body naming both readings |
| `src/kiro_crew/autonudge_judge.py` | one tool call of any kind meant acted | only a dispatch that could CHANGE something means acted, and only a host built-in may claim to be read-only |
| `src/kiro_crew/dashboard/chat_runner.py` | passed the tool-call count to the hook | passes the per-dispatch identities it already accumulates |
| `src/kiro_crew/autonudge.py`, `src/kiro_crew/decisions/log.py` | label row carried the count and the reply length | plus `tool_names_known`, so a later read can exclude the rows the names never reached |

**The label.** A count cannot tell a read from a write, so the label had to start from the names. The runner already accumulates a tuple of identities per dispatch for its read-only-preparation check, so `owner_acted` reads those instead of the tally. A tool counts as having changed something unless it is positively known read-only, which is the direction this label already errs in: a read scored as a write costs one flat row in the curve, while a write scored as a read teaches the judge to suppress.

A name is only evidence once you know who published it, and only one tier can prove that. The built-in half IS the approval gate's own `_HOST_READ_ONLY_BUILTIN_TOOLS`, not a copy, because that set is already pinned to names whose `governance.BUILTIN_TOOL_SCOPES` row carries no write scope. A hand-spelled copy admitted `code`, which writes files and can shell out, and a turn whose only dispatch edited the tree would have been labelled a quiet cycle. Only the KAS tool ids are spelled locally, because the table owning that mapping lives under `acp` and the agent-SDK boundary keeps application code off that layer; a test joins the two sets.

There is deliberately NO read-only allowlist for MCP tools: every MCP dispatch counts as mutating, whoever serves it. Four review rounds found read-named MCP tools that write on ordinary cold-cache paths -- the knowledge FTS migration, `SkillSearchIndex.sync` (DDL, INSERT, and a DROP on a tokenizer bump), a persisted summary sidecar, `history_index._ensure_open`'s `DROP TABLE` on an index-version bump, and `_repair_notebook_index` behind `memory_recall`. That last one had been audited by hand and judged safe because it issues a GET rather than a POST, which is exactly the argument for removing the tier: if a hand audit cannot tell a read from a write, a list of 25 such claims is not evidence, and the failure it produces is the only direction this label must never fail in. Tests pin the absence, so re-adding a tier reddens rather than passing quietly.

When no names reach the hook the count decides, exactly as before. That is the honest answer for an older caller, a runner that never reached the hook, or a backend with no identity channel: such a turn cannot be SHOWN to have been idle.

**The mapping.** Rule 3 split into rules 3 and 4, and rule 4's exception now requires four things together:

```python
needs_owner.value == NEEDS_OWNER_QUIET
and needs_owner.p >= NEEDS_OWNER_MIN_P
and needs_owner.p > outcome.p
and outcome.p < ACTION_OVERRIDE_MIN_P
```

The confidence floor alone ranked nothing, because argmax already puts the outcome over 0.5 and `NEEDS_OWNER_MIN_P` sits below that. So the quiet must also out-rank the outcome it is silencing. Two pins hold the comparison down: a `quiet` at 0.51 does not silence a `needs_action` at 0.59, and a `quiet` at 0.62 does silence a `needs_action` at 0.55. An equal-confidence tie wakes, because a tie is not evidence the owner is right. The QUIET body names both probabilities, so a human reading the transcript sees the comparison that produced the silence rather than just its result.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible. `tool_identities` and `tool_names_known` are optional keyword arguments that default to the previous behaviour, so a caller that predates them is unaffected. `owner_action_reading` returns a 4-tuple instead of a 3-tuple; its only caller is in this diff. No stored data is re-read: the new field appends to newly written label rows, and older rows simply lack it.

One behaviour does narrow on purpose: an action outcome between 0.4 and 0.6 that used to wake will now stay quiet when a better-supported owner-quiet disagrees with it. That is the defect being fixed, and #14678 recorded the decision on main before this PR asks for it.

## Tests

- The quiet veto is swept as an if-and-only-if over the probability grid, not spot-checked: no outcome outside the exception can produce silence, and every one inside it must. This re-derives base `test_quiet_is_an_allowlist` and is strictly stronger than the assertion it replaces.
- Two ruling pins on the ranking clause: quiet 0.51 vs needs_action 0.59 wakes; quiet 0.62 vs needs_action 0.55 stays quiet. A third pins the equal-confidence tie to WAKE.
- The QUIET body is asserted to contain both probabilities.
- The label is exercised per tier: a read-only built-in, a write-capable built-in, and a dispatch with no identity at all. A separate sweep asserts that every MCP call is mutating across read-shaped and write-shaped names and across first-party and third-party servers alike, and two pins assert the module exposes no MCP read-only surface at all.
- A test joins the local KAS ids against the approval gate's own set, so the two cannot dr

author: johnprempeh2
body:
Closes GRE-87.

## What changed
- `scripts/client-instance.sh` (code in `scripts/client-instance/`): `create`, `start`, `stop`, `status`, `backup`, `verify` for one client instance.
- `scripts/client-instance/editions.ts`: section 5 of the product brief (GRE-83) as code. It builds `GSAM_MANAGED_CONFIG` and `GSAM_HIDDEN_SETTINGS` for `managed` and `managed-plus`.
- `doc/CLIENT-INSTANCES.md`: run-book (start, stop, status, check, back up, upgrade).

No app code changed.

## How it keeps instances apart
- One folder per instance: config, embedded database (own port), storage, secrets key, logs and backups. It has its own auth secret (`.env`, mode 600).
- Server port is the first free port from 3300 and the database port is the first free port from 55400. Ports 3100, 3200 and 54329 are refused, and so are folders under `~/GSAM` and `~/.gsam` (checked for both `$HOME` and the account home).
- The server gets a clean env (`GSAM_HOME` and `GSAM_CONFIG` for this instance only). No `DATABASE_URL` or agent tokens reach it from the caller's shell.
- `authenticated` mode on loopback. Sign-up is closed after setup.

## Findings for Harbor / Everest (brief vs build)
1. **Company creation is refused while `GSAM_MANAGED_CONFIG` is set.** The app returns 403 `cloud_managed`. So `create` starts once without it, only to make the operator log-in, the company and the client log-in, then restarts with both values. Every later `start` sets both values.
2. **`enableStreamlinedUi` and `enableStreamlinedLeftNavigation` have tier `preference`.** `GSAM_MANAGED_CONFIG` rejects them, so the app would not start. They default to on, and hiding `instance.experimental.*` stops anyone changing them. The script checks that they are on.
3. **4 hidden settings have no 403 route in the app.** They only hide the UI: `instance.environments`, `company.secrets`, `company.export`, `company.invites` (see `settings-visibility.ts`). The check proves they are hidden in the UI and does not claim a 403. A 403 floor for them is app work (Ridge, through Everest).
4. `company.import` returns 403 `cloud_managed` before the hidden-settings floor runs. It is still a 403.
5. Managed-tier features that section 5 does not name (`enableApps`, `enableMcpAggregators`, `enableIssuePlanDecompositions`, `enableRunnerPreviewIngress`) are not pinned. They keep the app default.
6. Managed plus accepts only features on the section 5 "off" list, never `enableOwnerInstanceAdmin`. The list is an input (`--passed-features`) that must come from Beacon's passed verdicts on GRE-81.

## Log-ins
- Operator: instance admin, for Greatstone.
- Client: board **owner** of the one company. The client is not an instance admin.
- Passwords are random and printed once to the terminal. They are not written to any file or log. I checked `server.log` and the instance logs.

## Tests run
- `node cli/node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs --test scripts/client-instance/editions.test.ts`: **7/7 pass**. This includes the app's own `parseManagedConfigEnv` accepting the values.

author: lidge-jun
body:
Cuts written on the beat now land on the beat, and agents can inspect a rendered film without watching or hearing it.

**Timing (wp2).** Scene boundaries are rounded from cumulative time. Rounding each scene separately used to shift a 40 s, 132 BPM film by up to 4 frames. On examples/opencodex-mix, cuts within 50 ms of the beat went from 3 of 14 to 11 of 14. This part also adds the `bar` unit and makes media reads honor `out`. Files read several times in a segment are cut up front, auto-camera keys are capped at 24, and oversized perspective expressions fail with a path instead of running ffmpeg out of memory.

**Render watchdog.** ffmpeg occasionally deadlocked on a segment with ten looped inputs. The same command finished in 15 s when rerun. The runner now kills a child whose progress frame stops for `VID2_FFMPEG_STALL_MS` (default 180 s) and retries the segment once.

**Analyze and review (wp3).**

- `vid2 analyze` reports shots, cut deltas against beats and onsets, motion, luma and palette, per-shot LUFS, frequency band shares, keyframes, labelled contact sheets and a spectrogram.
- `vid2 review` sends that evidence plus QA to an OpenAI-compatible image model.
- With `--listen`, it also sends a music excerpt to an audio-capable Responses model. That feedback is used only when the reply has `heard_audio: true`.
- Neither model is called unless it is configured.

**QA speed.** QA and analyze stills now seek to the target frame. They used to decode from the start of the file, which made QA on a 40 s 1080p film take several minutes.

**Validation.** Local tests were not run for the final commit, so this PR's CI is the verification. The earlier wp2 commit passed the full local gate (typecheck, lint, 314 tests, skills check, privacy scan). Real runs through the local proxy showed `analyze` producing 16/16 cuts on beat for opencodex-mix, and `music2 critique` returning `heard_audio: true` with gemini-3.8-flash. The live `review --listen` run did not complete: it waited on the slow QA path this PR fixes, so that run still needs to be repeated.

author: sonnivasquez
body:
Fixes #13590

## What changed

`buildSkillPromptMessage` (`packages/coding-agent/src/extensibility/skills.ts:490`) stripped YAML frontmatter with an LF-only regex:

```ts
const body = content.replace(/^---\n[\s\S]*?\n---\n/, "").trim();
```

For CRLF `SKILL.md` files the regex never matched, so the whole frontmatter block (name/description/triggers/…) was injected as the skill's prompt body in `/skill:<name>` invocations, RPC/ACP skill commands, and autoload injections.

It now reuses the canonical `parseFrontmatter` (same parser the loader path in `discovery/helpers.ts` uses, which already normalizes CRLF→LF), preceded by a leading-BOM strip:

```ts
const body = parseFrontmatter(content.replace(/^\uFEFF/, ""), { level: "off" }).body.trim();
```

`{ level: "off" }` because only `.body` is consumed here — no need for YAML warnings on the prompt-build path. No call-site behavior changes.

Also adds 5 cases to `packages/coding-agent/test/skill-prompt-message.test.ts`: CRLF, BOM+CRLF, BOM+LF, closing `---` with no trailing newline, and a no-frontmatter guard (content must pass through unchanged).

## Verification

- Repro of the original report: `/^---\n[\s\S]*?\n---\n/.test("---\r\nname: x\r\n---\r\nbody")` → `false`; the same input through the new path yields `"body"` with no `name:` leak.
- Exercised the new strip path directly with `bun -e` against the checked-out `packages/utils/src/frontmatter.ts`:

  | input | result |
  |---|---|
  | LF | `"body"` |
  | CRLF | `"body"` (previously the entire YAML block leaked) |
  | BOM+CRLF | `"body"` |
  | closing `---` without trailing newline | `""` (previously whole file leaked) |
  | no frontmatter | unchanged |

- `bun --cwd=packages/coding-agent run check:types` (tsgo --noEmit) passes clean.
- The extended test file could not run on this machine: `bun test` fails identically on a clean tree because the `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` addon (`pi_natives.darwin-arm64.node`) is not built locally (needs bazel). Verified by stash-testing on an unmodified checkout — same failure, so it is pre-existing and unrelated. CI should run the new cases.

## Why this matters to me (contributor)

Revisé el diff completo. El código que quitaba el bloque de metadatos solo reconocía saltos de línea de Mac/Linux (`
`); Windows guarda con `
`, así que en esos archivos no quitaba nada → el modelo recibía `name:, description:...` como si fuera la skill.

## Notes

- One logical change; no call sites, loader, or parser were modified.
- Contributor licensing: MIT, as per CONTRIBUTING.md.

author: zeoxel
body:
## 摘要

按平台文档 [MiniMax H3 视频生成 API](https://matrix.mzsjai.com/docs/matrix/models/minimax-h3) 对齐 H3 适配（仍走文档声明兼容的 `/v1/videos`）。

### 1. 三档型号分别声明素材能力（修复线上参考生视频失败）

| 型号 | 文档规则 | 改前 | 改后 |
|---|---|---|---|
| t2va | 仅纯文本 | 可收 9 张参考图、可首帧 | 仅文生 |
| fl2va（含 `-fl2va-vdn`）/ 2k | 首帧（旧 `images` 按首帧、尾帧解释），不收参考素材 | 可收 9 张参考图 | 仅首帧 / 文生 |
| ref2va | 必须 1～9 张参考图，首帧只属于 fl2va | 可首帧 | 仅参考图 |

生产数据：45/47 个租户默认视频模型是 fl2va 且未设参考生视频桶，参考生视频回落到 fl2va。调用记账里 **fl2va 失败 31 次 / 成功 2 次**，其中包括 `conditions allows at most 2 entries`（参考图被当成首尾帧）；ref2va 成功 11 次。

### 2. size 只下发文档可识别的五档

文档：未列出的 size 不报错，会回落到 768P + 16:9。旧算法对 1:1 / 4:3 算出 992x1024 这类值 → 竖版/方形项目拿到横屏成片。现映射为 `1344x768 / 768x1344 / 768x768 / 1024x768 / 768x1024`，其他比例吸附最近档并告警；显式「宽×高」只取比例。`minimax-h3-2k` 不在该表约束内，沿用原吸附规则。

### 3. 参考生视频桶补默认 ref2va

能力改对后，默认 fl2va 的租户做参考生视频会在解析阶段报「缺参考图能力」。`seed_default_backends` 在**默认视频模型缺参考图能力且 `default_video_backend_r2v` 为空**时补 `ref2va`；默认模型本身能兼顾两条路线（如 Seedance）或用户已手动选过的不动。握手时自动生效；上线时对存量租户统一跑一次（只填空值）。

### 已在生产处理（不属于本 PR 代码）

4 个项目在项目级固定了已下线的 `-ref2va-lora` / `-fl2va-lora`（解析报 `capabilities_unresolved`），已改为文档对应的基础型号，原文件备份在生产 `mozia-reel-data/logs/backup-lora-pins-20260928-1604/`。

## 测试计划

- [x] 更新/新增单测：三档型号能力；五档 size 与最近档吸附、显式像素只取比例；2k 保留原规则；Sora 不受影响
- [x] 新增集成测试：默认 fl2va 时补 ref2va（新租户与存量租户下次握手）；默认 Seedance 不补；用户已选不覆盖
- [x] 运行 `ruff` / `lint-imports`，后端全量 11121 passed，`audit_tests.py --check` 0 违规；`basedpyright` 唯一 error 为 main 既有的 `tests/unit/lib/test_video_artifact_facts.py:187`（夜间 CI 同样失败），与本 PR 无关
- [x] 用本分支 backend 代码对生产网关真实生成：ref2va + 2 张参考图 1:1 → 768x768（141s）；fl2va 首帧 9:16 → 768x1344（928s）
- [ ] 上线后对存量租户跑一次参考生视频桶补齐，抽查一个参考生视频项目出片

## 未包含

- 迁移到文档推荐的 V2 `/v1/video/generations`（显式 `content[].role`）：旧接口文档声明仍兼容，本 PR 不动提交与轮询协议
- fl2va 首尾帧：`openai-video` 端点层 `end_image_capable=False`，未开启

author: oursland
body:
These fourteen commits make ccx reject malformed material, user element and load input with an *ERROR and exit code 201. Before them it read or wrote outside its arrays. There is one commit per defect, so each can be cherry-picked on its own. Each commit message has the report and the input change that reproduces it.

They were found by fuzzing. I ran 15,540 malformed variants of 518 input decks under AddressSanitizer. The decks were this repository's test suite, FreeCAD's FEM examples and test decks, and the conda-forge recipe's test models. This is one of eight PRs from that run.

**designvariabless: reject an unknown \*DESIGN VARIABLES type.** Any TYPE other than COORDINATE was treated as ORIENTATION. sensi_orien then found no orientation tie and dereferenced the unallocated istartdesi (sensi_orien.c:303). Reproducer: test/sens3d.inp with `TYPE=COORDINATE` changed to `TYPE=X`. `TYPE=0`, `TYPE=-1` and a blank `TYPE=` do the same.

**dloads: reject a non-positive element number on \*DLOAD.** Only `l.gt.ne` was checked, so element 0 or -1 indexed ipobody in bodyforce (bodyforce.f:40) or lakon. Reproducer: test/channeljoint3.inp with `EALL,GRAV,9.81,0.,0.,-1.` changed to `-1,GRAV,9.81,0.,0.,-1.`.

**elastics: reject an \*ELASTIC card without data lines.** If the only *ELASTIC card has no data lines, ntmat_ stays 0 and materialdata_me reads elcon out of bounds (materialdata_me.f:202). Reproducer: test/achteld.inp with the `210000.,.3` line under *ELASTIC removed.

**usermaterials: require a positive CONSTANTS on \*USER MATERIAL.** CONSTANTS=0 or blank handed umat an empty property array. CONSTANTS=-1 gave `nelcon(1)=-99`, and materialdata_me indexed elconloc with it. Reproducers:

- test/beamabq.inp with `CONSTANTS=0`.
- test/largerot2.inp with `CONSTANTS=-1`.
- test/sc123creep.inp with a blank `CONSTANTS=`.

**mohrcoulombhardenings: require a preceding \*MOHR COULOMB.** *MOHR COULOMB HARDENING sets material code -53, which means four elastic constants. Without a *MOHR COULOMB card before it only two exist, and materialdata_me read `elcon(3:4)` out of bounds. Reproducer: test/mohr2.inp without its *MOHR COULOMB card.

**userelements: require positive NODES, INTEGRATION POINTS, MAXDOF.** Only the upper bound of 255 was checked. `INTEGRATION POINTS=-1` or blank, or `MAXDOF=0`, reached mi(1) and mi(2), so the element arrays were dimensioned too small (resultsmech_u1.f:604, linel.f:40). Reproducers:

- test/freq_test.inp with `MAXDOF=0`.
- test/freq_test.inp with `INTEGRATION POINTS=-1`.
- test/userbeam.inp with a blank `INTEGRATION POINTS=`.

**usersections: require a positive CONSTANTS on \*USER SECTION.** With CONSTANTS=0 or blank, no properties were stored. If no other card defines properties, prop is never allocated, and resultsmech_us3.f:267 dereferenced NULL. Reproducer: test/freq_test.inp with `CONSTANTS=0` on *USER SECTION.

**damageinitiations: reject \*DAMAGE INITIATION without CRITERION.** Without a CRITERION, itype and nconstants were uninitialised, and the data loop ran with a garbage count. Reproducer: test/damage2.inp with `,CRITERION=RICE TRACEY` removed.

**allocation: initialise nconstants for \*DAMAGE INITIATION.** allocation.f counts the data lines of *DAMAGE INITIATION before damageinitiations reads them, and it sets `nconstants` only for a known CRITERION. Without one, it skipped `nconstants/8` continuation lines per data line, with `nconstants` uninitialised or left over from an earlier card. That can run off the input block before damageinitiations reports the missing criterion. The same damage2 variant as in the previous commit still segfaulted on the -O2 build; the -O0 and AddressSanitizer builds happened to survive. `nconstants` now starts at 0. This one is not from the fuzzing itself: I found it while checking the previous commit on master.

**initialconditionss: check element nodes before evaluating sigini.** *INITIAL CONDITIONS,TYPE=STRESS,USER computes integration point coordinates from co while the deck is being read. An element with undefined nodes indexed co out of bounds (initialconditionss.f:235). Reproducer: test/resstress2.inp without its *NODE card.

**calinput: stop when no element was defined.** A deck with no elements got as far as results.c with ne=0 and dereferenced a null fn1 (results.c:241). Reproducer: test/spring7.inp with the element line `1,1,2` removed.

**elementcpuload: give one empty range when no element is active.** When damage deletes every element, `nepar=0` gave `num_cpus=0`. The callers then read zero-length per-thread buffers. elementcpuload now returns one thread with an empty range, as mafillsmasmain.c does when there are no contact elements. Reproducer: test/damage1.inp with the Johnson-Cook melt temperature 1000. changed to 1e308. That deletes every element, and the job now finishes.

**films: reject a non-positive element number on \*FILM.** This is the same missing lower bound as in dloads. Element 0 or -1 on a *FILM line read `lakon(l)` before the array (films.f:283). Reproducer: test/artery5.inp with `1,F3FC,12,10.` (line 62) changed to `-1,F3FC,12,10.`. On 2.23 that variant ran until the fuzzing timeout, so the defect only showed when I ran the timed-out variants under AddressSanitizer on master. All 14 decks in test/ that use *FILM are unchanged.

**radiates: reject a non-positive element number on \*RADIATE.** This is the same defect in the neighbouring card, which I found by reading the code. Master gives a heap-buffer-overflow at radiates.f:297 for test/oneel8ra.inp with `1,R1,-12.,1.` (line 32) changed to `-1,R1,-12.,1.`. That deck now exits 201. All 10 decks in test/ that use *RADIATE are unchanged.

### Notes

- The defects were found on the 2.23 release. The line numbers in the commit messages refer to it, and its ccx_2.23.c is CalculiX.c on master.
- The eleven original fuzzing commits apply to master unchanged. The allocation, films and radiates commits are new, found while checking the port on master.
- The usersections commit adds `ndprop=0` next to the line where the "section and discrete element cards" PR adds `ipos=0`. Applying both gives a trivial conflict: keep both lines.

### Testing

Built with gfortran/clang at -O2 on macOS arm64, and with AddressSanitizer on Linux aarch64. I tested this PR alone, and together with the other seven in the series, all merged onto master:

- **This PR alone** removes 37 of master's 288 AddressSanitizer reports on the 417 crashing mutants, and adds none. It also fixes the *FILM variant above, which is not among the 417.
- **Valid models.** All 637 decks in test/ give the same exit code and the same `.dat` as master, apart from timing lines.
- **The 417 mutants that crashed on 2.23, under AddressSanitizer.** Master gives 288 AddressSanitizer reports; with the series, 1 remains: the master-only preinitialnet path that the separate checkforhomnet PR removes. The mutants now end as follows:
  - 331 with an *ERROR and exit code 201;
  - 18 run normally;
  - 66 stop in SPOOLES' "matrix is singular" `exit(-1)`, which is outside this series;
  - 1 times out.
- **The same 417 mutants, macOS -O2 build.** 266 end in a signal on master, none with the series.
- **148 mutants that ran indefinitely on 2.23.** With a 60 s limit, 117 time out on master and 9 with the series. Those 9 are nonsensical models that keep a solver iterating. One more ends in SIGABRT, as it does on master.
- **Static checks.** Every changed Fortran file compiles with `gfortran -fsyntax-only -std=legacy -Wline-truncation`, commit by commit. A check that compiles all Fortran units as one file, so gfortran can compare every call with the routine it calls, shows no new argument mismatches.

## Problem
A collaborator opening a Mercury-bound workspace on intelligent-tyms (2026-09-28) got "a workspace that reads from the MCP server mcp.mercury.com can only be opened by its owner", even though the live catalog lists Mercury as `same-account`.

`McpFacetBase.addObserver` / `recordRead` read the sync `sharing` getter. In gatekeeper-mcp that answers from a module-level catalog cache, which is empty on a cold isolate, so every catalog server fell back to `owner-only` (and admitted observers were excluded from reads) until the background fetch landed.

## Fix
- `McpFacetBase` gains `protected async currentSharing()` (defaults to `this.sharing`), used by `addObserver` and `recordRead`.
- gatekeeper-mcp overrides it to `await ensureCatalog(env)` first. Portal / Intelligence connectors are unchanged (their policy is sync config).

## Tests
- New facet test: cold default `owner-only`, loaded `same-account` → observer admitted after replay, later read not excluded.
- mcp-shared 334 passed, gatekeeper-mcp 60 passed. No new lint errors (the 356 existing ones and the `session-context.test.ts` TS2416 are pre-existing on tyms-brand).

body:
## Purpose

Narrow and strengthen the TTF-Q novelty claim after a targeted literature audit.

## Added positioning

The manuscript now explicitly distinguishes TTF-Q from established work on:

- ecological predictor collinearity — Dormann et al. (2013);
- simulation-based ecological power/study design — Maslen et al. (2023);
- simulation validation of complex ecological models — DiRenzo et al. (2023);
- transparent reporting of statistical simulation studies — Williams et al. (2024).

## Claim boundary

This PR does not claim any of those ingredients as new. It sharpens the contribution to the **joint response-blind evaluable-envelope object**: nested predictor-information survival, information-loss location, endpoint signal concentration, null qualification, and conditional detectability on dyadic geometry.

Simulation reporting text now also states that complete predeclared scenario grids are reported rather than selecting favourable cells.

## Scope

Manuscript/audit only. No method implementation or frozen result changes.

body:
Refs #2. Stacked on #93 (and #91, #90; #89 is merged).

## Scope

Add a separate version-1 offline control-plan validator and path/value-free exclusion preview. Plans distinguish initializing a remote dataset, migrating local SQLite data, and attaching to an existing remote dataset. Migration binds an independently supplied plan digest and trusted inventory to the manifest digest, operation ID, source, and destination identities. Initialize and attach reject import manifests and list local portable domains that are not imported. Host credentials, device, enrollment, workspace, settings, and lifecycle categories stay retained.

The preview reports zero verified migrated records and denies activation. Occupancy and local-history fields are assertions, not source probes or runtime authority. The existing export manifest remains unchanged.

## Verification

- Nine focused control-plan tests cover digest/identity tampering, occupied destinations, hidden imports, exclusion reclassification, bounded inventory, operation-specific destination rules, and payload-free errors.
- The independent-digest regression retains the trusted hash and changes either an owner field or valid JSON whitespace. Bypassing only that verification in an isolated mutation probe causes both cases to fail.
- Full contract suite: 244 tests on Windows Python 3.14 (four platform skips) and WSL Python 3.12 (zero skips); all nine focused tests also passed on Windows Python 3.10. Initialize and attach compare the complete inventory-derived not-imported list. Five isolated mutants confirm that omitting a domain or bypassing each destination guard fails the relevant test.

## Remaining #2 work

Complete source observation/inventory, public consumer parity, supported versions, writer fencing, migration checkpoints and recovery, server-owned preflight and authorization, reverse migration, and host/path relocation before #2 can close. This is a partial contract stage; hosted checks and post-merge verification remain required.

author: j4yop
body:
## What this does

`scripts/validate_cloudinary_live.py` had never been executed. It has now been,
against a real free-tier account: **18 checks pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped.**

| Area | Change |
| :--- | :--- |
| `core/cloudinary_client.py` | Schema bootstrap, metadata write, search, transformation log, all 4 URL builders, enum validation |
| `services/webhook_service.py` | Signature scheme → documented construction, SDK verifier, replay window |
| `scripts/validate_cloudinary_live.py` | 6 wrong SDK paths, SKIP state, error-body reporting, brand-asset provisioning |
| `core/config.py`, `tests/conftest.py` | Test-suite isolation from ambient credentials |
| **666 tests, 95% coverage** | 11 tests rewritten because they asserted the bugs |

## The harness reported PASS on a call that did nothing

`ensure_metadata_schema` called `cloudinary.admin`, which does not exist. The
`AttributeError` was swallowed by `except Exception: # Already exists: update in
place`, misdiagnosed as a field conflict, and the method returned a result marked
**`live`** containing an error. The harness checks `not result.fixture` → **PASS**.

Fixed at three levels: the API path; **no exception-driven control flow** (list
fields first, then create-or-update — the SDK raises `BadRequest` rather than
`AlreadyExists` for a duplicate `external_id`, so catching the "right" class
silently degrades to create-fails-then-update on every re-run); and
`_schema_failure()` returning `fixture=True` so a failed live call cannot read as
live.

## The transformation grammar was wrong, and nine green tests said it was fine

| Defect | Real symptom |
| :--- | :--- |
| `fl_layer_apply` in a delivery URL | `Cannot find matching layer start` — it's an *upload-time* flag |
| `l_folder/name` | Cloudinary uses a **colon**: `l_a:b:c` (verified for 1 and 2 levels) |
| `b_rgb:000000_80` | alpha is 8 hex digits, not `NN` after an underscore |
| font `Inter` | not on Cloudinary's servers — `Unsupported font family Inter` |
| `co_emerald_400`, `co_slate_300` | no such named colours exist |
| newline / `/` in overlay text | both terminate the layer, even encoded — the parser decodes before it splits |

The tests asserted the **shape** of these strings. They never asked Cloudinary
whether the URL loaded. That is precisely the failure this project exists to
catch, and it happened here.

## A category error: no upload could ever succeed

Nine of eleven metadata fields were `mandatory`, including `jev_triage_decision`,
`jev_confidence_score` and `sift_inlier_ratio`. Cloudinary enforces mandatory
fields on *every* upload — so the schema demanded a verdict and an inlier ratio
**at upload time**, which are the results of analysing an asset that hasn't been
uploaded. The harness failed with:

> `Field 'jev_confidence_score' is mandatory and cannot be left empty`

Now five mandatory (all known at capture time), six optional (all analysis
outputs). `validate_metadata` was *also* still checking `restrictions.values` for
enum membership after the schema moved to a `datasource` — so local validation had
silently stopped enforcing enums while still appearing to. It reads the
datasource now.

## The webhook scheme would have rejected every genuine notification

Cloudinary documents `sha1(raw_body + X-Cld-Timestamp + api_secret)` — a plain
hash with the secret **concatenated on**, not HMAC, with the timestamp in the
signed string. Every scheme here was `hmac(secret, body)`, and two of the three
were byte-identical.

Verification now delegates to `cloudinary.utils.verify_notification_signature`,
falls back locally when the SDK is absent *or* the configured secret isn't the
globally configured one (a dedicated webhook key would otherwise be verified
against the wrong secret), and enforces a freshness window so a captured request
cannot replay.

The refusal to assert that scheme from memory is the only reason it didn't ship as
a confident wrong answer.

## The suite ran live and seeded the account

Adding `.env` support meant a developer with credentials filled in got a
*different* test run from one without: `TestSeeder` uploaded **520 assets** to the
live account and the suite hung for ten minutes. `conftest`'s own docstring
already required that no test depend on a credential. Now
`VERITAS_NO_DOTENV=1` is set before `core.config` is imported, with tests
asserting the suite runs in fixture mode.

## Still unproven — said so, not assumed

- **`audit_pdf` is plan-gated**: `f_pdf` returns `401 deny or ACL failure` on free
  tier. Also verified — Cloudinary does **not** composite text onto a `raw` PDF;
  the file comes back byte-identical, so the layer stack is silently discarded.
  The builder now uses the only form that composites, and the harness reports
  **SKIP** with the reason rather than calling a paywall a defect.
- **`donor_reel`** needs a video asset; the probe is an image. **SKIP**.
- **Webhook signature** needs Cloudinary to POST to a public URL.

## Two harness improvements that paid for themselves

A **SKIP** state, because a harness that reports "not run" as "failed" trains you
to ignore red, and one that reports it as "passed" is worse. And it now surfaces
**Cloudinary's error body**, which was being discarded as `0 bytes` — that turned
four of these fixes into one-line diagnoses instead of guesswork.

author: moshez
body:
The usability fixes from the screenshot audit, each backed by the type checker rather than only by e2e tests.

**Stylesheet (`src/style.bats` replaces `css/app.css`)**
- Text colour and background are set only together (`surf`), with a `SURF` proof that the pair reaches 4.5:1 in the light, sepia and dark themes. The proof is css's new `CONTRAST` dataprop (css#33) over the palette. Control edges and accents need 3:1 (`EDGEP`).
- The base rules give every control a 44px minimum target, text fields a 16px font and a 2px focus ring. They are the only `!important` rules.
- The sheet's byte budget is part of its type.
- Fixes: text-field borders were 1.36:1 (now a 3:1 edge role); the scrubber fill was 2.1:1 on the bar; the scrubber, sliders, tabs and buttons were under 44px; justified text is dropped under 600px; the native search clear button is hidden.

**Elements (`src/ui.bats`)**
- Controls can only be made by constructors that name them:
  - a text button is named by its text alone (label in name, WCAG 2.5.3);
  - an icon button is given its name;
  - images are decorative;
  - roles that need a name get one.
- `ui_attr` takes a typed attribute that cannot set a name or a role. Tags are a datatype with no interactive tags.
- The shelf button was labelled "Shelf shown" while it showed "Library"; it is now named by what it shows.

**Dialog (`src/modal.bats`)**
- The dialog asks a datatype (`ask`) that decides its buttons and whether the second one is destructive. The answer comes back paired with the question.
- Deleting a book, highlight or bookmark, a factory reset and a settings reset happen only on the `Confirmed` answer to the question that named them. The match is exhaustive.
- Highlight and bookmark deletes and "Reset to defaults" now ask first.
- A cancelled note begun from a selection removes its highlight on every path: button, Escape or a click outside.
- The duplicate-import question holds its promise resolver linearly, replacing the int id with a `-1` sentinel.

**Other usability changes**
- Each book row has a visible 44px "Book menu" button. The menu used to be reachable only by right-click or long press.
- The library search has a clear button.
- Destructive buttons are styled as destructive.
- The annotations icon is now a pencil (✎).

**Checks run locally**
- `bats check` passes.
- All 177 e2e tests pass (updated for the confirmations and the book rows; new checks for the clear button and for right-click).
- On the audit of the screenshot flows: no target under 44px, no text under 4.5:1, no input under 16px.

## Summary
Automates the routine dependency updates from #312 with **Dependabot**. It's built into GitHub, so no app needs installing (unlike Renovate).

### `.github/dependabot.yml`
- **Weekly, Monday 06:00 Europe/Madrid.** One grouped PR per ecosystem and directory, containing all **patch and minor** updates:

  | Ecosystem | Directory | PR |
  |---|---|---|
  | npm | `/` (legacy static JS tests) | 1 |
  | npm | `/frontend` | 1 |
  | npm | `/mcp-server` | 1 |
  | Cargo | workspace (`Cargo.lock`) | 1 |
  | GitHub Actions | workflows | 1 — SHA pins from #298 are updated along with their `# vX.Y.Z` comment |
- **Majors are ignored** (`version-update:semver-major`) and stay manual, planned as issues like #300–#311.
- PRs get the `housekeeping` label and the `chore(deps)` / `chore(ci)` commit prefixes.
- Validated against the official Dependabot schema (`check-jsonschema --builtin-schema vendor.dependabot`).

### CI: npm audit gate (new)
- The issue assumed CI already ran `npm audit`, but only `cargo deny check advisories` was there.
- This PR adds `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` after `npm ci` in `frontend-build` and `mcp-tests`, the two packages that ship. All three npm packages currently report 0 vulnerabilities.
- Update PRs are therefore audited in both ecosystems.

### Works on Dependabot PRs
- The CI workflow uses no secrets, only `github.token`.
- It declares `pull-requests: write`. Dependabot PRs get a read-only token by default, but GitHub applies a workflow's explicit `permissions`, so the coverage-comment steps should keep working.

### Docs
The new *Dependency Updates (Dependabot)* section in `.github/workflows/README.md` covers the schedule, groups, why majors are ignored, how to review, and the `@dependabot` commands for splitting a failing group.

### Also
- `.gitignore`: ignore `backups/`. `marreq-core/scripts/db_backup.sh` writes whole-database dumps there, and they contain password hashes.

## After merging (repo settings, optional)
- **Settings → Code security → Dependabot alerts / security updates:** enable them if they aren't already. Security updates are separate from these version updates.
- The first run happens on the next Monday, or earlier via **Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot → Check for updates**.

## Test plan
- [x] `dependabot.yml` and `marreq-ci.yml` pass their official JSON schemas
- [x] `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` passes locally in `frontend` and `mcp-server` (0 vulnerabilities)
- [x] CI green on this PR, including the new audit steps (0 vulnerabilities in both)

author: yamierick
body:
Suggested by Dr. Jones (2026-09-28) after the HSR door-to-door maps: time saved by one option against another is a **difference that can be either sign**, and v0.1 only had sequential log scales. This adds a diverging scale and an example. Everything uses synthetic data only, as the repo's rules require.

## What changes

- `colour.diverging()` gives orange below the centre, a pale middle and blue above. `colour.diverging_norm(lo, hi, centre=0)` sets the scale. Legends mark both clipped ends (`≤`, `≥`).
- **Missing values** (NaN) are one neutral grey, `colour.MISSING`, per metric. So "against air" can be grey where no airport is in reach, while the same hexagon stays coloured under "against the car".
- `Metric.cmap` also accepts a Colormap. `Metric.note` puts the colour meaning on the legend. Its default reproduces v0.1's "darker is higher (log scale)", so existing specs draw identical pages.
- On the 3D page, column height is the value's size, either sign; the colour gives the sign.
- `fmt.signed(unit, digits)` formats values like "+0.4 h" and "−1.2 h", with a true minus sign.
- `examples/synthetic_comparison.py` uses two made-up cities, a town with no airport, and a new service between the cities. It has three metrics (against the faster alternative, the car, air) and two views (trips each way). It also shows how to bin a quantity that is not additive: sum people × hours and people, then divide.

Version is 0.2.0, with the CHANGELOG and README updated.

## Checked

- 20 tests pass; `ruff check` is clean.
- New tests cover:
  - the diverging legend's positions and end marks;
  - end and missing colours;
  - the signed format;
  - the example conserving people and the people-weighted mean;
  - grey and a dash where air is missing;
  - 3D height as the absolute maximum;
  - v0.1's default note unchanged.
- Both example pages checked in a browser, all three metrics, both views. Town C is grey under "against air" and orange elsewhere.

## After merge

Please tag `v0.2.0`. `hsr-robotaxi-scenarios` pins this branch's commit until the tag exists, then moves to the tag.

author: bennouli
body:
A group on the timeline is now recognisable without the card box: a small counter circle on the axis with a hover note naming the members, and beside the stack a vertical strip of arrows and dots showing which members are in view, with a "1 von 6" position line under the cards.

Closes #40

## Changes

- **Counter** (`GroupMarker`): 22 px circle, 1 px `border-fg`, `bg-surface`, count in `text-label` weight 500; hover and `focus-visible` invert to `bg-accent text-accent-fg`; `cursor-zoom-in`. Activating it zooms into the group as before. `GROUP_MARKER_SIZE_PX` is now 22 and is applied through `style` because `useEntryLayout` uses it for the marker gap.
- **Group hover note**: `GroupMarker` uses `Tooltip` with `useTooltipTrigger`. Its content is built from #41's line parts:
  - `TooltipMeta` from `formatGroupMeta` ("6 Einträge · 1917–1922").
  - `TooltipTitle` "Gruppe · Klicken zum Hineinzoomen", `aria-hidden` because the button's name already says it.
  - One `TooltipBody` per member title.

  It opens on the side of the axis away from the stack, and `aria-describedby` points at it.
- **Indicator strip** (`GroupStack`): `ArrowUp`, one 5 px dot per member (`border-fg`, `bg-fg` while in view, only drawn for groups of at most 6), then `ArrowDown`, all from `lucide-react`. The hand-drawn SVG is gone. By default the strip sits left of the stack. The new `anchoredAt="end"` prop puts it on the right. It lines up with the stack's axis-side edge (new `side` prop).
- **Arrow spacing**: in groups of more than 6 there are no dots between the arrows. There the strip keeps the arrows' centres at least 24 px apart, the WCAG 2.5.8 target spacing.
- **Arrows** use `aria-disabled` instead of `disabled`, as the zoom buttons do: `text-fg/30` at the ends, and they stay focusable. The old workaround that moved focus back to the group when a button became disabled is removed.
- **Position line**: `small-caps text-label tracking-label text-fg-muted`, still `aria-live="polite"`. The text comes from the new `formatPosition` in `src/lib/format.ts`.
- **Spacing**: stack members still render through `EntryCard inline` → `EntryLabel`, now 14 px apart. `STACK_GAP_PX` is 14, so `SLOT_HEIGHT_PX` is 48. `GROUP_STACK_CONTROLS_HEIGHT_PX` is 12, the height of the position line, because the last slot's gap already separates it from the cards. `groupStackHeightPx` returns the taller of the card column and the strip.
- **Formatters** in `src/lib/format.ts`:
  - `formatGroupMeta` and `formatPosition` are new.
  - `formatGroupName` and `formatGroupZoomName` replace `CardLayer.groupLabel` and `CardLayer.markerLabel`. They produce the same strings, now with the singular. `CardLayer.test.ts` only covered those two, so it moves into `format.test.ts`.
  - `formatGroupYears` is private and holds the shared year range.
- **Motion**: the 250 ms `transition-transform` on the list stays. It is the stepping animation and already has `motion-reduce:transition-none`. No hover state has a transition.
- **Comment**: the stale doc comment about the wheel is fixed. The wheel zooms the timeline over the stack, and the stack still doesn't handle it.
- **DESIGN.md**: dropped the "arrows move to lucide in #40" note.

## Verification

- Rebased onto `staging` with #55, #56 and #58:
  - Head `857c72f`: `pnpm check` green (704 unit tests), `pnpm e2e` **31 passed**.
  - Head `0d223bf` (second review fixes): `pnpm check` green (lint, typecheck, 704 unit tests, `check:tokens` ok, prettier clean), `pnpm e2e` **31 passed**.
- Before the rebase:
  - `pnpm check` green.
  - `pnpm e2e` (serialized on the shared port, run four times in total):
  - Run 1 and run 2: 23 passed, 1 failed. Both failures were the known desktop keyboard-walk flake (`keyboard.spec.ts:52`, desktop). `pointTimes` came out of order by one pair: `1083412800000` arrived after `1159531200000`.
  - `--repeat-each 4` on the walk alone: 6 passed, 2 failed (desktop only).
  - Run on the pre-rebase `c6d5ca3`: **24 passed**.
- New unit tests:
  - The dots follow ArrowDown ×2 and End (acceptance criterion 2).
  - A group of more than 6 has no dots.
  - Strip side for `anchoredAt` and `side`.
  - `groupStackHeightPx` reserves the strip's height when it is taller than the cards.
  - The arrows stay put and keep focus at the ends.
  - The marker's note content and `aria-describedby`.
  - Axe on stack and marker.
- Browser: headless Chromium screenshots of `/` at 1280×800, 1920×1080 and 390×844. They were taken before the rebase and not retaken after it. Checked in them:
  - The above- and below-axis stacks, the counter circles, the strip with dots and arrows (disabled up-arrow at 30 %) and the "1 VON 4" line.
  - Phone stacks with 4 and 5 members.
  - The strip does not reach toward the axis.
  - Hover of the note was not captured in a screenshot. It is covered by the unit test (keyboard focus) and by axe in e2e.

## Deviations

- **The strip sits outside the 170 px stack box.** It is `absolute`, 22 px to the left: 14 px strip plus an 8 px gap. That keeps the labels and the connector on the anchor x. Placement (#46, now merged) reserves no width for it, so the strip can overlap a left neighbour's label by up to about 14 px. Owner decision.
- **`anchoredAt` is unused in production.** Staging has no stack anchored at its end. The prop exists and is tested so placement can switch it on.
- **The strip's sizes are JS constants applied through `style`**: 14 px buttons, 12 px icons, 5 px dots, 3 px gaps, 8 px offset. The Tailwind spacing scale isn't used for them because they feed `groupStackHeightPx`.
- **The group hover note's content is built here, though #41's `## Done` lists it.** The orchestrator assigned it to #40. #41 (merged) supplies the shell and the line parts, which the private `GroupTooltipContent` in `GroupMarker.tsx` uses.
- **The strip's height math stays in `GroupStack.tsx`** (`stripHeightPx`, `hasDots`, `groupStackHeightPx`). It is not in a sibling geometry module because `bandGeometry` imports `groupStackHeightPx` and `GROUP_STACK_CONTROLS_HEIGHT_PX` from there, and the brief said to keep those exports. `groupStackHeightPx` already lived there.
- **`GroupMarker` has no non-interactive variant any more** (`onActivate` is required). Production always passed it, and the `role="img"` variant would have shown "Klicken zum Hineinzoomen" on a marker that cannot be clicked.
- **Files outside the issue's `## Touched`:**
  - `src/lib/format.ts` and its test: the no-assembled-text rule requires the formatters there.
  - `bandGeometry.ts`: `STACK_GAP_PX` 8 → 14, the 14 px spacing the issue asks for.
  - `DESIGN.md`: a stale one-line note removed.
- **The counter is 22 px, under the 24 px target minimum.** The size comes from the issue. Its spacing to other targets depends on placement.
- **On touch, the group note doesn't open.** A tap zooms in, as it did before; `touchToggle` is not passed.
- **Collapsed desktop groups now cover 2 rows instead of 3** (`bandGeometry` test updated): 2×48+12 = 108 px ≤ 108. Expanded desktop stays at 3 rows (156 px).

## Definition of Done

- A group is recognisable by the counter and the indicator strip without a box: **Ja**. The card box and its bordered buttons are gone. The counter circle and the arrow/dot strip identify it (screenshots).
- The dot strip reflects the window after stepping with the keyboard: **Ja**. The dots' `data-in-view` follows ArrowDown/End in a unit test, and the fill comes from the same `topIndex` the list uses.
- Stacks pass the keyboard walk and axe (`pnpm e2e`): **Ja**. Axe is green at both widths and in both colour schemes. The walk passes on the final run. Its intermittent desktop ordering failure is the known flake on `staging`, and the group steps it exercises pass.
- Nothing from `## Not done` was built: **Unberührt**. The issue has no such section. Span bars, the note's shell and placement were not touched. The note's content was built here (see Deviations).
- Works with the keyboard alone and ax

author: vinodbhorge
body:
Raised from review feedback on `Blue-Dots-Economy/bluedots-e2e#39`. Part of the rollout tracked in `Blue-Dots-Economy/bluedots-e2e#28`.

## In plain terms

This workflow has one switch, `block`, that decides whether findings fail the build. It controls two very different things at once: known vulnerabilities in dependencies, and passwords committed into the code.

Those deserve different answers. A dependency vulnerability is usually a backlog item — every repo here sets `block: false` precisely so a pre-existing list of CVEs does not fail every pull request. A committed password is not a backlog item: on a public repository, pushing it *is* the leak, so a scan that only reports one tells you about something you have already published.

Because it was a single switch, the second answer had to follow the first. This adds a second switch so each repository can answer them separately.

## Why now

Consolidating `bluedots-e2e` onto this shared workflow (`bluedots-e2e#39`) silently downgraded its secret scan. Its bespoke workflow hardcoded `--exit-code=1` — a finding failed the job unconditionally — and #29's stated acceptance criterion was *"a pull request adding a known test secret fails the check."* Moving to the shared caller with `block: false` turned that into report-only, and the pull request listed four gains and no losses. Caught in review.

Flipping `block: true` was not the fix: that same input also drives `trivy-fs` severity and exit code (lines 150, 233 today) and `image-scan`, so keeping secrets blocking would have made HIGH/CRITICAL dependency CVEs fail the build too — a different decision with different noise.

## What changes

A new `block-secrets` input, `default: false`, and the gitleaks step now reads:

```yaml
--exit-code ${{ (inputs.block-secrets || inputs.block) && '1' || '0' }}
```

**Backward compatible by construction.** The two are ORed, so a caller that sets neither keeps following `block` exactly as before. `block-secrets: true` strengthens the secret scan without dragging the CVE scanners along; there is no way to use it to weaken anything.

## Verified in a fork

Tested at `vinodbhorge/bluedots-automation#1`, using this repository's own caller (which uses a local `./` path) against its known `gcp-api-key` finding:

| Setting | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `block-secrets: true`, `block: false` | **`scan / gitleaks: failure`** — 193 commits scanned, `leaks found: 1` — while **`scan / trivy-fs: success`** stays report-only |

The backward-compatible case is exercised by this pull request's own run: this repo's caller does not set `block-secrets`, so gitleaks should follow `block: false` and stay green despite that same finding.

## Who should set it, and when

Not everyone, and not yet. A repository with findings already in its history will red-wall every pull request the moment this goes true — `aggregator-dpg` has 8 and `signals-dpg` has 9, all currently untriaged. Triage first, then set it.

`bluedots-e2e` is the immediate case: its history is clean (118 commits, no leaks), so it can set `block-secrets: true` straight away and restore the guarantee it had before consolidating.

## Release Notes

- New `block-secrets` input on the shared security-scan workflow, letting a repository fail the build on a committed secret without also failing it on dependency CVEs.
- Defaults to following `block`, so existing callers are unaffected.

author: dickhardt
body:
Finding 4 in `aauth-dev/monitor` `plan/CALL_LOG_PLAN.md`, approved by Dick 2026-09-28: "skip unsigned unless AAuth-Requirement."

- `callLogMiddleware` drops the record for a request with no `Signature` and no `Signature-Key` header unless the response carries `AAuth-Requirement`.
- Applied after `skip`, so the workers that pass their own `skip` (access, test-resource, playground, registry) inherit it too.
- A request carrying only `Signature-Key` is not unsigned — it is an AAuth attempt and is still logged.

What it removes, checked live today: whoami and notes answer an unsigned `GET` with 401 `signature_required` and no `AAuth-Requirement`; a scanner's `/.env` gets 404. Both are dropped. senzing `POST /v1/search_entities` and encrypt `POST /send` answer unsigned with 401 `AAuth-Requirement: requirement=person-token`; both are kept.

Version 0.1.2; lockfile workspace entry edited by hand (it still said 0.1.0). `npm test`: 802 passed. The new test fails on 0.1.1.

After release, each fleet worker needs a lockfile bump — every worker's `package-lock.json` on `main` still resolves `@aauth/call-log` 0.1.0.

body:
## Что было не так
На iPhone «Пригласить друзей» так и не открывал окно, хотя «Поделиться» лотом через тот же `shareMessage` работает. Отличия были в порядке действий:
- «Поделиться» — по нажатию запрос к боту → сразу `shareMessage`;
- «Пригласить» — сообщение готовилось заранее (иногда за минуты), по нажатию `shareMessage` с этой заготовкой.

Кроме того, после вызова `shareMessage`, на который Telegram так и не ответил, библиотека Telegram отклоняет все следующие вызовы ошибкой `WebAppShareMessageOpened` до перезапуска приложения — поэтому второе нажатие уходило в запасной путь «(link)».

## Исправление
- «Пригласить» повторяет «Поделиться» один в один: по нажатию «Готовлю приглашение…» на кнопке → `invite_prepare` → сразу `shareMessage`.
- Заранее готовится только ссылка (для строки «Копировать»).
- Любая ошибка — тостом с кодом: ответ Telegram (`MESSAGE_EXPIRED`…), `WebAppShareMessageOpened`, ошибка бота.
- Старый Telegram (< 8.0) — ссылка копируется и открывается окно отправки.

## Проверка
Headless Chromium с заглушкой Telegram: окно открылось → «Приглашение отправлено ✓»; `MESSAGE_EXPIRED` → тост с кодом; «зависший» прошлый вызов → тост `WebAppShareMessageOpened`; бот 502 → тост `prepare_failed`; ошибок на странице нет. На iPhone не проверялось.

author: iray-tno
body:
A `@theme` written the way [Tailwind's own documentation](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/theme) writes one lost its colour:

```css
@theme {
  --color-brand: var(--color-indigo-600);
}
```

`design.theme.entries()` hands back what was *written* rather than what it resolves to, so this reached `toHex` as the string `"var(--color-indigo-600)"`, failed to convert, and was dropped by the rule right below it — the one that leaves a colour out rather than guessing at it.

That rule is right, and this was not a case of it. The colour is not unknown; it is written down one line away.

## Why it mattered more than one token

The failure was silent, and silent in the worst shape. A project whose tokens are *all* semantic names over palette entries — which is what a design system looks like — got:

- a `Theme` with **none of its own colours in it**
- no diagnostic
- a Native lowering with nothing to emit, because React Native has no custom properties to fall back on

So the Web half would have limped along on `var()` passthrough and the Native half would have rendered a marker, for a theme that is entirely valid Tailwind.

## The fix

Follow the reference against the same theme it was declared in. Chains are allowed — one semantic name pointing at another is the same idea a level on — and a hop limit bounds them, so a token that refers to itself ends the walk rather than the process. `var(--x, fallback)` takes the fallback when `--x` is not a theme entry, which is what CSS does with it.

A reference to something **outside** the theme with no fallback is still left out. That one genuinely is a colour this cannot resolve, and the no-guessing rule still applies.

## Tests

Six: the documented form, a two-step chain, a fallback that is taken, a reference that goes nowhere, a self-referential pair, and the existing behaviour is untouched.

Not run locally — this worktree cannot resolve the test's dependencies. Biome passes.

## Where it came from

Writing `@hozo/ui`'s token file (#638, PR #640), where every token is a semantic name over a palette entry. The workaround there was to write each value out twice — the palette entry in a comment and its oklch in the declaration — which works and is exactly the sort of thing a library should not have to do. Once this lands, #640's `theme.css` can say what it means.

Independent of #639 and #640: touches `packages/tailwind/` only.

author: identity-wael
body:
Follow-ups to #933/#935/#939 in the BigQuery validating front (`internal/bigqueryfront`).

**Base:** this branch is `origin/main` with `origin/fix/933-bigquery-scripts` (PR #959, not yet merged; it includes #947/#940) merged in, then one commit. Land #959 first, or together; the diff against main includes #959's changes.

## #955: failed scripts leave the catalog out of step (fixed)
Root cause, from goccy/googlesqlite v0.3.1 and bigquery-emulator v0.8.1 source, measured against the pinned image:
- The engine changes its in-memory catalog as each statement runs, and `Catalog.Sync` reloads only rows `WHERE updatedAt >= lastSyncedAt`, so a rollback restores the rows and not the catalog.
- The emulator updates its own table list (`tables.get`/`list`) from a query only when the query succeeded (`syncCatalog`).
- New finding: **jobs.query rolls a failed script back, but a query job (jobs.insert) commits the statements before the failing one**, because the emulator records the failed job in the script's transaction. For example, `INSERT INTO t VALUES (9); SELECT * FROM nope.nope` kept the row as a query job and did not keep it through jobs.query.

After a failure, `resyncCatalog` puts things back with statements of its own. Each one was measured to do this:
- A drop-and-fail script, sent through jobs.query (which rolls it back), takes a table out of the catalog and leaves its rows.
- `CREATE … IF NOT EXISTS` adds it again from a schema.
- `DROP … IF EXISTS` removes one.
- `tables.patch` fixes the listed schema.

What gets synced depends on how the script failed:
- Rolled back: the catalog is made to match the table list.
- Committed: the table list is made to match the catalog.

A failed query job now fails with the emulator's own error, as in BigQuery. It is still 501 through jobs.query, and still 501 when the script has a transaction. I found no upstream issue or fix in goccy/bigquery-emulator or goccy/googlesqlite (main unchanged). Not covered: `DROP SCHEMA` and functions (#976); reporting upstream is #974.

## #956: variables replaced aliases and columns (fixed)
`renameVariables` now uses the lexer to rename only references. These are left alone: aliases, table/CTE/function names, CREATE TABLE/INSERT/MERGE-INSERT column lists, `STRUCT<>` fields, `EXCEPT (…)`/`USING (…)` columns, `UPDATE SET` targets, and `EXTRACT(… FROM v)` handling. BigQuery's docs don't say whether a column or a variable of the same name wins, so a statement that may read another name (an alias or range variable it defines, `t.n`, a column of a table it reads via tables.get or the script's own CREATE, or a table with unknown columns) is **501 before anything runs**.

## #957: extracts the front writes (partial; stays open)
The front writes these itself to the instance's Cloud Storage, as the export docs describe them:
- NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON for STRING and INT64 columns (INT64 as strings, `<>&` in unicode notation)
- GZIP
- one-character delimiters
- an empty table's header row

The job belongs to the front: jobs.get, jobs.list, cancel and delete all work on it. Still 501, because I can't verify them: Avro, Parquet, several URIs, other CSV/JSON column types, JSON NULLs, nested JSON.

## #958: jobs.list configurations (fixed)
`projection=full` now gives each job's configuration. It comes from jobs.insert answers, or from one `jobs.get` for jobs the front hasn't seen. The client's text is still restored (#939).

## Tests
- Unit tests: `go test ./internal/bigqueryfront` (new: `TestSelectColumns`, `TestFailedScriptResyncsTheCatalog`, `TestExtractsTheFrontWrites`, `TestJobListGivesConfigurations`; `TestRenameVariables`, `TestExtractJobs`, `TestFailedScriptThatWroteIs501` updated).
- Official Go SDK compat tests, against my own instance (storage,bigquery): new `TestBigQueryScriptVariableNamedAsAnAlias`, `TestBigQueryFailedScriptLeavesTheCatalogInStep`, `TestBigQueryExtractsTheFrontWrites`, `TestBigQueryJobListGivesConfigurations`; `TestBigQueryFailedScriptThatWroteIs501` and `TestBigQueryExtractToCloudStorage` updated. All `^TestBigQuery` tests pass.
- `go vet ./...` and `-tags compat`, gofmt, `make docs-check`.

docs/compatibility.md rows and CHANGELOG updated.

Follow-ups filed: #972 (emulator jobs.list ignores paging/filters), #973 (jobs.insert without jobReference → 500), #974 (report the catalog bugs upstream), #975 (CSV empty STRING vs NULL), #976 (DROP SCHEMA / functions not resynced).

Closes #955
Closes #956
Closes #958
Refs #957
