author: bprosefan
body:
## 무엇을 & 왜

COB·이자·전표번호·거래일이 모두 "오늘이 영업일인지, 다음 영업일이 언제인지"를 알아야 하는데 기준이 없어 각자 `LocalDate.now()`를 쓰고 있었습니다. 시스템 시각과 분리된 **논리 업무일자**를 `business.api.BusinessDateProvider` 하나로 제공합니다(PH-40, glossary 6번).

- **저장형**입니다. `today()`는 시계가 아니라 DB에 저장된 값을 돌려줍니다(Apache Fineract `m_business_date` 참고).
- Fineract와 다른 점: Fineract는 날짜를 `plusDays(1)`로만 넘기지만, 여기서는 **다음 영업일로 넘길 때 주말·공휴일을 건너뜁니다.**
- **테이블 2개로 나눴습니다.** 매일 바뀌는 값 1개(`business_date`)와 한 번 넣고 거의 안 바뀌는 목록(`holiday`)은 성격이 다릅니다. 주말은 테이블에 넣지 않고 요일로 판정합니다.

**폐기한 접근 — 초기 영업일 하드코딩(`2026-10-02`)**
처음엔 머지 예정일을 초기값으로 박았습니다. 하지만 V 파일이 실행되는 날은 머지일이 아니라 환경마다(팀원 로컬·CI·`main` 배포) 다릅니다. 일찍 적용되면 미래 날짜가 되고, 이를 막으려면 "10/2 이후 릴리스" 같은 운영 규칙이 필요했습니다. 그래서 **초기값은 의미 없는 과거(`2026-01-01`)로 두고, 서버가 뜰 때 오늘 달력에 맞추도록** 바꿨습니다. 언제 머지·배포해도 됩니다.

## 관련 이슈

- Closes #471
- 관련 #472 (거래일 `trade_date` 컬럼 — 이 PR의 provider를 P4가 10/16에 대입)
- 관련 #473 (`now()` 직접 호출 감사·ArchUnit — 이 PR 이후)

## 변경 사항

| 구분 | 파일 | 내용 |
|---|---|---|
| Flyway | `V202609281930__create_business_date_and_holiday.sql` | `business_date`(현재 영업일 1행)·`holiday` 테이블, 초기값 `2026-01-01` |
| Flyway | `R__seed_holiday.sql` | 2026 공휴일 22일 (법정 18 + 대체 4). 노동절(5/1)·제헌절(7/17) 포함 — 2026-04-30 규정 개정. 2026년 행을 `DELETE` 후 다시 넣어 파일이 곧 정답 (파일에서 지우거나 고친 날짜가 DB에 남지 않음) |
| 공개 계약 | `business.api.BusinessDateProvider` | `today()` · `nextBusinessDay(date)` · `isBusinessDay(date)` — `tasks.md` PH-40 계약 그대로 |
| 공개 계약 | `business.api.BusinessDateAdvancer` | `advanceFrom(businessDate)` — PH-43 COB 마지막 스텝이 부를 영업일 전환 |
| 내부 | `BusinessDateCatchUpScheduler` | **서버 기동 시 + 매일 00:00 KST** 영업일을 달력에 맞춤 (오늘이 영업일이면 오늘, 아니면 다음 영업일. 저장값이 그보다 이전일 때만) |
| 오류코드 | `CommonErrorCode.BUSINESS_DATE_NOT_FOUND` · `FUTURE_BUSINESS_DATE_CLOSE` | `CMN9001` (500) — 영업일 행 없음(데이터 결함) · `CMN9002` (500) — 아직 오지 않은 영업일 마감 시도. `api_conventions.md` §4-1 등록 |
| 테스트 훅 | `business/support/BusinessDateTestFixture` (src/test) | `moveTo(날짜)` · `currentInDb()` — 다른 도메인 테스트에서도 주입해 쓰면 됩니다 |
| 문서 | `schema_reference.md` · `corebank_erd.md` | 두 테이블 추가 |

**바뀌지 않는 것**
- **자동이체·예약이체는 휴일에도 지정일(달력 날짜)에 실행합니다** — 영업일로 바꾸지 않습니다(REQ-AUTO-001 유지, 예약이체도 같은 규칙으로 결정). 휴일에 실행된 건의 거래일은 다음 영업일입니다.
- 휴일 등록 API 없음(범위 밖), `COB_DATE`(마감 대상일) 없음 — 필요하면 PH-43에서 추가.
- 기존 `LocalDate.now()` 사용처는 건드리지 않았습니다 — #473에서 다룹니다.

## 리뷰어가 특히 봐줬으면 하는 부분

1. **"하루 넘기기"가 아니라 "달력에 맞추기"로 만든 이유** — 매일 자정에 무조건 한 영업일씩 넘기면 연휴에 영업일이 앞서 나갑니다(10/3 0시 10/6 → 10/4 0시 10/7). 맞추기는 몇 번 불러도 결과가 같고, 늦게 배포돼도 한 번에 따라잡습니다.
2. **동시성은 락 대신 조건부 UPDATE(compare-and-set)** — `WHERE business_date = :expected`로 WAS 2대가 동시에 불러도 한 번만 바뀝니다.
3. **테스트가 잡은 버그 1건 (`67979eed`)** — COB 전환을 동시에 8번 부르면 7번이 `CMN0303`을 던졌습니다. 진 스레드가 CAS 실패 후 "이미 넘어갔나?"를 일반 SELECT로 확인했는데, `REPEATABLE READ`라 트랜잭션 초반 스냅샷(옛 영업일)을 읽었기 때문입니다. 재확인을 `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`로 바꿨습니다(`BatchExecutionLockJpaRepository`와 같은 방식).
4. **`@EventListener(ApplicationReadyEvent.class)`는 이 레포에서 처음 씁니다.** `business_date` 행이 없으면 기동이 실패합니다 — 요청마다 500이 나는 것보다 기동 시점에 드러나는 편을 택했습니다(판단). 새 DB 첫 기동 직후 밀리초 단위로 초기값이 보일 수 있지만 ALB 헬스체크 전이라 실사용 영향은 없다고 봤습니다.
5. **판단으로 정한 것** — 오류코드를 새 접두어 대신 `CMN9001`로 둔 것(`CMN`은 P5 소유, 영업일은 공통 기반), 12/31은 은행 정상 영업이라 휴일에서 뺀 것.
6. **PH-43에 넘기는 것** — ① 자정 스케줄만 제거하고 기동 시 맞추기는 남긴다. ② COB "영업일 확인" 스텝은 **저장 영업일이 오늘 달력보다 미래면 건너뛰어야** 합니다. 안 그러면 토요일 밤 COB가 아직 오지 않은 월요일을 마감합니다. 스텝이 빠져도 드러나도록 `advanceFrom`에도 가드를 넣었습니다(아래 7번).
7. **리뷰 반영(P4)** — ① `today()`가 휴일에 미래 영업일을 돌려줄 수 있음을 주석에 명시. ② `advanceFrom`이 오늘 달력보다 미래인 영업일을 받으면 `CMN9002`로 거부. 조건은 `≤`(PH-43 COB 23:30 시작 계획 — 금요일 마감이 자정을 넘겨도 통과). 자정 이후 COB로 바뀌면 `<`로 좁힙니다. ③ 휴일 시드를 연도 단위 `DELETE` 후 재삽입.

**검증**
- `./gradlew test` 전체 **1,828건 통과** (실패·에러 0) · CI `Build & Test` 통과
- `BusinessDateIntegrationTest` 31건 (Testcontainers MySQL, `@Transactional` 없이 커밋 기준·DB 직접 조회로 검증)
  - 시드 공휴일이 정확히 22건이고 전부 `isBusinessDay() == false` / 9/28·12/31은 영업일, 노동절·제헌절·주말은 아님
  - 다음 영업일: 10/2→10/6, 9/23→9/28, 10/8→10/12, 휴일에서 시작해도 그날 제외
  - 맞추기: 연휴에 매일 불려도 안 앞서감 · 한 번에 따라잡음 · 되돌리지 않음 · 8개 동시 호출 수렴 · **새 DB 기동 직후 초기값(1/1)이 아니라 오늘 기준** (기동 시 맞추기를 빼면 실패)
  - COB 전환: 9/23→9/28(추석 연휴 건너뜀) · 재실행해도 두 번 안 넘김 · 8개 동시 호출에도 한 번만 · 어긋나면 `CMN0303` · 행이 없으면 `CMN9001` · **미래 영업일이면 `CMN9002` · 오늘 영업일은 통과(경계)** — 가드를 빼거나 `<`로 바꾸면 각각 실패함을 확인. 가드 때문에 테스트 날짜는 과거로 옮김
  - 동시성 테스트는 수정 전 실패(8중 7) → 수정 후 3회 반복 통과 확인
- `LayerArchitectureTest`에 `business` 규칙 추가(17/17), `FlywayMigrationTest`(`ddl-auto: validate`로 엔티티-테이블 일치) 통과
- **확인 못 한 범위:** "영업일을 옮기면 배치·이자·전표번호가 따른다"(P5.md 완료 기준)는 소비 코드(P2·P3·P4)가 아직 없어 검증하지 못했습니다.

### Fix builder generation for abstract classes: Issue #119 

**Description:** 
This PR fixes an issue where the class-diagram generator creates a concrete build() method for classes declared as abstract, so there don't occur any compiler errors anymore.

- **Solution**: Added an if-check during the code generation phase to check if a class is abstract and properly handle or omit the generation of the build() method for it.

- **Testing**: Added a dedicated test case featuring an abstract class model to verify that builders for abstract classes are generated correctly without build() and that the build passes without errors.

author: marvin7122
body:
**Part 13/14 of the export stack.** Depends on #3531 (none for part 1). This branch is the fork stack part rebased onto current master; it contains the commits of its ancestors. Review only this part's own diff: https://github.com/marvin7122/qlever/compare/upstream-stack/11...upstream-stack/16. Merge order: part 1 first, then each next part (they rebase cleanly onto master after the parent lands).

Draft: the body and CI are being finalized; this PR is marked ready when that is done.

---

## Why

Resolving vocabulary IDs to strings does random reads into the offsets and data arrays of the vocabulary. For an in-memory vocabulary much larger than the CPU caches these miss to DRAM. This PR adds software prefetching (`_mm_prefetch` / `__builtin_prefetch`) a fixed distance ahead in a pipelined lookup loop and wires it into the batched lookup of in-memory vocabularies.

## What

- `src/util/SoftwarePrefetch.h`: `ad_utility::prefetchForRead` and `ad_utility::forEachWordPrefetched(words, indices, distance, f)`. While word `i` is resolved, the loop prefetches the offset entry of word `i + distance` and the first data line of word `i + distance / 2`.
- `src/engine/PrefetchingBatchResolver.h`: `PrefetchingBatchResolver` (`resolveVocabIndexIds`, `resolveCompactVectorPipelined`, `idsToStringAndType`), configured by `PrefetchConfig`. `resolveCompactVectorPipelined` delegates to `forEachWordPrefetched`.
- `src/util/CompactStringVector.h`: `offsetsSpan()` / `dataSpan()` are public (read-only spans), so the loop can address lines of words it has not resolved yet.
- `benchmark/PrefetchingBenchmark.cpp`: synthetic baseline vs prefetch distances 4 to 32 (not a CMake target).

## How it is wired

- Runtime parameter `vocab-lookup-prefetch-distance` (`SizeT`, default `0` = off, unchanged behaviour). Enable with `--set-runtime-parameter vocab-lookup-prefetch-distance=8`.
- `VocabularyInMemory::lookupBatch` (now in the .cpp) reads the parameter once per batch. With 0 it calls `sequentialLookupBatch` as before, otherwise `forEachWordPrefetched`. The `vocabulary` library links `global` for this.
- Reached by CONSTRUCT export (`ConstructBatchEvaluator` -> `idsToStringAndType` -> `lookupBatch`) for `in-memory-uncompressed` directly and for `in-memory-compressed` through `CompressedVocabulary::lookupBatch`. SELECT export resolves IDs one at a time, and the on-disk vocabularies read words with pread/io_uring into fresh buffers, so neither path has resident vocabulary memory to prefetch.

## Tests

- `VocabularyInMemoryTest.LookupBatchWithPrefetchDistance`: `lookupBatch` equals `operator[]` (order, duplicates) for distances 0, 1, 2, 8, 9, 1000; an empty batch throws.
- `PrefetchingBatchResolverTest`: equivalence with `ql::exportIds::idsToStringAndType`, compact-vector path, empty inputs, and `ForEachWordPrefetchedBoundaries` (distances 0, n, n+1, SIZE_MAX; unbuilt vector; out-of-range and SIZE_MAX indices).
- Ural (seq 4751, head `0d5958e88`): VocabularyInMemoryTest 11/11, PrefetchingBatchResolverTest 5/5, CompressedVocabularyTest 71/71.

## Measured

Same binary (`1bcc4ecac`), distance 0 vs 8, DBLP rebuilt with `in-memory-compressed`, CONSTRUCT (turtle), warm, n=3, Ural, identical bytes, all gates PASS (seq 4752):

| query | distance 0 | distance 8 | delta | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| H-vocab-title-large | 0.1757 s | 0.1798 s | +2.37% | within noise |
| H-vocab-creator-large | 0.1224 s | 0.1193 s | -2.49% | within noise |
| H-size | 0.4238 s | 0.4148 s | -2.11% | within noise |

Run dir: https://github.com/marvin7122/thesis_repository/tree/733ec8ca/experiments/runs/pr87-dblp-inmem-ab

Earlier evidence: isolated resolution of 1M random IDs against the mmapped Wikidata vocabulary: +33% at distance 8 (run `prefetch-wikidata-ural`); synthetic 1M-entry cache-resident vocabulary: -57% to -67% (run `prefetch-why-ural`, the vocabulary fits in L3).

## Limitations

- No end-to-end gain on DBLP: the lookup is 0.6-3.9% of export CPU samples on these queries, and `ConstructBatchEvaluator` sorts and deduplicates the batch IDs, so offsets are read in ascending order that the hardware prefetcher already covers. The parameter therefore stays default off.
- Only in-memory vocabularies engage; the default `on-disk-compressed` index does not.
- Not measured: an in-memory vocabulary much larger than DBLP's (e.g. Wikidata in-memory) with unsorted batches, where the isolated gain is expected to matter most.
- `resolveVocabIndexIds` of the resolver prefetches only the `Id` array; it is kept for the API but not wired.

## Conventional title required

`feat(recording): native takes join take review (native recording P4)`

## Related issue

Part of #842 (native-recording-suite PRD). Phase 4, "Take review integration" (`docs/prds/native-recording-suite.prd.md`).

## Goal

Native takes recorded by the built-in recorder (Phase 2, #858; Phase 3's DAW-agnostic contract and line identity, #864, merged f6844b5 — its status cell was stale on the PRD and is corrected here) need to join the review pipeline so "there is one take-review experience whatever the source": the narrator can assign a native take to a manuscript line, mark a keeper among a line's takes, and undo that mark — all on the same Proof page REAPER-sourced take review already lives on.

## What changed

- **`RecorderSetTakeLine` (new binding):** the first UI caller of Phase 3's `Service.SetTakeLine` — it takes only an `entityId` (a paragraph or chapter id); the manuscript's own recorded source checksum is read host-side (mirroring `bindings_preview.go`'s own small copy of the same lookup), so a stale UI can never stamp a wrong one.
- **`RecorderSetTakeKeeper` (new binding) + `internal/recording/keeper.go` (new):** a "keeper" mark on a take, its own project-owned sidecar (`Recordings/keeper.json`, same shape and corruption handling as `identity.go`'s `line-identity.json`). Marking a take the keeper clears the mark on every other take sharing its line (one keeper per line, mirroring what a REAPER active take already means without a REAPER active-take concept to lean on, Q5); a take with no line has no group to clear. Every change is narrator-confirmed and always undoable. Never touches the take's audio.
- **`NativeTakesPanel.tsx` (new, `apps/ui/src/components/proof/`):** on `ProofChapterPage.tsx`, beside `RecordingCheckCard` — this chapter's native takes grouped by line, each playable; a not-yet-assigned take can be assigned to one of the chapter's paragraphs; a line's takes can have one marked keeper, undoable. Assignment is offered only while the project's current engine is `builtin` (`RecorderState.engine`), so a REAPER-only chapter's page is unchanged; an already-assigned take (and its keeper mark) keeps showing regardless of the project's current engine (Q2/D86: REAPER and native recording coexist).
- **`TakeReviewReads.tsx`, `TakeComparisonView.tsx`, `TakeComparisonDialog.tsx`, `TakeReviewScanDialog.tsx`, `FindingDetail.tsx`: unchanged.** ADR 0545 records why: native takes are not wired into `internal/repeats`'s pickup/duplicate detection scan. ADR 0485 (Phase 3) already documents, and deliberately leaves unfixed, a finding-id/evidence-version gap that scan's member-key scheme has for a GUID-less native take — closing it would reshape every existing REAPER-sourced take-review finding's id, silently orphaning narrators' stored review decisions. That's a detection-engine change, not this phase's "take review integration" (its own Solution Detail row: "mark the keeper take among several"; success measure: "Playwright/visual coverage of the merged UI; narrator can mark a keeper and undo it" — a UI/organizing goal, not a scan-engine one).
- **`hostAPIVersion` 80 → 81** for the two new bindings (`apps/desktop/app.go`, `app_test.go`, `apps/ui/src/hostApi.ts`, `Host.*` regenerated via `scripts/dev/bump-host-api.mjs`).
- **`ADR 0545` (Proposed):** the scoping decision above, in full.
- **`docs/guides/using-the-app/booth.md`:** a short paragraph pointing narrators at the Proof page's Native takes panel.
- **PRD:** Phase 3's status cell corrected to `complete` (was stale, still read `in review`); Phase 4 set to `in review`.

## Local checks run, with results

- `go build ./...` (apps/desktop) — clean
- `go vet ./...` (apps/desktop) — clean
- `golangci-lint run . ./internal/recording/...` — 0 issues
- `go test ./...` (apps/desktop) — all pass, except the catalogued pre-existing flake `TestInstallNeedsAKnownJobAndADownloadThatHasFinished` (#509's flake list, item 4: a `TempDir` cleanup race), confirmed by re-running it alone 3× clean — not from this change
- checklocks: not run — crashes in this sandbox on any package regardless of change (a Go-toolchain/tool-version mismatch, reproduced on an untouched package too); will run in CI's `quick-windows`
- `UPDATE_CONTRACTS=1 go test ./...` — goldens regenerated (`recorder-state-recording.json`, `recorder-state-takes.json` for the new `keeper` field; `bootstrap-*.json` for `apiVersion` 81)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` (apps/ui) — clean
- `npx eslint` on every new/changed file — clean
- `npx vitest run` (apps/ui, full run after the D91-triggered merges) — all pass; targeted: `wireContracts.test.ts`, `interactionFeedback.test.ts`, `components/proof/`, `components/booth/BuiltinRecorder.test.tsx` (new: `NativeTakesPanel.test.tsx`, extended `wireContracts.test.ts` coverage for `recorderSetTakeLine`/`recorderSetTakeKeeper` and `keeper`, `interactionFeedback` catalog rows for the five new call sites)
- `npx playwright test tests/visual/app.spec.ts -g "proof-chapter"` (the rows touched: `native-takes-unassigned`, `native-takes-keeper`, and a regression check of `current`) — content passes at every viewport (desktop, small-desktop, tablet), screenshots inspected by hand; the run's only reported failure in this sandbox is a pre-existing `console.error: 404` also present on the untouched `current` state with this change reverted (a local browser-binary substitution artifact — this sandbox has no wails3/pinned-Chromium toolchain match; will verify clean on CI's pinned browser)
- `node scripts/ci/adr-index.mjs --write` — index regenerated and current
- `npx markdownlint-cli2` on every changed Markdown file — clean
- pre-commit hook (`quality.mjs fix/check-go`, `fix/check-ui`, `markdownlint-cli2`) — clean on every commit

Not run: the full `pnpm check`, the full visual suite, the atlas (no primitive/`styles.css` changed) — targeted checks only, per the worker protocol (D43/D44).

## Mockup check (D46, D91, D92)

**D92 classification.** `docs/prds/mockups/edit-and-proof-workspace/04-takes-panel-ab.webp` (this PR's original citation) is **superseded**: it depicts REAPER item takes with a waveform and word-level A/B comparison — an already-shipped, different surface. Not scored against it.

**No approved mock (research or per-PRD) depicts the "Native takes" card.** Phase 4 of the PRD carries no mockup gate. The nearest research mock, `docs/research/mockups/audiobook-studio-benchmark/04-proof-pickups.webp`, covers the Proof chapter page's shell and right-column card stack (a note detail card, then a card below it — "Pickup session" in the mock) — the same convention `RecordingCheckCard` and this PR's new card extend — but its own card content is pickups/REAPER-specific and never shows a native-take card. Listed on #510 per D92 ("newer mock, pending owner review").

| Mockup | Covers | Capture | Match % | Differences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `04-proof-pickups.webp` (research, approved) | Page shell: header, breadcrumb, notes table, right-column card-stack convention | `native-takes-keeper`, `current` (desktop/small-desktop/tablet) | **Not independently re-scored here** — this PR touches none of this shell (no new primitive, token or layout change to it); any gap is pre-existing across every Proof-page state, A-V1's audit scope, not this PR's | — |
| `04-proof-pickups.webp`'s card-stack convention, structural only (no mock shows this card's content) | The "Native takes" card itself | `native-takes-unassigned`, `native-takes-keeper` (desktop/small-desktop/tablet) | **Not scorable against a target image that doesn't exist for this content** — qualitative only, below | Card chrome (white `Panel`, bold heading, muted small-caps section labels) matches the mock's card idiom exactly: same primitive as `RecordingCheckCard`/the mock's own "Pickup session" card. Row buttons use `Button variant="ghost"` (bordered, no fill), the same variant `TakeReviewReads`' per-row actions already use on this pag

author: jgyy
body:
## Summary

Ports [Pokémon Claude Red](https://github.com/levy-street/pokemon-claude-red) — a from-scratch, zero-image-files JS remake of Pokémon Red (~27k lines, all procedural pixel art) — into a real Godot 4.7 / 3D project. All 3D models, materials and animations are generated from the original game's own data using **headless Blender**, with no manual modelling and no original game images anywhere in this repo.

Converting a 151-species, 223-map game to bespoke 3D art is a multi-month project by hand. This PR is a **real, working vertical slice with a complete data foundation**, not a mockup — see the "What this actually is" table in the README for exactly what's real vs. roadmap.

- **Data layer — complete**: all 151 species, 165 moves, the full type chart, all 223 Kanto maps, and the 73-member cast, extracted verbatim from the source's own data tables (`pipeline/scripts/*.js`, run with Node).
- **3D asset pipeline — complete, 151/151 species generated, 0 fallbacks**: `pipeline/blender/*.py` reads each species' original 2D vector-art definition (ellipsoids/capsules/polygons) and builds real 3D geometry, materials, and `Idle`/`Walk`/`Attack` animations from it, scaled to the species' real Pokédex height — plus a tintable humanoid character base, a 14-piece overworld tile kit, and 9 battle VFX meshes.
- **Overworld — working for all 223 maps**: tile-accurate 3D grid movement/collision built from the real per-tileset `pass`/`grass`/`doors`/`counters` lists, bidirectional warps, route connections, and wild-encounter rolling against the real per-map slot tables.
- **Battle system — working for wild encounters**: turn-based battle scene using the original Gen-1 damage formula ported line-for-line into `BattleMath.gd` (same STAB/type-chart/crit/random-factor steps).
- **Title screen, minimal party menu, scene routing** tying it together.
- **Tests + CI**: a 26-assertion in-engine test suite (`godot4 --headless -- --run-tests`) and `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which imports the project, runs the tests, and captures real headless screenshots (via `xvfb-run` + Godot's software GL renderer) as build artifacts.

Not yet implemented (data is already extracted and ready to wire up — see the README roadmap): trainer battles, catching, the bag/PC/save, and overworld dialogue/story scripts.

## Screenshots

*(Real, in-engine headless screenshots — same command CI runs.)*

**Title (a genuinely generated Bulbasaur):**
![Title](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jgyy/redgodot/claude/pokemon-claude-godot-3d-e7b4g8/docs/screenshots/title.png)

**Overworld (Pallet Town, built from the real tile-grid data):**
![Overworld](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jgyy/redgodot/claude/pokemon-claude-godot-3d-e7b4g8/docs/screenshots/overworld.png)

**Battle (real Squirtle vs. a real Pidgey):**
![Battle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jgyy/redgodot/claude/pokemon-claude-godot-3d-e7b4g8/docs/screenshots/battle.png)

## Architecture

See the README for the full diagrams (autoload/scene architecture, the JS→JSON→Blender→glTF pipeline, the tile classification flow, and the battle state machine) — summarized:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["pokemon-claude-red (JS source)"] -->|Node: stub G, eval, dump JSON| B["pipeline/extracted/*.json"]
    B -->|copied as-is| D["godot/data/*.json"]
    B -->|headless Blender: primitives→mesh, pal→material, groups→armature| C["godot/assets/models/**/*.glb"]
    D --> E["Godot 4 project"]
    C --> E
```

## Test plan

- [x] `godot4 --headless --path godot --import` (asset import) — clean, no errors
- [x] `godot4 --headless --path godot -- --run-tests` — 26/26 assertions pass (damage formula incl. crit/STAB comparisons, type chart, 151 species / 223 maps loaded, map tile classification, wild-encounter slot table)
- [x] Headless screenshots of title / overworld / battle captured via `xvfb-run godot4 --rendering-driver opengl3` and visually verified (see above)
- [x] All 151 generated `.glb` files verified (`pipeline/blender/verify_glb.py`): valid glTF header, ≥1 mesh + material, expected animation names
- [ ] CI workflow not yet observed running on GitHub Actions itself (validated locally with the exact same commands the workflow runs)

## Summary
- implement PRO-09 Grok as a peer of the existing Pervue provider adapters
- use Grok Build's shipped one-shot **headless** interface rather than a persistent ACP/app-server runtime
- run one `grok` child per Pervue turn with bounded Pervue history, private cwd, private `GROK_HOME`, and private prompt/agent files
- target the stable CLI's `--agent <definition-file>` surface (not upstream-main-only `--agent-profile`)
- reuse cached Grok/X OAuth according to Grok's auth-path precedence while disabling direct API-key billing and filtering ambient provider secrets/custom endpoints
- keep ordinary/context turns text-only by explicitly denying `Agent,search_tool,use_tool`, clamping built-ins, and disabling hosted web search
- report Grok Web search **unsupported for now** because stable 1.0.41 does not expose the structured backend-search stream documented on upstream `main`
- parse Messages output fail-closed, verify required init fields, and normalize provider failures
- add Grok to provider selection/setup and mark PRO-09 IMPLEMENTED — VERIFY

## Why headless instead of ACP/app-server
`grok agent stdio` is the long-lived ACP integration surface. Pervue does not need a persistent Grok server, so each turn uses a one-shot headless child and Pervue resends its bounded conversation history on follow-ups. This matches the ownership model used by the other non-Codex providers.

## Shipped-CLI compatibility
Review against real Grok Build 1.0.30 and stable 1.0.41 exposed two differences from upstream `main`: stable rejects `--agent-profile`, and its search path uses the `search_tool`/`use_tool` MCP umbrellas rather than the backend `web_search` frames documented upstream. This PR now targets the stable behavior:
- agent definitions are passed with `--agent <file>`
- `search_tool` and `use_tool` are explicitly denied
- Grok's advertised `web_search` capability is false, so the extension disables Web for Grok and no search turn is launched
- protocol `streaming` is also false for now; partial/thinking frames are consumed only as internal activity to refresh idle timing

## Security / privacy boundary
- prompt/browser context never appears in argv; it is written to a private 0600 prompt file
- each child gets a private per-turn `GROK_HOME`
- cached auth lookup respects existing `GROK_AUTH_PATH`, then `GROK_HOME/auth.json`, then `~/.grok/auth.json`
- `GROK_DISABLE_API_KEY_AUTH=1`; ambient xAI API keys/custom endpoints are not inherited
- subagents, memory, workflows, web fetch and provider-side customization surfaces are disabled/clamped
- `system/init` requires OAuth auth, a compatible Grok model (including version-resolved aliases), the canonical private cwd, an empty effective tool set, empty skills, and no active MCP server
- missing init fields and any later tool-bearing block fail closed with specific normalized reasons
- private workspaces carry a liveness marker so another browser/profile cannot sweep a live turn; stale recovery and recursive deletion happen off the host loop
- shared private-provider helpers centralize 0700/0600 creation, conversation-ID validation, private child names, bounded stderr tails and deadline arithmetic

## Verification
Deterministic Grok coverage now checks authenticated/signed-out/relocated-auth status, one-shot first/follow-up turns, version-resolved model aliases, search refusal before launch, every init boundary (auth/model/cwd/tools/skills/MCP), malformed/tool activity, result-error classification, cross-host live-workspace preservation, cancellation, and invalid model/conversation rejection.

Final CI on `db6930ed58acd948c6a1611310821da2212d5c1c`: **11/11 green** across Linux debug+release, Windows, macOS, Rust 1.85, fuzz, packaging, extension checks, protocol fixtures, and extension↔host round trip.

author: ptrepkapc
body:
## Operators can issue an e-receipt by hand from the order's documents, as they do an invoice

**Symptom.** For an order with a tax ID, the order screen's "Utwórz dokument" menu lets the operator issue an invoice at any time. A consumer order had no equivalent. Its e-receipt started only automatically, when the order reached "Dostarczone" and the store's e-receipt automation was switched on. Several cases had no way to get a receipt from the provider:
- a sale that must be fiscalised before delivery;
- an order delivered before e-receipts were enabled;
- a store that keeps the automation off.

The only option left was "Dodaj", which records a receipt issued somewhere else.

**Root cause.** `ReceiptAttemptService` had two ways to create an attempt, and both needed an earlier event:
- `startAutomatic`, called only from `ReceiptTrigger` for `automaticCandidate` orders;
- `reissue`, which requires an earlier dead attempt.

**What changed.**
- New `ReceiptAttemptService.issueManually(storeId, orderId, actor)` creates the order's first attempt (`<orderId>:R1`) through the same `create` path the automation uses. From there the attempt behaves exactly like an automatic one: issue, polling, retries, document, marketplace event, buyer's e-mail and alerts. The operator's name is stored as `createdBy`. It refuses, each with its own message:
  - an order that already has any attempt (`receipts.action.issue.exists`). A live attempt already owns the receipt, and a dead one is replaced with the existing "Wystaw ponownie";
  - an order that does not qualify (`receipts.action.reissue.notEligible`: tax ID, another closing document, cancelled, RMA replacement or zero total);
  - a store without a working receipt provider (`receipts.action.reissue.noProvider`).
- `canIssueManually(store, order)` applies the same conditions for the view. The provider check shared with `reissue` moved into `hasProvider`.
- New endpoint `POST /dashboard/orders/{orderId}/receipts/issue` in `OrderReceiptsController`. It uses the same flash-message handling as the other receipt actions and is closed to `SUPER_ADMIN`, like invoicing.
- `orderDetails.html`: "Utwórz dokument" gets an "E-paragon" item, confirmed with the standard `confirmSave` dialog, whenever `canIssueReceipt` is true. The menu button is also enabled when it is the only item. After issuing, the attempt appears in the "E-paragon" section above the documents.

**Deliberate decisions.**
- **Delivery is not required.** The invoice menu does not wait for delivery either. The sale date falls back to the moment of issuing, since there is no delivery date yet. `ReceiptProcessor` re-checks only `orderQualifies` before calling the provider, never the delivery status, so an early attempt is not blocked later.
- **The automation switch is not required.** The switch controls what the application does on its own. A store that keeps it off can still use its configured provider on demand. Once an attempt exists, `startAutomatic` never creates a second one, so the order cannot be fiscalised twice when it is delivered later.
- **"Dodaj" (record a receipt issued elsewhere) is unchanged.** A manual receipt document closes the order (`isInvoiced`), after which "E-paragon" is no longer offered.
- The buyer's e-mail follows the store's receipt settings; there is no per-issue "send" checkbox as for invoices.

## Related PRs

Stacked on app#231 ("Receipts: issue e-receipts without waiting for the payment, declaring only what was paid"), which lets an unpaid order get a receipt without payment data. This matters most here: an order issued before delivery is usually unpaid. app#231 in turn needs commerce-link/receipts-api#2, receipts-fakturownia#2 and receipts-dev#2 (0.2.0) merged first. Merge app#231 first; this PR's base then moves to `main`. No changes in `receipts-api`, `receipts-fakturownia` or `receipts-dev`.

## Tests

- `ReceiptAttemptServiceTest`:
  - a manual issue creates `R1` for an undelivered order with the automation switched off, is queued, and blocks a later automatic start;
  - it is refused after an existing attempt, for an order with a receipt document, and without a provider. In each case `canIssueManually` agrees.
- `OrderReceiptsControllerTest`: the endpoint passes the operator's name and shows the success message or the refusal reason.
- Checked end to end on the local stack with the `receipts-dev` provider. An unpaid order in status "Nowe" (2269.00 PLN, no payment) was issued from the menu. It was fiscalised without payment data, the receipt document was attached and the e-mail sent. The menu item then disappeared.
- Full suite (with app#231 merged in): 4644 tests, 0 failures.

author: maklind88
body:
## Summary
Keep authorized central reads separate from unsent local recovery, without adopting another actor's draft or treating a read as an unverified save receipt. Full closure history and evidence are in `docs/architecture/MEDICAL_PENDING_READ_BASELINE_2026-09-28.md`.

## Latest Follow-Up: Session-Owned Profile Reads
- Bind profile/user-list refreshes to their initiating session object, captured token, central read scope and request owner. Stale 200/401 responses cannot replace users/roles, notify consumers or sign out the next account.
- Coalesce only within the same session/token/scope. Older completions cannot clear newer request bookkeeping.
- Source-executed regressions cover actor/team changes, in-place token rotation, sign-out, same-token reauthentication and overlapping requests.
- Two real-browser regressions delay the previous account's profile/user-list response until the next account has a protected Schedule POST pending. Both fail against the prior auth file and pass with the fix; the next account retains its identity and one revision-guarded save is acknowledged.
- Previous head 94cbb012 passed automated review, CodeQL and QA attempt 2. Attempt 1 had one intermittent Schedule owner-return acknowledgement timeout. No state trace was uploaded; its exact cause is still unproven. This follow-up fixes a separately reproduced related race, not a claim that a green rerun explains every intermittent failure.

## Preserved Earlier Protections
- Exact authorized central Medical reads remain distinct from local pending recovery and UI-only differences.
- Database/object-storage reads and persisted snapshots retain authorized tombstone revision metadata. A bare 404 is not a delete receipt.
- Fresh reads acknowledge only owned exact tombstones with absent native values and advancing revisions; new edits, other owners and persistence failure remain pending.
- Protected write/delete admission durably records ownership and pending generation before native mutation. Prepared-write markers distinguish crash phases; failed raw operations never queue; observed successors are retained.
- Bulk clear rejects protected values/pending tombstones before mutation. New authorized edits remain possible during reconciliation; queued/active exact Medical/deletion receipts retire at the ready event.

## Verification
Exact head: `55674b27c2cc312d01d42c7335efec2945ab1b69`.
Base: `c3c4a8431c14bd8c98619dafde7f1c6fbd2f21a7` (behind 0).

- Final local matrix: 3,224/3,224 passed (3,139 API/contracts, 75 central-state browser, 10 Medical clinical).
- Final risk selection: 320/320 passed across ten repetitions (22 new contracts, 2 late-response browser cases, 8 Schedule account/reload cases).
- Negative verification: initial 18 contracts failed 16 cases before correction; both new browser cases failed against unchanged 94cbb012 auth code. Temporary old-code routing removed.
- `qa:static` passed: check, release rules, incident readiness, storage/save policy, security, Supabase, performance and architecture. Same 84 existing architecture warnings; no budget/timeout increase or safety bypass.
- `git diff --check` passed; clean pushed worktree. Fresh exact-SHA GitHub QA, CodeQL and independent automated review requested.

## Scope And Release Control
Same twelve-file PR boundary: app-state API; shared auth/hydration, sync, data safety and facade; six QA files; architecture report. Latest follow-up changes five files within that boundary. No module product files, database/schema changes or main/staging pushes.

Review candidate only. No auto-merge or deploy. Whole-platform offline integration and true multi-user conflict resolution are separate work; local mock tests are not Live verification.

author: mergify[bot]
body:
This is an automatic copy of pull request #20282 done by [Mergify](https://mergify.com).

----

## Problem

Audit entries for several console actions (GROUP_CREATED/UPDATED/DELETED, MEMBERSHIP_CREATED/DELETED on groups, DICTIONARY_CREATED/UPDATED, and others) record the user as `system` instead of the authenticated user. API, application and role events in the same session record the right user.

Jira: https://gravitee.atlassian.net/browse/APIM-15172

## Root cause

`AuditServiceImpl.createAuditLog` is `@Async`. The context defines several `TaskExecutor` beans (`indexerThreadPoolTaskExecutor`, `asyncNotificationThreadPoolTaskExecutor`) and none named `taskExecutor`, so an unqualified `@Async` falls back to a `SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor`. Its threads do not carry the `SecurityContext`, so `getAuthenticatedUsernameOrSystem()` returns `system`.

The `createApiAuditLog` / `createApplicationAuditLog` / `createEnvironmentAuditLog` / `createOrganizationAuditLog` default methods call `createAuditLog` on the target itself, which bypasses the proxy and runs synchronously. That is why those events were correct. Services that call `auditService.createAuditLog(...)` directly (groups, memberships, dictionaries, tenants, categories, pages, themes, users, parameters, ...) went through the async proxy and lost the user.

## Fix

Remove `@Async` from `createAuditLog`, so every audit entry point runs synchronously in the caller's thread, as the four default methods already did. Repository errors are still caught and logged, so callers are unaffected by audit write failures.

## Tests

- New `AuditService_AuthenticatedUserTest`: Spring context with `@EnableAsync`, calls the service **through its proxy** with an authenticated user, and asserts the stored audit user.
  - Before the fix: `should_record_authenticated_user_when_called_through_proxy` fails with `expected: "console-user" but was: "system"`. The organization-audit case passes, which matches the reported asymmetry.
  - After the fix: both pass. All `AuditService*` tests (13) are green.
- Mutation check: the red run above is this same test against the unfixed code (`@Async` present).

## Backports

The same `@Async` and the same executor setup exist on master, 4.9.x, 4.11.x and 4.12.x.

**Security-sensitive:** touches audit logging (attribution of audit entries).


----

author: entelecheia
body:
Closes #175

## Summary

In a non-login shell the local client of `dot peer diff`/`dot peer sync` resolved to macOS openrsync, which escapes non-ASCII names as `\#ooo`, so the inventory failed valid NFD names with "not NFD-normalized".

- `LocalRsyncPath` probes `rsync`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/rsync`, `/usr/local/bin/rsync`, rejects openrsync and 2.x (same rule as `RemoteRsyncPath`), and returns the absolute path.
- `PeerDiff` and `PeerSync` resolve it together with the remote `--rsync-path` (`resolvePeerRsync`), before any transfer. Every local rsync of a peer run goes through `cfg.rsyncBin()`: workspace and home inventories, pull/push (`runRsync`, `runPeerRsync`), delete passes, replica push. Handover inherits it through `PeerSync`.
- Only openrsync locally: diff and sync exit non-zero before transferring; the error names each rejected path and its version banner.
- Both inventories pass `-8`, so rsync 3.x keeps raw bytes under the C locale (glibc treats high-bit bytes as unprintable there). A name that still contains `\#ooo` is reported as an rsync escaping problem, not an NFD violation.
- `dot peer doctor` prints the local rsync path and version (fails the check when none is usable).
- CI: macOS installs rsync 3.x; a new step fails if the real-rsync non-ASCII test skips.

## Verification (acceptance criteria)

- [x] AC1, `/usr/bin` first on PATH, NFD Korean names: `TestPeerDiff_NonASCIINameThroughResolvedLocalRsync` puts an openrsync stub first on PATH (fails if used as a client), sets `LC_ALL=C`, marks the NFD migration, and diffs a peer holding `docs/한글-보고서.md` (NFD). The run resolves the real 3.x client and lists the name byte-exact. Mutation check: reverting the workspace inventory to bare `rsync` makes this test fail.
- [x] AC2, only openrsync locally: `TestPeerDiffAndSync_RefuseOpenrsyncOnlyBeforeTransfer` (diff and sync error naming the stub path and "openrsync"; the stub never ran as a client), `TestLocalRsyncPath_OnlyOpenrsyncNamesPathAndVersion`.
- [x] AC3, real-rsync test with a non-ASCII name through the local resolution: the AC1 test; CI step "Peer real-rsync evidence" requires it to PASS on ubuntu and macOS.
- [x] Escape classification: `TestParsePeerRemoteInventory_EscapedNameIsNotAnNFDError`.

Local (current Mac, dot worktree): `go vet ./...`, `go test ./... -race -count=1` all ok, `golangci-lint run ./...` 0 issues, `make docs` regenerated `dot_peer_doctor.md`. Two-Mac behavior over real ssh is unverified here.

## Review record

- OCR delegation review (Claude Code, read-only) at 9464fb2: two minor findings, both fixed in 75229c0 (escape error names the real causes: control characters, a literal `\#`, or openrsync; the config-time PATH lookup keeps only a clean result, no `exec.ErrDot` path).
- Re-review at 75229c0 (fresh reviewer): no Important findings. Nits accepted: the rejected-candidate error includes the whole `--version` text; `-8` is exercised only on the glibc leg (macOS rsync 3.x prints raw bytes either way); a control character in a tracked host path now fails the run closed instead of syncing a wrong name; the local rsync check runs before the fence (a demoting coordinator without rsync 3.x errors instead of demoting; nothing transfers).
- CI at 75229c0: all jobs green.


🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_013oBZSNsemusFYkxndrGFob

## Summary by Sourcery

Ensure peer operations use a verified rsync 3.x client end to end, preserving non-ASCII filenames and failing early when no compatible local rsync is available.

New Features:
- Add local rsync discovery that selects an absolute, verified rsync 3.x binary and rejects openrsync or older versions before peer operations.
- Expose local rsync availability and version in `dot peer doctor`.
- Preserve non-ASCII inventory names under the C locale and classify rsync octal escapes separately from NFD normalization errors.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure all peer inventories, transfers, deletion passes, and replica pushes use the resolved local rsync client instead of an unverified PATH lookup.
- Prevent peer diff and sync from transferring when only an incompatible local rsync is available.
- Fix peer handling of valid NFD non-ASCII filenames when macOS openrsync would otherwise escape their bytes.

Enhancements:
- Resolve and pin both local and remote rsync implementations before peer diff or sync runs.

CI:
- Install rsync 3.x on macOS CI runners and require the real-rsync non-ASCII peer test to execute successfully.

Documentation:
- Document the local rsync prerequisite and doctor check.

Tests:
- Add coverage for local rsync selection, incompatible-only environments, non-ASCII peer inventories, and rsync escape classification.

## Summary

Refs #3761 - this PR addresses **items 3, 6 and 9 only**. Items 1, 10, 11, 12 and the tracked items are out of scope (other workers / live-trace investigations).

- New counter `orleans.lattice.saturation.refusals` (`LatticeMetrics.SaturationRefusals`), tagged `tree` and `source` (snake_case of `LatticeSaturationSource`, zero-primed per source via `[InstrumentedEnum]`). Every raise site records before it throws: WAL admission (`WalCommitLogWriter`), atomic-write saga (`AtomicWriteGrain`), `LatticeGrain` / `LatticeGrain.Cursor`, and `TxRegistryGrain.Admission`.
- Per the prescribed fix, the internal refusal - a background starvation drive refused a replay permit in `BPlusLeafGrain.Activation` - is no longer an exception. It returns the new `LeafStarvationDriveOutcome.AdmissionRefused` verdict, is counted under `replay_permit_admission`, and `LatticeWalGcScheduler` maps it to the new `drove_admission_refused` arm on `orleans.lattice.wal.gc.blocked_leaf_reactivations`.

### Item 6 - SQLite pin-store writes fail with "database is locked" under bulk ingest

- New `RepoContextGrainStorageLockRetryPolicy` (bounded, jittered, exponential; `PinStateWrites` default = 2 re-issues from a 250 ms base, scoped to pin-store state names) applied in `RepoContextLockAttributingGrainStorage` to `WriteStateAsync` / `ClearStateAsync` when the failure is a SQLite lock. A failed lock-contended write leaves the row and the grain state's ETag unchanged, so a re-issue is safe; non-lock faults are not retried. `DurabilitySelector` wires the policy for the SQLite pin store.
- New counter `lattice_repocontext_grain_storage_lock_retries_total{operation,outcome}` on the existing lock meter (`outcome` = `recovered` | `gave_up`, zero-primed).

Authorization denials, region rejection and unmarked exceptions still throw exactly as before.

author: niclas-lindgren
body:
## Problem
`operator publish --confirm-public` was held by `changed_interval_without_accepted_booking` for the rvv-0030 Skien correction. The tournament-scoped gate treated *placement*, *booking evidence* and *publication* as one concern, so RVV could not publish its proposed season plan to ask host clubs to reserve the slots — a circular dependency.

## Change
- `tournament_scheduler/pipeline/publication_scope.py` classifies every added/interval-changed tournament as:
  - **booked** — accepted, source-backed confirmation for the exact interval,
  - **proposed** — publishable, publicly labelled as awaiting host confirmation,
  - **contradicted** — its own evidence explicitly rejects/conflicts with the placement.
  `ELIGIBLE` publishes booked and proposed placements alike; `HELD` is now reserved for a contradicted placement or an unexplained public-entry removal; `BLOCKED` still covers projection/schema inconsistency and unauthorized hosting transfer; `NOT_CHECKABLE` still falls back to the semantic-audit gate.
- `booking_status_report` exposes a typed `conflict` flag, so a club authority the independent calendar directly contradicts is a first-class contradiction rather than a re-parsed follow-up string.
- Publish preflight messaging, `SKILL.md`, `publish.md`, `audit-publication.md` and `season-delivery.md` now state that missing accepted booking is not itself a blocker, while a proposed placement must never be presented as confirmed and must never be fabricated/downgraded into one.

No unscoped bypass flag, no audit-verdict downgrade, no booking-state mutation.

## Evidence
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_publication_scope.py tests/test_publish_publication_scope_gate.py -q` → **20 passed**
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_operational_booking_state.py tests/test_publish_audit_gate.py tests/test_booking_assessment.py tests/test_club_booking_source.py tests/test_approval_lifecycle.py tests/test_refresh_calendar_evidence.py -q` → **166 passed**
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_html_exporter.py tests/test_pages_publish.py tests/test_publication_evidence.py -q` → **90 passed**
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_stage4_export.py -q` → **70 passed**
- `scripts/check lint quick` → **3497 passed, 1 skipped** (ruff + fast suite)
- Read-only reproduction against the live `.pipeline/stage4_export.json` reviewed plan and current canonical season: `status=ELIGIBLE`, `proposed=['rvv-0030']`, `held=[]`, `booked=[]`. The existing public HTML already renders rvv-0030 as `action_required`/`stale` (`MÅ RE-BEKREFTES`), never as `booked`.

## New regression coverage
- changed and added proposed intervals (publishable)
- stale/interval-invalidated confirmation (the rvv-0030 shape) → proposed
- accepted booking → booked
- explicit rejection → held (added + changed)
- calendar contradiction (`conflict`) → held
- unexplained removal → held
- typed `conflict` signal in the booking-status projection

## Not in scope / not done
No operational season mutation, export, audit submission or publication was performed. The pre-existing dirty canonical/export files in the worktree were left untouched and are not part of this PR.

author: kartsan03
body:
Closes #222.

## Why

`instructions` is a static string, so a server that serves several experiences cannot give each client its own system prompt. The only workaround is to mutate the shared options before a request and restore them after. @ropiteaux proposed accepting a function in #222, and you agreed there. That thread was about v1's `McpModule.forRoot`, so this is the same idea on the v2 `McpStrategy`.

## What

`McpServerOptions.instructions` also accepts a function of the raw transport request:

```ts
new McpStrategy({
  instructions: (req) =>
    (req as IncomingMessage | undefined)?.headers['x-experience'] === 'foo'
      ? fooInstructions
      : defaultInstructions,
  // ...
});
```

It is resolved in `createServer`, which now takes the request that caused the server to be created:
- once per session on stateful 2025-era HTTP (the `initialize` request)
- once per request on stateless 2025-era and on `2026-07-28` traffic (`createBoundServer` already had the request)
- with `undefined` on STDIO, matching `resolveUser` and tool handlers

A string works exactly as before. A resolver that throws ends up in the existing `handlePost` catch, so the client gets the usual 500 JSON-RPC error and the error is logged.

`McpTransportContext.createServer` gained an optional `rawRequest` parameter. That is additive, so custom transports that call it without arguments keep compiling.

## Tests

`tests/mcp-instructions.e2e.spec.ts` runs for both eras (`describe.each(ERAS)`), on stateful and stateless transports. Two clients send different `x-experience` headers and each gets its own `getInstructions()`. There is also a check that a static string still works.

- Without the source change, the 8 per-client cases fail (`Received: undefined`).
- Full suite: 940 pass, 0 fail.

Docs: the `instructions` row in `docs/server-examples.md` now mentions the function form.

body:
#393 removed the npm upgrade step and switched the release script to `pnpm publish`, so publishing ran on the npm 10.x bundled with Node 22. npm trusted publishing (OIDC), which published 2.0.2, requires npm >= 11.5.1, so every publish since has failed and 2.1.0 never reached npm.

- Run the release job on Node 24, which bundles npm 11
- Restore `npm publish --provenance` as the release script
- Drop NPM_TOKEN so changesets/action uses the OIDC path
- Log the npm version for easier debugging

body:
## Summary

Adds 30 configurable actions for directly starting and stopping individual setlist steps.

This makes it possible to assign dedicated buttons to setlist steps using a keyboard, MIDI controller, footswitch, or Stream Deck.

## Behavior

- Pressing a step shortcut while playback is stopped selects and starts that step.
- Pressing the shortcut for the currently playing step stops playback.
- Pressing a shortcut for another step immediately switches playback to that step.
- The existing Space shortcut continues to provide general Play/Stop control.
- Shortcuts targeting a step that does not exist in the current setlist do nothing.

## Settings

Adds a new **Setlist** group to the Hotkeys settings with configurable actions from:

- Step 1 Start/Stop
- Step 2 Start/Stop
- ...
- Step 30 Start/Stop

No default key combinations are assigned, avoiding conflicts with existing shortcuts.

## Implementation

- Adds direct step-jump support to the setlist runtime and runner.
- Routes the new actions through the existing unified action dispatcher.
- Reuses the existing setlist playback and selection behavior.
- Adds translation fallbacks for dynamically generated action labels and descriptions.

## Testing

- Tested manually with four setlist steps and a Stream Deck.
- Verified starting, stopping, and switching directly between steps.
- Verified that the existing Space Play/Stop shortcut remains unchanged.
- All existing tests passed.
- Added a runtime test for directly jumping to a requested setlist step.

author: blackvs
body:
This PR adds aicrewd's route for aimem's coordination.v1 questions, `POST /v1/crew/coordination`, with the process pin on the facts that start work. It also adds per-operation introspection credentials and the vendored fixtures. It is the second half of b0; b0a (#38) supplied the store.

## Scope (frozen on the task)

**Objective**

- Serve `POST /v1/crew/coordination` as aimem's coordination.v1 specifies, frozen at aimem `8ac4ef1` after C5w, C5c-w and C5-w2. Answers come from b0a's `CoordinationFact`.
- The route follows the introspection route's shape:
  - the credential must permit `crew.coordination`, and one that doesn't answers like an unknown one;
  - the version header and the body version must both be 1;
  - the hub, a nonce echo, a strict body, one snapshot, no cache.
- **Process pin** (operator decisions D-b1(a) and (ii)):
  - `offer`, `accepted_attempt` and `independent_claim` carry `process: {repo, commit, manifest}`, copied verbatim from aicrew's record.
  - No other kind carries a pin.
  - A pin is recorded only in the hub selection's forms, and the repository limit rises from 256 to 512 bytes.
  - A malformed recorded pin answers inactive.
- **Schema v15:** `introspection_credentials.operations`. Existing credentials keep `crew.introspection` only (D-b0-1). `aicrew introspection-credential issue|rotate -operations`, and `list` shows the operations.

**Acceptance criteria**

- The fixtures are vendored with their provenance and replayed. The replay covers shapes, versions, size, the `k1_` and `p1_` digests, secret placement, and the pin cases, with each malformed pin run against aicrew's validator.
- A mirror of aimem's acceptance checks runs on real replies.
- A fake aimem runs end to end over all six kinds, including the inactive cases.
- Pin forms are checked when a pin is recorded, with the backstop tested.
- No secret appears in replies, refusals or logs.
- Mutations are caught.
- The docs are updated.

**Non-goals:** begin and settle routes (b1), the read-scope client (b3), any aimem change, deployment.

## Changes

- **`internal/server/coordination.go`:** the route, its refusal texts, and the reply types, which are exactly the fixture's shape. The member's generation is a string, and `expires_at` is truncated to the second.
- **`internal/server/introspect.go`:** `refuseFrom` shares the envelope with the new route's own texts.
- **`internal/server/server.go`:** the route is registered as owning its body.
- **`internal/store/attempts.go`:** `ValidProcessIdentity`. It repeats aimem's `process.Ref.Validate` rules and additionally refuses a manifest of exactly `..`, which aimem's `checkRepoPath` accepts even though the written rule keeps the path inside the repository. `TrustedProcess.valid` uses it, so offers and claims refuse malformed pins.
- **`internal/store/coordination.go`:** `independent_claim` facts carry the pin, and a malformed recorded pin makes the fact inactive.
- **`internal/store/introspection.go`:**
  - `IssueIntrospectionCredential(…, ops...)` records the operations, and defaults to both.
  - `AuthenticateIntrospection` now requires `crew.introspection`, and the new `AuthenticateCoordination` requires `crew.coordination`. Both refuse as unauthenticated.
- **`internal/store/store.go`:** schema v15.
- **`cmd/aicrew`:** the `-operations` flag, and `operations` in the printed metadata.
- **`internal/server/testdata/coordination-v1/`:** `examples.json` and `openapi-proposal.json` at aimem `8ac4ef1`, with a PROVENANCE note. The blob IDs were checked against aimem's tree.
- **Docs:** CREW-CONTRACT gets a "Coordination facts (aimem → aicrew)" section, and its proof and pin passages are corrected. DEVELOPMENT covers `-operations` and enabling coordination by rotation.
- **Guards:** the server's exposure guard allows the two new store calls, since both authenticate by peer credential, and the route inventory lists the new route.

## Evidence

- **Tests:**
  - `TestCoordinationFixtureShapes`: the request and reply types take exactly the fixture's six exchanges and inactive replies. Our re-encoded replies equal the fixture's, and the pin appears exactly on its three kinds. It also checks the `k1_` and `p1_` vectors, and that every malformed fixture pin is refused.
  - `TestCoordinationReplySize`: the largest possible reply fits aimem's 16,384-byte read bound.
  - `TestCoordinationEndToEnd`: all six kinds run through the real store operations. A fake aimem asks the real route before each commit and applies aimem's checks: strict shape, nonce, service and hub, expiry, operation, kind and role, task, `k1_` digest, required and absent fields per kind, the references against the hold and the intended worker, the pin's form, and the pin against the current selection. Each fact's member is asserted. No reply carries a proof, settled proofs answer inactive, and no secret reaches the logs.
  - `TestCoordinationRefusals`: a fact that stops being true before aimem asks gives `coordination_rejected`, and a moved selection gives `process_mismatch`. Both settle the step.
  - `TestCoordinationRequestRules`: the fixture's version cases; an introspection-only credential; an unknown credential; another hub's credential; content type, unknown field, trailing data and nonce errors; a declared oversized body, sent as headers only; and a coordination-only credential refused by the introspection route.
  - Store: `TestProcessPinForms` covers valid pins, including a 512-byte repository, and 16 malformed forms, including `..`. It checks that offers and claims refuse malformed pins before any proof exists. `TestMalformedRecordedPinAnswersInactive`, `TestIntrospectionCredentialOperations` and `TestMigrationV15KeepsCredentialsToIntrospection` complete the store tests.
  - CLI: `TestIssueOperations`, plus usage cases.
- **Mutations: 19 of 19 caught.**
  - independent_claim without its pin;
  - a pin on `stopped`;
  - no malformed-pin backstop;
  - the repository scheme unchecked;
  - the repository limit back at 256;
  - the commit shape unchecked;
  - `..` accepted;
  - a manifest escaping the repository accepted;
  - no pin forms at record time;
  - coordination authenticated as introspection;
  - operations unchecked;
  - the migration granting coordination;
  - the pin normalized;
  - the pin's fields swapped;
  - the version header unchecked;
  - the body version unchecked;
  - the hub unchecked;
  - the nonce not echoed;
  - the wrong member session.
- **Stability:** `go test -count=50` passes on the new store, server and CLI tests.
- **Local checks:** `gofmt -l .` is empty; `go vet ./...` passes, including with `GOOS=linux` and `GOOS=darwin`; `go mod verify` passes; `go mod tidy -diff` is empty; `go test -count=1 ./...` passes.

## Notes for review

- The p1_ vectors check the test's own digest. aicrew computes `p1_` only when it reads receipts by proof, which comes in b3.
- `TestCoordinationFixtureShapes` fails if a malformed fixture pin is ever accepted. Pins that carry an extra field (`ref`, `digest`) cannot be represented in aicrew's three-field pin type at all.

author: sigurdm
body:
Stacked on #9622 (which is stacked on #9621).

Changes `isRuntimeVersioned` from `true` to `false` for the weekly integrity check tasks in `setupAnalyzerPeriodicTasks`:
- `check-datastore-integrity-users`
- `check-datastore-integrity-packages`
- `check-datastore-integrity-audit-logs`
- `check-tarball-integrity`

### Why
`NeatTaskStatus` keys runtime-versioned tasks by `(name, runtimeVersion)` and non-versioned tasks by `(name, '-')`. Because all four integrity checks audit shared, unversioned Datastore entities, SQL tables, and GCS archive buckets (`canonicalPackagesBucketName` and `latest/api/archives/`) rather than `runtimeVersion`-scoped state:
1. **No post-deploy stampede:** With `isRuntimeVersioned: true`, every `runtimeVersion` deployment has no prior `NeatTaskStatus` entry for `(taskName, newRuntimeVersion)`, causing all four weekly scans to start immediately on deploy alongside startup backfill tasks (`backfill-new-fields`, `synchronize-exported-api`, `backfill-task-tracking-state`).
2. **No duplicate runs across active versions:** While the previous App Engine version remains running alongside the newly deployed version, non-versioned status records share the global `(taskName, '-')` lock and completion timestamp, so the checks run once every 6 days across deployments.

body:
## Resumen

Frontend del issue #39 (OE-5, OE-2): **bandeja de identificación**, **lista ONI** e **historial de resoluciones manuales** en el detalle de obra.

- **Bandeja de identificación** (`/identificacion`): los casos ONI pendientes con la entrada del reporte, la evidencia, los IDs de fuente y las obras candidatas con su puntaje. Tres acciones por caso — asignar a una candidata, buscar otra obra en el catálogo o descartar el registro —, todas con nota obligatoria y remoción optimista.
- **Lista ONI** (`/lista-oni`): todos los casos (pendientes, asignados, descartados) con estado, responsable y última actualización, filtros por estado/fuente/periodo aplicados por el servidor y el historial de cada registro.
- **Historial de resoluciones manuales**: sección al final de la ficha de obra, desde `GET /auditoria/obra/{id}` (asientos `identificacion.asignada`).
- **Navegación**: "Identificación" y "Lista ONI" entre "Distribución" y "Anomalías", solo administrador, con badge del conteo de pendientes.

Las decisiones de diseño (D1–D9, incluida la de no usar react-query y la de no preseleccionar ninguna candidata por ADR 0007) están razonadas en el plano: [`docs/planes/39-bandeja-identificacion/plan.md`](https://github.com/rosvend/intela/blob/feature/39-matching-review-inbox-oni/docs/planes/39-bandeja-identificacion/plan.md). Las cuatro capturas del Make v9 quedan en `docs/mockups/`.

## Tipo de cambio

- [x] `feature` — funcionalidad nueva

- [ ] Cambia una **cifra o regla normativa** (requiere cita al reglamento)
- [ ] Cambia el **esquema de datos** (requiere migracion)
- [ ] Cambia un **contrato de API** (requiere regenerar los tipos del frontend) — **no**: este PR *consume* el contrato ya mergeado (`GET /identificacion/casos` de #174 / #176 y la resolución manual de #175 / #186). No toca `api/openapi.yaml` ni `web/src/contrato.d.ts`; los tipos salen de `npm run contrato`, nunca escritos a mano.

## Cumplimiento de Clean Architecture

**N/A**: el PR es solo de `web/` (React + TypeScript). No toca `internal/dominio/`, `internal/aplicacion/` ni los adaptadores, así que la regla de dependencia, las fronteras de módulo y `PuertoReloj` no entran. Se dejan sin marcar en vez de marcarlas en falso.

Los cuatro invariantes del dominio, comprobados del lado del cliente:

- [x] No se suman importes por fila: **ninguna vista de este PR muestra montos** (ni la bandeja, ni el panel, ni la lista ONI, ni el historial). La bandeja muestra el puntaje de similitud como decimal es-CO (`0,71`), nunca como porcentaje ni como cifra de dinero.
- [x] Ningún camino de tipos lleva de una parrilla a un porcentaje de pago: el payload del asiento `identificacion.asignada` se lee campo por campo con `leerResolucionAsentada`, y ninguno es un porcentaje.
- [x] Lo declarado que no suma 100% se retiene: el PR no calcula reparto; solo muestra `estado_declaracion` y `suma_porcentajes` tal como los sirve el servidor.
- [x] Ninguna firma emite orden de pago: no hay camino de pago en el PR.

**Trazabilidad** (`RD 16`): la nota de la resolución es obligatoria (1..300 caracteres, recortada en el cliente igual que en Go) y el historial de la obra muestra usuario, fecha, decisión, nota y la referencia de origen (`uso_id · reporte_id`). Un payload ilegible **no se esconde**: se pinta con su propio aviso.

## Evidencia de pruebas

En `web/`:

```
$ npm run lint
> eslint .
(sin hallazgos)

$ npm run typecheck
> tsc --noEmit
(sin errores)

$ npm test          # incluye `contrato:check` (openapi-typescript --check)
 Test Files  59 passed (59)
      Tests  800 passed (800)

$ npm run build
> tsc -b && vite build
✓ 433 modules transformed.
✓ built in 1.17s
```

Línea base antes de #39: 48 archivos / 692 tests. Este PR suma **11 archivos de prueba y 108 tests**.

- [x] Pruebas nuevas para el comportamiento nuevo: `tipos`, `resolucion`, `Dialogo`, `PanelResolucion`, `BandejaIdentificacion`, `ListaOni`, `HistorialResoluciones`, `pendientes`, `iniciales`, `contrato` y el recorrido de integración `identificacion/flujo.test.tsx` (`<App />` con un servidor falso **con estado**: resolver un caso → sale de la bandeja y del badge → la lista ONI lo sirve "Asignada" con su responsable → su historial → "Ver la obra" → la bitácora de la obra con usuario, fecha, decisión y nota).
- [x] `ci` en verde en este PR *(se comprueba al abrirlo)*.

## Issues vinculados

Closes #39

## Riesgos y notas para quien revise

- **Falta una revisión independiente.** La revisión de `revisor-front` (Sonnet, esfuerzo alto) **no se pudo ejecutar**: en la sesión de trabajo el único modelo enrutable era `deepseek-flash` y el runtime rechazó `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` ("not allowed for this Session"). La revisó el agente autor con el checklist del plano: 84/84 textos literales de §5 presentes, D1–D9 uno por uno, y la cobertura de §6 verificada test por test. Hallazgo de esa revisión, ya corregido aquí: de los cuatro desenlaces del 409, el "sin causa reconocida" solo estaba probado en la función pura y no en la bandeja — es el que no se puede confundir con "ya resuelto", porque ese sí saca el caso de la lista.
- **Desviación consciente del plano**: el filtro `?desde=` de D4 **no se implementó** porque `GET /identificacion/casos` no declara ese parámetro. Mandarlo sería un filtro que el servidor ignora en silencio, o filtrar en el cliente sobre una sola página contradiciendo lo que la pantalla promete. Está razonado en `web/src/identificacion/ListaOni.tsx` y conviene decidir si el contrato gana el parámetro o el plano lo pierde.
- **Pendiente del backend (no bloquea)**: el 409 no trae `codigo`, así que `causaDelConflicto` distingue las tres causas por el texto centinela **dentro** del mensaje — el de alias llega envuelto por Go (`resolver el uso "uso-1": ese identificador ya apunta a otra obra: …`) y por eso no se puede comparar con el prefijo del ejemplo del contrato. Cuando el contrato traiga el `codigo`, esa lista se va.
- **Nit**: el badge del sidebar dice "1 pendientes" a un lector de pantalla (el texto " pendientes" es el que fija el plano §5); el número visible y la pastilla de la bandeja sí singularizan.

author: gyguan
body:
Closes #345

## 根因
上一版只支持未知名称的 Map wrapper；真实 Provider 仍可能返回 JSON 字符串或单元素数组作为中间 envelope，导致 `fenced>object` 后仍在根节点报 `$.title is required`。

## 修改
- Canonical Paper discovery 支持 Map / 单元素数组 / JSON-looking string。
- 允许多层组合，最大深度受限。
- 数组只接受单元素 envelope，不扫描普通业务数组。
- 跳过 questions/options/hints/tags 等业务集合，避免误识别。
- 最终仍要求唯一 Canonical Paper 候选，多候选 fail-closed。
- 找不到时输出安全的 `rootKeys` 摘要，不记录题目正文。

## 回归
- JSON string envelope。
- singleton-array envelope。
- Map + array + JSON string 组合。
- fenced + 组合 envelope 的 ModelClient 端到端场景。
- 无候选时 root keys 诊断。

author: mahendrabishnoi2
body:
Part of #99.

## Summary

- **Plan:** adds [`docs/backup-and-restore-plan.md`](https://github.com/forgelog/forgelog/blob/claude/backup-remote-options-w795ij/docs/backup-and-restore-plan.md). It covers three phases: OS backup, versioned JSON export/import, and cloud backup. It also records the agreed decisions (discard a restored in-progress workout with a notice, keep watch backup off, encryption-only cloud backup, Android first).
- **PR 1 of Phase 1, restore detection:** backup is still disabled, so this has no user-visible effect until a database is actually restored.
  - Migration 6 adds a single-row `backup_state` table, with `src/db/repositories/backupState.ts` exposed through `mobileStore`.
  - `src/backup/installationMarker.ts` writes `forgelog-installation.json` to `Paths.document`. PR 2's backup rules will leave it out, so a restored database always arrives with a mismatched installation ID.
  - `src/domain/restoreDetection.ts` classifies each launch as adopt, normal or restored.
  - `src/application/restore.ts`: `checkForOsRestore` writes the marker before updating the database, so a crash in between repeats safely on the next launch. On restore, it discards a stale in-progress workout through the normal lifecycle (a finished copy on the watch still wins) and records a restore notice.
  - `App.tsx` runs the check on Android before wear sync starts and before the navigator renders. The check is memoized and a failure is non-fatal.
  - Home shows a dismissible "Restored from backup" card when a notice is pending.
  - Adds the `expo-file-system` dependency, and gives `src/backup` the same lint import rules as `src/sync`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test --ci --coverage`: 56 suites, 389 tests passing
- [x] `pnpm run check:coverage`
- [x] `pnpm run lint`
- [x] `pnpm run typecheck`
- [x] Real in-memory DB tests for each launch case, an idempotent repeat run, a failed transaction followed by a retry, the active-workout discard, and keeping completed history
- [x] Home flow tests for showing and dismissing the notice
- [ ] On-device verification. Needs PR 2 to enable backup, then the `adb shell bmgr` steps in the plan.

author: dtymoszenko
body:
First half of the Docker release: a **server mode** with a password login, like Actual Budget's server. The Docker image (next PR) runs FlyBudget in this mode.

## What changes
- `FLYBUDGET_SERVER_MODE=true` enables login. On the first visit you create a password; after that every `/api` route except `/api/health` and `/api/auth/*` requires a session.
- Passwords hashed with scrypt. Sessions are random 256-bit tokens stored only as SHA-256 hashes, sent as an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie (Secure over HTTPS), valid 30 days.
- 10 failed login/setup/change attempts per 15 minutes, then 429.
- Changing the password signs out every other device.
- New env vars: `FLYBUDGET_HOST`, `FLYBUDGET_ALLOWED_HOSTS`, `FLYBUDGET_TRUST_PROXY`, `FLYBUDGET_DATA_KEY_FILE` (for Docker secrets). Server mode won't start without an encryption key, so bank credentials are always encrypted.
- Client: login / first-run screen (`AuthGate`), and a **Settings → Server** tab (only in server mode) to change the password or sign out.
- Migration `0013_server_auth` adds `auth_config` and `sessions`.

The **desktop app and `npm run dev` are unchanged**: no login, same host/origin/token guards.

## Testing
- New tests: password hashing, the full auth flow (setup, login, logout, change password, rate limit), server-mode host allowlist. All 150 server tests pass; client typecheck/build/tests pass.
- Ran the server locally in server mode: 401 without login, setup/login/logout work, cross-site login rejected (403), app pages served at real URLs.

author: dstebila
body:
Adds the textbook RF/RP switching lemma as the worked example for identical-until-bad hops (Bellare-Rogaway 2006, Figure 2; Shoup 2004, section 5.1).

- `Games/PRP/RFvsRP.game`: the lazily sampled random function / random permutation pair, written to be identical until a collision flag `bad`.
- `Games/Helpers/Probability/CollisionFlagSampling.game`: the birthday fact of `DistinctSampling` in flag form (values stay uniform; only the collision report is silenced).
- `Proofs/PRP/RFRP_Switching_Event.proof`: proves `Pr[bad] <= count_Query(count_Query - 1)/(2|X|)`.
- `Proofs/PRP/RFRP_Switching.proof`: hops from `RFRPSwitching.RandomFunction` to `RandomPermutation` with one identical-until-bad step, using the event proof as a lemma.

Needs the engine support in ProofFrog/ProofFrog (branch `upto-events`), whose PR bumps the submodule pin to this commit.

body:
## Aanleiding

Na #204 (het tekenbudget van 55.000 naar 250.000 tekens) op productie opnieuw gedraaid voor Van
den Udenhout: van 11 naar 59 knopen, alle eerder ontbrekende diensten erbij (financiering, lease,
verhuur, schadeherstel, onderhoud: 36 diensten in totaal).

## Bevinding

Het model vond eigenlijk 87 knopen. De vaste grens van 60 (`MAX_NODES`) kapte de rest af, en de
zes automerken (Audi, CUPRA, SEAT, Škoda, Volkswagen, Volkswagen Bedrijfswagens) vielen daarbij
weg, ook al stonden ze er eerder wel. Dezelfde soort fout als het tekenbudget: een vaste grens die
nooit tegen een echte grote klant was afgezet.

## De reparatie

`MAX_NODES` van 60 naar 200, ruim boven wat Van den Udenhout liet zien. `persistTree()` blijft
`droppedByCap` melden in `gaps` als zelfs dat niet genoeg is, dus een grens die opnieuw te krap
blijkt blijft zichtbaar in plaats van stil af te kappen.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npm run test:unit` (5524 geslaagd, ongewijzigd)
- [x] `npm run test:chain` (985 geslaagd, ongewijzigd)
- [x] `npm run build`

author: badsgahhl
body:
Franz druckt Anhänger, stanzt oben ein Loch hinein und zieht ein Bändchen durch — und die Zange geht mitten durch den Produktnamen. Zwei Regler, beide im Abschnitt **Bogen & Schild**:

- **Loch oben fürs Bändchen** (0–20 mm) hält oben auf jedem Schild einen Streifen frei. Die Schrift rückt nach unten.
- **Preis steht** (oben · mittig · unten) verschiebt den Preis in dem Platz, den er ohnehin hat.

## Warum das Loch nicht mitskaliert

Anders als jedes andere Maß hier ist der Streifen echte Millimeter: eine Lochzange stanzt auf dem A10-Anhänger dasselbe Loch wie auf einem Viertel-A4, und ein Streifen, der mit dem Format schrumpft, versagt genau dort, wo Anhänger überhaupt erst gebraucht werden.

Damit ist es die einzige Einstellung, die ein kleines Format zerlegen könnte — also ist sie bei einem Drittel der Schildhöhe gedeckelt, und die Seitenleiste schreibt hin, was von den eingestellten Millimetern übrig bleibt, statt stillschweigend weniger zu nehmen. Auf dem 64er-Bogen sind das 12,4 von 20 mm.

## Warum der Preis nicht kleiner wird

Zwei leere Flex-Elemente über und unter dem Preis wachsen im eingestellten Verhältnis. Der Platz selbst bleibt unangetastet, der Preis wird also verschoben und nicht verkleinert — „runterschieben", nicht „kleiner machen". Der Abstand zum Preiszusatz wandert dabei vom Container an den Zusatz, was ohnehin der einzige Fall ist, in dem die Geometrie ihn mitzählt.

## Der Schutz für alles, was kein Anhänger ist

Beide Regler sind ab Werk aus (Loch 0 mm, Preis mittig), und das ist die eigentliche Absicherung: ein Schild, das niemand aufhängt, ist nicht ungefähr wie vorher, sondern identisch.

Belegt an zwei Stellen:

- **Tests** — die Voreinstellung lässt jede Maßzahl unverändert; der Streifen geht vom Preisblock ab und nicht vom Namen; über *alle* Raster bei maximalem Loch und maximalem Rand bleibt die Inhaltshöhe positiv und der Preis druckbar; die Preisposition verändert keine einzige Box.
- **Chromium** — ein Bogen mit vier Schildern, darunter eines mit Preiszusatz und eines mit Aufschlüsselung, kommt vor und nach der Änderung byte-identisch heraus (gleiche MD5 des Screenshots in Druck-Medien).

`pnpm lint`, `pnpm type-check`, `pnpm format` und alle 346 Tests laufen durch.

## Nicht in diesem PR

Beim Nachmessen ist ein älterer Fehler aufgefallen, der schon in `main` steckt: beim Umschalten auf Druck-Medien lädt Chromium die Schrift neu, `loadingdone` verwirft daraufhin alle Messungen und misst neu — während die Mess-Sandbox im Druck per `display: none` ausgeblendet ist. Jede Messung ist dann 0, und die Spalte der Zusatz-Beträge fällt von 11,6 mm auf 0,265 mm zusammen. Das gehört in einen eigenen Fix, nicht hierher.
