author: go-to-k
body:
## Summary

cdkd persists a secret dynamic reference (`{{resolve:secretsmanager:...}}` / `{{resolve:ssm-secure:...}}`) as its EXPRESSION, not its value. A custom resource whose ServiceToken was built from one therefore reached `CustomResourceProvider.delete` as that expression, which passed the absent / non-string / masked (#3938) guards and was sent to `GetFunction` and the Delete invoke as a function name. It fails name validation exactly like the `***` mask, which on #3938's pre-fix real-AWS run left the readiness waiter polling for its full 10 minutes before the invoke failed with a message naming neither cause.

The delete now checks `dynamicReferenceTokens(serviceToken).length > 0` right after the #3938 mask arm and returns `{ outcome: 'skipped', reason: CR_REFERENCE_SERVICE_TOKEN_SKIP_REASON }` before any AWS call. The warning names the logical id (never the reference text), says CloudFormation does not support secure dynamic references in custom resources, and gives the same bounded remedies as #3938 (tear down by hand + `cdkd state orphan`, or restore the ARN while the handler still exists).

## Divergence from the issue's suggested fix

#3960 (filed in the #3938 review) proposed RESOLVING the reference on delete. Declined: CloudFormation documents that "Dynamic references can't be used for secure values (like those stored in Parameter Store or Secrets Manager) in custom resources" (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/dynamic-references.html). SECRET references are persisted as expressions (a plain `{{resolve:ssm:...}}` is stored resolved as a whole leaf; one embedded in a longer leaf can still be recorded as its expression, issue #2036, and is skipped by the same arm with wording that does not assume a secret), so the main records this reaches are ones CloudFormation would never have created; the "exhaust every addressable source" rule in `.claude/rules/provider-delete-path.md` does not reach them, since the record holds a pointer to a secret rather than an address, and threading a resolver into the delete path to revive them would extend a divergence rather than close it. The CFn-parity fix -- refusing a secure reference in custom-resource properties pre-flight -- is filed separately (see Follow-ups).

## Also in this PR (comments only)

- `src/deployment/secret-redaction.ts` (`recordMaskOnlyValuesIn`) and `src/deployment/deploy-engine.ts` (`registerNoEchoAttributes`): the rationale said a masked ServiceToken "passes both of that method's guards"; since #3938 it is a named skip that keeps the record.
- `src/deployment/secret-redaction.ts` (`recordNestedStackParameterExpressions`, residual (f)): said `cdkd scrub` cannot repair a pre-carry child record; since #3958 (#2252) scrub walks each nested child with the parent row's bag and re-runs the carry for the row.

## Review decisions

- Declined: folding the R1/R2 grep ladder and Phase 2's into a shared shell function (code-review nit 3) -- the two arms assert different reasons and records, and a shared helper would couple a fixture fix in one to the other.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/provisioning/custom-resource-masked-service-token.test.ts`: a whole secretsmanager reference, a whole ssm-secure reference, an ARN assembled around a secret reference and one assembled around a plain ssm reference (issue #2036) are each skipped with zero AWS calls; the warning content (and that the reference text is not echoed); the reason shape; inverted controls (an unterminated `{{resolve:` opener and a reference in a NON-token property both still reach `GetFunction`).
- Mutation probe: disabling the new guard turns the 3 skip cases and the warning case red; restored byte-exact.
- Integ: a new arm in `custom-resource-masked-service-token` seeds a Secrets Manager secret with the handler's ARN, deploys a `ReferenceDependent` whose ServiceToken is `{{resolve:secretsmanager:...}}`, asserts the PREMISE (the recorded ServiceToken is that expression), destroys and asserts exit 2 with the reference reason and the invoke-failure reason ABSENT, orphans the record and deletes the secret. The fixture now sweeps state object versions as every secret-seeding fixture must. Not yet run on real AWS: `/run-integ custom-resource-masked-service-token`.

## Follow-ups

- #3976 -- refuse a secure dynamic reference in custom-resource properties pre-flight (CFn parity); it reworks this fixture arm, so it waits for this PR.

Closes #3960

author: saforem2
body:
Four spacing and marker fixes on the landing widgets and prose code blocks.

## Widget rows (`3a3bcee`)

The work / posts / talks lists sat flush at a **19px pitch** while the
last.fm history beside them runs **32px**, which read as cramped rather
than dense.

Their boxes are a fixed 218.5px and already scroll, so gap buys room by
spending visible rows. Matching 32px outright would take 11.5 visible
rows down to 6.8; `row-gap: 0.25lh` lands the pitch at **23.8px** and
keeps **9.2**.

Touch tap targets still measure 24.7px against the WCAG 24px floor, now
with real separation between adjacent targets instead of none.

## Code block margins (`fdd65f3`)

Blocks carried `margin-block: 1lh 0.5lh` — **25px above, 12px below**.
Nearly every block in a list is introduced by its own item (`ezpz:`,
`BlendCorpus:`), so each one sat closer to the *next* item's label than
to its own. The grouping read backwards. Swapped to `0.5lh 1lh`.

The old top value was protecting the language badge that straddles the
top border. Measured rather than assumed: the badge is **16px**, and
across **206 badged blocks** none clips, with **1.5px** of headroom at
the tightest.

The case a full top margin was really for — a block directly after
another block — does occur: **74 adjacent pairs** at each width. But 68
of them are `text` fences carrying no badge, and the remaining 6 clear
by **11px** on the larger bottom margin.

## Nested block alignment (`7d9c506`)

`li > pre.astro-code { margin-left: 2ch }` was computing to 0px. The
rule is unlayered and `* { margin: 0 }` in `@layer base` beats it on
this property in this cascade — the same quirk already noted on
`pre.astro-code`'s `overflow`. So it had never once taken effect, and
every nested block sat flush with its own marker instead of with the
text that marker introduces.

Sized off the rendered marker advance rather than a round number: a `ul`
bullet advances **11.36px** against an 8px `ch`, so `2ch` overshot by
4.64px. `1.42ch` matches exactly; ordered lists take `2.42ch` for the
wider `N. ` decimal.

Two pages also had their fence at column 0, making the block a sibling
of the whole list rather than a child of the item introducing it.
Indented those to 4.

## Stray dash on nested `ol` items (`4bd8d74`)

WebTUI's `typography.css` sets `content: '- '` on `ul li::before` — a
**descendant** selector, so an `<ol>` nested anywhere inside a `<ul>`
collects the dash on top of its own decimal marker and renders
`- 1. text`. **54 list items across 13 pages** were doing this.

`slides.css` already carries exactly this fix scoped to slides, with a
comment naming the same cause; this is the document-scope copy. No
`!important` needed — the package rule sits in `@layer components` and
this one is unlayered, so it wins on origin alone.

It also closes the last alignment gap. The stray dash advances 11.36px,
so an `ol` item inside a `ul` indented its text by 30.72px while
`ol > li > pre` offset by 19.36px.

## Verification

Measured in headless Chrome against the built site, at **1000px and
460px**, after `document.fonts.ready`:

- All **344** nested `li > pre.astro-code` across **24 pages** now sit
  at **exactly 0px** from the text their marker introduces — against 4
  outliers at −11.36px before the marker fix.
- All **4185** `ul > li` keep their bullet; all **628** `ol > li` now
  carry only their number, none showing `- 1.`.
- **0 of 206** badged blocks clip, tightest headroom 1.5px.
- Coarse-pointer pass at 390x844 for the tap-target floor.
- Full build: 151 pages, no errors. `format:check` and `lint` clean.
- Notebooks zero this margin (`.nb-body`) and slides set their own
  (`0.9lh 0.5lh`), so both are untouched.

> One note on history: `8588a00` was force-updated to `fdd65f3`. The
> tree is byte-identical — only the message changed, because three of
> its claims (including "0 adjacent pairs") turned out wrong when
> measured properly.

body:
Re-runs valhalla#4552's CostMatrix comparison with the map Valhalla ships (4.5.0), main and absl. Notes and scripts, no header change.

| seconds per file of 20 requests | 4.5.0 | main | absl |
|---|---|---|---|
| Berlin, 20 sources/targets | 13.04 (13.02-13.10) | 13.00 (12.97-13.04), 0.997 | 13.03 (13.01-13.06), 0.999 |
| Berlin, 50 sources/targets | 46.74 (46.35-46.98) | 47.23 (46.79-47.97), 1.011 | 46.25 (45.80-46.43), 0.990 |
| Mannheim-Usedom, 20 sources/targets | 30.54 (30.49-30.62) | 30.40 (30.26-30.50), 0.995 | 30.43 (29.91-30.81), 0.996 |
All three builds are within 1.1% on every row, inside each row's own spread. The original found the same: "all in all it hardly matters".

**Why:** the map is a small part of a matrix request. `ReachedMap::add`, where the map is inlined, is 3.6% of the service's time, and out-of-line map code is 0.36%. The rest is the graph search itself: expansion, connection checks, A* heuristic, tile reads and edge costs.

**Setup:**
- Valhalla master, built in a rootless podman container on Germany's tiles.
- A long-running service with one worker, pinned to two cores.
- Four rounds, rotated order. `scripts/ab/valhalla/` has every step.
- The Mannheim-Usedom file uses points that route to Kassel. With plain random points, 14 of its 20 requests failed with "unconnected regions", because the box reaches outside Germany.

Closes #318

author: cdagesse
body:
Follows #69. Turns on what we sized: every published model gets a market report and a Visor refresh about every two weeks.

## Changes
- **Rotation covers the whole catalog.** The nightly's Visor rotation now cycles through every published model with a Visor alias (400 today), stalest first, instead of only the 156 with a report. `perNight` becomes 29 (400 ÷ 14).
- **Reports go live after the first pull.** A model without a report is marked `ready` as soon as its first successful pull finds data; the snapshot pass in the same run builds it. First pulls in the rotation take a year of sales, capped at 20 pages (2,000 rows) per query.
- **Chunked inserts.** A first pull of a mainstream model (E-Class: 5,000 sold + 5,000 inventory rows) failed in the manual run this morning because the nightly inserted each set in one statement, past Postgres's 65,535-parameter limit. The three inserts now run in chunks of 200 like the backfill.
- Health headline counts "N new reports"; env docs size `VISOR_MONTHLY_BUDGET` (whole catalog every 14 days needs about 5,000 a month plus first pulls).

## Budget
At the current `VISOR_MONTHLY_BUDGET` of 10,000 the nightly allowance is 258 calls, so first pulls run at about 20 models a night and the 342 unpulled models are covered in about 16 nights; 15,000 makes that about 12 nights. Old Cars Data is unaffected.

## Verified
typecheck, lint, 289 tests, build. The manual nightly run on production today (after #69) pulled 12 models with 136 calls, re-cleaned 86, rebuilt 362 snapshots and finished in 96 s.

author: avicennasis
body:
A token on a streamed trunk takes up to two minutes, and there was no way to stop a run early and keep any of it. SIGINT took its default action at whatever instruction the process was on: the forward in flight was lost, --save-state never ran, the --out JSON was never written, and the cache and trunk reports never printed. git grep for sigaction, signal( or SIGINT over src and include finds only pthread_cond_signal. So the only way to keep the first 40 tokens of a run was to wait for the other 160.

The first Ctrl-C now sets a flag (src/cli/k3_cancel.h, 60 lines) that the decode loop reads once per step, at the top. The step in flight completes, so its KV rows and recurrent state are exact, no further step starts, and then everything a finished run writes is written: the state file, the --out JSON, the decoded text, the peak RSS line, the cache and trunk reports. The exit code is 5: distinct from 0, so a harness cannot take a partial token list for a complete one, and distinct from the 130 a shell reports for a process SIGINT actually killed, which is the case this exists to be told apart from. The --out JSON gains "interrupted":true|false next to stopped_at.

A second Ctrl-C kills. The handler re-arms SIG_DFL before returning, so a user who does not want to wait out the step in flight is not trapped by the first one, and it says so on stderr through write(2), which is async-signal-safe where printf is not, because the next safe point can be two minutes away and silence for that long invites the second press. signal() rather than sigaction() because MinGW has the first and not the second, and the CRT maps a console Ctrl-C onto SIGINT through it, so one spelling covers all three platforms.

The handler is armed only when the decode loop is about to start. Ctrl-C during the minutes of weight loading still kills at once; there is nothing to save yet. --chat is untouched: its REPL has its own loop and turn structure, and a per-turn cancel there is a separate change that can reuse the same header.

tests/unit/test_cancel.c checks the contract without a checkpoint: the first SIGINT is survived and observed, the flag is sticky and cleared by re-arming, a signal arriving mid-step lets that step finish and keeps the next from starting (exactly four of a hundred steps complete), and a forked child that raises twice dies of SIGINT (skipped on Windows, no fork). Wired into make test, CMake and ctest (interrupt). Diff: 22 lines in k3_run.c, the header, the test, 13 lines of build wiring.

Verified locally, since CI does not run on fork PRs here. gcc 13 and clang 18 on Ubuntu 24.04, portable baseline: make test green, test_ops 22 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, CANCEL TESTS PASSED, SCALE TEST PASSED, ENGINE MATCHES THE REFERENCE EXACTLY, ALL WEIGHTLESS TESTS PASSED. The -Werror portable build clean. ASan/UBSan clean on the CI list plus test_cancel, 0 runtime errors. CMake + ctest 16/16. ruff and shellcheck clean. mingw-w64 cross build under wine: test_cancel passes with the fork case skipped. On a generated tiny checkpoint (tools/make_tiny_checkpoint.py): kill -INT four seconds into --gen 4000 --incremental --save-state exits 5 after 226 tokens with "interrupted":true and stopped_at -1, writes the state (229 positions) and the JSON; those 226 ids are the prefix of an uninterrupted --gen 231 run; --load-state from that file with two new ids produces the same 12 ids as one straight incremental run over the 232-id concatenation. Ctrl-C before the loop arms (during load) exits 130 as before. Two Ctrl-Cs sent back to back from a shell coalesced into one (standard signals do not queue) and the run still exited 5 cleanly; the second-press kill is proven by the fork case in test_cancel, where the two raises are sequential.

author: rileyr
body:
A main-branch run (36445233964, after #1208) failed `face (browser, 1/2)` on `tests/startup.spec.mjs:138`: after `stop(service.child)` the launcher's build directory `hale-dna-head.7mu2LChd` was still in the case's TMPDIR.

## What happened

The failing run's launcher log (in the failure artifact's trace) ends with the head's own line:

`[+102.1s] lotus: the drain begun by signal 15 did not finish within 5000 ms (a run() that never reads self.draining?); ending as the signal's default action would`

So the head got SIGTERM and its drain used the whole 5000 ms grace. `start.sh` removes its build directory only after the head is gone, and the spec's `stop()` SIGKILLed the launcher 5000 ms after its own SIGTERM, the same length as the runtime's grace, so the launcher never reached its EXIT cleanup. The two windows are equal and the cleanup runs after the drain, so any drain that uses its whole grace loses that race.

Why the head's drain used the grace is **not known**. It does not reproduce locally: 16 runs of the spec case with the page open stop in 30-141 ms on 16 CPUs, and about 105-136 ms pinned to 1 or 2 CPUs. #1208 applies to the head (`HeadMain` is built in `serve`, with `srv` on pool `io`, `senses` on pool `senses` and `watch` pinned), but it changed only where the pool join sits, not what it waits on. This PR does not fix the hang; it makes it findable and stops it from being hidden.

## Changes

1. **Runtime.** When the drain grace expires the watcher's one line now also says what the drain was still waiting on: each started cooperative pool with its mode, whether its worker is mid-iteration and in which locus, and its queued cells; then the live loci that read `draining`, by name. No behavior change; the process ends the same way at the same time. Example, from a program with a stuck pool worker and a pinned locus inside a subprocess:

   `... did not finish within 500 ms (...); still waiting on: pool `io` (blocking): a worker is mid-iteration, 0 queued in locus `Stuck`; live loci that read draining: `Napper` x1, `Root` x1; ending as the signal's default action would ...`

   To carry names, pool workers record the locus label around each handler, arenas made through the labeled constructors keep the label codegen already passes, and `lotus_drain_observer_add` takes the locus name (codegen passes it). Test: `drain_grace_names_the_wait` (a run() blocking a pool worker past the grace; a pinned locus past it; a drain that finishes prints nothing).
2. **Fixture.** `stop()` now allows 20 s (the runtime's grace is 5 s, not the ~15 s I first assumed), and each launch's log is checked at teardown for `did not finish within`: a head that needs its grace fails the case with the line above instead of passing on a lucky window. I forced the line with `LOTUS_DRAIN_GRACE_MS=0` to see it go red, and it does.

## Verification

- `hale-codegen`: 1610 passed (nextest); `hale_native_suite` and `check_cli`: 75 passed; `hale fmt --check .` clean.
- `startup.spec.mjs` (all 3 cases) passes locally against a `hale` built from this branch.
- The `ulimit -v 8000000` I was asked to use makes Chromium fail to launch (V8's address-space reservation), so node ran with a `timeout` only; the head and API stay bounded by the harness's own `prlimit --as`.
- Not benched: the pool workers gain a label store around each handler (three loads and two stores).

## Architecture

- Part: the head's stop and the drain grace (the runtime's signal drain; the face launcher's teardown).
- Invariants kept: the grace, the exit path and the signal the process dies by are unchanged; nothing but the one line reads the new labels; a hung drain is now a red case.
- Deferred: why the head's drain used its grace in that run (the head's watcher loop checks `draining` only between iterations that run a git subprocess and an HTTP call, so a stop can wait one full iteration; bounding those calls is the head's own fix, later, once the line names what was waited on).

author: docktermj
body:
Closes #199

## What and why

Module 2's Step 8 quoted the Homebrew cask's shipped `SUPPORTPATH=${INSTALLPATH}/senzing/er/data` as fact. It also said `sdk_guide(topic='install', platform='macos_arm')` carries that gotcha "verbatim", and told the guide to "relay either" tool. On MCP server 1.37.14 (2026-09-28), `sdk_guide` says "Do not pin the literal: it has already drifted once": 4.4.x shipped `er/data`, and 4.5.0.26245 ships a Linux path. `explain_error_code('7426')` still quotes the 4.4.x literal. A Bootcamper on cask 4.5.0 who looked for `er/data` would find a different string and wrongly conclude the diagnosis does not apply.

## Changes (`plugins/senzing-bootcamp/skills/module-02-sdk-setup/SKILL.md`)

- **Historical macOS note:** the `er/data` literal is now scoped to "on cask 4.4.x and earlier". Its 4.4.0.26206 / 4.3.3.26191 / 1.32.3 provenance is unchanged.
- **The "both tools agree" note:** re-stamped to 1.37.14, 2026-09-28. It now says the tools agree on the diagnosis and the fix but not on the literal. It marks `explain_error_code`'s macOS literal as 4.4.x-only, names `sdk_guide` as the tool to relay for the platform detail, and drops "verbatim" and "So relay either one". The ⛔ line cites INV-169.
- **The `language='python'` note:** re-stamped to 1.37.14, because that call was re-run.
- **macOS verification step 2:** it now says the shipped ini's `SUPPORTPATH` "does not resolve to a directory holding `*TransRules.sz`, whatever its literal", and tells the guide to test the directory's content, never the string. It adds that on cask 4.5.0 the shipped ini's `CONFIGPATH` and `RESOURCEPATH` are Linux paths too, and it quotes no literal.
- **Unchanged:** the fix, the `test -d` / `*TransRules.sz` checks, "do not use the shipped `.ini` as-is", and the Windows/Scoop and Linux text.

## Approach

Implemented directly (implement-github-issue Phase 5a): one skill file plus its test.

body:
Phase 2B of #69.

## Why
The first real fresh-ChatGPT test of .46 found a host-compatibility defect:
- ChatGPT successfully opened user-supplied /modular and resolved live Production .46.
- Manifest/module architecture, DAG, integrity and activation behavior were sound.
- ChatGPT's normal public-web retrieval path rejected synthesized deep /snapshot/<SHA>/... reads.
- Continuing through a GitHub connector would not be a valid fresh-user transport assumption.

## .47 fix
Keep the exact-SHA snapshot transport, but make /modular itself the navigation surface:
- HTML resource index generated from exact-C LATEST + MANIFEST.
- Clickable exact-SHA links for Stage-1, LATEST, MANIFEST, MIGRATIONS, manifest schema, current versioned release, BOOTSTRAP_FULL and every manifest module (required + optional).
- FIRST_PARTY_RESOURCE_INDEX added.
- Transport version 3.3-chatgpt-linked-optin.
- /modular changes from noindex,nofollow to noindex,follow so user-initiated ChatGPT can follow page-provided links without making the route discoverable.
- /modular/config.txt remains a plain-text compatibility alias exposing the same exact-C resource links.
- ChatGPT is instructed not to synthesize/substitute snapshot URLs or search/GitHub connector results.

## Explicitly unchanged
- /, /install and /config.txt remain the supported one-response BOOTSTRAP_FULL installer.
- /modular remains absent from About/sitemap/default install instructions.
- Engine API 1.0 / workspace schema 2.3 / LOCAL STATE unchanged.
- All 22 MANIFEST module records/digests are identical to .46.
- Stage-1 3,472 B; mandatory modules 109,264 B; BOOTSTRAP_FULL 62,811 B.
- No gameplay/provider/account/persistence/domain module changes.

## Validation strategy
CI runs deterministic source gates first, preserves exact artifacts, then runs the external live-edge validator last.
Expected first result before deployment:
- source/runtime/recovery gates PASS;
- final live-edge gate FAIL because production Worker is still .46.

After exact-head source gates are clean:
1. deploy the exact .47 Worker candidate to existing lwai-bootstrap while GitHub main remains .46;
2. rerun CI/live validator;
3. run another fresh ChatGPT /modular test without assuming a GitHub connector;
4. only if the linked-resource bootstrap succeeds do we consider any later default-cutover release.

Production .46 remains last-known-good. This PR does NOT change the default installer.

author: kigawa01
body:
## 概要
issue #118「インフラ構成ページが重い」の主因である **Proxmox 連携クライアントの接続失敗・長時間待機** を解消します。

## 原因
本番ログで `/api/infrastructure` が **30〜60 秒**かかっているのを確認（`fetchInfrastructureHosts took 30028ms` / `fetchInfrastructureDetails took 60682ms`）。

内訳は Ktor **CIO** クライアントが pveproxy 相手に断続的に
- `java.io.EOFException: Not enough data available`
- `Connection reset` / `server prematurely closed the connection`
- 20 秒の request タイムアウト到達

を繰り返しているためです（両レプリカで同時多発を確認）。

一方、**同一クラスタ内からの curl / wget / 生JVM HttpsURLConnection は常に成功**（busybox から 10/10・60〜320ms、curl は HTTP/1.0/1.1/2・8 並列すべて成功）。つまりネットワーク・Proxmox 側ではなく、CIO クライアント実装とこの pveproxy（自己署名TLS）の相性問題です（当ファイルの過去コメントでも「wget/生JVMでは再現しない」と記録済み）。

## 変更
- Proxmox 専用クライアントのエンジンを **CIO → OkHttp** に変更
  - 自己署名証明書の扱いは従来どおり専用クライアント内で trust-all（OkHttp config の `sslSocketFactory` / `hostnameVerifier`）
  - タイムアウト境界は従来と同じ（接続 10 秒・読み書き 20 秒・リトライは `withTimeoutRetry` の 5 秒間隔 1 回に一本化）
- Kubernetes API・Keycloak・Prometheus 等他クライアントは CIO のまま（問題が観測されていないため対象外）

## 検証
- `gradle :server:compileKotlin :server:test` 成功
- ローカルからの実 Proxmox 通信では OkHttp は 10/10 成功（並列 8 本でも 4〜8ms）
- 本番デプロイ後のログ（`fetchInfrastructureHosts took ...`）で所要時間の低下を確認予定

## 補足
- 本番で Proxmox 自体は認証付き `/nodes` を 60ms で返しており、応答性に問題なし
- CI（main push）で自動ビルド・Harbor への push・image-tag PR が流れます

author: dalnogirl
body:
Closes #138. Nothing a player sees changes. The wire format, the 400s and the cursor encoding are the same as before.

## Where this diverged from the issue

- **The body schemas went to `protocol/`, not `http/`.** They describe what the browser may send, as `ClientMessageSchema` already does. `PostSeekRequestDto` and `UpdateProfileRequestDto` used to be hand-written copies of the server's schemas, with nothing keeping them in step. Now they are `z.input` of the schemas. It's `z.input` and not `z.infer` because the browser builds the pre-parse shape: the first `.default()` on a body field would make it required on the web side otherwise.
- **Only the query schema lives in `http/`.** The cursor encoding stays server-side, and so do the limit cap and `z.coerce`.
- **`listPlayerGames` returns `next?: ArchivedGameCursor`, not a boolean.** The route needs the last row's `finishedAt` and `id` to encode `nextCursor`, and the summary DTO carries neither.
- **New `ArchivedGamesRequestDto`**, so every inbound REST shape is a `RequestDto`. `fetchPlayerGames` takes one instead of a bare `before` string.
- **Naming conventions in CLAUDE.md.** WS keeps `ClientX`/`ServerX`. Every inbound REST body or query string is `XRequestDto`, and outbound REST stays plain `XDto`. The old "REST bodies are plain types" line was also wrong about the `usecases/` signatures, so that bullet is rewritten.

## Worth a look in review

- `ArchivedGamesQuerySchema`'s shape `satisfies Record<keyof ArchivedGamesRequestDto, z.ZodTypeAny>`. A field added to the DTO and not parsed fails to compile, and so does one parsed but not declared. I checked the first case by adding a field.
- `postSeek` takes `PostSeekRequestDto`, the input type, while the route passes zod's output. They're identical today. The day they aren't, the route stops compiling, and that's where the decision belongs.

## Not in here

- Renaming outbound REST types to `…ResponseDto`.
- Renaming WS messages.
- Moving the DTO mappers out of `usecases/`.

body:
## Summary

A sole administrator who loses their password and sessions previously had no recovery channel. Add a protected, manual-main Actions workflow that rotates the original administrator's credentials without changing their identity or reopening setup. Normal deployments cannot initiate recovery.

## Changes

- Add migration 0013 with an immutable recovery-use ledger, a nullable credential recovery digest and atomic recovery guards.
- Gate the manual workflow on the exact repository/workflow/main source, current main, owner-reviewed GitHub Environment, main-only environment branch policy and existing D1 ownership/migration ledger.
- Read a short-lived recovery bundle only from an Actions Environment Secret, derive the existing fixed scrypt profile and send only password/token hashes in parameterized SQL.
- Add sanitized status/readback, explicit replay handling, no automatic mutation retry, a private-file bundle preparation tool and an owner runbook.

## Testing

- `npm ci`: passed; npm audit reported 0 vulnerabilities.
- Targeted workerd/D1 isolation: 4 tests passed for original identity, new login, old password and session rejection, closed setup, concurrent/expired requests and rollback of credential/audit/session changes on failure.
- Actions driver/tooling: 6 tests passed for the fixed scrypt profile, closed/expiring bundles, main/manual guards, read-only status, replay, ambiguous network outcomes, environment policy and 0600 files outside the checkout.
- Full `npm run verify`: passed (924 Worker tests, 315 Node tests, format/lint/typecheck/build and local preview smoke).
- No reset of the live test-site administrator is performed or claimed.

## Security Review

Manual security review performed for the changed diff. No obvious security issue found. There is no new HTTP reset route, secondary administrator, Worker secret, raw dispatch credential, Repository Variable credential, artifact or secret logging. The update requires the original ID, expected credential version, unconsumed token digest and database-checked expiry. Existing session-revocation and credential-audit triggers run atomically; transient login counters reset only on successful owner recovery. GitHub token permissions are `contents: read` and `actions: read`; existing Cloudflare permissions/resources are reused.

## Risk / Rollback

Recovery intentionally revokes every old session. An unknown write outcome requires inspection and explicit owner action; no automatic retry occurs. The bundle tool uses a one-hour validity window; the validator caps it at 24 hours. Keep migration 0013 and its immutable ledger when reverting the workflow. The prior Worker remains compatible with the nullable column and triggers.

## Suggestions / Follow-up

The owner must privately provide `ADMIN_RECOVERY_BUNDLE` in the protected `administrator-recovery` Environment when recovery is actually needed. Keep the selected new password in a password manager and remove the consumed Secret/private files afterwards. This task exercises only synthetic isolated credentials and deliberately leaves the live administrator unchanged.

## Codex Work Log

- Inspected singleton authentication, password hashing, session/version triggers, audit schema, source guards and existing environment settings.
- Added atomic owner recovery, protected workflow, configuration validation and private-file tooling.
- Tested forgotten-password recovery and adversarial/replay/failure cases in isolated workerd/D1 and SQLite data.
- Created and read back the `administrator-recovery` environment: only owner `jacklilyhello` is required reviewer, and only branch `main` is allowed.
- PR head `f76fd0a0ec6ef89c727df30effef4bfad5c2e397`: [CI passed](https://github.com/jacklilyhello/cloudflare-wiki/actions/runs/36451529573), no unresolved review threads; squash merged as `b5777306dff3d7f7f4f61442673e343cc6f463b4`.
- [Main CI](https://github.com/jacklilyhello/cloudflare-wiki/actions/runs/36451943972) and [Deploy Test](https://github.com/jacklilyhello/cloudflare-wiki/actions/runs/36451944011) passed, including migration 0013, unchanged bootstrap, provider readback and Actions smoke.
- Independent `cf.emby.wiki` smoke and `/health` verified the exact merge SHA. No live administrator recovery was dispatched.

## Problema
No Google Shopping muitos iPhones novos aparecem como card genérico "Apple iPhone 15", sem capacidade no título. Na busca `iphone 15 128gb` esses cards caíam em `titulo_rejeitado` e nunca iam ao Product Offers, onde cada oferta costuma mostrar a capacidade.

## O que muda
- Busca **com capacidade** aceita como candidato (`candidato_generico`) o card sem capacidade no título, **desde que** bata com a busca sem a capacidade (`iphone 15`). Plus/Pro, usado/seminovo, vitrine, acessório e outra capacidade (256GB) continuam fora.
- **Segurança:** a oferta vinda desse card só é aceita se o título da oferta mostrar a capacidade buscada e for nova. O `offer_para_item` usa a consulta inteira, e o confirmer da página continua valendo.
- O genérico fica atrás do card com capacidade dentro da mesma classe. Não ganha a sondagem de vendedor único fora da allowlist e não entra no atalho de PDP do Shopping.
- Busca sem capacidade (`controle dualsense branco`, `iphone 15`) não muda.

## Testes
- Novo `tests/test_card_generico_capacidade.py` (14 testes). Cobre: quais títulos contam como genérico; motivo `candidato_generico`; ordem específico > genérico; genérico de vendedor único fora não ganha sondagem. Replay com 5 ofertas: só "Apple iPhone 15 (128 GB) - Preto" é aceita; 256 GB, usado, sem capacidade e 15 Plus são rejeitadas.
- `pytest`: **531 passed, 1 skipped**.

author: mbround18
body:
# Description

Integrates community PR #1564 by @NotAFlightRisk (Iain) with review follow-ups on top.

Their diagnosis was correct: the Gale profile-zip endpoint answers with a 302 to the mod CDN, but the pooled client is built with `redirect::Policy::none()`, so the raw 3xx reached `check_status` and was rejected as non-success — **`GALE_SYNC_CONFIGS=true` could never work.** Routing that one request through the existing manual redirect walker is the right fix, and it reuses the right abstraction rather than inventing one.

Their commit is preserved as-is (`9aac57a`); everything else is in a follow-up commit addressing three gaps found while reviewing it.

## Contributions

**From #1564 (@NotAFlightRisk):**

- Routed the Gale profile-zip request through `utils::thunderstore_http::send` so the 302 to the CDN is actually followed, and extracted the status check into a `check_status` helper so it can be applied after the redirect walk.

**Review follow-ups:**

- **Paced the request.** `send` only routes through the shared pool when `should_pace` matches a mod repository host. Gale is not one, so the request was sent direct and unretried — silently giving up the exponential backoff, `Retry-After` handling and host-wide 429 gate that the previous `send_with_backoff` call had. Added an explicit `Pacing` opt-in rather than changing `send`'s signature at its several `valheim_mod.rs` call sites.
- **Refused a redirect that drops TLS.** The walker allowed `https -> http` and merely withheld the `Referer`. Since whatever the plaintext hop returns is what gets unpacked over the server's live BepInEx configs, losing an encrypted hop is now an error. A base URL override that was already plaintext (an `http` local mirror) is unaffected — only *losing* TLS is refused.
- **Made the rate-limit gate per host.** Pacing Gale through the shared pool exposed that `HttpPool.gate` was a single pool-wide instant, so a 429 from any one host paused every request in flight. Tolerable while only mod repositories used the pool; not once a third-party API joined it. The gate is now a map keyed by host, entries dropped as they elapse. The struct's own docs already claimed it answered "for the whole host" - the implementation now matches.
- **Bounded the archive.** The body was read with an uncapped `bytes()` and every entry written with no size budget, so a hostile or corrupt response could exhaust memory or inflate without limit. The download is now streamed against a compressed cap (64 MiB) and extraction against an uncompressed one (256 MiB), with extraction staged so hitting either cap leaves the live configs untouched. Real profiles are config text, orders of magnitude under both.

### Notes for review

- Config sync is applied atomically. Entries unpack into a staging directory beside `BepInEx/config` and only move across once the whole archive has been read and is within budget, so a refusal partway through leaves the live configs untouched rather than half applied.
- The rate-limit gate is now keyed by host, so pacing Gale through the shared pool does not let a Gale 429 stall mod downloads from a repository that is answering fine.
- Verified no credentials leak on the rerouted path: `with_repository_auth` gates on `owns_host`, which is hardcoded to `thunderstore.io` / `hexium.gg` and deliberately ignores base-URL overrides, so the Gale host receives no token. Cross-origin hops already strip `authorization`, `cookie` and friends.

### Tests added

- `pacing_always_retries_a_non_repo_host` — a non-repository host returning 503 is retried and then succeeds under `Pacing::Always`.
- `pacing_auto_leaves_a_non_repo_host_unretried` — the same host under `Pacing::Auto` is hit exactly once, which is what pinned down the regression.
- `downgrade_is_detected_only_when_tls_is_lost` — the full scheme matrix, including that an already-plaintext mirror keeps working.
- `a_gate_on_one_host_does_not_hold_another` - a pause on one host must not hold a request to another; this is the regression the per-host gate removes.
- `an_elapsed_gate_is_forgotten` - a spent gate entry is dropped rather than accumulating for the life of the process.
- `refuses_configs_that_expand_past_the_cap` — uses a small explicit budget so no real zip bomb is needed, and asserts the over-budget file is not left behind.

## Checklist

- [x] I added one or multiple labels which best describes this PR.
- [x] I have tested the changes locally.
- [x] This PR has a reviewer on it.
- [x] I have validated my changes by running the container on a Debian-family host (Debian, Ubuntu, Pop!_OS, Mint, ...). (Only needed for Odin or Docker Changes)

`cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` are clean, and **326 tests pass, 0 failing**, on Rust 1.98.1.

`utils::fetch_public_ip_address::tests::test_fetch_ip_from_api` passes here too; it only failed in the environment the change was authored in, where a proxy blocked the live IP API it calls. #1563 makes it hermetic regardless.

### End-to-end verification

Run against a real `GALE_SYNC_CODE` with `GALE_SYNC_CONFIGS=true`, pointed at a scratch `GAME_LOCATION`:

- **On this branch:** 71 mod entries resolved and **86 config files written** into `BepInEx/config`, including nested ones such as `shudnal.ConditionalConfigSync/*.cfg`. The redirect to the CDN is followed and the profile unpacks.
- **On `main`, same code, same profile:** 71 mod entries resolved, but `BepInEx/config` **is never created** - zero files. Config sync fails on the raw 302 and, being non-fatal, warns and carries on silently.

That is the reported bug reproduced and the fix confirmed on the one path no unit test can cover.

#### In the container

Repeated end to end in the real server image (`--target valheim`, Ubuntu 24.04.5), built and run on Pop!_OS 24.04 (`ID_LIKE="ubuntu debian"`), as `odin mod:install --from-var` against a mounted `GAME_LOCATION`:

- 71 plugins installed and **86 profile configs written**, alongside a sentinel config planted beforehand that came through byte for byte, confirming the staging change leaves untouched files alone.
- `HTTP pool: 235 request(s), 0 retry/retries, 0 rate limited, 0 failed`, no errors logged.
- No `.gale-config-sync-*` staging directory left behind.

#### The odin stage could not reach anything

Validating in the container turned up that the `odin` build target (`debian:13-slim` plus the two binaries) had **no CA certificate store at all**, so every HTTPS request from that image failed at TLS before reaching the network - it burned all five retry attempts on what looked like a network fault. The valheim image was never affected, since it copies the binaries into a `steamcmd/steamcmd:ubuntu` base carrying its own bundle, but the odin stage declares its own entrypoint and CMD, so it is meant to be runnable and as shipped could not reach a single mod repository.

`ca-certificates` is now installed in that stage. Rerunning the sync that previously failed, from the odin image alone: 71 plugins installed, 86 profile configs written, 235 requests with 0 failures, sentinel config intact. The valheim image still builds on top of the stage unchanged.

A pre-existing config file placed in `BepInEx/config` beforehand survived the sync byte for byte, confirming the staging change does not disturb files the profile does not carry.

body:
Fixes: #390

> **Stacked on #378.** It targets #378's branch so the diff shows only this change; retarget to `main` once #378 merges. **Breaking**, meant for the next major release.

## PR Type

- Bugfix
- Feature (breaking)

## What is the current behavior?

Resizetizer tells a Skia head apart partly by `$(UnoRuntimeIdentifier)` (`'Skia'` → generic Skia app kind, `'WebAssembly'` → wasm). Uno Platform 7.0 (unoplatform/uno#24186) stops setting that property on heads and identifies them with `UnoHasRuntimeHost=true` instead. A 7.0 head whose target framework is a plain `netX.0` therefore matches no app kind and gets no icons or splash screen. Uno.Sdk keeps setting `UnoRuntimeIdentifier=Skia` on desktop heads only to keep Resizetizer working.

## What is the new behavior?

`UnoRuntimeIdentifier` is no longer read. Heads are classified from their target framework:

| head | app kind |
|---|---|
| `-android` (app), `-ios`/`-maccatalyst` (exe), `-browserwasm`, WinAppSDK `-windows` | their own, as before |
| `-desktop` | generic Skia |
| any other exe/winexe with `UnoHasRuntimeHost=true` (tvOS, a plain `netX.0` head) | generic Skia |
| libraries, and anything without a runtime host | none |

The generic kind still comes after #378's subtraction of the platform kinds, so android, ios and browserwasm heads, which also carry `UnoHasRuntimeHost` in 7.0, keep their own kind. The `OutputType` check keeps libraries out, since some runtime packages pass the flag on to referencing projects.

### Breaking change

Shared-project heads (Uno Platform 5.x and earlier: `.Wasm`, `.Skia.Gtk`, `.Skia.WPF`, `.Skia.Linux.FrameBuffer` on a plain `netX.0`/`netX.0-windows`) were recognised only by `UnoRuntimeIdentifier` and now fall back to `netstandard`, so they get no icons or splash screen. tvOS and other Skia heads with no packaging branch need `UnoHasRuntimeHost`, which the Uno 7 runtime packages set. Such projects should stay on the previous major.

Once Uno.Sdk pins this release, `Uno.Common.Desktop.targets` can drop its `UnoRuntimeIdentifier=Skia` shim.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Tested code with current [supported SDKs](../README.md#supported)
- [ ] Docs have been added/updated which fit [documentation template](https://github.com/nventive/Uno/blob/master/doc/.feature-template.md). (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] [Unit Tests and/or UI Tests](doc/articles/working-with-the-samples-apps.md) for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features) (if applicable)
- [ ] [Wasm UI Tests](doc/articles/working-with-the-samples-apps.md#running-the-webassembly-ui-tests-snapshots) are not showing unexpected any differences. Validate PR `Screenshots Compare Test Run` results.
- [ ] Contains **NO** breaking changes
- [ ] Updated the [Release Notes](https://github.com/nventive/Uno/tree/master/doc/ReleaseNotes)
- [x] Associated with an issue (GitHub or internal)

## Other information

**Validation.** `AppKindClassification.proj` now has 22 cases.
- It adds six `UnoHasRuntimeHost` cases (android, ios, browserwasm, desktop, a plain `net9.0` exe and a plain `net9.0` library).
- It moves tvOS/macOS onto `UnoHasRuntimeHost`.
- Its shared-project cases now expect no app kind.
- The `*-skia-renderer` cases still set `UnoRuntimeIdentifier` and must classify exactly like their plain counterparts.

```
dotnet msbuild src/Resizetizer/test/MSBuild/AppKindClassification.proj -t:Validate
```

- With this PR: all 22 cases pass.
- With #378's targets alone, it fails on exactly the changed rows: `plain-netx-runtime-host` (not recognised), and `sharedproject-wasm` / `sharedproject-skia-gtk` (still recognised).

It is evaluation-only. No app was built or launched.

author: roznet
body:
## What & why

Adds a **Historical** tab next to Forecast Overview on the maps page. You pick a past date, a 30-min time slot, a model lead (Latest, D-1..D-6), a source (METAR / TAF / Worst / Majority / GFS / ICON / ECMWF) and a metric. Every watchlist airport is then shown as its METAR, its TAF read at that instant, or a model forecast. The colours come from the same metric catalog as the forecast tab.

All selection logic lives on the server so a future iOS tab only has to render.

**Backend**
- `tasks/historical_map.py` (new) handles selection and the payload:
  - **METAR:** latest report at or before T, including SPECI, no older than 90 min.
  - **TAF:** the raw TAF from the latest observation row within 6 h, **re-read at T**.
  - **Models:** latest run **fetched** at or before `T - lead days`, within 24 h of that cutoff. The valid time is the latest sample hour at or before T on the same day, at most 3 h old. When a source has nothing, the response carries a reason code (`beyond_horizon` / `no_valid_time` / `no_run`) instead of an empty block.
  - **Endpoints:** `GET /maps/historical?at&lead` and `GET /maps/historical/range`. The range endpoint reports the earliest METAR date and the earliest model date separately, plus the leads each model supports.
- `map_queries.assemble_map_airports`: per-airport assembly (runway winds, alternate-required, baked consensus) pulled out of `get_forecast_map_data`, whose behaviour is unchanged. METAR/TAF go under `observed` and **never feed the consensus**.
- `analysis/taf_reading.read_taf_at`: the TAF reading from `route_weather._apply_taf_at_eta`, extracted so the route briefing and the historical map read a TAF identically. The briefing's behaviour is unchanged.
- `archive.read_archived_rows`:
  - Snapshots older than the 10-day MySQL window are read from the daily Parquet archive, with a fallback to MySQL for days that were never archived.
  - Observations are read from the monthly archive only if raw-row pruning is ever enabled.
- **Caching:** once an instant is final (T is more than 2 h old), its payload goes into an in-process LRU of 32 entries and is sent with `Cache-Control: immutable`. I deliberately did not use `verification_cache`, because every slot of every past day is a possible key and that table would grow with browsing.

**Web**
- `visualization/historical-tab.ts` reuses `WeatherMap`.
  - Changing the source or metric just recolours the map; only date/time/lead trigger a fetch.
  - Unavailable sources stay clickable and explain why they have no data.
  - Clicking a marker opens a side panel comparing all five sources, with the raw METAR/TAF.
  - Deep-linked via `hist.*` URL keys.

**Known limits** (listed as follow-ups in the issue):
- Model data exists only for 06/09/12/15/18Z, so there is nothing from 19Z to 05Z.
- Model history starts about 10 days before the archive was enabled.
- Web only for now.

## Issue linkage

Closes #629

## Testing / verification

- `pytest tests`: 6074 passed, 22 skipped. The new `tests/test_historical_map.py` has 26 tests covering:
  - METAR/SPECI selection and staleness;
  - TAF TEMPO reading and expired TAFs;
  - runs fetched after T never being used;
  - lead selection and horizon limits;
  - night-time gaps;
  - consensus excluding observations;
  - an archive round-trip (a day served from Parquet matches the same day served from MySQL);
  - the endpoints.
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean and `vitest`: 870 passed.
- `ruff`: no new findings on the touched files; the existing ones are unchanged.
- Manual check in Chromium via Playwright against a local server with seeded synthetic data (28 airports, one live day plus one day served only from the Parquet archive):
  - map rendering and the lead/source switches;
  - the side panel;
  - the night-time reason text;
  - the URL round-trip;
  - no console errors.
- Not yet run against production-size data.

body:
Closes #98

## What
With afterglow active, printing (especially from the resume's Print button) used the dark tokens on white paper. Ink, `orange-deep` (#ffb073) and `ink-muted` all came out as pale text.

- **`scripts/build-dizzy-tokens.mjs`** now emits an `@media print` block that re-declares the daylight `color-scheme`, colour and shadow tokens on `:root:not([data-theme="daylight"])`.
  - That selector covers an explicit `data-theme="afterglow"` and the no-JS OS-dark fallback, and outranks both by specificity and source order.
  - The OS-dark fallback and the print override are built by one `override(media, theme)` helper, so the two can't drift apart.
  - **`src/dizzy/tokens.css` is regenerated** with `npm run dizzy:tokens`, not hand-edited.
- **`src/styles/site.css`** print block: fenced code switches back to `--shiki-light` (afterglow otherwise keeps the dark pair), and `.dz-tag` gets `print-color-adjust: exact`, so tag tints survive when background graphics are off.
- **`src/dizzy/tokens.test.ts`** asserts that every themed token in `tokens.json` appears in the print block with its daylight value.

## Decisions
- The issue suggested `[data-theme="afterglow"]` as the selector. `:not([data-theme="daylight"])` is deliberately wider, so a no-JS visitor on an OS-dark machine also prints in daylight.
- `--retro-line` and `--retro-vignette` are not reset for print. Their only consumer is `body::after`, which print already hides.

## Verification
- `npm run test`: 37/37 pass. That includes the drift test and the full print-token assertion; a mutation that prints in afterglow fails it.
- `npm run dizzy:tokens`: the regenerated files match the committed ones byte for byte.
- `npm run build` on node 22: 37 pages. The built CSS contains the daylight `@media print` token block.
- Implementation-time check: Playwright on `/resume/` with print media emulated. Afterglow (stored) and OS-dark with JS off compute the same colours as daylight: body/h1 `rgb(20,48,46)`, orange-deep `rgb(156,61,0)`, ink-muted `rgb(63,95,92)`, tag tint `rgb(201,242,246)`. The screen theme is unchanged.

author: peters
body:
Fixes a race in Hetzner server creation. Another session's paid Hetzner smoke hit it today.

## What happened

A cloud's first **Start cloud** on Hetzner failed after about 44 s with "The operation's server does not hold exactly its workspace volume". By then the server was running with the volume attached, and **Reconnect cloud** reached Ready in 5 s.

`ensure_server` waits for the create action and its follow-up actions, including the volume attach, then checked `placed()` against the server object from the create response. That snapshot is taken before the attach it starts, so its `volumes` can still be empty.

## Fix

When a volume was requested and the create response doesn't show it yet, the server is read again after its actions finish and verified as the operation's server before `placed()` checks it. Requests without a volume, and every reconcile path (which already read the server live), are unchanged.

## Tests

- New `a_volume_attached_after_the_create_response_is_read_once_its_actions_finish`: the create response shows no volume, the attach action finishes, and the re-read server holds it. Without the fix it fails with exactly the error above.
- `cargo test -p horizon-cloud` passes (342 tests), along with fmt, maintainability and the blocking and strict clippy tiers for the crate.

The shared per-zone private network outliving a cloud's deletion, also noticed in that smoke, is by design: networks are free and reused by every cloud in the zone, so this PR doesn't change it.

author: lapeninns
body:
## Summary

- `ops/local-ci/roots/run-roots.sh` used to run every container root one after another in a single container, on a git worktree plus a bind mount of the repository `.git`. `--jobs 1` (the default) keeps that single serial container. `--jobs N` gives each container root (`fast`, `coverage`, `quality`, `build`, `visual`), each of the 8 a11y shards and each of the 16 e2e packs its own capped `docker run --rm`, split the same way as `ci.yml`. Caps: 4 CPU/8 GiB for fast, coverage and build; 2 CPU/6 GiB for quality; 2 CPU/8 GiB for browser work. The longest work starts first, measured by hosted median pack times, or local root times for fast and quality. At most N containers run at once, and each is admitted against the memory Docker has left after other containers, less 2 GiB.
- Clones: `git clone --local --no-hardlinks` into `~/.cache/nabaperks-local-ci/`. The trees are `tree-serial`, `tree-slot-1..N` and `tree-host`, and each is fetched, checked out and cleaned before reuse. So a `--jobs N` run holds at most N+1 clones, about 0.75 GiB each with checkout (measured 2026-09-28), not one clone per task. Containers mount only the cache directory and named volumes, never the repository or its `.git`.
- Containers are labelled per run. An interrupted run removes only its own containers and signals only its still-running slot subshells, never PIDs it has already reaped. The run ends with a per-root wall-time summary and exits non-zero when any root failed. Host roots (lighthouse, zap, db) now report their failures instead of aborting the script.
- `--dry-run` prints the plan. A unit test checks the plan against the `ci.yml` e2e and a11y matrices, and also checks the ordering, the caps, the mount sources and the per-slot clone.
- Research: nektos/act (72,137 stars, MIT, checked 2026-09-28) schedules jobs through a fixed pool of N workers (`pkg/common/executor.go` NewParallelExecutor). I adapted that pool shape in bash 3.2 with no new dependencies. act itself was not adopted because it runs the candidate's workflow YAML.

## Verification

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` (as part of `pnpm quality:check`, exit 0)
- [ ] `pnpm build`: not run. The change covers only operator shell scripts, docs and a unit test, and nothing in the app build or runtime.
- `pnpm quality:check`: exit 0. 810 contract tests and 2404 unit tests passed; lint, types, dead code, duplication, debt, docs:check and agents:check all passed.
- `node scripts/ci/node-test-runner.mjs --test tests/unit/local-ci-run-roots.test.mjs`: 3/3 passed.
- Prettier check on the changed Markdown and test files, `git diff --check` and `bash -n` passed. `shellcheck` reports only the SC1091 info notes that are already present on the base.
- Stubbed-docker run (`--jobs 2`, 3 tasks): it used 2 clones (`tree-slot-1`, `tree-slot-2`), summarised 3 roots and sent no kills on a normal exit. Interrupted after one slot had been reaped: it killed only the 2 live slot PIDs, not the reaped one.
- The mirror `config/ci-qualification-inputs/tests/contracts/devops-local-ci.test.mjs.source` is byte-identical to its source. `needsSelectionComparison` is false for all four changed paths.
- Not obtained: after the per-slot clone change, I did not repeat a real Docker run of the full root set. Hosted CI is still the merge authority, and local results are advisory.

## Design System

- [x] No UI change. `DESIGN.md`, `app/globals.css` and the shared components are untouched.
- [x] Copy stays plain British English with no emoji or exclamation marks.

### Summary

Contribution source: AI-assisted

Agent Share visitors can now use tools that declare `humanIntervention`. When the creator grants a tool, its approval flow comes with it. The **visitor** is the approver, and the run follows the visitor's own selected approval mode (manual / allow-list / auto-run). The creator is never asked to approve a visitor run.

- **Share gate** (`shareGate`, `aiAgent`): `required` / `always` APIs are no longer stripped from granted tools. The visitor's approval mode is passed into the share run config.
- **Share chat router** (`shareChat`):

- **Intervention notification** (`agentInterventionNotification`, `agentInterventionReview`): a share-visitor run carries `shareVisitorUserId` and is `review_only`, so owner-facing delivery can skip it.
- **Client**: share-chat service calls, gateway / conversation control / question submission for share runs, and a new `PendingInterventionBar`. `ApprovalActions` hides "remember / always allow" for visitors, because that would write into the creator's allow list.

body:
This is a minimal change just moving the parts that are monkey patched so scikit-build (classic) will work after the 1.0 release. Another option would be to move to sciit-build-core, but that changes a bit more (and I think builds on this pretty well).

:robot: _AI text below_ :robot:

Fixes #1250.

`setup.py` monkeypatched `skbuild.setuptools_wrap._classify_installed_files` and used `skbuild.cmaker.CMaker`. scikit-build 1.0 (now based on scikit-build-core) removes both. This PR removes that dependency and keeps the wheel layout the same:

- A CMake install step lays out the `cv2` package under `<prefix>/cv2`, with the same rules as the old regexes. OpenCV's `OPENCV_CMAKE_HOOKS_DIR` (`POST_FINALIZE` hook) adds it, so the `opencv` submodule is not changed. Required files still fail the build if missing.
- `cmake_process_manifest_hook` keeps only `cv2/**` from the install.
- The Python include dir and library now come from `sysconfig`.

This works with scikit-build 0.x and 1.0. I built headless wheels locally on macOS arm64 (Python 3.12) with scikit-build 0.19.1 before and after the change, and with 1.0.0rc1 after. The file lists and contents match, except for the compiled module and the generated `cv2/typing/__init__.py` (the import order changes from build to build). I did not test Windows (ffmpeg DLL, `python3XY.lib`) or the Linux Qt plugins and fonts locally.

author: nickruigrok
body:
## What

A deploy now uploads the release's Workers to the client's account and sends them all traffic, one Worker at a time. This is the step after its resources and migrations. It builds on #184, now on `main`.

- **One Worker at a time** (step `workers`):
  - Each Worker is uploaded, sent all traffic and recorded before the next is uploaded.
  - The order is a topological sort of the service bindings: a Worker goes live only after every Worker it binds (connect before core). A cycle is refused (`service_binding_cycle`).
  - A script upload is live the moment it lands, so core's never runs against the connect it replaced.
- **Upload** (`src/deploy/upload.ts`, `src/deploy/versions.ts`):
  - Each Worker is built from the release's manifest as imported: its compatibility date and flags, its modules and its static files. All of them are read from R2 and checked against the manifest again: modules by SHA-256, static files by their content key.
  - Each `d1` binding's id must be exactly its own placeholder (`$D1_<binding>_ID`, one helper shared with `scripts/release`), for a database the Worker lists. It's filled in with the account's database id. Any other `$` value is refused (`unknown_placeholder`).
  - Worker, Workflow and database names in the manifest must be names the Workers API takes, checked in the manifest schema.
- **Durable Object migrations.** A version can't carry Durable Object migrations, so a Worker's first upload, or one whose release adds migrations, goes as a script upload and deploys at once.
  - It carries the migrations after the tag the account's script is at, read as Wrangler reads it (`GET /workers/services/<name>`).
  - A tag the release doesn't have is refused (`unknown_migration_tag`), where Wrangler would replay them all.
  - Otherwise the Worker goes as a new version.
- **Secrets** (`src/deploy/secrets.ts`). Each Worker is uploaded with exactly its secrets, keeping none from before, so a version works after a rollback and rolls back with its secrets.
  - **Derived per client:** a client's own secrets are derived, never stored, as `HMAC(masterKey, "<purpose>:<clientId>:<generation>")`. One shared helper does this, `deriveClientSecret` in the new `@grasp-os/shared/client-secrets`, and the router secret uses it too, with an unchanged result:
    - `ROUTER_SECRET` under `ROUTER_KEY`, 64 hex characters, for core;
    - `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` under `CLIENT_KEY`, 64 hex characters, for core;
    - `CAPABILITY_SIGNING_KEY` under `CLIENT_KEY`, 64 hex characters, for core and connect;
    - `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` under `CLIENT_KEY`, 32 bytes in base64 as connect's vault takes it, for connect.
  - **Rotation** (`rotateClientSecrets`): raises the client's generation and records `clients.rotated_at`, audited as `client.rotate_secrets`.
    - The window starts when the new generation goes live, not when it's raised: `clients.rotation_live_at`. The router step (#186) sets it when it writes the map with the new generation; this PR on its own never sets it, and with it unset the previous keys are always given.
    - Until then, and for 7 days after, a deploy also gives the previous generation's keys where a Worker takes them. That's `ROUTER_SECRET_PREVIOUS` on core, and `CAPABILITY_SIGNING_KEY_PREVIOUS` and `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS` on connect, whose cron seals tokens again under the new key within that week. So a rotation deployed late still keeps them.
    - After the week, they're left off.
    - A new rotation is refused until the last one is live and its week has passed.
    - `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` has no previous value, so a rotation signs everyone out.
  - **Shared:** the caller passes only the secrets every client shares, by Worker (`DeploySecrets.shared`: the OAuth apps' secrets, the Composio key, from the secrets bridge).
    - No shared secret may take a derived name or a previous name (`reserved_secret_name`).
    - A required secret without a value stops the deploy (`missing_secret`) before that Worker is uploaded.
- **Core's vars:**
  - The client's settings become JSON vars, but only settings named by a deployment config var (`deploymentConfigVars` in `@grasp-os/shared/deployment-config`: `SIGN_IN`, `FEATURES`, `MODEL_GATEWAY`, `MEMORY_LIMITS`, `AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS`, `AUDIT_ARCHIVE_RETENTION_DAYS`). Any other is refused (`unknown_setting`).
  - `PLATFORM_CHANGE` names who started the deploy, `release`, the release, and when the deploy started. Core records it as `platform.updated` once per version.
  - A var or shared secret named like a binding or another secret is refused (`binding_name_taken`).
- **After each deploy:** cron triggers, workers.dev on or off as the release says (preview URLs off), and the Worker's Workflows. Each is a PUT or a set, so it can run again.
- **Stale deploys.**
  - Starting a deploy marks the client's older unfinished ones `superseded` in the same batch.
  - Running a deploy that isn't the client's latest is refused (`deploy_superseded`), so a stale one can't put an older release or older secrets back live.
  - Right before each thing that goes live (a script upload, a deployment to 100%, a `client_workers` write), the deploy checks that it's still the client's latest and not superseded, and stops with `deploy_superseded` otherwise. The single runner stays the precondition; this closes the window, not the race.
  - A deploy superseded while it runs also stops at its next recorded step. The updates of a step, of a failure and of done change only a row that isn't superseded; a step or done that changes no row throws `deploy_superseded`, and a superseded row stays superseded.
- **Records and audit.**
  - Each uploaded version is recorded on the deploy row with a fingerprint of everything that went into it (`client_deploys.versions`). The fingerprint covers the rendered secret names and values (the previous keys included, when given), the vars, the bindings as filled in, the code and static files, and the pins.
    - A resumed deploy deploys a recorded version only while its fingerprint is the same now; otherwise it uploads again.

Create `CLIENT_KEY` in the grasp-os-ops Secrets Store: a long random value such as `openssl rand -base64 48`. Every client's `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `CAPABILITY_SIGNING_KEY` and `TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` are derived from it, so it's as sensitive as all of them together. author: sam-aydlette
body:
SCN-Type: routine-recurring

## Changed

The operator's access to the Terraform state backend lived in a **hand-made** user-inline policy, `tfstate-bootstrap`. Nothing in the repo defines it. It granted `s3:*` on the whole state bucket and the lock table's *management* actions, but none of the lock-*item* actions (`GetItem`, `PutItem`, `DeleteItem`). That never mattered while the bootstrap stack kept local state. Once #376 moved that state to the backend, `terraform init -migrate-state` failed with `AccessDeniedException` on `dynamodb:PutItem`, and the migration had to run with `-lock=false`.

This adds `aws_iam_group_policy.operators_state_backend` to the `operators` group. That's where the other two former user-inline policies were already relocated ("the two former user-inline policies, relocated to the group"); this one was missed. It is also scoped down from the original:

| Statement | Grants | Was |
|---|---|---|
| `StateBucketManagement` | Bucket-level `ListBucket`, `GetBucket*`, `PutBucket*`, encryption and lifecycle get/put, on the state bucket only: what managing its versioning, encryption, public-access block, lifecycle, policy and tags needs | `s3:*` on the bucket and every object |
| `StateObjects` | `GetObject`/`PutObject` on exactly the two state keys (`infrastructure/…` for local plans, `bootstrap/…` for this stack) | (covered by `s3:*`) |
| `StateLock` | The lock-item actions, plus the lock table's existing management actions | Management actions only; **no lock-item actions** |

## Verified

- **Plan:** a read-only `terraform plan` against the migrated remote bootstrap state (`-lock=false`, because the operator lacks the lock until this applies) shows **1 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy**: the new group policy only. That also confirms the rest of the trust root matches its code after the #376 migration and apply. The remote state object was not modified.
- **`terraform fmt` and `validate`** pass.
- **This PR's own `compliance-check`** should report the trust root as `changes_pending` with exactly this address. That makes it the first live proof of #376's trust-root plan against the migrated state.

## Residual / needs human

After merge, from a checkout synced to `origin/main`:

```
cd infrastructure/bootstrap
terraform plan -lock=false
terraform apply -lock=false
aws iam delete-user-policy --user-name saydlette-dev --policy-name tfstate-bootstrap
terraform plan
```

- **The last `terraform plan` runs with locking on.** It must succeed and show no changes. That proves the group policy covers everything the hand-made policy did.
- **If it fails** on a denied S3 bucket action, recreate the user policy temporarily and tell me the action, so I can add it here rather than widening by hand.

## Couldn't verify

- That the scoped actions cover every refresh call for the state bucket. The final locked plan above is that check.

Schritt 6.3b1 (Spur B, Karte `phase-6.md`). 6.3b ist jetzt aufgeteilt:

Seit 6.3a steht die Lightning-Adresse nur noch auf Wunsch im Profil. Ohne sie brach der Zap im Chat bisher mit „Empfänger hat keine Lightning-Adresse“ ab. Jetzt fragt die App den Empfänger versiegelt nach einer Rechnung, und dessen App stellt sie mit der eigenen Wallet aus – ohne LNURL-Dienst und ohne Quittung auf einem Relay.

- **Protokoll `ln-rechnung.ts`:**
  - Anfrage (innen Kind 25022, `p`, `amount` in msat) und Antwort (innen 25023, `e`, `p`, `bolt11`) nur im Umschlag (NIP-59).
  - Beträge nur in ganzen sats, bis 0,1 BTC.
  - Der Zahler nimmt die Antwort nur vom Gefragten, zur eigenen Anfrage und nur mit einer gültig signierten Rechnung über genau den Betrag.
- **App `ln-rechnung-anfrage.ts`:**
  - `frageRechnungAn()` sendet an den Posteingang des Empfängers und wartet bis zu 75 s.
  - `beantworteRechnungsAnfrage()` antwortet nur Kontakten und nur auf frische Anfragen.
  - Gebremst: je Kontakt eine Anfrage je 30 s, insgesamt zehn je Minute.
  - Die Rechnung kommt nur aus der eigenen Wallet (NWC `make_invoice`, ohne Beschreibung, `eigeneRechnung()` in `shell/zahlschienen.ts`).

  - Mit öffentlicher Adresse: anonymer Zap wie seit 6.3a.
  - Sonst: die versiegelte Anfrage (nur ganze sats).
  - Gezahlt wird über die Schiene, die den Betrag prüft.
- **Posteingang:** `alsRechnungsAnfrage()` hängt am Ende der Kette in `oeffneUmschlag()`. Die vier Tests, die die Kette wörtlich prüfen, kennen das neue Glied.
- **Texte:**
  - Aussage „ln-rechnung“ (belegt, Regel `kein-bolt11`) mit Szenario.
  - Texte in der Offenlegung des Profils und in der FAQ: Die App muss offen sein, Fremde bekommen keine Rechnung.

author: git286
body:
Part of #1743, follow up of #1822 which made the interceptor honor `debug_redact`.

#1822 only covered the one log call in the unary interceptor. Any other slog call that logs a proto, an actor ref on an egress decision, a spec on a debug line, still went out as-is. This PR moves the redaction into `ContextHandler` in `internal/contextlogging`, the slog handler every server installs through `serverboot.InitLogger`, so every slog call in the process is covered.

How it works:

- `Handle` scans the record for `proto.Message` attributes, directly, inside groups, or behind a `LogValuer`. It copies the record only when something changes: a message with a populated `debug_redact` field, or a `LogValuer` (resolved once here, so it does not run again in the terminal handler). A record with neither passes through with zero allocations. `WithAttrs` does the same once for attributes bound with `With`.
- `protoredact` now exposes `NeedsRedaction` and `Redacted`. `NeedsRedaction` checks the type first (memoized per descriptor, false for most RPC messages) and then whether a labeled field is actually set. So an `ActorTemplate` with no env, or a `ListActorTemplatesResponse` full of them, is not cloned at all. `ForLog` and the exported walk are gone.
- The interceptor logs request and response bodies as they are and relies on the handler.

Performance, measured with the benchmark in `contextlogging_test.go` (JSON handler to discard, arm64):

- Line with no proto: about +55ns over the bare JSON handler, 0 allocs.
- Line with a clean proto (`ObjectRef`, `ListActorsResponse` with 50 actors): same as bare JSON, 0 allocs. Before this PR the interceptor cloned these on every RPC.
- Line with a message that needs masking: same cost as today, the clone and per field masking.
- 50 env-less templates in one response: 51 allocs for the check instead of 460 for a clone.

Things this does not cover, stated in the `Handle` comment: a proto inside a slice, map or plain struct, a proto formatted into a string before the call, a payload inside `google.protobuf.Any`, and the OTLP copy of actor events. None of these shapes is used with a labeled type today.

Other changes that come with it:

- `ateom-gvisor` calls `serverboot.InitLoggerWithWriter` like atelet and ateom-microvm instead of building the handler by hand. That made `serverboot.LogLevel()` unused, so it is removed. Its comment was also inviting exactly the pattern that skips redaction.
- The interceptor tests and the ateapi functional test harness install the same handler stack the servers use. Without this the functional tests would have printed tokens and env values to stderr now that the interceptor logs bodies raw.
- `serverboot` gains a test that `InitLoggerWithWriter` installs the redacting handler, which is the contract the interceptor now depends on.

No docs change. A section in the API style guide about when to mark a field `debug_redact` and what it guarantees is a good follow up, I will send it separately.

- [x] Tests pass
- [x] Appropriate changes to documentation are included in the PR

author: avicennasis
body:
mem_available_bytes() was /proc/meminfo behind #ifdef _WIN32, so on macOS it returned 0. Nothing failed loudly: both refusals that compare the plan against the machine, the KV cache check and the whole-plan check before allocation, are written as "if (available > 0 && need > available)", so a probe that says 0 silently switches both guards off, and --preset auto refused with a message about /proc/meminfo on a platform that has never had one. On an M1 running main a2ad8e5 the function returns 0.00 GB (checked directly, not inferred), so a Mac user asking for --cache-gb 500 got no refusal, just the allocator failing later.

The probe moves into src/cli/k3_sysmem.h (one function each for available and total, a branch per platform, 100 lines most of which is comment). Darwin reads free + inactive + purgeable pages from host_statistics64, the same set of pages the kernel will give up without paging anything out, which is what MemAvailable estimates on Linux; total is hw.memsize. Windows keeps ullAvailPhys but caps it by ullAvailPageFile, the remaining commit limit: a machine with a small pagefile can refuse to commit an allocation while physical memory sits free, and the engine's arenas are committed up front. Linux is unchanged. The MemTotal read the auto budget did inline goes through the same header, and the "needs /proc/meminfo" message no longer names a file that does not exist on two of the three platforms. Net change in k3_run.c: 18 lines in, 49 out.

tests/unit/test_sysmem.c asserts the two numbers are known, ordered, and plausible on whichever platform runs it, and on Linux that they agree with an independent sscanf of /proc/meminfo. It fails on main as it stands today on macOS (available 0.00 GB) and passes with this change. Wired into make test, CMake and ctest (memory_probe).

Verified locally, since CI does not run on fork PRs here. Linux, gcc 13 and clang 18 on Ubuntu 24.04, portable baseline: make test green, test_ops 22 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, SYSMEM TESTS PASSED (available 34.67 GB of 134.98 GB, agreeing with /proc/meminfo), SCALE TEST PASSED, ENGINE MATCHES THE REFERENCE EXACTLY, ALL WEIGHTLESS TESTS PASSED. The -Werror portable build clean. ASan/UBSan clean on the CI list plus test_sysmem. CMake + ctest 16/16. macOS 26.6.2 on an M1 with Apple clang 21.0.0: the probe from main compiled standalone returns 0.00 GB (the red); on this branch test_sysmem passes under -Werror with available 58.55 GB of 68.72 GB (hw.memsize 68719476736; vm_stat at that moment: 2295175 free + 1167144 inactive pages of 16384 bytes, purgeable not shown by vm_stat), make test is green end to end with the OpenMP flags emptied because that Mac has no libomp (0 warnings; 22 passed, SCALE TEST PASSED, oracle exact, ALL WEIGHTLESS TESTS PASSED), and bin/k3 on the tiny checkpoint with --cache-gb 500 now refuses up front with "this needs 500.00 GB and the machine has 58.57 GB available, a shortfall of 441.43 GB" where main proceeded; with --cache-gb 0.5 it runs and prints available 58.57 GB in the plan. Windows: mingw-w64 cross build under wine, test_sysmem included (wine reports its own numbers, so the values mean little there; the build and the ordering assertions are what that run checks).
