body: GitHub release `backpass-v0.1.29` already exists, but npm never received `0.1.29` because the original publish failed on `format:check`. The tag was retargeted to `f13cc56` (the 0.1.29 release plus the README trailing-space fix). Captain sanctioned republishing `backpass@0.1.29` only. This PR adds a one-off recovery path to `.github/workflows/release-please.yml` so we can republish that existing tag via trusted publishing / provenance, without bumping the version and without creating a new release-please release. ## Behavior - Normal `push` to `main` is unchanged, except the existing `release-please` job now has `if: github.event_name == 'push'` so a dispatch cannot create a release. - `workflow_dispatch` inputs: `tag_name` (required) and `version` (required). - New `npm-republish` job runs only on `workflow_dispatch`. - Recovery is hard-allowlisted to `tag_name == backpass-v0.1.29` and `version == 0.1.29`, must be dispatched from `main`, checks out `refs/tags/${tag_name}`, and asserts `package.json` version matches the input. Anything else fails loud. - Then the same gate + publish sequence as today: pnpm/node 24 with registry-url, frozen install, lint, format:check, typecheck, test, `npm publish --access public --provenance`. - `permissions` still include `id-token: write`. No product code, README, or package version changes. ## After merge Do not merge this PR as part of this agent run. After it lands on `main`, dispatch **release-please** from `main` with: - `tag_name`: `backpass-v0.1.29` - `version`: `0.1.29`

author: sandychapman
body:
`test_token_set_rejects_non_finite_expiry` aborts CI runs at random, on PRs that have nothing to do with it:

```
ERROR gw1 - Different tests were collected between gw3 and gw1
77 skipped, 1 error
```

## Cause

The three tokens are built when the `@parametrize` decorator is evaluated — once per xdist worker process — and `generate_unsigned_jwt()` stamps the current time:

```python
now = issued_at if issued_at is not None else int(time.time())
claims = {"sub": principal_id, "iat": now}
```

Workers that collect either side of a second boundary produce different tokens. pytest derives the test id from the parameter, so the workers disagree on what was collected and xdist aborts the entire run — nothing executes.

It is a wall-clock race, so it fails roughly half the time. It cost two runs on #1875 before I traced it.

## Reproduction

Two collections 1.2s apart on `main` produce different ids:

```
run 1: test_token_set_rejects_non_finite_expiry[eyJhbGciOiJub25lIiwidHlwIjoiSldUIn0.eyJzdWIiOiJ…
run 2: test_token_set_rejects_non_finite_expiry[eyJhbGciOiJub25lIiwidHlwIjoiSldUIn0.eyJzdWIiOiJ…
```

## Fix

Pin `issued_at` so every process builds the same token, and name the cases explicitly. The ids were previously whole JWTs, which is why the failure was unreadable — the log scrubber saw a token and printed `***`:

```
before: test_token_set_rejects_non_finite_expiry[*** exp]
after:  test_token_set_rejects_non_finite_expiry[jwt-exp]
```

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| `test_client_auth.py` | 73 passed |
| `packages/nemo_helix_plugin/tests/` under `-n 4` | 1735 passed |
| ids stable across two separate processes | ✅ |
| ids unstable on `main`, same check | ✅ reproduced |
| `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` | clean |

Added `test_non_finite_expiry_params_do_not_vary_between_xdist_workers`, which reads the parametrize argvalues back and compares them against deterministically generated tokens. Reintroducing a wall-clock `iat` fails it — confirmed by mutation rather than assumed.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage to verify that generated test tokens remain consistent across independent test collections.

author: marmota-alpina
body:
## Contexto

`AC_PCD` passou a atender a pessoa com deficiência que não optou pelas cotas da lei, independentemente de escola e de renda (UNI-REQ-0141 e UNI-REQ-0142). A reserva de PcD do processo sem as cotas federais, que justificava `PCD_PURO`, é a mesma `AC_PCD`. A Educação do Campo passa a usá-la.

Story: #1664.

## O que muda

**Configuração**

- `PCD_PURO` sai de `CodigoModalidade`, dos códigos protegidos (de 13 para 12) e do seed. A migration `RemovePcdPuroEFundamentaAcoesAfirmativasNa532` apaga a linha semeada.
- A base legal de `AC_I` e `AC_Q` passa a ser a Res. 532/2021, art. 2º. A Res. 22/2014 que ela citava foi revogada pelo art. 3º da 532/2021.

**Seleção**

- `RegraDistribuicaoVagasCodigo.ComPcdPuro` vira `ComAcPcd` (`DISTRIB-VAGAS-COM-AC-PCD`). O rol fechado é `[AC, AC_PCD]`, a regra é de quadro fixo e fica fora do ramo federal.
- A linha 26 do catálogo de regras é reescrita no lugar: código, rol, invariantes e base legal (Res. 532/2021, art. 1º).
- A base legal da regra do PSIQ passa a ser a Res. 532/2021, art. 2º.

## Dados existentes

Não há produção. As migrations não protegem nem convertem o que já existe:

- modalidade cadastrada que cite `PCD_PURO` é recadastrada;
- processo de homologação que cite `DISTRIB-VAGAS-COM-PCD-PURO` ou o hash anterior do PSIQ é recadastrado.

A revisão levantou esses pontos (guarda da ADR-0112, rascunhos com `PCD_PURO` sob a regra institucional, referência a `PCD_PURO` a partir de outra modalidade). Foram recusados por essa decisão.

## Intervalo até a #1672

Para um processo `[AC, AC_PCD]`, a proposta de regras de derivação (`GET …/regras-derivacao/normativas`) ainda oferece `AC_PCD` com a condição `EGRESSO_ESCOLA_PUBLICA = false`, da matriz atual. A troca dessa condição é o objeto da #1672, que depende desta issue e tem critério de aceite explícito para isso. A proposta é só uma sugestão: o admin a ajusta na configuração até lá.

## Portal

As páginas do catálogo de erros sobre os códigos protegidos e sobre o rol das regras estão em unifesspa-edu-br/uniplus-developers#277. **Este PR entra primeiro.**

## Verificação

- Build sem avisos e `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` limpos.
- Unitários e arquitetura: 18 assemblies verdes.
- Integração: 9 assemblies verdes, incluindo:
  - as duas migrations contra Postgres real;
  - o seed de modalidades sem `PCD_PURO` e com a base legal das ações afirmativas;
  - o catálogo de regras com `DISTRIB-VAGAS-COM-AC-PCD` e a base legal das duas regras reescritas.
- Revisão independente de correção e dos critérios de aceite. Os testes da base legal das regras entraram por ela.

Closes #1670
Refs #1664

author: kshitijk4poor
body:
## What

Adds Claude Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`), which Anthropic released on 2026-09-28, and fixes the one request shape that breaks on it.

**WHO / WHEN / WHY:** Anthropic launched Sonnet 5.5 on 2026-09-28 ([announcement](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5), [model page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/overview), [migration guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/sonnet-5-5/migration-guide)). As of this PR no open PR or issue covered it. It is already live on OpenRouter and on Nous Portal as `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.

## Changes

| Surface | Change |
|---|---|
| `hermes_cli/models_catalog_static.py` | `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` added to `OPENROUTER_MODELS`; the `nous` list derives from it. `claude-sonnet-5-5` added to native `anthropic`, and `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5` to `bedrock`. The Bedrock default at `[0]` is unchanged. |
| `website/static/api/model-catalog.json` | Regenerated with `scripts/build_model_catalog.py` |
| `agent/usage_pricing.py` | Sonnet 5 and 5.5 share one native Anthropic row: $2 / $10, cache read $0.20, 5m cache write $2.50 (the migration guide says "the same prices as Claude Sonnet 5"). Main's Sonnet 5 comment said the $2/$10 intro price reverts to $3/$15 after 2026-08-31; Anthropic's [pricing page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing) still lists $2/$10, so that stale instruction is removed. |
| `agent/anthropic_adapter.py` | Reasoning-off requests now send `thinking: {"type": "between_tools"}` to Sonnet 5.5 on anthropic.com. See below. |

These already resolve correctly through the existing `claude-sonnet-5` prefix entries, so they needed no change: 1M context (native + Bedrock), 128K max output, the adaptive-thinking / xhigh / no-sampling-params gates, and the 180s reasoning stale-timeout floor.

## Thinking-off breaking change

On Sonnet 5.5, `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` returns HTTP 400. The lowest setting is now `between_tools`, which turns off up-front thinking. It takes no other thinking field and returns 400 at `xhigh`/`max` effort. The disable path therefore sends it with no other fields and no `output_config`, so the API default effort of `high` applies.

Without this change, every path that turns reasoning off would 400 on native Anthropic: title generation, the compression fast lane, and `/reasoning none`. Opus 5.5 hit the same class of bug in #120069.

Relays behave differently. Live probe of Nous Portal `/v1/messages` with `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` on 2026-09-28:

| `thinking` sent | Portal response |
|---|---|
| omitted | 200 |
| `adaptive` | 200 |
| `disabled` | 400 "Reasoning is mandatory for this endpoint and cannot be disabled." |
| `between_tools` | 400 "Invalid Anthropic Messages API request" |

So on endpoints outside anthropic.com, the Sonnet 5.5 family keeps the mandatory-thinking omission. That includes Bedrock via the AnthropicBedrock SDK, which passes the `bedrock-runtime` URL, and Azure; neither was verified for `between_tools`. Omitting the field never 400s; the cost is that thinking stays on. `_accepts_thinking_disable` now returns False for this family, and `base_url` is keyword-only on `_thinking_kwargs`, so no caller gets the native shape by default.

## Verification

- `tests/agent/test_anthropic_thinking_disable.py`: Sonnet 5.5 gets `between_tools` (bare, even when xhigh is requested) on `None` / api.anthropic.com, and the omission on Portal and Bedrock; `claude-sonnet-5` still gets `disabled`. Mutation check: removing the third-party guard fails exactly the Portal and Bedrock rows.
- `tests/agent/test_usage_pricing.py`: Sonnet 5.5 rates equal Sonnet 5 rates (relationship test, not a snapshot).
- Targeted suite (75 files: every `tests/agent/test_anthropic*`, transports, model-switch, catalog, pricing, metadata, bedrock, auxiliary): 1393 passed, 42 failed. All 42 failures are identical by name on `origin/main` (re-run on the merge-base). After the follow-up commit, the touched files pass 434/434. Ruff is clean.
- Live, through Portal `/v1/messages` with this adapter's real kwargs: reasoning off → 200; high → 200 (adaptive + summarized); xhigh with a tool → 200 with `tool_use`. Also live through Portal `chat_completions` via `AIAgent` with reasoning off: returned `TEST-OK anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`.
- **Not live-tested on native anthropic.com** (no Anthropic key available). The `between_tools` shape there comes from the vendor's migration guide.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- **Forced `tool_choice`** (`any`/`tool`) also returns 400 on Sonnet 5.5, as on Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1. No in-tree caller forces tool choice on the Anthropic path; auxiliary pass-through is the only route. #123690 adds the generic guard; Sonnet 5.5 belongs in its `_NO_FORCED_TOOL_CHOICE_CLAUDE_SUBSTRINGS`, but not in the mandatory-thinking set, since it accepts `between_tools`. I've commented there.
- Bedrock pricing is not added: AWS has not published a Sonnet 5.5 SKU rate that I could verify, so cost shows unknown there instead of a guessed number.
- OpenRouter's chat-completions path sends `reasoning: {enabled: false}` for reasoning-off. Whether OpenRouter maps that to Anthropic's `disabled` (which would 400) is unverified; there's no OpenRouter key here. Portal on chat-completions was verified: reasoning off returns 200.
- #121016 (Opus 5.5 → mandatory set) touches the adjacent tuple in `anthropic_adapter.py`. It composes with this PR (Opus 5.5 has no `between_tools`), and whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

author: shiny-code-app[bot]
body:
## Why

On a non-production Odoo instance, `launchplane_settings` left Shopify alone in two cases: when Launchplane sent no override payload, and when the payload had no Shopify section. A restored production copy therefore kept production's store key, token and webhook key. This is one of the layers that let OPW testing reach the live Shopify store on 2026-09-28 (cbusillo/odoo-tenant-opw#155). The original bridge cleared Shopify when values were missing. That clear was lost in `cfe89ac`.

## What changes

- In both of those cases, when `PLATFORM_INSTANCE` is not exactly `prod`, the addon now clears the Shopify settings and logs a warning that names the instance and the reason. It clears the same keys as the explicit `clear` action: store key, token, webhook key, API version, `test_store` and the legacy store URLs.
- **An empty or unknown `PLATFORM_INSTANCE` counts as non-production**, so this fails closed. Only the exact value `prod` keeps production's settings.
- An explicit `apply` or `clear` behaves as before on every instance. Shopify settings without an action are still rejected, before anything is cleared.
- Production is unchanged in every case.
- Side effect for local instances: a store configured by hand, with no Launchplane Shopify `apply`, is now cleared at every settings apply. That is the intended fail-closed behaviour. To keep a development store, send it as an `apply` action.
- `launchplane_settings/AGENTS.md` records the rule.

Not changed here: `launchplane_settings_applied=true` is printed by odoo-devkit's startup script whether or not anything was applied, not by this addon, so it stays with cbusillo/odoo-devkit#126. A preview takes its `PLATFORM_INSTANCE` from its template lane's runtime environment, so a preview built from a `prod` template would count as production here. That inheritance is the Launchplane-side finding 8 on cbusillo/launchplane#2554.

## Verification

- Ran the `launchplane_settings` tests in the OPW Odoo 19 tenant image against a throwaway database, with this branch mounted: 13 tests, 0 failed.
- The new tests cover:
  - no payload on `testing`, on an empty instance and with the variable unset
  - a payload without a Shopify section (other config parameters still apply)
  - an explicit `apply` on `testing`
  - production with no payload, and with a payload without Shopify
- Planted faults:
  - With the non-production clear disabled, the no-payload and no-Shopify tests fail (4 failures).
  - With production treated as non-production, the production test fails (2 failures).
- JetBrains: UNKNOWN (`language_sdk_missing`). This repo has no Python project or documented SDK setup, so PyCharm has no interpreter for the worktree. The helper-created `.idea` files were removed. Ruff on the changed files reports only 4 findings, all on lines this PR does not touch.

Refs #35

author: mydcc
body:
[no issue] — the items in this PR are the sources; sync-backlog.yml creates the GitHub issues from them only after this merges, so there is nothing to close yet.

## What

Ten backlog items from a review of the last two days on `develop` (33 PRs,
#3672-#3720). No code changes in this PR — items only, so the issues exist
before the fix PRs reference them.

## The incident

On 2026-09-28 three bot PRs (#3692, #3680, #3718) were squash-merged and each
replayed a stale sandbox tree over `develop`: 23 files deleted outright, ~200
reverted to older content, including `tradeService.ts`, `orderGate.ts`, both
locale files and the whole `docs/bitget-api/` directory. #3720 restored it by
hand.

The restore itself was verified independently — `git diff c1ab8fab^ develop`
touches only the 13 intended changes plus new backlog items. That part is clean.

The **cause** is not, and it is two separate defects:

### BUG-0582 (P0) — the guard was never required

`.github/workflows/pr-base-revert-guard.yml` exists and worked: it reported
**FAILURE** on #3680 and #3692. Both were merged anyway. The check is absent
from `required_status_checks` on `develop`, so a red result was advisory:

    gh api repos/mydcc/cachy-app/branches/develop/protection
    -> contexts: Conventional Commits, Closing References, Decimal.js
       Enforcement, i18n String Compliance, Unit Tests, TypeScript Type Check,
       ESLint, Backlog & Documentation Links, check-translations

Neither #3680 nor #3692 carried `allow-base-revert`, so this was not a
deliberate opt-out. The guard was written on 2026-09-14 for exactly this
incident class (BUG-0447) and had no veto for two weeks.

### BUG-0583 (P1) — and it is blind on the shape AGENTS.md prescribes

The guard reported **SUCCESS** on #3718, which also did damage.

`git fetch origin pull/3718/head` recovers the tree the guard cleared:

- merged head `d6e58dec`, parent `ea116d72`
- the squash on develop has a **byte-identical tree** (`f4fb2108…`) — GitHub
  applied the head tree wholesale
- `journalSort.ts` exists at `ea116d72`, missing at `d6e58dec`

So the tip was itself a 189-file snapshot committed over the good commit, and
**the branch never merged `develop`**. That makes the two anchors collapse:

    merge-base(base, head)   = 9358fde2
    first^1 (forkRev)        = 9358fde2     <- identical

When `forkRev == mergeBase`, every line the payload removes is by construction
present in `forkRev`, so `baseRemoved` is always 0 and the check can never fire.
This is the default for any branch that has not merged base — which is exactly
what AGENTS.md's "Jules Sandbox Hygiene" tells agents to do. The guard's
coverage is the inverse of what is wanted: it catches the stale snapshot an
agent produced *despite* the rule, and misses the one produced *by* following
it. The existing fixture passes only because it merges base first.

The fix is decided in the item (content era via `git log --find-object`, not a
graph anchor). Recorded there: walking first-parents to the first base-reachable
ancestor was tried against these refs and is a **no-op** — that value already is
`9358fde2`.

### BUG-0584 (P1) — no release since 2026-09-20

Every push to `develop` fails `Release` with `EGITNOPERMISSION`. Last tag is
`v1.6.0-beta.364` (2026-09-20); `package.json` still reads the same. `release.yml`
uses `RELEASE_TOKEN || GITHUB_TOKEN` and the log shows an *invalid* token being
sent, so `||` does not fall through — the secret exists (set 2026-08-22) and has
most likely expired. Eight days of merged work unreleased, unnoticed. No backlog
or TODO entry covers it.

## Code items

Two of these are **regressions of items currently marked `done`** — that is the
part worth a human look.

- **BUG-0586** — BUG-0331 ("flash close strips protection before refusal") is
  `done`. BUG-0551 (2 days ago) added a refusal source into the same window.
  `cancelAllOrders` (1462) succeeds and strips TP/SL, *then* the session guard
  fires (1471). Position open and unprotected; the rollback classifies
  `OrderRefusedError` as indeterminate and parks the order as
  `_isUnconfirmed` for a request that never left the device.
- **BUG-0587** — BUG-0565 is `done`. `fetchPendingOrders` and
  `tradeService.readFreshPositions` (close-all path) hydrate the store with no
  read ticket, while their siblings in the same file use `mayApply(ticket)`.
- **BUG-0588** — money path, but **not the bug the first pass described**. The
  comment at `tradeService.ts:2531-2536` argued the stale-`previousQuantity`
  residual was minimal because a partial fill leaves `previousQuantity` stale.
  That premise is false: `amount` is the order's *total* on both venues and a partial
  fill does not shrink it, so the stale-low path into the daily-loss omission does
  not exist. What survives is the comment itself, which now argues something false
  on a money path. Fix is comment-only; `rmsService` is deliberately unchanged.
- **BUG-0589** — found while correcting BUG-0588. The Bitget normaliser maps `filled`
  from `filledQty`, a field that appears **nowhere** in `docs/bitget-api/`; the mirror
  documents `baseVolume`. A miss is silent, because the field is optional and the
  mapping falls back to `"0"` — so a Bitget partial fill reads as "no fill". Not a
  money path: the amend gate reads `amount`.
- **BUG-0585** — `journalSort.ts:76`: an unparseable date makes the comparator
  return 0 against everything, silently freezing the column. The `duration`
  branch in the same function does guard.

## Not filed

Six lower-severity findings were found and deliberately left out of this PR:
opposing null conventions between the two `journalSort` helpers, `PlaceOrderPanel`
leaving live entry enabled on
`failure:"unreachable"`, venue timeouts surfaced as "exchange rejected your
credentials", no timeout on the verification read, and Bitget order-entry TP/SL
fields still editable. Say the word and they become follow-up items.

## Test plan

Documentation only. `npm run backlog:check` → 467 items, front matter valid.
Index regenerated and committed in this PR as the workflow requires.

author: elderevil
body:
## Why

`#822` (item/dweller art backfill) and `#821` (randomize boosted vault legendary roster) were marked **MERGED**, but neither reached `master`:

- `#823` was **squash-merged** to `master` at 17:37:36Z (`d14df020`), orphaning its branch commits.
- `#822` was then merged at 18:13:22Z with **base `feat/nonhuman-ageless-state-effects`** — the branch that had *already* been squash-merged 36 minutes earlier — so its merge commit landed on that dead-end branch.
- `#821` was merged into `feat/item-dweller-assets`, likewise never PR'd to `master`.

Ancestry check on `master` returned `NO` for `834649b0`, `1e3f106b`, `2c3b487b`, `b080fa42`.

**Impact:** prod (`v2.154.0`) is missing 284 static images and most asset mappings — only 16 of 43 catalog weapons were mapped, so unmapped weapons silently rendered the 10mm-pistol fallback, and most outfits fell back to a generic glyph.

## What

Re-lands the content of `#822` + `#821` onto `master` via 3-way reconstruction (`master`'s ageless content is preserved; only art + roster changes are added):

- 284 new images (147 apparel, 46 pet, 37 weapon, 34 legendary-dweller, 20 junk)
- asset maps: `weapon_assets` 16→46, `outfit_assets`, new `junk_assets`/`pet_assets`, `legendary_dweller_assets`
- catalog expansions + read-time junk image resolution
- `AssetGalleryView`, `ItemCard`/`items.ts` fixes
- #821 boosted legendary roster randomization (+ exact gear-name matching)

**No ageless regression:** the delta vs `master` contains no ageless files. The single import conflict in `vault_service.py` was resolved by keeping both imports (`Weapon` and `can_use_radaway`).

## Verification

- Backend full suite: **2345 passed, 2 skipped**
- Frontend: **lint + typecheck clean**, **2287 tests passed (214 files)**
- `ruff check` clean on changed files; no leftover conflict markers
- No release-managed files touched (`CHANGELOG.md`, `pyproject.toml`, `package.json`, `uv.lock`) — release automation owns those

## Note

History contains the orphaned pre-squash ageless commits as ancestors of the merged branch. **Squash-merge recommended** to keep `master` history clean.

Follow-up to #822 #821

body:
## What this changes

Formats the repository with the shared Prettier preset: `.prettierrc` is now `"@rxova/repo-config/prettier"` (semicolons, double quotes, the Astro plugin built in), `.prettierrc.json` and the root `prettier-plugin-astro` devDependency are removed, and every file is reformatted in this one commit.

Two follow-ons of the reformat:

- `packages/brand/scripts/generate-og.ts` found the dark palette by the literal `:root[data-theme='dark']`, which `tokens.css` now spells with double quotes; it matches either quote now. The social cards re-render byte-identical; only the manifest's fingerprint changes.
- Prettier also formats code inside Markdown, so knip read an import in a code-recipe sample string in the preview gallery as a real one; that page joins the displayed-code ignores in `knip.config.ts`.

The walkthrough before/after files stay untouched (`.prettierignore`).

## Visible effect

`pnpm lock:diff --base origin/main`: the built site differs only in code samples inside update entries (`/updates` and `/updates/repos/use-everywhere`), which now show semicolons and double quotes like the libraries' own docs, plus the never-deployed preview app's gallery pages. No markup, styles or scripts change.

## Heads-up

Open branches will conflict on formatting. Rebasing one onto this is easiest by running `pnpm format` on the branch first. `@rxova/brand` and `@rxova/astro-ui` ship their sources, so the next release carries the reformatted files; nothing about their behaviour changes, so this PR carries `skip-changeset`.

## How it was verified

- `pnpm run verify` passes (all 12 steps), and the pre-push hook ran it again.
- `pnpm lock:diff --base origin/main` as above.

* Keeping GitHub Actions pinned to specific commit hashes with version tags maintains security while enabling controlled updates

* Confirmed all GitHub workflow YAML files pass syntax validation with the updated action references
* CI pipeline execution will validate that CodeQL v4.38.2 actions function correctly in fortress-security-scans, codeql-analysis, and scorecard workflows

* **Risk**: Low - CodeQL action updates are minor version patches (v4.38.1 to v4.38.2) with minimal behavioral changes

author: akbar1214
body:
## 3/9 — generator: resolve a type's package from the schema being generated

Stacked on #39.

`basePackageForType` short-circuited to `basePackage` (the *generating* schema's package)
whenever the type's namespace equalled the **declaring** schema's namespace. Callers pass the
declaring schema, so that comparison always held and the package-map lookup below it was
unreachable for every call.

Correct only while all schemas shared one output package. With `schemaPackages` mapping two
schemas to two packages — split-merge metadata — a type declared in schema X but referenced
while generating schema Y resolved to Y's package. Inherited members of a cross-package base
then referenced classes that are never generated (`import com.derivedpkg.complex.Home`, where
`com.derivedpkg.complex` does not exist), so **the client did not compile**. When the second
schema happened to declare a same-simple-name type it compiled while silently referring to the
wrong type — a name clash javac rejects.

The comparison must be against the schema whose files are being *written*, not the one that
*declares* the type. `ContainerGenerator` holds its own copy of the method and got the same fix.

Two new cases, both using the project's javac `CompilationHarness` referee rather than string
assertions, and both showing the exact wrong `com.derivedpkg.*` references when red.

author: maximilianallan
body:
## Summary

Hospital reconstruction step 3 can build a cached 3dgrut image successfully and then fail at `import torch` with `libcudart.so.13` / missing cuBLAS libraries. The pipeline previously used the external 3dgrut Dockerfile's CUDA 11.8 default without controlling subsequent pip dependency resolution. CUDA 11.8 also does not support the Blackwell GPU used for validation.

Use a repository-owned Dockerfile with CUDA 12.8.1 and a consistent PyTorch stack, and verify that stack during the build:

- Pin PyTorch 2.7.1, torchvision 0.22.1, torchaudio 2.7.1, and NumPy <2 throughout pip installation.
- Check PyTorch and Kaolin imports and assert the expected PyTorch/CUDA versions before completing the image build.
- Build and run `i4h-3dgrut:cu128` using the pinned upstream checkout as the build context.
- Fix the step 2 checkout path, update submodules after selecting the tested revision, and return to the pipeline directory before step 3.
- Add pipeline regression tests and a repeatable GPU training/export smoke test.

The supplied cached-build log establishes the runtime mismatch, but does not identify which installation introduced the CUDA 13 library dependency. This change makes the intended stack explicit and detects replacement during the build.

## Validation results

Validated commit `12081c4dd0408965c18c02445e566a33084b9372` on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition with driver 595.91.07:

- Docker build completed; PyTorch reported `2.7.1+cu128` and CUDA `12.8`, and Kaolin imported successfully.
- `pip check`: **No broken requirements found.**
- CUDA matrix multiplication and backward pass completed with finite results.
- 3DGUT renderer and MCMC CUDA extensions compiled and loaded.
- Ten training steps completed on a generated fixture containing 16 COLMAP views and 512 points.
- USDZ export completed; ZIP integrity and opening the scene with USD both passed.
- Both pipeline regression tests passed.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed for all five changed files.

## Reproduce the tests

From the repository root, prepare the documented upstream revision:

```bash
cd hospital-digital-twin/reconstruct_from_video
git clone --recursive https://github.com/nv-tlabs/3dgrut.git
git -C 3dgrut checkout 38664dde3b0a4a35d2baf91ebee11f3de3eae8c3
git -C 3dgrut submodule update --init --recursive
```

Build the image, check dependencies, and run the GPU smoke test:

```bash
docker build --progress=plain -t i4h-3dgrut:cu128 \
  -f Dockerfile.3dgrut 3dgrut

docker run --rm i4h-3dgrut:cu128 \
  conda run --no-capture-output -n 3dgrut python -m pip check

docker run --rm --gpus all --runtime=nvidia --ipc=host \
  -v "$PWD/tests:/tests:ro" i4h-3dgrut:cu128 \
  conda run --no-capture-output -n 3dgrut python /tests/gpu_smoke.py

PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover \
  -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
```

Expected smoke-test result:

```text
PASS: CUDA forward/backward, 10 training steps, readable USDZ export
```

From the repository root, run the formatting checks:

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  hospital-digital-twin/reconstruct_from_video/Dockerfile.3dgrut \
  hospital-digital-twin/reconstruct_from_video/README.md \
  hospital-digital-twin/reconstruct_from_video/scripts/reconstruct.py \
  hospital-digital-twin/reconstruct_from_video/tests/gpu_smoke.py \
  hospital-digital-twin/reconstruct_from_video/tests/test_reconstruct.py
```

## Scope and limitations

The container now requires a host driver compatible with CUDA 12.8; a host CUDA toolkit is not required. GPU validation used synthetic, pre-generated COLMAP inputs and ten training steps. It did not exercise COLMAP feature extraction/mapping, long-run convergence, or reconstruction quality on real hospital footage. The original user's cached image was not available for inspection.

author: nutphu-alt
body:
Restructures `e_coli_dataset/` so the path to the deliverable is legible without reading all 30 scripts.

## Layout

```
e_coli_dataset/
├── dataset/        15 xlsx + the source-data README (was data/)
├── pipeline/       01, 02, 03, 12, 16, 17, 21, 22 — the 8 that produce design_panel.csv
├── experiments/    the other 22 + 31_make_slides.js
└── output/         unchanged, gitignored
```

Every move is a `git mv`, so file history is preserved.

The original `01..31` numbering is kept deliberately — it keeps the handoff's code inventory and every `importlib` string valid, and the eight pipeline scripts still sort into execution order.

**The pipeline needs core dependencies only.** The design panel does not use ESM-2 (step 12 found the embedding block doesn't help the design regime), so no PyTorch and no model downloads on the critical path.

## Fixes

- **`14_tune_xgb_extrapolation.py`** resolved `BASE_DIR` via `parent.name == "code" else Path(".")`. The dead `/sessions/bold-admiring-volta/` path was already gone from this repo, but that conditional would have silently pointed at the working directory the moment the file left `code/`. Now plain `parent.parent`.
- **`28` and `29`** import `21_design_variants`, which now lives in `pipeline/`. Both add `pipeline/` to `sys.path` — the only cross-folder import in the tree.
- **`01_clean_gfp_data.py`** reads `dataset/` instead of `data/`.

## Docs

Root README, `EDA_summary.md` (folder tree + 10 step headings), `PROJECT_HANDOFF.md` code inventory, and `.gitignore` updated for the new paths. New `e_coli_dataset/README.md` covers layout, run order, and why the five negative-result scripts stay:

| Script | Question | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `14`, `15` | Retune XGBoost for extrapolation? | No — Δ +0.0015, CI [−0.015, +0.018] |
| `20` | Two-stage classifier + regressor? | Marginal — AUC 0.778→0.791 |
| `23` | ESM-2 zero-shot log-odds? | Significantly worse — −0.0345 ρ |
| `25` | Wider ESM embedding block? | Flat — every CI spans zero |
| `28` | Retune the design oracle? | No — CI [−0.074, +0.223] |

Two are load-bearing: `14` writes the paired baseline `18_evo_benchmark.py` compares against, and `23` builds the feature matrix `26_esm_benchmark.py` needs for its comparison arms. Neither can be dropped without breaking a positive result.

## Verification

- All 30 scripts byte-compile from their new locations
- All 10 `importlib` targets resolve; the two cross-folder imports tested at runtime
- `pipeline/01` run from the restructured tree: 141,469 → 141,150 rows, backbone counts exact
- `pipeline/02` run: zero train rows touching a held-out position in any backbone; the 2 position-holdout dedup groups are the documented avGFP/amacGFP byte-identical curiosity, not a regression
- Nothing generated leaks past `.gitignore`

author: evanfeenstra
body:
Docs only: `mcp/src/lab/AGENTS.md`, plus the matching comment in `createLabStrut.ts`.

[stakwork/strut#76](https://github.com/stakwork/strut/pull/76) makes the builder's chat history append-only so the prompt cache survives between turns. One part of that change freezes the system prompt per chat:

- strut calls `chatSystem` once, when a chat's first turn builds its prompt, and replays that prompt verbatim on every later turn.
- The `Workflow Builder` page therefore reaches **new** chats. A running chat sees an edit only by opening the page itself.

The lab doc said the section is read "each chat turn". It now describes the per-chat behavior.

**Merge order:** mcp still pins strut at `3408776`, so this describes behavior mcp gets only once #76 merges and the strut pin is bumped. Merge this with that bump.

## Pourquoi

Suite de la [PR #68](https://github.com/gremtek13/jd-precompta/pull/68). L'outil de contrôle des FEC de la DGFiP (Test Compta Demat) est publié en source ouverte. Il ne peut pas tourner ici : il lui faut une interface graphique Tk et une base de données. Mais ses règles se lisent dans son code, et l'une d'elles touche l'application : un numéro de compte doit commencer par trois chiffres.

Le compte d'une catégorie est le seul compte de l'application qui se tape à la main (onglet Écritures, « Comptes manquants »). Il part tel quel dans chaque écriture, puis dans le FEC, et « Enregistrer » acceptait n'importe quel texte.

- `saveCompte` refuse un compte qui ne commence pas par trois chiffres et dit pourquoi. Il retire les espaces tapées (« 606 100 » devient 606100) et efface le refus précédent.
- Deux tests d'écran. Cinq mutations mordent : le code tel qu'il était, tout refuser, l'ancre retirée (« C606 » passerait), les espaces gardées, et le refus resté affiché.
- CLAUDE.md consigne ce que la lecture de l'outil a appris :

author: gargit
body:
## What

Two reasons a RomM game got "No Emulator Configured", or launched in the wrong core. Both are the same class as #120.

### 1. Platforms with no recommended RetroArch core (`67de370`)

`getDefaultCoreForSlug` only returned a core marked `isRecommended`. About 85 platforms have cores listed but none marked. For those it returned `null`, and RetroArch was started with the ROM but no `-L`, so it tried whichever core it had loaded last (`libretro_path`), usually one for another system. Affected systems include:

- Vectrex, Jaguar, SG-1000
- PC-FX, Neo Geo CD
- VIC-20, ZX81, PICO-8
- Pokémon Mini, Game & Watch

The BIOS lookup goes through the same function, so it found no entry for them either.

It now falls back to the first core that lists the platform. A recommended core still wins.

### 2. RomM's platform slugs (`a46b298`)

RomM names platforms by IGDB's slugs. For many systems Freegosy emulates, those aren't the slugs Freegosy's lists use:

| RomM | Freegosy |
|---|---|
| `famicom`, `new-style-nes` | `nes` |
| `sfam`, `satellaview`, `sufami-turbo`, SNES/SFC variants | `snes` |
| `pc-fx` | `pcfx` |
| `pc-8800-series`, `pc-9800-series` | `pc88`, `pc98` |
| `neo-geo-cd`, `neo-geo-pocket-color` | `neogeocd`, `ngpc` |
| `wonderswan-color`, `swancrystal` | `wonderswancolor` |
| `zxs` | `zxspectrum` |
| `amiga-cd32`, `commodore-cdtv` | `amiga` |
| `nintendo-dsi`, `nintendo-ds-lite`, `nintendo-dsi-xl` | `nds` |
| `philips-cd-i`, `tic-80`, `wasm-4`, `uzebox`, ... | `cdi`, `tic80`, `wasm4`, `uzem`, ... |

63 in all, in `lib/core/emulator/platform_slugs.dart`. They come from RomM's `backend/utils/platform_slugs.py`, plus the hardware variants its player maps to a core in `frontend/src/utils/index.ts` (e.g. `game-boy-pocket`, `sega-nomad`).

`canonicalPlatformSlug` is applied wherever a slug is looked up:

- **Emulator:** the strategy registry (emulator and per-platform preference).
- **RetroArch core:** the core list (default core, core picker) and the core used at launch.
- **Save folders:** RetroArch's and ares'.
- **ares:** its `--system` name.
- **ROM folder.**
- **BIOS sync** for an emulator.

Only systems a listed core runs are included. `sega32` (32X), for example, stays unknown, because no core in the list runs 32X; supporting it would mean adding it as a new platform. `turbografx-cd` is left to #124. Three names in RomM's player map look like typos (`commmodore-128`, `game-televisison`, `game-boy-adavance-sp`) and are left out.

## Testing

- `flutter analyze`: no issues. `flutter test`: all pass.
- **Default core:**
  - every platform a core lists gets a default core;
  - `pcfx` gets `mednafen_pcfx`;
  - a recommended core still beats one listed before it (`pcengine`).
- **Aliases:**
  - every alias leads to a system with a default core, and gets the same cores as its target;
  - no alias shadows a slug a core already lists;
  - RetroArch's save core and ares' system name follow the alias.
- **Not tested by hand:** no games for these platforms here.

author: ciaranm
body:
**Stacked on #1131.** This branch carries #1131's two commits, so merge #1131 first; after that, this diff is 4423f8d2 plus 415a99fd, which registers the `projection_skip_size_floor` lane in CMake: it was missing, so that lane had never run in the suite. It is based on `main` rather than on #1131's branch so that deleting that branch cannot close this PR.

## What

This adds variable **time-axis** sizes to the energetic rungs of `Disjunctive2D`'s cumulative relaxation (`relaxation_overload`, `relaxation_edge_finding`, `relaxation_time_table_edge_finding`) and to `cumulative_projection`. Before, all four needed constant sizes on both axes. #984 lists this under what is still open.

Such a rectangle is counted at the size's **declared** lower bound, the way 1D `Disjunctive`'s energy rules count a variable duration. Shrinking a rectangle cannot create an overlap, so everything inferred about the shrunk rectangles also holds for the real ones. The cost is that a rectangle the search has lengthened is counted at its floor. The current lower bound would be stronger, but it is a state fact, and the activity flags, window energies and flagged rows are all cached at `Top` as model facts. A rectangle declared from zero is still left out.

## Proof side

The floor enters the proof in one place: each pair refutation under the flagged row, where the before flag's row carries the size as a term.
- A `Top` RUP `size >= floor`, cached per rectangle, cancels that term.
- In non-strict mode each variable size also puts a zero-size escape into its pairs' clauses. That escape is pinned false at `Top` as well. The pin is needed: with two escapes in one pair, the pair clause's RUP does not reach both.
- The projection hands its `Cumulative` the floor as a **constant** length. Nothing on `Cumulative`'s side changes, and it never needs the proof-only end a variable length would.

Time-tabling (route B) is unchanged. It counts the current lower bound under a reason, as it already did.

## Tests
- `variable_size_*` in `disjunctive_2d_relaxation_test`:
  - Each energetic rung's fixture is run with every width a variable over `[w, w + 2]`, strict and non-strict. It must fire exactly as it does with constants, and must not fire with the rule off.
  - Per rung, an enumeration over positions and widths is checked against brute force.
- Three new mutation lanes, each rejected at the pair clause's RUP: `skip_size_floor`, `projection_skip_size_floor` and `skip_floor_escape_pins`.
  - The widths run **two** past the floor on purpose. A width over `[2, 3]` is `b0 + 2·b1 >= 2`, from which unit propagation fixes `b1`, and on that fixture all three mutations verify.
- Full suite 966/966 (GCC), rerun after rebasing onto #1131's test trim. The relaxation test's fixtures and all five sweep lanes also pass on a clang build. The relaxation test and the three new mutation lanes are clean under Sanitize.
- `-Werror` is clean on GCC and clang for the two changed `.cc` files.
- Fuzz (the scheduling harness, Disjunctive2D-only, with variable sizes made more frequent and wider): 17,985 seeds, 3,598 of them also under ASan/UBSan, with 0 anomalies. Every result either agrees with brute force or with the reference solve, and every proof verifies.
  - Of those, 13,483 seeds were a dense variant: smaller boxes, with the energetic rules on more often. There the relaxation's edge-finding fired on 387 seeds, its overload check on 80 and the projection's rows on 2,131. 378, 79 and 2,060 of those seeds respectively had a rectangle with a variable size and a positive floor. The harness's markers do not say which axis fired, so these counts are not per-axis.

## Not in this PR
Variable **resource-axis** sizes. That size is `ComparatorNetwork`'s duration, which the optional-task mode multiplies by the activity flag as a constant, so it is a separate piece of work.

Part of #984, and of #976.

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude Code, Opus 5.5).

author: ignisfrostburn
body:
## Summary
Fixes an issue where a newly verified sample on a brand-new Patient → Session → Sample chain could land in `sync_failed` on its first sync attempt without writing app-level logs or diagnostic failure details.

### Root Cause
1. **Parent Chain Foreign Key Race Condition**: Completing verification directly triggered `SyncSampleUseCase`. If the sample belonged to a newly created patient or session that had not yet synced to Supabase Postgres, the remote write failed with a foreign key constraint violation (`samples_session_id_fkey`).
2. **Missing Failure Context & Diagnostics**: Failure paths logged generic errors without structured context or failure classes. Early returns (such as missing local rows) returned `Result.failure` without logging.
3. **Lack of On-Device Diagnostic Info**: Medtechs and QA had no visibility into why a row was stuck in `sync_failed` without attaching a debugger.

---

## Key Changes
- **Parent Chain Ordering Fix**:
  - `SyncSampleUseCase` now ensures its parent session is synced (`SyncSessionUseCase`) before pushing the sample.
  - `SyncSessionUseCase` now ensures its parent patient is synced (`SyncPatientUseCase`) before pushing the session.
  - Eliminates foreign key violations on first-attempt verification syncs for brand-new chains.

- **Structured Failure Logging & Classification**:
  - Added structured `[SyncFailed][Entity:Id][Class:FailureClass]` logs across `SyncSampleUseCase`, `SyncSessionUseCase`, `SyncPatientUseCase`, and `SyncReportUseCase`.
  - Classifies errors into identifiable failure types (`NETWORK_ERROR`, `PARENT_SESSION_SYNC_FAILED`, `FOREIGN_KEY_VIOLATION`, `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `FILE_NOT_FOUND`, `MISSING_ENTITY`).

- **On-Device Diagnostic Error Surface**:
  - Added `observeLastError` and `recordLastError` to `LastSyncStore` and `DataStoreLastSyncStore`.
  - `SyncPendingDataUseCase` now records failure details when a sync pass encounters errors.
  - `SettingsViewModel` and `SettingsCards` now display the `lastSyncError` on the Settings screen under **Data & Sync** whenever failures exist.

---

## Acceptance Criteria Checklist
- [x] Every path that sets `sync_failed` logs the throwable with enough context to identify the sample and failure class.
- [x] Resolved parent chain race condition on brand-new Patient → Session → Sample chains.
- [x] Surfaced last-error details on-device under Settings → Data & Sync so failing rows can be diagnosed without a debugger.

---

## Test Verification
- **Unit Tests**: All 1,463 unit tests passed (`:app:testDebugUnitTest`), including new test cases in `SyncUseCasesTest.kt`.
- **Linting & Code Style**: `detekt` static analysis passed with zero issues.

author: glebpom
body:
A subscription tab whose generation the server ends with SubscriptionEnded now turns ended instead of staying active: it keeps its rows and the reason, is never restored on its own, and its resubscribe button reopens it under the same name, returning to ended with the refusal when the server declines. Closing an ended tab removes it without a deletion.

Restorations now belong to the connection that sends them and go out before the session's transaction is attached again, as the Rust client orders them, so an open transaction no longer refuses them and a finished or failed attach no longer strands a tab in restoring. Such an attach now ends only the commands issued in the transaction; subscription starts and deletions, domain listings, inspections, and commands issued outside it keep their place.

The console's remaining queues are bounded by records and bytes: the hand-off from its controls to the session loop to 64 requests and 4 MiB of text, the requests held or awaiting replies to 256 and 16 MiB, the command history to 256 commands and 256 KiB, and the graph snapshots to the one observed domain. At most 64 requests are in flight, the server's per-session limit, which moves into the wire crate as a shared constant; ordered requests beyond it now wait in issue order instead of being refused by the server. A superseded completion drops its partial reply. A refused request is reported where its outcome would have appeared, and walking back past the omitted commands says so.

The transaction inspector no longer requests its report in a loop. Accepting a reply reopened an already open inspector, which re-ran the request effect, so an open inspector re-read its report continuously and a search framing could override FIT. A report is now read again only when the inspector opens or changes target, the attached transaction changes, or the operator refreshes.

Unit tests cover the tab transitions, restoration ownership, attach endings, the request bounds and the in-flight window, the transfer drop, the command history, snapshot retention, and the inspector's request cadence. New nspl_repl.feature scenarios cover an ended and resubscribed tab on one and three nodes, restoration after the transaction finished or while it stays open across a leader change, and the console's own refusal of a request past its outstanding bound. The web console chapter, the client session protocol chapter, the transaction quiescence chapter, the implementation manual's evidence, and the NSPL skill describe the behavior.

author: fransqaas
body:
## Root cause of the creation outage

After #311 deployed, a free resume of the dead "Rookie Web QA 2" fighter took over its quarantined request (the new takeover path works) and failed again, but this time the new proxy log said why:

```
TypeError: Invalid redirect value, must be one of "follow" or "manual"
("error" won't be implemented since it does not make sense at the edge; use "manual" and check the response status code).
```

`handleProxy` passed `redirect: 'error'` to `fetch` for every template-renderer job (Gemini source views and the FAL nano-banana atlas), introduced in #296. workerd rejects the value before connecting, so every new Rookie/Champion creation since 2026-09-15 died at `source:side` in under a second, charged its credits and was quarantined. Legacy-renderer jobs used `'follow'`, which is why Player One's official job worked minutes earlier. Body size was a coincidence.

## Change

- `proxyRequest` accepts only `'follow' | 'manual'`; the Gemini and FAL atlas routes pass `'manual'`.
- On Meterkey routes a 3xx upstream answer is refused as 502 `provider_request_not_dispatched` (outcome header `not-dispatched`, so the reservation is released and the request may be retried as new work), with a log line. PixCLI keeps its own redirect handling.
- Tests: fail-closed redirect refusal; a source scan that fails if `redirect: 'error'` ever returns; the atlas integration test now expects `'manual'`.

`tsc -p worker` clean; `proxy`, `requestBody`, `providerSessions`, `providerSessions.integration` pass (83 tests).

## After deploy

Resume "Rookie Web QA" / "Rookie Web QA 2" (free) and confirm `source:side` reaches meterkey and the fighter becomes playable.

author: xzistance
body:
Forecasting scores now separate miners by how far they sit from a neutral baseline, instead of clustering everyone who clears the gates.

Accuracy counts events worse than a coin-flip Brier against the miner, bounded at −1. Calibration is the recency-weighted calibration error minus a 0.10 baseline, so a typical miner scores near 0. Edge is centered on matching the market and scaled so a few points of market-relative Brier move the composite. Rho still discounts short samples; the logistic midpoint is 100 effective predictions, with saturation around 170.

Adds new w_brier column to logging for better understanding.

author: joeydi
body:
The home hero's puzzle cube is now something you can play with. It starts the same way as before: the layers spin, then it scrambles and solves itself. Now it can also be handled.

- **Drag a cube** sideways to turn its horizontal layer, or up/down to turn the vertical slice its face belongs to (on the top face, whichever slice runs along the drag). The slice follows the pointer.
- **Let go** and it coasts into the nearest quarter turn. A flick carries through as many quarters as its speed allows and slows into the stop. A coasting slice can be caught mid-turn.
- **Leave it for 3 s** and it undoes the turns in reverse until the pink layer is whole again (about 6 s at most, however scrambled), then the loop starts over. Touching it during the undo stops it.
- **Touch:** only the cube's outline captures touch; swipes elsewhere on the illustration still scroll the page.

## How
- `scenes/puzzle-cube.ts` is rebuilt on a cube state: each cube's position on the grid and its rotation. `frame(t)` replays the same scripted turns and matches the old version to within float error at every t, so posters and the `/admin/illustrations` scrubber are unchanged.
- The new `play()` player runs the loop, handles drags and throws, and keeps a history of moves to undo. Moves on the same layer are merged, so spinning one layer round and round costs nothing to undo. The feel is set by constants at the top of the file (`IDLE`, `FRICTION`, `SPRING`, `MAX_SPIN`, `UNDO`).
- `SceneDef` gets optional `play` and `hitArea`. GLIllustration uses the player on the page and puts a drag area, clipped to `hitArea`, over the canvas. It only takes input once the canvas is live, so there's none on the static poster, without WebGL2, or under reduced motion.
- `gl/pick.ts` is new and works out which cube face is under the pointer.

## Testing
- `tsc` and `eslint` are clean.
- A headless run confirmed `frame(t)` matches the old version, and simulated drags, throws, catches and the undo back to the pink-middle formation.
- **Still to check in a browser:**
  - drag feel, and that the headline doesn't cover the cube at 1024–1920
  - touch on a phone at 390

author: l0ste
body:
## Problem

`types.rs` carried a hand copy of `VersionedTransactionWithStatusMeta::encode` from solana-transaction-status, plus its meta builders (one still marked `// FIXME: use native transform`), the accounts-only encoder and the version check. Inner instructions were mapped by hand in three places instead of calling `map_inner_instructions`. `getBlock` built its response by hand instead of calling `ConfirmedBlock::encode_with_options`.

Around those copies, Surfpool does not match Agave:

- `getBlock` with no `encoding` returns `jsonParsed`. Agave returns `json`. The local `getTransaction` lookup had the same wrong default, but every current caller sets an encoding, so nobody saw it.
- Every stored transaction (success, failure and airdrop) has `returnData: {programId: 1111…, data: ["", "base64"]}`. Agave stores `None` when the return data is empty, so the field is left out. `simulateTransaction` already does this.

## Fix

Three commits:

1. `refactor`: deletes the copies and calls the public functions instead (`VersionedTransactionWithStatusMeta::encode`, `ConfirmedBlock::encode_with_options`, `map_inner_instructions`, `parse_ui_inner_instructions`). A single `From<TransactionWithStatusMeta> for VersionedTransactionWithStatusMeta` handles the conversion. All callers already own the stored value, so it is moved and never cloned. Output is unchanged: a differential run over 3,581 cases (every encoding × max version × rewards flag, legacy/v0/v1, ok/err, full and empty metas) found 0 differences against 4.2.1.
2. `fix`: `json` becomes the default for both `getBlock` and local `getTransaction`, and empty return data is filtered out at the three places where transactions are stored, which matches `agave-svm`.
3. `getBlock` with `transactionDetails: "signatures"` answers from the block header without loading any transaction, as before, so a missing transaction record can't drop a signature.

## Test

- `test_get_block_transaction_details_and_rewards` covers full, signatures, accounts and none, plus `rewards: false`. It passes before and after the refactor.
- `test_get_block_defaults_to_json_encoding`, `test_get_transaction_local_defaults_to_json_encoding` and `test_stored_transactions_omit_empty_return_data` all fail on main and pass here.
- `test_get_block_signatures_come_from_block_header` stores a header signature with no transaction record and checks signatures mode still returns it.
- Hand-made mutants: 7 of 8 fail at least one test. The one that survives drops ALT keys from `simulateTransaction` inner instructions. That path is only covered by the differential check.

## Validation

- `cargo +nightly fmt --all -- --check` passes. Clippy (`-p surfpool-core --all-targets`) shows no new warnings compared with main.
- `cargo test -p surfpool-core --lib` passes except the 3 `test_simulate_add_alt_entries_fetching` cases, which also fail on main. `test_send_transaction_skip_sig_verify_processes_and_updates_state` passes when run on its own.
- Encode speed was measured in a release build with an alternating timed loop: a v0 transaction with an ALT, 20 accounts, 9 inner instructions and 25 log lines. `getTransaction` is 4–11% faster and `getBlock` (100 txs, full) is 3–9% faster. The old code cloned the meta a second time inside `encode`.

Not included: Agave master rejects `base58` with `maxSupportedTransactionVersion >= 1` on `getBlock`/`getTransaction`, but that check isn't in any released Agave yet (not in v4.2.2), so mainnet still accepts it and this PR leaves it alone.

author: pbrunot
body:
## Problem

`pc/hfs_atomsfe.py` did `u_src = rq * orb[:, i]`. atomSFE's `orbitals` are already u = r·R, so every exported row was actually r²·R. The renormalization step hid the mistake. The consequences:

- **Every radial density was pushed outward:** H 1s peaked at 2.3 a₀ instead of ~1.05, and He 1s at 1.29 instead of ~0.57. The eigenvalues were correct; only the export was wrong.
- **Core shells looked too big next to the valence shell** in heavy atoms, by about 1.3–1.8×. Calibration only corrects the valence subshell, so this distortion remained.
- **The size factors were compensating for this bug.** The Clementi-Raimondi factors (0.44 for H, ~0.56 for period 2) were documented as LDA self-interaction error, but they were really correcting the export bug.

How it was confirmed: an independent spin-unpolarized LDA solve for H and He matches the old table's "u" when multiplied by r, to within 2e-4. The corrected table matches u itself to within ~1e-3; the remaining difference comes from PZ81 vs VWN correlation.

## Changes

**Data fix**
- **Exporter:** `pc/hfs_atomsfe.py` no longer multiplies by r. It also prepends u(0)=0, so points below the first solver node ramp linearly to the origin instead of taking `np.interp`'s constant clamp.
- **Committed table repaired in place:** `pc/hfs_tables_reduced.npz` was corrected directly, because the full tables and the atomSFE install are not in the repo. Each row was divided by r, the clamp plateau was replaced by a linear ramp, and the row was renormalized. The procedure is documented in `pc/RUN_HFS.md`.
- **Generated files rebuilt:** `data/hfs_tables.bin`, `micropython/hfs_tables.bin`, `src/physics/atom_size_calib.h` and `micropython/hfs_atom_size_calib.py` were regenerated with the repo's scripts. The table factors are now ~0.8–1.2 (H 0.94, Fe 1.21, U 0.82), down from 0.44–0.9.
- **Generator path:** `tools/hfs_table_gen.py` now writes its header to `src/physics/hfs_tables.h` instead of the stale `src/hfs_tables.h`, and emits `inline constexpr` to match the committed file.

**Circle at the peak radius, in every viewer**

The bounding circle is now drawn at the radius of maximum radial density (the peak radius) instead of the p90 radius, which encloses 90% of the subshell's points. For the valence subshell, the peak radius is exactly the Clementi-Raimondi radius that the calibration targets. p90 remains the framing and zoom reference, so on-screen size and zoom behaviour are unchanged.

- **Device (C++):**
  - `radialModeOnGrid()` in `pointcloud.h` finds the peak, and `RadialTable::peakR` is set by the hydrogenic and both HFS samplers.
  - `AtomSubshellRange`, `OuterSubshell` and `DissectionEntry` carry `peakR`, scaled by the calibration factor.
  - The circle uses it in the full-atom view, the dissection and `renderAtomDissectFrame`.
- **Python (PC, web, MicroPython):**
  - Two new helpers in `atom_cloud.py`: `valence_subshell()` and `subshell_peak_radii()`.
  - `AtomPreset` exposes `peak_r` (the valence subshell's) and `peak_r_by_subshell`. `build_dissection_steps()` now carries each step's circle radius.
  - `atom_view_pc.py`, `web_atom.py`, `screenshot.py` and `micropython/atom_view.py` draw at those radii.
  - The full-atom circle uses the valence subshell rather than the subshell that reaches furthest by p90. In the hydrogenic model (web and PC default), carbon's 2s reaches further than its 2p. With the HFS tables the two agree for all 92 elements.

**Docs**
- The README, `RUN_HFS.md`, `hfs_tables.py`, `hfs_atomsfe.py`, `atom_view_pc.py`, `plot_atomic_radii.py` and `multielectronic_atoms.html` no longer attribute the offsets to self-interaction error.

**Out of scope:** Pd is left as is on purpose. Its factor is now 2.88, because the 169 pm literature value is a 5s-type radius and Pd's valence subshell is 4d.

## Validation

- **Validation harness:** `python3 pc/validate_atoms.py --model hfs --all --strict`
  - old table: **STRICT FAIL**, H and He at 2.27× the literature radius
  - new table: **STRICT PASS**, period 2 median 0.95, period 4 median 0.89
- **Device code on the host:** `atom_cloud.cpp`, `hfs_radial.cpp` and `pointcloud.cpp` were built with g++ `-Wall -Wextra` against stubbed ESP headers, with no warnings.
  - Hydrogenic `peakR` is exact: 1s = 1, 2p = 4, 3d = 9, 2s = 3+√5 a₀.
  - With the HFS tables, the outer `peakR` equals the Clementi-Raimondi value: H 53, C 67, Fe 156, Xe 108, Au 174, U 175 pm.
- **Python ports:** for H, C, Ne, Fe, Xe and Au, the full-atom circle radius equals the Clementi-Raimondi value in all three: PC with tables, web/hydrogenic, and MicroPython tables.
- **Screenshots:** `pc/screenshot.py` atom and Fe dissection screenshots render with the new circles.
- **Generator output:** regenerated `hfs_tables.bin` is byte-identical.
- **Not run:** the device build and on-hardware test (`pio run`, `pio run -t uploadfs`) still need to be done. The data changes only reach the board after `uploadfs`.

## [4.15.1] - 2026-09-28

### Fixed

- **The notices refresh made the pull request it was fixing unmergeable** (`template/.github/workflows/refresh-notices.yml`) — the workflow regenerated `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` on a Dependabot cargo branch with an ordinary `git commit` and `git push`, which produces an **unsigned** commit. `signing-commit.json` requires signed commits on `~ALL` branches and excludes exactly `refs/heads/dependabot/**/*`, so that push is accepted — and the file's own comment concluded from this that the API route would only be needed "if that exclusion is ever narrowed."

  ⚠ **The exclusion does not reach the merge, and that is the defect.** `main` is not excluded, so a pull request carrying an unsigned commit cannot be merged into it at all. No approval unblocks it either, because what refuses is `required_signatures` rather than a review rule — which makes it look like a review problem and sends whoever hits it after the wrong fix first.

  Measured on a real pull request in a generated project, not reasoned about: all twelve required contexts green, `statusCheckRollup: SUCCESS`, an approval given by the repository owner, and `mergeStateStatus` still `BLOCKED`. Its two commits were Dependabot's own at `verified: true` — Dependabot signs — and this workflow's at `verified: false, reason: unsigned`. So every cargo pull request that needs a notices refresh, which is all of them, was unmergeable until somebody re-committed the same bytes by hand.

  The commit is now created through GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch`, which signs what it writes. `expectedHeadOid` makes it a compare-and-swap, so a push landing between the read and the write fails the mutation instead of silently reverting it. Attribution still lands on the App rather than on `github.actor` — the mutation credits the token's owner and offers no author override, which is the behaviour wanted here anyway, and it removes the `git config` dance and the `/users/{bot}` lookup that existed only to fake it.

  ⚠ The result is **verified rather than assumed**: the workflow reads `verification.verified` back from the new commit and fails loudly if it is not `true`. A commit the API declined to sign is the exact failure this change exists to prevent, so it is not left to be discovered by the next person who cannot merge.

author: eimanw
body:
The last two HIGH findings were msgpack 1.1.2 (GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964) and setuptools 70.3.0 (CVE-2025-47273), and neither was actually installed. Both are lines in pip's own _vendor/vendor.txt, the manifest of what pip bundles, which Trivy parses as an installed package list. Upgrading the real ones to pip 26.2.1 and setuptools 84.0.0 left the report unchanged for exactly that reason: the versions on disk were never what was being read.

The app runs uvicorn out of /opt/venv and installs nothing at runtime, so both package managers are removed from the final stage instead of being upgraded or added to an ignore file. That deletes the reported code rather than explaining it away, shrinks the image, and leaves a runtime that cannot install anything even if a process in it is compromised.

Verified locally: fastapi, uvicorn, sqlalchemy, alembic, redis, openai and app.main all still import in the built image, and no pip or setuptools remains under site-packages.

author: lacvapps
body:
Sets `METAL_ASSIGN_TIMEOUT_MS=90000` on the staging API. It's staging only for now; production-us and production-eu follow in a separate PR once this checks out.

After a rootfs rebuild, every stale project cold-boots on its next open, and those boots routinely run past the 30s default. The wake page already polls and rejoins the boot running on the host. Chat and render requests don't: they fail at 30s even though the boot is still going. During the v2.0.17 rollout that showed up as `get_pod_url` "assign timed out" errors, plus failed render and chat-stream requests.

The trade-off is that failover gets slower when a host accepts the connection and then hangs. A host that's down or refusing connections still fails fast.

author: mojjj
body:
Not a defect the port introduced, but one only the port hits: **EF Core cannot translate what EF6 tolerated.**

```csharp
db.Accounts.FirstOrDefault(x => x.Name == name)
    ?? db.Accounts.FirstOrDefault(x => x.Name.Equals(name, StringComparison.CurrentCultureIgnoreCase));
```

The first query translates. **The fallback does not** — EF Core throws `InvalidOperationException` on `string.Equals` with a `StringComparison`. And because it sits behind a `??`, it runs **only when the exact match finds nothing**.

So `AccountByName` threw for precisely the *"no such account"* answer that every caller detects by testing the result for null. `AccountVerify`, which signs players in, had the same line.

## Why nothing caught it

Every check written before this used a name that **already existed** — the lobby probe registers and logs in as `LobbyProbe`, the battle probe picks accounts out of the fixture. The working half was exercised over and over; the broken half never was.

It surfaced only when a context captured from a real engine named a player the fixture had never heard of.

Fixed with `ToLower()`, which translates on both stacks. `tools/battle-result-probe` now asks about a name that does not exist **first, before anything else**, and the positive control — restoring the old query — reproduces the throw.

## The rest: the two ends of the game chain join

The dedicated probe writes its finished `SpringBattleContext` out (`ZK_BATTLE_CONTEXT_OUT`); the storing probe reads it back (`ZK_BATTLE_CONTEXT_IN`). What gets stored is now a context **a real engine produced**, not one a test wrote:

```
   ok    captured from a real engine: founder=probe, map=Bluescreen fields v2, game=Probe Game 1.0
   ok    the captured battle was stored (155)
   ok    every player the engine reported was written (1 of 1)
   ok    the engine's own game id was stored
```

Its founder, map and game are created inside the same rolled-back transaction, because the fixture has never heard of them. That is not a workaround — a real deployment has those rows because the account registered and the registrar published the map. Creating them states the prerequisite out loud.

`tools/dotnet.sh` forwards the two new variables. It does **not** forward arbitrary environment, which is why the capture silently did nothing at first: the file was never written and the storing end quietly used its built-in context instead — a pass that meant less than it appeared to.

## Verified

- the site **and** the lobby server build under mono, exit 0, **0 errors**
- **46/46** EF6 database tests
- EF Core `read` and `write` harnesses, the host harness, the lobby probe
- **125 passed / 4 skipped**
- the whole engine-to-database chain green

author: basnijholt
body:
## Summary

The local shell approval, on the macOS card or in the `mindroom desktop run` terminal, is the only thing between a paired agent, which anyone who can message it can steer, and `/bin/sh -c` as the local user.
The docs promise that the approver sees the exact command and that the agent cannot approve its own command.
Each item below broke one of those promises for an agent on an allowlisted requester and agent pair with shell requests enabled locally.

- **Agent input could answer the approval.**
  Shell starts run on their own bridge lane, so while `run_shell` waited for approval the agent could still send `click`, `type_text`, `keypress`, and the other app control actions.
  The macOS approval panel floats above the leased app's window, so a click at the right point could press **Approve Once**, and keys typed into an allowlisted terminal could answer the terminal prompt.
  Fix: `DesktopShell.agent_input()` fences every app control action except `launch_app`.
  From the moment a request needs a decision until it is answered, new input is refused; input already in flight finishes first, and the request is presented one second later so events it posted have reached their target.
  Input and a visible approval are therefore never live together on the bridge's event loop.
  The pause covers one bridge's own approvals, so the docs now say to run at most one bridge per graphical session.
- **Agents could control MindRoom itself.**
  The macOS app offered MindRoom's own bundle in its application list, and with no request pending an agent could click **Allow Without Asking…**, renew its control lease, or add apps.
  Fix: saved configuration and `set_allowed_apps` refuse `chat.mindroom.menubar` and `chat.mindroom.desktophelper`, the bridge policy refuses them as a backstop for one-run `--allow-app` overrides, and the app no longer lists either.
  The docs now warn that controlling a terminal, a scripting or automation app, `primary-screen`, or a browser or Matrix client signed in as the user hands the agent the user's own authority.
- **Padding could hide part of a command.**
  Thousands of newlines or spaces pushed the tail of a command below the macOS card's 160-point scroll box, or scrolled its start off a terminal, with no warning.
  Fix: `run_shell` refuses a `command` or `cwd` with a run of more than 64 whitespace or invisible characters, more than two blank lines in a row, or more than 8 stacked combining marks, before any approval surface sees it.
  Invisible characters are the default-ignorable letters and marks outside the control and format categories (Hangul fillers, combining grapheme joiner, variation selectors) plus the Braille blank and null notehead.
  The terminal now escapes every space except the ASCII space and those invisible characters, and prints the command's length in characters and lines right above the choices.
  The macOS card shows the whole command above the buttons instead of clipping it, shows its size, escapes the same characters with the existing warning, and lays out the command and working folder in a text field whose paragraphs use a left-to-right base writing direction, so leading right-to-left text cannot reverse how a line reads and a copy is exactly the shown text.
- **A new request could replace the reviewed one under live buttons.**
  After the person answered request A, the reply still listed A as pending, and a request B arriving within the next status tick replaced A's text under the same, immediately active buttons.
  Fix: a decision clears the pending request at once, so the reply shows it settled, and the macOS card keeps **Approve Once** and **Approve & Allow…** disabled for one second after a request appears or replaces another one.
- **The working directory was inspected before approval.**
  `run_shell` checked `Path(cwd).is_dir()` before asking, so an agent could learn which directories exist from the error and its timing.
  Fix: only the form of `cwd` is checked before approval; existence is checked after approval, before the command starts.
- **Untargeted keystrokes could reach another app.**
  `type_text` without an element and `keypress` checked the allowed app once, then posted keys to whichever app was frontmost, for example a terminal the person switched to.
  Fix: a new `prepare_keyboard` guard checks that the validated app is still active before each 20-character chunk and before each chord.
  It reports that nothing was typed when focus was lost before the first key, and an unknown outcome when it was lost partway.
  Untargeted `type_text` also refuses line breaks, tabs, and other control characters; Enter and Tab go through the guarded `keypress`.

## Tests

New regression tests, each failing before its fix:

- `tests/test_desktop_bridge.py`: `test_app_input_is_refused_while_a_shell_command_awaits_approval` (11 app control actions), `test_shell_approval_is_shown_only_after_app_input_in_progress_finishes`, `test_launch_app_still_works_while_a_shell_command_awaits_approval`, and `test_mindroom_itself_can_never_be_an_allowlisted_app` (both bundle IDs).
- `tests/test_desktop_native_config.py` and `tests/test_desktop_native_host.py`: saved configuration and `set_allowed_apps` refuse both bundle IDs.
- `tests/test_desktop_shell.py`: padding refused before approval (14 cases, including invisible characters and stacked combining marks), working directory checked only after approval and padded `cwd` refused, decision clears the pending request, input refused while pending and while held back, approval held back behind input and its settle delay on the injected clock, expiry while held back, and revoke while held back.
  `test_ordinary_blank_lines_and_indentation_still_reach_approval` pins ordinary layout, accents, emoji, and Devanagari that must still reach approval.
- `tests/test_desktop_shell_prompt.py`: space and invisible-character escaping, and the size line right above the choices.
- `tests/test_desktop_provider.py` and `tests/test_desktop_accessibility.py`: untargeted typing and key chords stop once the app loses focus, a failure before the first key reports nothing typed, untargeted text refuses control characters, and the primary-screen target needs no focus guard.
- Swift: `DesktopApprovalWindowTests.testWholeCommandIsShownLeftToRightWithoutClipping` renders a 60-line right-to-left command in the real approval window and checks the field is tall enough for every line and laid out left to right; `DesktopControlPresentationTests` covers escaping, the size label, and the unchanged copied text; `DesktopControlStoreTests` covers MindRoom being excluded from the application list.

Commands run:

- `uv run pytest tests/test_desktop_*.py tests/test_import_graph.py tests/test_shell_execution.py`: 919 passed.
  On this host `os.defpath` has no `cat` or `sleep`, so these were run with coreutils prepended to `os.defpath`; without that, the existing shell tests that call those programs fail on `main` too.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files`: passed.
- `uv run tach check --dependencies --interfaces`: passed.
- Full suite `uv run pytest -n 6`: 27,045 passed, 23 skipped, 1 xfailed, 28 failed.
  26 of the failures are the `os.defpath` issue above and pass with coreutils prepended.
  `tests/test_coding_tools.py::TestGrep::test_grep_rg_and_fallback_parity_subdirectory` also fails at the base commit.
  `tests/test_background_script_approval.py::test_launch_preapproval_does_not_expand_from_live_script_config[missing-static-proxy]` failed once under load and passes alone; it does not touch desktop code.
- CI `swift-tests` (arm64 and x86_64): 169 tests, 0 failures.

## Summary by Sourcery

Harden desktop shell approval and agent-controlled input so local users can review the full command without agent-driven interference.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent agents from interacting with shell approval surfaces by pausing bridge input while approval is pending and delaying presentation until in-flight input settles.
