author: hexplus
body:
## Release 1.9.1: one Escape closes exactly one overlay

### Summary

Every dismissable overlay added its own `keydown` listener on `document` while it was open. When overlays were nested, for example a `DropdownMenu` inside a `Popover` inside a `Dialog`, or one dialog inside another, all of those listeners received the same key press, so a single Escape closed every overlay at once. Most overlays also closed without calling `preventDefault()`, so the rest of the page couldn't tell the key had already been used.

Calling `preventDefault()` alone doesn't fix the nesting problem. Listeners on `document` run in the order they were added, so the outer overlay usually handles the event before the inner one can mark it as handled.

This PR adds a single shared Escape stack that every dismissable overlay uses.

### New: `src/lib/dismissable-layer.ts`

- **One ordered stack of open overlays.** The most recently opened overlay is on top. An overlay that is closed and then reopened goes back on top.
- **One `document` `keydown` listener.** It is added when the first overlay opens and removed when the last one closes. Nothing touches `document` when the module is imported, so it is safe for SSR.
- **One Escape dismisses exactly one layer.** It closes only the top overlay and calls `preventDefault()`. Other keys are ignored. An Escape pressed while nothing is open is left untouched. `stopPropagation()` is never called.
- **An Escape that was already handled is ignored.** If the event arrives with `defaultPrevented` already set, a handler closer to the focused element has used it (the `Select` trigger, the `Combobox` input), so no overlay is closed. Without this, pressing Escape on a focused `Select` trigger inside a `Dialog` would close both.
- **API.**
  - `registerEscapeLayer(onEscape)` returns a function that removes exactly that registration. Calling it more than once is harmless.
  - `createDismissableLayer(onEscape)` returns a handle with `activate()` / `deactivate()`, following the same pattern as `createScrollLock`. Calling `activate()` while the overlay is already registered keeps its current position, so an overlay that stays open is never added twice.

### Components migrated

`Dialog`, `Sheet`, `Drawer`, `DropdownMenu`, `Popover`, `Select` (`SelectContent`), `ContextMenu`, `Menubar` and `NavigationMenu` no longer add their own `keydown` listener to `document`. Each one registers with the stack when it opens and unregisters when it closes or is disposed.

`Tooltip`, `HoverCard` and `Combobox` handle Escape with a listener on their own element rather than on `document`, so they are not changed. The keyboard navigation handlers (arrow keys, Home/End, Enter) are also unchanged.

No public API changes. Portal and visual behavior are unchanged.

### Resulting behavior

```text
Dialog
└── Popover
    └── DropdownMenu

Escape #1 → closes DropdownMenu only
Escape #2 → closes Popover only
Escape #3 → closes Dialog only
Escape #4 → nothing is open; the event is not prevented

## What changes

**1. The header's right-hand cluster is now one account menu**, opened from the avatar:
- the signed-in name or email at the top (falls back to the workspace name, as the avatar did),
- a **Dark mode** switch,
- **Sign out**, only when `onSignOut` is given (Stytch mode). Developer, password and Access modes show the name and the switch only.

Accessibility: this uses the shadcn/Radix `DropdownMenu`, so the menu has proper menu roles, arrow-key navigation, and focus returns to the avatar on Escape (asserted in `e2e/auth.spec.ts`). The trigger keeps its `Signed in as …` / `Signed in to …` name. The switch is a `menuitemcheckbox` drawn as a switch, because ARIA doesn't allow `role="switch"` inside a `menu`. Screen readers announce "Dark mode, checked". Flipping it keeps the menu open.

**System mode is no longer a visible choice, but it is still the default.** With nothing stored, the app follows `prefers-color-scheme` live. Flipping the switch stores `light` or `dark`, and that choice wins from then on, reloads included. `theme.ts`, `useTheme`, the storage key and the `index.html` bootstrap are unchanged, so a stored `system` value from the old toggle still means "follow the machine". The email preview, canvas and thumbnail stay light in both modes (`e2e/theme.spec.ts`). ADR-29 has an "Update 2026-09-29" paragraph.

**2. The workspace switcher shows at every width.** It was `hidden … xl:inline-flex`, which made "Workspace settings" and "New workspace" unreachable below 1280px. Another session had planned this fix; **this PR takes it over.** Below `xl` the switcher is capped at `max-w-40` and truncates long names. To make room, the product nav now gets its own row below `lg` (1024px) instead of below `md`. At 768px, brand + switcher + nav no longer fit on one row, and the overflow e2e test caught it.

**3. Sign out on the screens outside the header** (scope addition): `NoWorkspace`, `UnknownWorkspace` and `ListError` now show `Signed in as …` and, in Stytch mode only, a Sign out button. Previously, someone who signed in with the wrong account had no way out. A new `useSignedInIdentity` hook serves both the header and these screens, and replaces the inline fetch in `App.tsx`.

**4. The Primitives row in the code editor is removed**, along with `primitives.ts` and the `CodeEditor` imperative handle (`insertAtCursor` / `focus` / `indentSnippet`), which only it used. The tab strip now sits directly under the compile strip.

author: nilsbaumgartner1994
body:
## Was

Tagesablauf (deutsche Zeit, ganzjährig):

| Uhrzeit | Workflow | Was |
|---|---|---|
| 18:00 | `sync-fork.yml` | Fork-Sync (vorher 13:00 UTC) |
| 19:00 | `backend-daily-restart.yml` (neu) | Update und Neustart aller Backend-Server |
| 20:00 | `backend-daily-health-check.yml` (neu) | Health-Check; bei Fehler roter Lauf und optional eine Mail |

- **`backend-daily-restart.yml`**: Führt auf `test`, `swosy` und `studi-futter` denselben SSH-Deploy aus wie „🚀 Deploy Backend (Manual)“ (`scripts/update-and-generate-env.sh`: pull, `.env` neu erzeugen, build, Container neu starten).
  - Läuft nur in `rocket-meals/rocket-meals`.
  - `fail-fast: false`: Ist ein Server nicht erreichbar, werden die anderen trotzdem neu gestartet.
  - Kann auch manuell gestartet werden.
- **`sync-fork.yml`**: Der Sync läuft jetzt eine Stunde vor dem Neustart. So ziehen die Kunden-Server (`rocket-meals/swosy`, `rocket-meals/studi-futter`) beim Neustart einen aktuellen Fork.
- **`backend-daily-health-check.yml`**: Prüft `https://<host>/rocket-meals/api/server/health` auf allen drei Servern.
  - Gesund heißt HTTP 200 und Status `ok` oder `warn`. `warn` zählt als erreichbar, weil die Server zwischen `ok` und `warn` wechseln. Es erscheint nur als Warnung im Lauf.
  - Drei Versuche pro Server, eine Minute Abstand.
  - Bei einem Fehler wird der Lauf rot. Eine Mail geht nur raus, wenn die SMTP-Secrets gesetzt sind (per `curl`, ohne Action von Drittanbietern). Fehlen sie, wird die Mail mit einer Warnung übersprungen, die die fehlenden Secrets nennt.
  - Läuft nur in `rocket-meals/rocket-meals`.
- **README-Badge `🩺 Backend Health`**: Zeigt das Ergebnis des Health-Checks. Das Badge zeigt immer den letzten Lauf. Deshalb prüft der zweite, zeitlich nicht passende Zeitplan-Lauf nichts, sondern übernimmt das Ergebnis des letzten abgeschlossenen Laufs (Job `mirror-last-result`). Sonst würde im Sommer der 21:00-Lauf grün enden und einen Ausfall um 20:00 überdecken.
- **`.github/actions/berlin-time-schedule-gate`** (neu): GitHub-Cron läuft in UTC und kennt keine Sommerzeit. Alle drei Workflows planen deshalb die CEST- und die CET-Variante ein. Das Gate vergleicht `github.event.schedule` mit dem aktuellen Berliner UTC-Offset und lässt nur den passenden Lauf durch. Das klappt auch dann, wenn GitHub den Lauf verspätet startet.
- **`deploy-backend-manual.yml`**: Teilt sich mit dem täglichen Neustart eine Concurrency-Gruppe pro Server (`deploy-backend-<host>`). So laufen nie zwei Deploys gleichzeitig auf demselben Server.
- **README**: Badge, Neustart, Health-Check und die optionalen Secrets sind dokumentiert.

## Optionale Repository-Secrets für die Mail

| Secret | Inhalt |
|---|---|
| `SMTP_HOST` | SMTP-Server |
| `SMTP_PORT` | `465` (TLS) oder z. B. `587` (STARTTLS), Standard `587` |
| `SMTP_USERNAME` / `SMTP_PASSWORD` | Zugangsdaten |
| `HEALTHCHECK_MAIL_TO` | Empfänger, mehrere durch Komma getrennt |
| `HEALTHCHECK_MAIL_FROM` | optional, Standard ist `SMTP_USERNAME` |

## Prüfung

- `actionlint` meldet für alle vier Workflows keine Fehler.
- Gate-Skript für CEST, CET und `workflow_dispatch` durchgespielt.
- Health-Check-Skript lokal gegen die echten Server laufen lassen, dazu ein absichtlich nicht existierender Host. Ergebnis: ✅ / 🟡 `warn` / ❌ nach allen Versuchen, `failed=true`, Step-Summary korrekt.
- Mail-Step in drei Fällen getestet:
  - Ohne Secrets: Warnung, Exit 0, Mail wird übersprungen, der Lauf wird danach trotzdem rot.
  - Mit nur einem Teil der Secrets: Warnung nennt die fehlenden Secrets.
  - Voll konfiguriert gegen einen lokalen SMTP-Server mit STARTTLS und Login: Mail kommt an.
- Mirror-Job: Die `jq`-Auswertung liefert bei `failure` rot, bei `success` und ohne bisherige Läufe grün. Flags und JSON-Felder von `gh run list` habe ich gegen `gh` 2.63 geprüft.

## Hinweise

- Der Neustart ist ein **Update und Neustart**: Er deployt jeden Abend den aktuellen Stand von `master` bzw. des Forks.
- Geplante GitHub-Läufe starten zur vollen Stunde oft ein paar Minuten zu spät.
- Übernimmt der zweite Zeitplan-Lauf einen Fehler, verschickt GitHub dafür eine eigene Fehlerbenachrichtigung. Eine Mail über SMTP geht dabei nicht raus.
- Die Server-Liste gibt es jetzt dreimal: im manuellen Deploy (`ALL_HOSTS`), im Neustart und im Health-Check. An allen Stellen steht ein Hinweis, sie synchron zu halten.

author: randomcash
body:
## What changed

Quotes were floored to whole base units while settlement demanded `amount_received >= amount`, so a customer who paid the quote exactly could be a few wei short and the invoice could never settle. Two changes: quotes now round **up** (server and mcp-server), and settlement accepts a per-store shortfall tolerance, with a non-zero server default. When a tolerance is what settles an invoice, the shortfall and the setting behind it are recorded.

Tolerance design (the ticket left these open):
- **Relative, in percent of the invoice amount**, not absolute. Invoices can be denominated in crypto as well as fiat, so an absolute figure would mean wildly different things per currency.
- Default `0.0001`%; ceiling `1`%. The API refuses above the ceiling (422) and below zero; it never clamps. A DB CHECK backs it up.
- Stored in `store_settlement_settings` (unique per store, cascade delete), beside `stores` like the token policy. No row means the server default.
- The comparison stays `BigDecimal`; the tolerance is an explicit allowance, not reduced precision.

## How I verified

New `event_consumer/tests/settlement_tolerance.rs` drives `handle_payment_confirmed`: 2.68e-14 short of 20 settles and records an allowance (source `default`); an exact payment records none; 19.99 of 20 (0.05%) does not settle under the default but does under a store setting of 0.1 (source `store`). `settlement.rs` unit tests cover the ceiling, an inclusive boundary, and that zero tolerance demands the full amount. Quote tests assert the ticket's case rounds up. I did not run an ablation (default set to zero) by hand. The migration and its CHECK were applied and reverted against a scratch Postgres database; the `#[ignore]`d Postgres integration tests were not run, and the new Pg repository has no test of its own.

`test_handle_payment_confirmed_one_unit_below_exact_amount_stays_unpaid` now sets an explicit zero tolerance: it tests that 2^96-scale comparison does not round, and a one-unit gap there is inside the default tolerance.

## How it is reached

- Settlement: `handle_payment_confirmed` in `confirmation_handler.rs` (both the paid and late-paid transitions use it).
- `GET/PUT/DELETE /stores/{id}/settlement-tolerance` (store-settings permission).
- `GET /invoices/{id}/settlement-allowance` returns the recorded shortfall, percent and source.

## What to look at hardest

The default and ceiling values are my choice. Tolerance is applied to the late-paid transition too. The new traits live in `data-service`, not commons, to avoid a cross-repo pin change; consequently `InvoiceResponse` (in commons) has no allowance field, hence the separate endpoint.

## What I did not do

The invoice quote's stored rate was not reproduced: the ticket's invoice quoted 10 wei below 20 × its stored rate, so quoting used a rate with more precision than stored. Rounding up fixes this regardless. No client UI for the setting.

## Sensitive paths

Migrations (new tables), `server/src/api/invoices*` (quote rounding, new route), and settlement/paid-decision logic in the confirmation handler. Check that the tolerance can only widen acceptance by at most 1% and that the default is never zero.

---

### Commits

```
7944156 RCS-466: Exact payment of the quote can settle: quote rounds up, settlement has a per-store tolerance
```

Opened by the autonomous worker for **RCS-466**. Sensitive paths (auth, crypto, `evm/`, wallet and key derivation, migrations, invoice/payment/payout/refund handlers, secrets, movement of funds) are human-merged without exception.

## Summary

Adds Blender-style modifiers to the Prop Creator modeler and makes the Prop Creator easy to use on phones and tablets.

### Modifiers
The modeler now has 15 non-destructive modifiers, applied on export. The **Add Modifier** menu is grouped like Blender's.

**Generate**
- **Array** and **Radial Array**: copies in a row, or around an axis.
- **Bevel**: chamfers edges sharper than an angle, clamped so faces do not overlap.
- **Boolean**: difference, union or intersect with another object.
  - Uses BSP CSG, with T-junction repair so results are closed meshes.
  - Selecting a cutter and then the target makes the cutter a **Helper**: drawn as wire, not exported.
- **Decimate**: collapse or planar.
- **Mirror**, **Solidify**, **Subdivision Surface**, **Triangulate**, **Weld**, **Wireframe**.

**Deform**
- **Cast**, **Displace** (noise), **Simple Deform** (twist / bend / taper / stretch), **Smooth**.

Each modifier is a foldable card with enable, reorder, duplicate, apply and remove. Reference cycles between booleans resolve safely.

### Responsive / touch
**Modeler**
- The header scrolls in one row, and Done stays visible.
- The properties sidebar can be hidden with `N` or a header button.
- Below 768 px there is a bottom tab bar (Scene / Object / Modifiers / Material / Mesh / FiveM) that opens a sliding sheet.
- Touch:

**Pack view**

**Both:** camera framing uses the narrower field of view, so portrait screens fit the model.

author: patrykmolczan
body:
## Root cause

The Dashboard armed a **12-second timer on mount** and called `signOut()` if `loadData()` had not finished:

```js
useEffect(() => {
  if (!loading) return
  const timer = setTimeout(() => { signOut() }, 12000)
  return () => clearTimeout(timer)
}, [loading])
```

`loadData()` serially fetches lookups → projects → filter-options → analysts, and **`/api/projects` alone is ~1.8 MB / 2,000 records**. Measured server-side performance is healthy (Lambda avg **281 ms**, 24h max 3.4 s, cold start ~0.6 s), so roughly **10.8 of the 12 seconds** is just transferring, parsing and rendering that payload on the user’s device.

On a slow VPN or cellular link that exceeds 12 s — and the app then **wiped a completely valid Cognito session** and hard-redirected to the login page.

This is the cause of the “SSO succeeds but I get kicked back to the login page” reports affecting ~4 of 88 users.

### Why it looked like an SSO problem

| Observation | Explanation |
|---|---|
| Azure/IT logs show SSO success | SSO genuinely succeeded ~10 s earlier |
| Our login audit shows 11/11 success | Recorded on the callback page, before the dashboard loads |
| “Kicked out as the Dashboard was loading” | Literally what the timer did |
| Same user failed on Chrome, Edge **and iPhone Safari** | Same network → same slow load on all three |
| Clearing cache/cookies never helped | Irrelevant to transfer speed |
| Only ~4 of 88 users | Only those on slow links crossed the 12 s line |

## The fix

A slow network is not an expired session. The timer **no longer touches the session at all** — it only releases the blocking spinner so the dashboard and its Refresh button become usable, and any still-in-flight request populates the page normally when it lands. Threshold raised 12 s → 45 s so normal slow loads are never interrupted at all.

**Dead-session protection is fully preserved** — unchanged — by the separate periodic **30-second session-expiry check** immediately below it, which calls `getSession()` and signs out when there is no valid session.

## QA — no regressions

- `tsc -b --noEmit`: **clean**
- `npm run build`: **clean**
- `eslint`: **no new issues.** One pre-existing `exhaustive-deps` warning removed (signOut no longer referenced by that effect); 11 pre-existing errors unchanged.
- **Compiled-bundle diff, baseline vs fixed, across the entire 1.6 MB bundle — exactly ONE line differs:**

```diff
- let e=setTimeout(()=>{i()},12e3);      // i = signOut
+ let e=setTimeout(()=>{I(!1)},45e3);    // I(!1) = setLoading(false)
```

That is conclusive proof of zero unintended behavioural change anywhere else in the application.

**1 file changed, 16 insertions, 4 deletions** — 2 functional lines, the rest explanatory comments.

**Merge theLomax/SODaVis-Tests `import-formats` with or before this.** The `test/private` pointer is its commit.

RefTown's standard export is `.xlsx` (KB #237) and its public import templates are `.xls`; the importer read text only.

- **Excel reader** (`src/import/excel.ts`): SheetJS 0.20.3 from its official CDN (the npm-registry copy is stale), loaded only when a spreadsheet is picked (~160 KB gzip, its own chunk). The first sheet, or one named Games, becomes the same rows the CSV path produces. Dates and times are decoded from their serials, so no timezone moves a game. Excel is recognized by its first bytes, not its name.
- **RefTown format** (`profiles/reftown.ts`), built from RefTown's public import template plus the export's `GameID` and `Official_N` (KB #267). **No real export has been checked.** The template has no status and no fee column:
  - a format can default the status when the file has no status column (a blank cell in a status column that exists is still unknown);
  - a file with no fee column marks its games' pay as unknown (`fees.notInSource`), so no fee anomaly is raised per game. This applies to any format, custom ones included.
- Repeated `Official` headers pair in order; official/position columns no longer count toward detection confidence.
- **Format picker** on Import: auto-detect (default), platforms, saved formats, or map a new one. Shows each platform's export steps and limits the file dialog. A mismatched pick is flagged with a one-click switch; changing the format re-reads the file under review; the file box is cleared after each read, so picking the same file again after Cancel works (it silently did nothing before).
- The review step warns when a file has no pay: income and $/hr read low until pay can be added (plan 6.6).
- Plan items 6.5–6.7 added (import formats, RefTown pay, localization); the readme's "RefTown is a configuration exercise" line corrected.

**Testing:** 405 unit tests pass. The build succeeds with xlsx split out. In the app, both themes: an invented RefTown `.xlsx` imports 3 games, a re-import offers 0 new, a wrong format pick is flagged and switched, changing format mid-review works, and there are no fee anomalies or console errors. `test/private/e2e.mjs` passes with the real Assignr CSV through the new reader.

- Select the trusted build adapter after Next's tsconfig path rewriting; omit the built-in browser chat SDK's placeholder bearer while preserving explicit request credentials.

The probes match the SDK's security settings and isolated runtime layout, omit the extra ignore-user-config guard, and use the actual production bridge without an enabled-tools filter. These establish native restrictions and positive MCP dispatch, not real provider completion or customer throughput.
- Minimal version admission adds only exact `0.157.1`. Both admitted versions/models retain executable digest/path/version checks and all seven restricted catalog assertions; adjacent releases and cross-version attestations are rejected. The environment/dispatch regression group passes **2 suites / 35 tests**, plus full typecheck and changed-file lint.

The real Next resolver and installed OpenAI SDK tests pass 7/7. The actual ProcessNode → ModelHandler → restricted Codex regression and dispatch group passes 12/12: three approved MCP tools, no local executors, ordinary sticky arming preserved, and a reintroduced synthetic resource offer still rejected before SDK startup. Two new error-provenance regressions failed before the fix, reproducing the exact trusted-error-to-availability mask through production protected MCP dispatch, then passed; the affected bundle/private dispatch group passes 3 suites / 16 tests, typecheck and lint. All required CI gates, full suites and the published baseline passed on `51987ca4`. All required CI gates also passed on `2a52968c`. All required CI gates passed on preceding exact head `8c184052`, including full suites/published baseline, isolated baseline, Linux/Windows production builds, lint/types, release safety, installer and persona checks; no skips or quarantines were added. The older local broad diagnostic was stopped after authoritative CI completed.

The minimal concurrent verification change adds eight regressions covering shared hashing/version checks, per-caller file checks, identical-key rejection eviction, sequential rehash, distinct digest/version/path isolation, same-length byte drift with unchanged mtime, identical-byte file replacement, symlink retargeting and fresh caller policy. The environment/dispatch group passes **2 suites / 43 tests**, final full typecheck and changed-file lint pass, and independent source/test review passed. This is a source-level reduction in repeated verification work, not a real 500-request capacity acceptance claim.

Failed native MCP tool events now emit an error-level fixed diagnostic code/category and trusted run/node/known-tool labels. Raw native errors, URLs, item IDs, arguments and results are excluded; tool transcripts and invocation statistics remain bridge-owned, with no retry. Four regressions verify failed pre-handler event capture, sensitive-field exclusion and bridge deduplication. The private/ordinary Codex adapter group passes **2 suites / 57 tests**, full typecheck/lint/diff checks and independent review pass. Successful-process startup stderr is not exposed by the installed SDK, so this diagnostic observes emitted native tool failures and does not claim to recover discarded startup warnings or establish their cause.

## Packaging

This PR contains domain-neutral hooks and reference fixes. The optional hackathon banking policy, routes, compatibility shims, signer dependencies and application acceptance tests are preserved on `codex/banking-runtime-integration` and reviewed separately against this branch.


### Digest-before-execution correction

Final exact head `8f8c571f374eccee912c0160d2326fc0b9e0ff73` rejects a CLI digest mismatch immediately after hashing, before launching `--version`; exact version validation and all fresh profile/catalog/path/identity/credential guards remain. The regression proves identical concurrent bad digests share only one hash with zero executable launches, identical retries rehash without execution, and a subsequent valid digest verifies normally. No completed verification cache is added. Environment and dispatch gates pass 2 suites / 47 tests, full typecheck, scoped lint and diff checks pass, and independent review passes. CI is green on exact head `8f8c571f374eccee912c0160d2326fc0b9e0ff73`: full suite and published baseline, isolated suite and baseline, Ubuntu/Windows production builds, lint, typecheck, and Ubuntu/Windows release safety all passed in [verify run 36520306323](https://github.com/mario-andreschak/FLUJO/actions/runs/36520306323); [installer run 36520306266](https://github.com/mario-andreschak/FLUJO/actions/runs/36520306266) and [persona acceptance run 36520306297](https://github.com/mario-andreschak/FLUJO/actions/runs/36520306297) also passed. author: synap5e
body:
## TL;DR

- **Changes:** on Windows, the hardware UUID behind `installation_id` is now read with one PowerShell call plus a quick `reg query` (`si.uuid()`) instead of the three PowerShell calls that `si.system()` makes one after another. macOS and Linux are unchanged.
- **Justification:** the three cold `powershell.exe` spawns often miss the 2 s boot budget. A launch that misses falls back to a random id. #1583 made those launches reuse the persisted id instead of rotating it; this PR makes them miss less often in the first place.
- **Stakes:** feature-flag rollouts and per-install targeting key on this id. A machine that keeps missing the budget ends up on a random id rather than its machine-derived one.
- **Existing installs:** installs that already have a good id keep it. Both calls read the same WMI field and parse it identically, so the UUID, the hash and the id are unchanged, and nobody is re-bucketed.
- **Reviewer attention:** *small, one function in `deviceId.ts`.* The claim to check is that `si.system().uuid` and `si.uuid().hardware` are byte-identical on Windows (see Migration).

## The bug

- `deriveMachineId()` races the lookup against `MACHINE_ID_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000`. On a timeout, an error or an empty UUID, the launch takes `random_fallback`.
- On Windows, `si.system()` resolves only after three separate cold `powershell.exe` spawns: `Win32_ComputerSystemProduct`, then `MS_Systeminformation` (root/wmi), then `Win32_bios`. Only the first one supplies the UUID.
- Before #1583, about a third of Windows profiles reported more than one `installation_id` over a week (macOS: 0.3%).
  - About half of those were stable most of the time with occasional new ids, which fits timeouts. This PR targets that group.
  - The other half got a new id on every launch, which fits PowerShell/WMI being blocked or broken on those machines. A faster lookup does not help them. #1583's reuse of the persisted id is what keeps them stable.

## The fix

- New `lookupHardwareUuid()`. On `win32` it returns `si.uuid().hardware`. Other platforms still call `si.system()`, so macOS and #1583's Linux machine-id path are unchanged.
- On Windows, `si.uuid()` runs `Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystemProduct | select UUID | fl` in one spawn, plus one `reg query`.
- Timeout, validation, fallback and #1583's reuse rule are unchanged.

## Migration

- **Windows installs whose lookup already succeeds:** no change. Both calls read the same WMI field with the same parsing (`util.getValue(lines, 'uuid', ':').toLowerCase()`), so the UUID, the hash and the id are identical. This was checked against the `systeminformation@5.31.5` source; a mocked test can't prove byte-identity. The dependency is not pinned. Instead, `deviceId.dependency.test.ts` fails CI when the `systeminformation` version resolved in `pnpm-lock.yaml` differs from 5.31.5, with a message to recheck this equivalence on win32 before updating the constant.
- **Windows installs running on a persisted random id:** their next successful lookup replaces it once with the machine-derived id, which is the existing behaviour from #1583. After that the id is stable, and it matches what they'd get after a reinstall.
- **macOS / Linux:** no change.

## Known limitations

- Machines where PowerShell or WMI never answers still run on a persisted random id (#1583 keeps it stable).
- Telling slow machines apart from blocked ones would need a per-launch `id_class` or lookup-duration property. No launch event has one yet, and this PR doesn't add one.

## Validation

- `deviceId.test.ts`: 35 pass, 7 of them new or rewritten for this change.
  - On win32, the UUID is read through `si.uuid()` and `si.system()` is never called.
  - On macOS and Linux, `si.system()` is used and `si.uuid()` is never called.
  - A lookup that never settles falls back at exactly the 2 s budget (still pending at 1999 ms), and keeps the persisted id.
  - If WMI returns no UUID on every launch, the first random id is kept across 3 more boots.
  - Hashing the `si.uuid()` hardware UUID gives the persisted id. Both library calls are mocked, so this test cannot prove byte-identity with `si.system()`; see Migration.
- `deviceId.dependency.test.ts`: the lockfile guard passes at 5.31.5, and fails with the recheck message when the lockfile entry is changed to another version.
- These tests were checked against deliberate breakage: reverting `deviceId.ts` to `main`, routing every platform through `si.uuid()`, and changing the timeout constant each make the relevant new tests fail.
- `typecheck`, ESLint and Prettier pass.
- Not run on a real Windows machine.

## Change breakdown

| Category | Files | Paths | Added | Deleted | Share of changed lines |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Product code | 1 | `src/main/lib/deviceId.ts` | 22 | 1 | 14.4% |
| Test code | 2 | `src/main/lib/deviceId.test.ts`, `src/main/lib/deviceId.dependency.test.ts` | 134 | 3 | 85.6% |

Total changed lines: **160** (added + deleted). No documentation, configuration, generated files, lockfiles or vendored code.

author: yoojin-nam
body:
## Summary

`analyze-stats` `table-types/incremental_value.md` taught two things the methods literature warns against:

1. **"Report ΔC … and the DeLong paired test"** as the test of added value. When nested models are fitted and evaluated on the same data, the DeLong test of ΔAUC misbehaves: its null distribution is not normal and it is conservative for small and moderate effects (Demler, Pencina & D'Agostino, *Stat Med* 2012, doi:10.1002/sim.5328). In simulation its size fell below 0.006, with much lower power than the likelihood-ratio and Wald tests (Vickers, Cronin & Begg, *BMC Med Res Methodol* 2011, doi:10.1186/1471-2288-11-13).
2. **"Prefer continuous NRI or category-free NRI."** The category-free NRI can overstate a marker's incremental value even in independent validation data. With three or more categories the same review recommends against NRI altogether, and it names the improvement in net benefit as the preferred single summary (Kerr et al., *Epidemiology* 2014, doi:10.1097/EDE.0000000000000018).

The `analyze-stats` `SKILL.md` summary contradicted itself on the second point: it warned that continuous NRI "tends to be inflated", then recommended it.

This surfaced while reviewing #542, an external exemplar that had followed this guide faithfully.

## What changed

- **One test, then one estimate.** Whether a prespecified term adds information is tested through its coefficient: a likelihood-ratio test on the same observations in the development data. ΔAUC is then reported as the size of the gain, with a paired CI, not as a second test.
- **Paired DeLong is kept where it belongs.** It stays for comparing two scores frozen before evaluation on held-out patients, which is what it was built for; Chen et al. (*BMC Med Res Methodol* 2013, doi:10.1186/1471-2288-13-98) found it held its nominal type I error in simulation there. For a non-regression augmented model, such as a retrained network, that held-out comparison is the evidence.
- **NRI is optional.** If reported, it is split into event and non-event components (with two categories, these are the changes in sensitivity and specificity). The continuous NRI is never the evidence.
- **Table and code.** The table gains a footnote for the development-cohort LR test and a net-benefit CI column. The code examples are now runnable; the R snippets were run locally with pROC 1.19 and survival, and the Python one with statsmodels.

## Independent review

A Codex adversarial review confirmed every attribution above: Demler, Vickers including the 0.006 figure, Kerr's four NRI claims, the pROC CI sign, and the LR-test code. It also caught one real scoping error in my first draft. That draft read "fitted on the same data" where it meant "fitted and evaluated on the same data", which contradicted the held-out exception. I also took its four corrections to lines that predated this change:

- calibration is assessed on the test set, and any recalibration is done on other data
- which NRI component moved is reported, rather than a non-event-only NRI being called "weak"
- NRI/IDI are optional
- a small ΔC with a wide CI is no evidence of added discrimination, which is not evidence of no added value

## Validation

- `python3 scripts/run_ci_mirror.py`: 251/251 validate-job gates passed
- `gen_skill_docs.py --check` OK; distribution manifest regenerated for the two changed shipped files

author: pointlessbassmusic-byte
body:
The NWS arm beats climatology on four of five dates and is the strongest signal in the stack, so the one test not yet run on it was the one that matters for trading: does it carry anything the *price* hasn't absorbed?

Same threshold-free regression as Results 2 and 5 — (outcome − market) on (NWS − market) — over 168 settled strike-band rows, with a cluster bootstrap over the 28 station-days because a day's six bands share one temperature:

```
beta = +0.036     cluster-bootstrap 95% CI [−0.106, +0.222]     t = 0.43
control (climatology in place of NWS) = −0.004
```

| arm | Brier |
|---|---|
| market | 0.0802 |
| market + β·(NWS − market) | 0.0801 |
| 0.9 market + 0.1 NWS | 0.0804 |
| 0.8 market + 0.2 NWS | 0.0819 |
| NWS | 0.1408 |

Adding the forecast to the price is worth 0.0001 of Brier. Every fixed blend is worse than the price alone. **The market already contains the forecast.**

## The mechanism, by price bucket

| market price | n | NWS says | actual |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.012 | 87 | 0.147 | 0.000 |
| 0.085 | 23 | 0.154 | 0.087 |
| 0.995 | 4 | 0.300 | 1.000 |

Right direction, far too wide a sigma. It beats climatology on direction and loses to a market that is already well calibrated exactly where NWS is not. Tightening sigma on these 28 station-days would be fitting the test set, and is not done.

The weather arm's standing is now exact: a genuine, measured **conventional baseline** for the substrate — the role the protocol always assigned it — and not a source of bets.

Docs only. 168 tests pass.

## Summary
- Investigated a report of incorrect-looking incident counts on session 88970988 (e.g. "11" total shown with "(car contact: 10, off track: 8, invalid: 6)" right next to it, which sums to 24, not 11).
- Confirmed the incidents logic is identical between the main site and any `?brand=` (e.g. AES) view - both render the same `IncidentsCell` component and hit the same `/api/pace/subsessions/:id/pace` endpoint; brand only affects CSS/theming in `PaceLayout.tsx`.
- Root cause: when iRacing gives us an official incident-point total (`pp.incidents`), the inline breakdown shown next to it was still the raw per-lap flag *occurrence* counts (from `lap_events`), which have no arithmetic relation to that total - a single lap can carry more than one flag, so the two numbers were never meant to add up, but showing them side by side implied they should.
- Fix: the official-total case no longer shows the inline breakdown. The flag detail is still available on hover, reworded to say explicitly it's supplementary reference info and won't necessarily sum to the total. The estimated (no official total) case is unchanged, since there the breakdown genuinely underlies the total via the existing point-weighting.

body:
Site estático para **gc.lagoinhajundiai.com.br**, na pasta `gc-lagoinha-jundiai/`. A pessoa informa onde está e encontra os GCs mais próximos, com contato direto com o líder.

## O que o site faz
- Busca por endereço, bairro ou CEP, com sugestões de endereço enquanto a pessoa digita (Mapbox). Também aceita a localização do celular.
- Mostra os 3 GCs mais próximos com a distância e ordena a lista completa pela distância.
- Lista todos os GCs com busca por texto e filtros de dia, público e formato (presencial ou online).
- Cada GC tem um botão de WhatsApp com a mensagem já escrita e um botão "Como chegar" que abre o Google Maps.

## Dados
- Lê a planilha do Google Sheets publicada como CSV (`SHEET_CSV_URL`). Se ela estiver fora do ar, usa a cópia `gcs-backup.csv`, que tem os 35 GCs atuais.
- Organiza sozinho os dados preenchidos de jeitos diferentes: horários como `20H` e `19H30`, nome e telefone no mesmo campo, abreviações como `JD` e a cidade depois de hífen.
- Aceita as colunas opcionais `LAT`/`LNG` e `ATIVO`. O painel `?admin` gera as coordenadas para colar na planilha.

## Chave do Mapbox
A chave fica no `config.js`, que está no `.gitignore` e não entra no repositório. O modelo é o `config.example.js`. O `config.js` precisa ser enviado para a hospedagem. Sem ele, o site usa apenas o OpenStreetMap.

## Testes
Testado no Chromium, no computador e no celular (390px). As APIs de mapa (Mapbox e Photon) foram simuladas, porque a rede do ambiente de teste as bloqueia. A busca com a chave real ainda precisa ser conferida depois da publicação.

body:
## O que muda

- **Diário** (`/diario`): escrever com título opcional, texto livre (até 5.000 caracteres, com
  contador), humor em cinco emojis e **sugestões para começar** ("Hoje eu senti…") que entram no texto
  com o cursor já no fim.
- Lista das entradas, da mais recente, com emoji, data por extenso e trecho. Tocar abre um modal para
  ler, **editar** ou **apagar** (com confirmação "Apagar para sempre?").
- Aviso de apoio (CVV/SAMU) no pé da página.
- `src/dados/diario.ts` com testes: validação, título padrão e **uma pessoa não edita nem apaga a
  entrada de outra**.
- Item **Diário** na coluna e na barra do celular.

## Por quê

Funcionalidade 5 (registrar o progresso): o diário é o registro livre, complementar ao check-in.

## Como testar

1. Coluna → Diário → tocar "Hoje eu senti…" e continuar digitando: o texto segue a sugestão.
2. Escolher um humor → "Guardar no diário" → aparece na lista.
3. Abrir → "Editar" → salvar; "Apagar" → "Apagar" confirma e remove.

body:
## Özet
Panelden sosyal içerik hazırlama, planlama ve yayın takibini baştan sona otomatik hale getirir.

**Zincir:** haber yayınlanır → cron sosyal taslak hazırlar → (otomatik planlama açıksa) bir sonraki boş saat yuvasına "planlandı" olarak yerleşir → Metricool'a teslim edilir → saati geçince panelde "yayınlandı" olur.

### Yeni
- **`tools/sosyal-kart.py`:** Her haber için 1080×1350 (4:5) JPEG sosyal kart üretir; 80 kart eklendi. Görsel türü (gerçek çekim, temsili fotoğraf, grafik, AI) kapak kaynak dosyasından okunur. `haber-kapagi.py` işini bitirince bu araç otomatik çalışır.
- **`src/sosyal-otomasyon.js`:** Panelden değiştirilen ayarlar KV'de tutulur: paylaşılacak ağlar, paylaşım saatleri, otomatik planlama, tazelik sınırı. Saat yuvası İstanbul saatine (UTC+3) göre hesaplanır. Paylaşım metni başlık, spot, haber adresi, görsel künyesi ve kategoriden türeyen etiketlerden oluşur.
- **Panel:** otomatik yayın ayarları kartı, gönderi başına küçük görsel, Metricool teslim durumu ve tek tıkla "Onayla ve planla".
- **Dış teslim kaydı (`metricool_id`):** Metricool'a başka yoldan teslim edilen gönderi kaydedilir; kuyruk onu ikinci kez göndermez.

### Hata düzeltmeleri
- `processMetricoolQueue` başarılı teslim kaydını `.run()` olmadan hazırlıyordu. Kayıt hiç yazılmıyor, gönderi "gönderiliyor"da kalıyor, Metricool kimliği kayboluyordu.
- Haber kartları medya kasasında olmadığı için AI beyanı her zaman `true` gidiyordu. Artık kapak kaynak dosyasından okunuyor.
- Sosyal kuyruk `.webp` kapak gönderiyordu; Instagram webp kabul etmiyor.

## Test
- **Birim:** `tools/sosyal-otomasyon-testi.mjs` (PR doğrulamasına eklendi). Ayar temizliği, saat yuvası ve dolu yuva atlama, 20 dakika eşiği ve metin/etiket üretimini kapsar.
- **Uçtan uca:** `wrangler dev --local`, yerel D1 ve istekleri kaydeden sahte bir Metricool sunucusuyla koşuldu.
  - Taze haber planlandı (29 Eylül 10:00 İstanbul); 2024 tarihli haber onaya düştü.
  - Metricool'a giden istek doğrulandı: JPEG kart, `tiktokData.title`, temsili fotoğraf için `isAigc:false`, künye ve etiketler.
  - Teslim kaydı ve Metricool kimliği yazıldı.
  - Saatsiz onay bir sonraki boş yuvaya (12:00) yerleşti.
  - Dış kayıtlı gönderi Metricool'a tekrar gönderilmedi (toplam 2 istek).
  - Saati geçen teslim edilmiş gönderi "yayınlandı" oldu.
- **Panel:** Playwright ile mobil ve masaüstünde işlendi; ayar kartı ve teslim satırları görünüyor, yatay taşma yok.
- `node --check`, a11y, link, gerileme ve asset denetimleri: temiz.
- `wrangler deploy --dry-run`: temiz.

author: agentydragon
body:
Step 7 of the cdk8s conventions plan (#8145), agent-tooling area: public-coder (app, proxy, sshpiper, devbox), ssh-mcp, google-mcp, github-api-proxy and CLIProxyAPI read Service references. Review 2e3cf37f06 (source); ba530fd79e is the regenerated output.

## What changes

- **`public_coder_devbox.py`**: `SSH` is the VM's sshd `ServiceRef`, selecting the VM's Pods by `kubevirt.io/domain`, the Service's own selector. The Service and the VM's interface port read it. `SERVICE_NAME`, `SSH_PORT` and `POD_LABELS` go. `service_ref` stays module-qualified because cdk8s-plus's `Pods` is imported bare.
- **`public_coder_sshpiper.py`**: `SERVICE` replaces `LABELS` and `PORT`. The Deployment, container port, probes, Service and both policies read it. The devbox egress is `public_coder_devbox.SSH.egress()`.
- **`public_coder_proxy.py`**: `PROXY` and `_METRICS` are `ServiceRef`s sharing name and Pods; `PROXY_PORT` goes. iron-proxy's listen address, the container ports, the Service, the Deployment and both policies read them. The ingress rule's devbox peer reads `public_coder_devbox.SSH.pods`. `LABELS` stays public because `clickhouse/installation.py` reads it.
- **`public_coder_agent_config.py`**: `_SERVICE` is the gateway reference. The container port, probe, Service, Deployment and both NetworkPolicies read it. `_EGRESS_PROXY` is `public_coder_proxy.PROXY.url`. The Agent's NetworkPolicy peers and ports come from `public_coder_proxy.PROXY` and `public_coder_sshpiper.SERVICE`. `NAMESPACE` and `LABELS` stay public, because `generate_manifests.py` passes them to the proxy and sshpiper charts.
- **`ssh_mcp/config.py`**: `SERVICE` replaces `SERVICE_NAME` and `HTTP_PORT`, and `MCP_URL` is `f"{SERVICE.url}/mcp"`. This module is outside the files the dispatch named, but it is where ssh-mcp's address lives: `backend.py` builds from it, and `agentplane/staging.py` imports `MCP_URL`.
- **`ssh_mcp/backend.py`**: the Deployment, container port, probes, Service and policy selector read `SERVICE`. The bearer is a `SecretKey` (`_BEARER`, built from the unchanged `BEARER_SECRET_NAME`/`BEARER_SECRET_KEY` that `agentplane/staging.py` imports), used by the mint and by `env_value`. The devbox egress is `public_coder_devbox.SSH.egress()`. `LABELS` goes.
- **`ssh_mcp/test_consumers.py`**: the URL-to-Service relation expects the `.svc` host.
- **`google_mcp.py`**: `SERVICE` replaces `_HTTP_PORT` and `_LABELS`. `GMAIL_MCP_URL` and `CALENDAR_MCP_URL` derive from `SERVICE.url`; nothing imports them yet. `BEARER` is a public `SecretKey` and replaces `BEARER_SECRET_NAME`/`BEARER_SECRET_KEY`, which nothing imported.
- **`github_api_proxy/proxy.py`**: `_SERVICE` (`proxy-tls` 443, `target_port` 8080), `_PROXY` and `_METRICS` `Port`s. The Service, TLSRoute backend, container ports, probe, policy and PodMonitor read them.
- **`cli_proxy_api/cli_proxy_api.py`**: the Service, container port, probes, Deployment and policy read the existing `SERVICE`; `_LABELS` goes. `PORT` stays public for `aiquota.py`.
- BUILD deps for the new imports. No shared module changed.

## Rendered effect

`render_diff.py origin/devel HEAD`: 16 fields in 12 objects across 5 Kustomizations. Everything else is byte-identical, including google-mcp, public-coder-agent-devbox (Service and VM) and the sshpiper `Pipe`.

- **`.cluster.local` dropped from a URL built with `.url` (5 fields, 4 objects)**:
  - ConfigMap `agentplane-staging/agentplane-actions-settings`: the ssh group's executor URL becomes `http://ssh-mcp.ssh-mcp.svc:8080/mcp`. **Reloader rolls `agentplane-actions` once.**
  - ConfigMaps `public-coder-agent/public-coder-agent-config` (the Matrix `proxy`) and `public-coder-agent-kubeconfig` (`proxy-url`), and Deployment `public-coder-agent`'s `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`: all become `http://public-coder-agent-proxy.public-coder-agent.svc:8080`. **The pod template changes, so `public-coder-agent` restarts once.** It uses `Recreate`, and its startup is IO-bound on the state PVC and can take many minutes. The Agent Pod is not hostNetwork, so `.svc` resolves through the cluster search path. NO_PROXY is unchanged, and nothing compares the proxy host as a string.
- **`protocol: TCP` added (7 fields)**: container ports `gateway`, `proxy`, `metrics` and `ssh` (Deployments `public-coder-agent`, `public-coder-agent-proxy` and `public-coder-agent-sshpiper`), and Service ports `gateway`, `proxy` and `metrics`. The API server already defaults this field, so the proxy's and sshpiper's stored pod templates should not change. I expect no rollout from this; I did not observe one.
- **Named targetPort becomes a number (2 fields)**: Service `cli-proxy-api` `http` → `8317`, and Service `github-api-proxy` `proxy` → `8080`. Each is the same container port.
- **Cilium devbox selectors (2 fields)**, both now from `public_coder_devbox.SSH.egress()`:
  - `allow-public-coder-agent-sshpiper-egress`: `k8s:kubevirt.io/domain` becomes the unprefixed `kubevirt.io/domain`. Cilium reads an unprefixed selector key as source `any`, which matches the Pod's `k8s:` label, the same form every `Pods.cilium` selector uses. Same peer.
  - `ssh-mcp` egress: `app.kubernetes.io/name: public-coder-devbox` becomes `kubevirt.io/domain: public-coder-devbox`. The virt-launcher Pod carries both labels (the VM template sets both), and `kubevirt.io/domain` is what the devbox Service, sshpiper and the proxy's ingress already select on. Same Pod.

No Job re-runs, and no Flux change.

## Left out, and why

- **Consumers in the agentplane area** (`agentplane/staging.py`): `_GMAIL_MCP_URL`/`_CALENDAR_MCP_URL`, the `google-mcp-bearer`/`bearer-token` literals, and the Cilium egress to `ssh-mcp` and `google-mcp` by `endpoint_labels`. After this lands they can read `google_mcp.SERVICE`/`GMAIL_MCP_URL`/`BEARER` and `ssh_mcp.config.SERVICE`.
- **The agentplane-actions admission in google-mcp and ssh-mcp** (`endpoint_labels("agentplane-staging", "agentplane-actions")`): the client's reference is `agentplane.actions.service(namespace)`, but the staging namespace is private to agentplane, so a consumer would still spell it. `//cluster/cdk8s/agentplane:actions` is also not visible to `//cluster/cdk8s/ssh_mcp`. The agentplane area needs to export staging's Actions Pods first (E5's `staging_config`), as ha-mcp's conversion also left it.
- **CLIProxyAPI's litellm and aiquota admissions**: litellm's reference is `litellm.proxy.service(spec)`, reachable only through `proxy_specs()`. Importing it here would also cycle once `litellm/config.py` reads `cli_proxy_api.SERVICE`. `aiquota` imports `cli_proxy_api`, so the reverse import is a cycle. `aiquota.py:93` and `litellm/config.py:29` still spell CLIProxyAPI's URL; `SERVICE` is on devel, so their areas can convert. The Go-template config's `port: 8317` also stays.
- **github-api-proxy's Alloy admission**: there is no Alloy `Pods` reference, and `cilium.SCRAPERS` admits the whole `monitoring` namespace, so using it would widen the rule.
- **Other areas' producers**:
  - `public_coder_agent_config`'s litellm `baseUrl` and egress peer (same per-spec litellm reference). Its NO_PROXY litellm hosts are compared as strings and keep both forms.
  - Its Authentik ingress peer (`component: server, instance: authentik`), which differs from `authentik.SERVER.pods` (`component: server, name: authentik`).
  - The proxy's ClickHouse egress and iron `client.HOST` rule, since ClickHouse has no `ServiceRef` yet.
  - google-mcp's `google-write-access-token`, whose producer is airlock.
- **`ssh_mcp.config.load(devbox_service)`** still derives the devbox host from the rendered Service. The value is equal to `public_coder_devbox.SSH.fqdn` and stays the FQDN, because ssh-mcp's known_hosts and sshpiper's `Pipe` compare it as a string. Reading `SSH` directly changes `generate_manifests.py`'s call.
- **The proxy's and sshpiper's admission of the Agent Pod**: it takes `app_namespace`/`app_labels` from `generate_manifests.py` and is unchanged.
- **Service labels**: none ad

author: ragibkl
body:
## What

A top-level `revoked` list in `keytree.yaml`:

```yaml
revoked:
  - SHA256:...   # old laptop
```

A key whose fingerprint is listed is never written to any server, whatever user or source it comes from (GitHub, GitLab or `keys:`). Blocks drop it on the next sync.

## Why

Shutting out one key without removing the person, or without deleting the key from GitHub, for example when that key is also used for git pushes.

## Behaviour

- Fingerprints use the `SHA256:...` form from `ssh-keygen -l`, which sshd also logs on each login. `keytree check` rejects anything else.
- Filtering happens where every key is added to a block, so it also covers cached keys and keys carried over during a GitHub outage.
- `keytree plan` lists revoked fingerprints.
- Keys added by hand outside keytree's block are not affected. The README says so.

## Upgrading (important)

v0.1.0 rejects unknown fields, so a `keytree.yaml` that uses `revoked` makes v0.1.0 servers stop syncing. They keep their current keys, so nobody is locked out. The README now has an **Upgrading** section: re-run the installer on every server before using a new field. After merging, tag `v0.2.0`.

## Tests

- Config: valid and invalid fingerprints, and `IsRevoked` with and without a key comment.
- Sync, under a temp `--root`: revoking removes the key and keeps the others; the key is not carried over during an outage with no cache; literal revoked keys are dropped; `plan` shows revocations.
- `go test -race ./...` and `test/e2e.sh` (Alpine and Ubuntu) pass.

| address | model | result | best % | check runs | notes |
| 0x43bc90 | deepseek-v4.1-flash | not reached | - | - | the worker session ended before writing anything; main's prior partial is retained unchanged |

Advice for docs/agent-guide.md, and two `data/symbols.csv` requests:
- `std::sort` cannot be used directly here: its recursive call is the mangled `std::_Sort`, which does not resolve to `FUN_0043c720` in `data/symbols.csv`. This sort has to be hand-written as inline helpers that call `FUN_0043c720` / `FUN_0043ca70` / `FUN_0043cb20` / `FUN_0043c990` by name.
- `0x43c360` is recorded as `Class_0043c360::FUN_0043c360`, but it is really `UElem_0043c390::?$vector::size` (every other vector `size` in the table is `UElem_<addr>::?$vector::size`). That mismatch is why `vector::reserve` scores higher (87.3%) yet leaves a bad reference.
- `vector::reserve` inlines `_Destroy` away for a trivial element, so the call at `0x43c108` disappears unless the element has a user destructor (which then changes the sort's allocation). The original's `_Destroy` at `0x43c390` is `ret 8`, an out-of-line call, which only happens for a non-trivial destructor.

author: bunnyxt
body:
## Summary

Slow requests could hold a pooled connection until their query finished on its own, long after the proxy had already given up on the client. A client paging deep into `/video` or `/member` (large `LIMIT ... OFFSET` plus a `COUNT` per request) could therefore exhaust the connection pool for every other endpoint.

- **Statement timeout.** Every MyBatis statement now has a 300 s timeout (`mybatis.configuration.default-statement-timeout` in `application.properties`). 300 s equals the Apache proxy timeout, so no client that could still receive a response is affected; beyond it the backend was only doing wasted work. The value can be lowered to 30–60 s once the slow `/member` and `/member/{mid}/video` queries are fixed. The empty `mybatis-config.xml` is removed because `mybatis.configuration.*` and `mybatis.configLocation` cannot be set together.
- **Page depth cap.** `/video` and `/member` reject requests where `(pn - 1) * ps > 10000` with the existing `400 invalid request parameter` response. The check runs before any query and is computed as `long`, so a huge `pn` cannot overflow into a negative offset.

## Verification

- Local run of the packaged JAR: `pn=501&ps=20` and `pn=10001&ps=1` pass validation; `pn=502&ps=20`, `pn=10002&ps=1` and `pn=2147483647` return 400 in the existing error format.
- Binding the packaged `application.properties` to `MybatisProperties` yields `configLocation=null`, `defaultStatementTimeout=300`.
- With the bundled Connector/J 8.2.0 and HikariCP against a MySQL 5.7 server over a real network link: `SELECT SLEEP(30)` with a 5 s query timeout fails after ~5.2 s with `MySQLTimeoutException`, the query disappears from `information_schema.processlist` (killed server-side), and a single-connection pool can immediately lend the connection again after repeated timeouts.

author: kryptobaseddev
body:
## Root cause
`@cleocode/core` depends on `@cleocode/git-shim`, so pnpm installs `packages/core/node_modules/.bin/git`. That file is a shell wrapper that runs `node "$basedir/../@cleocode/git-shim/dist/shim.js"`. It is a regular file with its own inode, so `resolveRealGit`'s realpath and inode checks accepted it as real git. `pnpm exec` puts that directory first on PATH. The shim therefore spawned the wrapper, re-entered itself, and the second hop failed with `recursive executable delegation refused` / `real git binary not found`.

## Fix
`resolveRealGit` now reads small text candidates (no NUL byte, 64 KiB or less). It pulls out their quoted `.js`, `.mjs` and `.cjs` targets and expands `$basedir`, `${basedir}`, `%~dp0`, `%dp0%` and `$PSScriptRoot` to the directory the candidate was found in. It skips the candidate when a target resolves to this shim or to a copy already in the delegation chain. Launchers for other tools and real binaries are still accepted.

## Red on broken code
- New test `skips a pnpm .bin/git shell wrapper that runs the shim`: on the old `shim.ts` it fails with exactly the production error, `[git-shim] ERROR: recursive executable delegation refused` / `real git binary not found`. It passes with the fix.
- Control test `still delegates to a non-shim script launcher on PATH` passes on both versions.
- End to end on macOS, from `packages/core`:
  - `pnpm exec git init --bare x` fails on the old shim and prints `Initialized empty Git repository` with the fix.
  - `pnpm exec vitest run src/__tests__/init-nested-git-root.test.ts`: all 15 tests fail on the old shim and all 15 pass with the fix.
- Linux is covered by CI running the regression test. I did not run it locally on Linux.

## Checks
All git-shim tests pass (126). Build, `tsc -b`, biome and the changeset lint pass. `cleo check arch` passes 30/30.

author: whilp
body:
Third cleanup from the audit of the tree outside the build system, after #2297 and #2306. Behavior is unchanged.

## What changed

- **core/fail.h:** new `cosmic_done`, the `true, ""` shape. It replaces the spelled-out `lua_pushboolean(L, 1); return cosmic_succeeded(L);` at 11 sites in `http.c`, `sqlite.c` and `store.c`.
- **core/sqlite.c:** `handle_close` folds its two identical branches, closed and borrowed, into one.
- **core/http.c:** the multi handle's refusal message is built by one macro (`MULTI_MESSAGE`). `MULTI_FAILED`, `handle_write` and `handle_finish` use it.
- **core/syscalls.c:** `execve` and `spawn` share `checked_argv` and `checked_variable`. The messages, argument indices and raise-before-allocate order are unchanged. In `spawn`, "argv is empty" is still checked first.
- **core/portable.c, core/vfs.c:** `read_at` is exported as `cosmic_read_at` (in `portable.h`). The VFS reads through it instead of carrying its own copy of the loop.
- **cosmic/archive.tl:** the NUL/backslash/drive-letter test is named once, as `foreign_syntax`.
- **cosmic/http.tl:** `Http.Options` inherits its fields from `raw_http.Options` instead of listing them a second time. `cosmic docs Http.Options` reads the same.
- **eval:** `arena.tl`'s `under` becomes `Fs.within`, and `summarize.tl`'s `starts` becomes `String.starts_with` and `Fs.within`. These scripts run on the pinned bootstrap cosmic; I checked that it carries both functions.
- **doc/design.md**
  - The C/Teal section now records that DNS is c-ares and HTTP/1.1 framing is curl.
  - Both met the rule's second half: each is fuzzed upstream (OSS-Fuzz), and `cosmic.http` needed a TLS client before a Teal one could be written.
  - On macOS, c-ares reads DNS settings through Apple's dnsinfo, which reaches a Mach service, so a macOS sandbox profile will have to allow that.
- **doc/roadmap.md**
  - The "DNS and HTTP in C" item that asked for this decision is removed.
  - It now says that `cosmic.test`'s `needs` is public, while the runner stays in `build/`.

Left out on purpose:
- The two write-all loops in `syscalls.c`: both run only in children whose coverage `build/c_functions.tl` exempts, so a shared helper would need an exemption of its own.
- Moving `zip.tl`'s dates onto `Time.civil`: that needs overflow handling, and it stays under its existing TODO.
- `design.md`'s checkbox ledger: it describes how test keys are computed, which is build-system territory.

## Verification

After merging main (#2307):
- `o/bin/cosmic test` passes: 2102 tests, all run, sandboxed.

author: dariy
body:
## Problem

`safeImagingDecode` did not apply EXIF orientation. A phone photo with Orientation 6 or 8 got sideways variants, cards and `og:image`. The stored width and height were swapped, so `srcset` descriptors and layouts were wrong.

## Change

- `safeImagingDecode` calls `imaging.Decode` with `imaging.AutoOrientation(true)`. Upload, library import, lazy variant, prewarm and Instagram import all use this decode.
- Upload and import store the displayed size, because they read the bounds after rotation.
- Migration `swap_dims_for_rotated_exif` swaps `width` and `height` for rows with a stored Orientation of 5 to 8.
- `MediaService.PurgeOrientedVariants` runs one time at scheduler start. It removes the variants of rows with Orientation 2 to 8. Then it rolls `thumbnail_generation` and drops the cached public pages, so that browsers get the new files. The setting `media_orientation_variants_purged` stops a second run.
- `docs/features/media.md` describes the behavior.

The pixels of the original file do not change.

## Proof

- New tests: `TestUpload_EXIFOrientationRotatesVariantsAndDims` (Orientation 6 JPEG gives 400x800 stored size and a 256x512 rung), `TestPurgeOrientedVariants_RunsOnce`, `TestOrientedMetadata`.
- `./scripts/check.sh`: all 13 checks pass.
- I did not do the manual check on :8001, because `exiftool` is not installed on this machine. The new upload test does the same steps through `UploadFile` and `Variant`.

author: levonk
body:
## Summary

Composes the existing Devin ACP transport (`devinAcpTransport`, ACP v1 JSON-RPC over stdio) into a real Cordis/Loader agent provider so ACRYL can drive `devin acp` end to end:

- **New plugin package `plugins/acryl-agent-devin`** — function plugin (`inject: ['acrAgentControl']`, schemastery `Config`, no default export) that builds `acpProvider(devinAcpTransport(config))`, registers it through `ctx.acrAgentControl.registerProvider`, and owns the transport inside a `ctx.effect()` disposer. `cordis.patch.yml` row id == package name.
- **Composition** — new `agent-control` and `devin-acp` coding-capability rows on desktop/web/tui; the Devin row ships `disabled: true` and is enabled only via `dsh-desktop.devin-acp` settings (binaryPath, authMode, cwd, model, permissionMode). Workspace plumbing: `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `verify-layout.mjs`, lockfile, release/CI build lists, nix derivations.
- **Agent-control dispatch** — `start`/`resume` now work on lazy (`runtimeId: null`) bindings; results merge into stored immutable snapshots; `stop` clears runtime state; attach collisions, unregister reconciliation, and merge-invariant validation are enforced.
- **`session/request_permission`** — inbound JSON-RPC requests now dispatch through a handler map whose results are written to the wire (`-32603` on throw, `-32601` unknown). Resolution order: `onPermissionRequest` callback → `permissionMode` policy (`dangerous`/`bypass` prefer allow kinds; `normal` fails closed by semantic option kind) → cancelled outcome. See the approval note below.
- **Provider-neutral session bridge** — `AcrylSessionBridge` routes non-`dsh-native` session bindings through `attach`/`dispatch`; the native `ctx.agents` path is unchanged when no provider is selected. Provider sends serialize per session; resume honors `providerSessionRef` via `session/load`.
- **Verification** — real-Loader lifecycle suite (activation, PENDING→ACTIVE, config-fail-before-apply, unload/reload with no orphan child PID, capability rejection, runtime collision, idempotent disposal), service-level attach→start→send→cancel→stop E2E against a stub ACP server, and a `DEVIN_ACP_SMOKE=1`-gated real-binary smoke spec.

50 files, +6,684/−86, 41 commits.

## Approval architecture note (please review)

`session/request_permission` is deliberately **not** wired into `ctx.approval`: the DSH approval service requires a DSH `Agent` identity and open-turn context that `AgentSnapshot` bindings cannot satisfy. The typed `onPermissionRequest` callback is the extension seam; `permissionMode` policy applies when no callback is installed. Note upstream's new `acryl-agent-control` (per-call approval machinery) may offer the right adapter point — that integration is left as a follow-up decision.

## Rebase note

This branch is based on `316a375`; `upstream/main` has since moved ~160 commits including the `apps/acryl-desktop` bounded-context reorg (moved `desktop-settings-contract.ts`/`profile.ts` paths) and the new `acryl-agent-control` capability in `coding-capabilities.ts`. A rebase will produce mechanical conflicts in those shared files plus `pnpm-lock.yaml`; happy to rebase on request or land the rebase in a follow-up commit.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run typecheck` — clean across all packages
- [x] `pnpm run build` — clean
- [x] `pnpm --filter acryl-control run test` — 113 pass + 1 gated-skip
- [x] `pnpm --filter acryl-agent-devin run test` — 15 pass (incl. 9 real-Loader cases)
- [x] `session-bridge.spec.ts` — 18/19 (one pre-existing cold-boot timeout flake)
- [ ] `DEVIN_ACP_SMOKE=1 pnpm --filter acryl-control run test` — real `devin acp` round-trip (requires `devin auth login` / `WINDSURF_API_KEY`; not run in CI)
- Pre-existing upstream failures unchanged (acryl-cli direct.spec timeout flake, desktop plugin-lifecycle canvas refs, acryl-ui provenance drift, harness-runtime env-dependent suites)

Feature docs (PRD, task ledger, mini-design, blocker report) are archived under `internal-docs/feature/archive/2026/09/devin-acp-integration/`.

author: douglasduteil
body:
**Problem**
The accept-a-blocking-moderation scenario still drives the browser through bunwright locators and matchers, so it reads as Playwright code instead of the steps a moderator follows. It also keeps bunwright in the feature suite longer than needed.

**Proposal**
Rewrite it as one buncept scenario that mirrors the original Cucumber steps (open the moderation, accept it from the toolbar, finish inside the validation modal, find it again among processed moderations). The existing actor from #1827 covers every step, so `packages/buncept` is unchanged.

**Why port one file per PR**
The 5-run gate on #1827 passed but could not tell the engines apart: the bunwright tests were green in the same runs, and the feature job's historical flake rate is low (about 6 in 96 runs since 2026-09-22). Porting one file per PR lets each CI run compare buncept and bunwright scenarios side by side on the same runner and load. bunwright is removed once the buncept scenarios have stayed flake-free over enough runs.

**Note for local runs**
Run the feature tests from the repository root after `bun run build`, as CI does. Island scripts are served from `bin/public/built` relative to the working directory: from `sources/web`, or without a build, client-only islands such as the moderation toolbar never mount and "✅ Accepter" cannot be found. This explains the local failures seen on `main` with both engines, not a bug in either engine.

Related: #1827 (buncept), #1801 (bunwright adoption).

author: mivoru
body:
Owner report: turning on notifications crashed the app, and it kept crashing on every launch until notifications were turned off again.

**Cause:** no `google-services.json` in the Android build, so `PushNotifications.register()` throws "Default FirebaseApp is not initialized" inside the native plugin (not catchable from JS). `refreshDeviceTokenIfPermitted` re-registers at every sign-in once permission is granted -> crash loop.

**Fix:** `register()` is never called unless the build sets `VITE_FOLKIDLE_PUSH=1` (only for a build that ships Firebase config). Without it, Settings shows "Push notifications are not set up yet"; the local resting reminder (no Firebase needed) stays. New test pins that `register` is never reached in that case. Board task 67 documents how to turn push on later.

Verified: vitest 652 (push.test.ts 16/16), svelte-check baseline 4. Client-only; reaches phones through the OTA bundle.

Repo-ready native-model slice built on the merged protocol-v1 ORML runner.

This PR adds an isolated `orml-runner-u2net` distribution for `smart-subject-mask`.

Pinned provenance:
- ORML source commit: `bb6333e62b17a9a0fc12ef889bc3642428e6f4f4`
- U2Net model: `u2netp-320x320-float32-1.0`
- model SHA-256: `79e8757f7c5342c4f2b0dab4c66c4bc128b077c9541db5c6a5b363ff75c8b54a`
- graph input: `inputs`
- graph output: `functional_1/tf_op_layer_Sigmoid_6/Sigmoid_6`
- matched ORX commit: `0a24780d8446f998b9f13b61a328b97d91878500`

- pure preprocessing/matte tests pin normalization and output resizing semantics
- explicit HTTPS model-fetch helper verifies the upstream SHA
- manual-only `U2Net Native Verification` workflow builds the pinned runtime, fetches/verifies the model, runs real U2Net inference, and then runs Cosmosis `acceptanceSmoke` through the configured process runner

- real native inference: intentionally not claimed VERIFIED until the manual native workflow succeeds
- BodyPix, classifier and super-resolution remain separate future pinned-backend slices.

author: copilot
body:
Brings in upstream [px0-ai/px0 @ `9d82e10`](https://github.com/px0-ai/px0/commit/9d82e10f6a2ef1307a0c76bcd8f34628e14b155b) and adds support for opening several repositories in one px0 session (upstream issue #162). The design was proposed earlier in this repo but had never been compiled.

```bash
px0 ~/work/mobile ~/work/frontend ~/work/backend
```

**Relative to upstream, only 11 files change: 477 lines added, 1 removed.** Everything else in the tree is upstream at `9d82e10` without `.git`, including its MIT `LICENSE` and root `README.md`.

### Design
Each repository gets its own unmodified px0 `*Server`, mounted at `<base>r/<name>/` using px0's existing base-path support. As a result, git, LSP, search, the agent integration and path sandboxing stay scoped to one repository with no changes to the request handlers. `server.go` is untouched.

- **Hub (`workspace.go`):** a new `workspaceHub`.
  - Repo names are URL-safe directory names. Duplicates get a suffix, so a second `app` becomes `app-2`.
  - `<base>` redirects (302) to the first repo, and `<base>api/workspace/list` feeds the switcher.
- **`main.go`:** adds an early branch for "more than one directory and no PR URL", plus a new usage line. Single-directory, file-target and PR-URL runs follow the original code path unchanged.
- **Frontend:** `web/src/workspace.js` replaces the repo name in the sidebar header (`#root-name`) with a `<select>` for switching repos. `boot()` calls it after meta loads, and outside `/r/<name>/` it does nothing. The switcher styles are appended to `web/style.css`.

### Deviations from the proposal
1. **Saved tabs are keyed by repo directory, not by name.** Upstream's `sessionFilePath` names the file after any non-`/` base path. Unrelated workspaces that each contain an `app` repo would therefore share `r_app.json` and restore each other's tabs. The hub sets `srv.session = newSessionManager("/", root)`, so each repo uses the same file a single-repo run of that directory would.
2. **Multi-repo mode also reads the `server.basePath` setting.** It now uses the same precedence as single-repo mode; the patch only read the `-base-path` flag.
3. **The switcher border uses `var(--line)` instead of `var(--border, #333)`.** `--border` isn't defined in px0's themes, so light themes would have fallen back to the hard-coded dark colour.

Nothing else needed changing: `agentManager.Close()` is already nil-safe, and all the method names the proposal used exist.

### Tests
The new tests cover the `-base-path` mount and its `<base href>`, and the session keying from deviation 1. The proposal's naming and routing tests are kept.

### Docs
- `README.md`: multi-repo example in Usage.
- `docs/features/workspaces.md`: the old README, rewritten as a feature guide.
- `docs/internals/architecture.md`: new "Multi-Repository Workspace Hub" section.
- `docs/features/README.md`: feature matrix row and section 7 entry.
- `docs/agents/README.md`: `web/src/workspace.js` in the module table, plus a documentation-mapping row.
- `UPSTREAM.md`: a comment ready to paste on #162, plus steps to fork px0 and apply the 11 files on top of `9d82e10`. It notes that upstream's CONTRIBUTING.md says they generally don't accept unsolicited PRs.

### Review notes
- **Scope limits:** search, quick-open and the file tree cover one repo at a time, and switching repos reloads the page.
- **Sandbox-only test failure:** upstream's `TestPRSessionPush` fails here because the sandbox sets `safe.bareRepository=explicit` through `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment variables. Unmodified upstream fails the same way, and the whole suite passes with `env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT go test ./...`.
- **CodeQL:** every alert is in upstream code this PR doesn't change.
- **Browser check:** the switcher hasn't been tried in a browser.

body: ## Problem Closes #1654 Related issue: N/A Validation tasks: none A Silo Web member of a Watch Party ends up on a black player page at the end of every episode, and drops out of the room until they reload. This change keeps room members out of post-roll, so the room's return to its lobby takes them back to the room page like the rest of the party. The web player enters post-roll 30 seconds before the end of a series episode, without checking for a room. When the room then returns to its lobby (#1489), the player's room exit runs `handleExit`, which only navigates to the room page from `foreground`. In post-roll it calls `exitPlayback()` and returns, so the player unmounts with its room socket and the watch route renders nothing. ## Approach Skip the early post-roll trigger when the request belongs to a room, using the same room id and token check as the other room branches in `WatchPlaybackChrome`. A room already decides what follows the item for everyone, and post-roll has nothing to offer there: its next-episode action only returns to the room page. The member stays in the full player until either its own `ended` event or the room's lobby snapshot sends it to the room page; both paths already navigate there from `foreground`. `handleExit` still does not navigate from post-roll. With this change no room member reaches that mode, so I left it alone rather than change exits for non-room playback. ## Validation - Web lint, format check, typecheck, production build, and bundle budget: pass. - `vitest run src/playback`: pass. The new host test renders the real provider and host with the player stubbed; its room case fails without the guard and passes with it. - `make test-web` was not run locally: the workstation runs Node 26, whose built-in `localStorage` shadows jsdom's unless web storage is disabled. CI runs the suite on Node 22. - Not exercised in a live room with the fix deployed. The bug itself was reproduced on a real deployment on two consecutive episodes, as described in #1654. ## Risks None identified. Non-room playback is unchanged. A room member now sees the full player for the last 30 seconds of an episode instead of the post-roll screen. ## Checklist - [x] I read and can explain the complete diff. - [x] This pull request addresses one concern. ## AI Disclosure - Harness: Claude Code (T3 Code) - Tool(s): Claude Code - Model(s): claude-opus-5-5 - Involvement: Fully AI-generated, human verified - Adversarial review: A separate Claude Code agent reviewed the diff against every route into post-roll, the room exit and end-of-media paths, non-room playback, and the new test. It found no blocking issue. Two low findings were applied: read the room from the active request instead of a ref, and check the room token as the other room branches do. author: isamu
body:
## Summary

Step 1 of #2267 (multiple files as tabs in the Files pane, part of #2257). **Nothing on screen changes and the pane still opens one file.** What changes is what the pane remembers — per cell in memory and per directory in localStorage (`files_pane_state`): a list of tabs with one in front, instead of one `openPath` with the file's facts beside it.

- `filesPaneState.ts`: `FilesTabState` — one file's own facts (path, Preview or not, caret, top line, preview scroll). `FilesPaneState` = `tabs` + `activePath` (the front tab by identity, not position) + the pane-wide `expanded` / `treeScrollTop`. `activeTab(state)` reads the front.
- `useOpenFile.ts` / `filesPreviewMode.ts`: a load is handed the **tab** it restores, not the whole pane; `restoresPreview` decides from the tab.
- `FilesPane.vue`: `snapshot()` writes the open file as the one tab; `restore()` opens the front tab.
- `filesPaneStore.ts`: reads **both** shapes — everything written before this becomes a single tab (the upgrade path) — and writes the new one. Each tab is capped as the old fields were; a bad tab is dropped, not the rest; tabs are capped at `MAX_TABS`.

Steps 2 (the tab strip, "add or go to the open tab" from every entrance, save every dirty tab on leaving) and 3 (keys through the prefix keys and the palette) follow. Step 2's strip will follow the tab look the app already has (the collection chat strip), so the UI stays one style.

## Items to Confirm / Review

- **The stored shape** — once a browser writes it, it stays; a later `root` on a tab (for files outside the pane's root) is additive, so no second conversion.
- **One thing written differently**: with no file open, the old snapshot still wrote a caret / top line / mode / preview offset that nothing ever read back. Those now belong to a tab, so with no file open nothing of the kind is written. What a restore puts back is unchanged. An empty `openPath` (never opened by a restore) reads as no tab.
- `test/src/components/filesPaneFixture.ts` (`oneFile`, `frontTab`) keeps the existing specs readable in the new shape; `TerminalGrid.spec.ts` still seeds localStorage in the **old** shape, which is now the upgrade-path check.

## Verification

- **Old vs new, run side by side** (throwaway harness, deleted): stored states in the old shape — generated over the path, mode, caret, top line, preview offset, expanded list and tree scroll, including wrong types, empty and oversized values — **264,600 states, 0 differences** in what a restore puts back (file, Preview, caret, top line, preview scroll, expanded, tree scroll); live round trips (in memory, through localStorage, and old-code-writes / new-code-reads) **480 comparisons, 0 differences**. The harness was mutation-checked: loosening the mode test, allowing an empty path, dropping the caret integer check and removing the expanded cap produced 10,080 / 12,600 / 4,200 / 25,200 differences (the last only after adding an oversized list to the generator, which it had lacked).
- What stays as tests: the upgrade path as a generated property (`parsePaneStore — the one-file shape becomes one tab`), the new shape's reading rules, and the updated pane specs. Break-verified: not reading the old shape, a front naming an absent tab, no tab cap, a snapshot without tabs, and a restore that does not hand over the tab each turn specs red.
- **Real run** (built, scratch HOME, Playwright): open `readme.md` in the pane beside an enlarged cell, reload → localStorage holds `{"tabs":[{"path":"readme.md",…}],"activePath":"readme.md",…}` and reopening the pane shows the file; with the **old** shape seeded (`openPath: "readme.md", showPreview: true`), the pane opens `readme.md` in Preview.
- All of `test/src` passes; `yarn lint`, `yarn typecheck`, `yarn build` pass.

## User Prompt

- #2257's remaining work: is opening several files hard?
- I do not use this much — can it be done naturally, without contradictions? If so, go ahead.
- What matters is that the UI is natural, easy to use, and consistent with the rest.

Refs #2267

body:
## Resumen

Reestructura el gasto de un modelo plano (1 gasto = 1 concepto) a **cabecera-detalle** y adapta el frontend. Registrado como Cambio 7 en `docs/CHANGE_LOG.md` (acordado con el cliente).

### Base de datos
- `202609280002`: el folio del proveedor pasa a `folio_proveedor`; nuevo `folio` automático `G-00001` (no se trunca a partir de 100 000); `subtotal`, `iva` e `iva_desglosado` con la regla `subtotal + iva = importe`; tablas `gasto_concepto` y `gasto_comprobante` (PDF/XML/imagen). Los gastos existentes se migran con IVA no desglosado, 1 concepto y su comprobante.
- `202609280003`: PostgREST queda **de sólo lectura** para `gasto`, `gasto_concepto` y `gasto_comprobante` (revoke + políticas restrictivas).
- `gasto.importe` sigue siendo el total final: cierres, presupuesto y reportes no cambian.

### API
- Alta y edición con `lines`, `supplier_folio` e `iva` opcional. **Precios con IVA incluido**, 16 % por defecto; el servidor calcula todos los totales.
- `GET /expenses/{id}`, comprobantes múltiples, `POST /expenses/extract-xml` (lector CFDI 3.3/4.0 **sin IA**, rechaza DTD/entidades) y `work_id` opcional en `POST /suppliers` (alta y asignación en una transacción).

### Frontend
- Editor de conceptos con totales en vivo idénticos al backend (BigInt, HALF_UP), conceptos exentos y varios comprobantes con reintento por archivo.
- Lectura automática del XML del CFDI y alta rápida de proveedor en un modal que no envía el gasto.

## Pruebas
- `pytest`: 129 unitarias + 4 de integración con Postgres/PostgREST reales (instalación nueva y actualización).
- Playwright: 63 en escritorio y móvil.
- Diferencial frontend ↔ backend: 5 000 gastos aleatorios, 0 diferencias. Lector CFDI: 400 facturas aleatorias cuadran exactamente.

## Despliegue
Requiere respaldo de la base, aplicar las 2 migraciones y reconstruir `api` y `web` juntos: el frontend anterior no es compatible con el nuevo contrato de la API.
