author: richpsharp
body:
Planning-status requests currently acquire the global Processing lock and run expiration updates across all plans. A raster series produces many such reads, so they compete with admission and completion even though they only need one plan's status.

This change makes those reads read-only. Expired requests still appear failed immediately using database time. Existing worker cleanup persists expiration between jobs, admission and planner claims still reclaim stale capacity, and completion checks only its own plan so late results cannot revive expired work.

Closes #586. Related to #584, which remains open for the broader latency investigation. Based on main; independent of diagnostics PR #585.

### Architecture

- Owner: Processing's PostgreSQL job store. Changed components: job-store implementation, JobStore port documentation, PostgreSQL integration tests.
- **Used by:** PlanningQueue and Processing worker cleanup. **Depends on:** PostgreSQL transactions and database time. **Coordinates with:** planning cancellation and planner claims through existing stored state.
- No dependency edges added, removed or redirected; no new service, schema, package or sibling knowledge.
- Public HTTP response shapes and errors are unchanged. The internal status-read contract now explicitly excludes mutation and admission locking.
- Remaining coupling: capacity-changing operations retain their existing shared advisory lock. Status reads still open a database connection; this does not resolve all sources of end-to-end planning latency.
- Preserved: owner isolation, retained-record expiry, queue capacity/FIFO, cache bypass, native cancellation cleanup and slot ownership. Deferred maintenance does not extend a plan's usable deadline.

### Verification

- Controlled local PostgreSQL benchmark: 25 simultaneous status reads while holding the admission lock for one second, three runs on main `cda8f19f2191062e53bc70ba499588c36e60acdd` and three on final commit `947c20c686123a54aff2e589a0543838ae823626`. Before: 0/25 completed while locked, median 1.031 seconds. After: 25/25 completed while locked, medians 0.063–0.068 seconds. This isolates lock contention, not production raster-series latency. Reproduction: reserve one plan, hold `pg_advisory_xact_lock(7610329)` in a separate transaction for one second, release 25 `get_planning` calls simultaneously through a barrier, record completion counts before releasing the transaction and each call's elapsed time.
- Added real PostgreSQL regressions for concurrent reads under a held lock, read-only deadline reporting and owner/TTL checks, worker cleanup, and rejection of late completion.
- `.venv-312\\python.exe -m black --check src/eolab_app/processing/job_store.py src/eolab_app/processing/ports.py tests/test_processing_planning_postgres.py` and `git diff --check` passed. Black reported an unreadable optional cache but completed successfully.
- `.venv-312\\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_processing_planning_postgres.py tests/test_processing_jobs.py tests/test_processing_calculations.py tests/test_processing_events.py --processing-dsn=postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:54358/eolab_processing_test_586 --basetemp=C:/Users/richp/AppData/Local/Temp/eolab-586-integration -q --tb=short`: **53 passed** against final source. Includes active cancellation waiting for native cleanup before releasing the planner, FIFO/capacity, source authorization, cached bypass, SSE ownership and restart recovery.
- `.venv-312\\python.exe -m pytest --basetemp=C:/Users/richp/AppData/Local/Temp/eolab-586-full --tb=short -ra`: **1,167 passed, 105 skipped, 38 failed**. All 38 failures are vector tests requiring the unavailable `osgeo` binding in this Windows environment (same limitation seen before this change); no unrelated fixes were made. Database-gated tests are skipped by that invocation and exercised separately above. Other skips retain their existing platform/integration prerequisites.
- GitHub **Processing PostgreSQL / disposable-postgres** passed on this commit: `python scripts/verify_processing_postgres.py` ([run](https://github.com/springinnovate/eolab/actions/runs/36499779887)).
- No frontend changes; a separate frontend test/build run is not required for this backend-only change. Coolify deployment will build the application.
- Actual GitHub state verified: **draft**, assigned to **richpsharp**.

### Deployed verification

WWF Connectivity successfully built and deployed **`947c20c686123a54aff2e589a0543838ae823626`**, version **0.8.0-7-g947c20c**, through [Coolify](https://lilling.ecoshard.org/project/m1no8hegcte7kzg7ztsgvfhy/environment/kxlgp7jbucw8noigsbaqg47a/application/0pwbswcsq7tc9fhlojwvsi6b/deployment/vbq0wfugbynye7l0438lkjta).

On [the saved raster-stack map](https://wwf-connectivity.ecoshard.org/maps/connectivity-all-human-impact-layers), opened analysis at map center (-13.79865, -48.71312), Plot raster stack → Area statistics, using the 200 km sampling box. Both `mean(a)` and a fresh `mean(a)+0.000586` completed **25/25 rasters**. The fresh series reported 7.850 seconds overall and 1.620 seconds for the first raster. These are functional production observations, not a controlled before/after end-to-end speed comparison; the controlled lock benchmark above isolates the improvement.

This deployment does not include the unmerged diagnostics PR #585, so its extra timing-report fields are absent. The existing report remains available. #584 stays open for remaining planner queue, connection and result-delivery latency.

author: akoskovacs
body:
## Summary

Before this change, the REPLs and the LSP completed `x.` in two separate ways. The LSP analyzes the buffer and uses the real type of the expression before the dot. The REPLs guessed the type from the text of the current line: `]` meant `List`, digits meant `Integer`, and any other name was treated as a type name. As a result, `pa.<TAB>` on a `Server<Entries>` binding, `s.<TAB>` on a string variable, call results, chains and lambda parameters completed nothing.

Now all three REPLs (BEAM, tree-walk and the browser REPL) use the same analysis as the editor. On Tab or `/complete`, the REPL builds the program it already builds for type-checking and asks the analyzer to type the receiver at the cursor. That program contains the session's definitions, then `main do` with its bindings replayed, then the line being typed.

Closes #426.

## Changes

- **`src/semantic/completion_at.{hxx,cxx}` (new):** the shared completion code.
  - `completionQualifierForType`, `scanDotReceiver` and `recoveredReceiverQualifier` moved here from `src/lsp/server.cxx`.
  - `scanDotReceiver` now also steps over a trailing block, so `xs.map { … }.` is recognized.
  - `completionClosers` closes the brackets and `do` blocks a half-typed line leaves open, so the line still parses.
  - `completeAt(db, analysisDb, path, source, cursor, interfaces)` is the single entry point: it completes members of a typed receiver, dotted module paths such as `IO.pr`, and bare names, including bindings in scope.
- **LSP (`src/lsp/server.cxx`):** uses the shared code; the moved functions are deleted from it.
- **BEAM and tree-walk REPLs (`src/main.cxx`):**
  - The readline completer and `/complete` both go through `replCompleteAt`.
  - Lines already typed inside an unfinished multi-line block are included, so a line inside `make X do …` completes with the block around it.
  - Deleted `g_replVarTypes`, `g_currentMakeTarget` and the per-binding type bookkeeping.
- **Browser REPL (`src/wasm_repl.cxx`):**
  - `kex_repl_complete` uses `completeAt`.
  - The session now remembers `let`/`var` bindings so they can be completed.
- **`src/common/completion.hxx`:** removed `inferLambdaParamType`, `inferPatternParamType`, `elementTypeOfList` and `matchBracketBack`. `resolveCompletionQuery` and `qualifierFromBefore` stay, because `kex -K` and the LSP's last-resort fallback have no program to analyze.

## Behavior changes

- `/complete` now prints each completed word in full, as it would be inserted: `/complete pa.` prints `pa.get`, where it used to print `Server<Entries>.get`.
- The browser build has no prebuilt prelude interfaces, so lambda parameters stay untyped there. Variables, literals and types defined in the session complete.

## Testing

- **`completion_test`:** new `completeAt` cases cover a variable, a call result, a chain, a lambda parameter (complete and half-typed), a literal, a `make`-block parameter, a module path and a scoped binding. Also added `completionClosers` cases.
- **`repl_cli_test`:**
  - `pa.` completes the serving slots and `Server`'s own methods in both REPLs.
  - Call results, chains, lambda parameters and literals complete in both REPLs.
- **`wasm_repl_test`:** a binding's members complete by its type.
- Each completion takes about 9 ms, so re-analyzing on every Tab is fast enough.
- The full `ctest` suite passes except `installed_layout_test`, which also fails without this change: the installed binary can't find the linuxbrew `libboost_context` library in this environment.

author: cskb75
body:
The body view now moves the way the game's organelle editor shows organelles at rest. The motion is ported from the scripts that drive it, and each organelle's values come from its scene.

## Motion (`src/ui/motion.ts`)

| What | Game source | At rest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weapons (31) and the Chemoreceptor Antenna | `gun.gd`'s `G.editor.active` branch; `chemoreceptor_antenna.gd` | The aim sways by `sin(t·speed)/5` rad (speed random 0.7–1.3). Each 60 Hz tick, every segment eases toward a direction that turns from the previous segment's toward the aim, so the line bends. |
| Pseudopods and the Axopodium (5) | `scn/cells/tentacle.gd`, no target | The first segment wobbles ±10° every ~2 s. Later points straighten after it, and a spring keeps segment lengths, so a wave runs down the tentacle. The frame-rate correction (`_interleaved`, 240 Hz reference) is ported too. |
| Flagella (6) | `lash.gd` in the editor, `scn/cells/hair.gd` | The connector's rotation eases to 0 and adds `sin(t·20)/4·0.2`, so it sways about ±14° every 3–6 s. The body keeps where it was (fluidity) and eases back straight (stiffness half-life), so it trails. |
| Internal organelles (73) | each scene's autoplayed `wiggle` animation | The sprite, not the masked pattern, scales 1 → 1.1 → 1 every 0.5 s, from a random start. |

The Chitin Shield and the three active strips don't move in the game, so they stay still here.

Bending lines are drawn like Godot's Line2D: the stretched (or tiled) texture is sliced along the simulated points. The plain Flagellum's tapered shape is rebuilt from its width curve. Moving elements update in place from a single `requestAnimationFrame` loop (`src/ui/clock.ts`), which pauses while the body view is off screen.

## Rarity outlines

The SVG `feMorphology` filter is gone: it ran every frame on every moving organelle and dropped the view to 16 fps. Outlines are now baked once per texture and colour on a canvas (`src/ui/outline.ts`), using `outline.gdshader`'s 24 taps and radius (3 texels, 6 for internal organelles), and drawn under the texture.

Like `Bodypart.update_rarity_texture`, only the main node is outlined: the Sprite, else the Line2D, else the Hair2. So pseudopods and the plain Flagellum have none, as in the game.

## Connections (`src/ui/Connections.tsx`)

- **Curve:** the game's `Curve2D`, with a 30 px handle back into the body from each external slot.
- **Line:** `EditorLine`, pinched to 57% mid-way. It's a dark gold edge around a core with a bright band sliding along on a 4 s sine (`editor_line_gradient.gdshader`). It's bright where the organelles at both ends work together and dimmed grey otherwise (`update_visibility`).
- **Flows:** the `ArrowLine` look. A thin line with a chevron every 101 px, fading in toward 70% and out at the end, scrolled with `arrow_scroll.gdshader`'s formula. Chevrons are coloured by flow type, and flows sharing a connection interleave.

## Switch and accessibility

An **Animate** checkbox sits next to the editor hint. It's on by default and remembered in the browser. It's always off, and disabled, when the system asks for reduced motion.

## Data

`tools/extract/organelle_art.py` now records each organelle's motion values (resolving the script inheritance from the pack), each line's points, and the outline radius in the published texture's pixels. The textures are unchanged.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 107 tests pass. `src/ui/motion.test.ts` covers the rest pose, sway limits, bending, fixed points past `num_segments` (the Cryophore), a stable wave at 30 and 60 fps, a zero-length frame, and the flagellum amplitude.
- `npm run build`: OK.
- **Browser, desktop and phone:**
  - Frames 1.3 s apart show the bending and trailing. The static pose returns when Animate is off.
  - Reduced motion: the switch is disabled and nothing animates.
  - Frame rate with the view on screen: 60 fps on the reference Bacterium, the Nanobot example (19 flows) and a fully equipped Helminth (18 organelles).
  - No console errors.

author: jeremiah-k
body:
## Overview

The physical-pair harnesses prove one hop at a time (one route, one direction, a handful of messages). Real traffic is richer: multiple routes firing simultaneously, rendering budgets different per transport, provenance chains spanning cross-transport hops, and sustained volume where the interesting failures (false dedup, lost receipts, extra deliveries) only show up. This harness exercises the full pipeline between physical nodes across four transports at once: Meshtastic, MeshCore, Matrix (disposable Synapse in Docker), and LXMF (RNode pair).

## Key Changes

- Opt-in harness (`MEDRE_RADIO_MATRIX=1` + device env vars, `-m "live and hardware"`) building a both-directions radio runtime with explicit relay prefixes and per-transport byte budgets (MeshCore 160, Meshtastic 200).

- Four radio-mesh tests, each with a stated coverage matrix (module docstring):
  - **Route matrix + isolation**: both directed routes produce sent receipts on the correct target adapter only; observed on the correct transport only; nothing leaks to the wrong mesh.
  - **Rendering on-wire**: relay prefixes carry the originating sender's label across each hop; UTF-8, combining chars, and newlines survive; the oversized MT input is sized inside the sender's own payload limit (Meshtastic rejects text the local radio cannot carry) and truncates exactly at the MeshCore relay boundary.
  - **Provenance chain**: peer native packet id → canonical event (native-ref resolution, tracking every packet id across bounded observation resends) → receipt (per resolved event, routed target adapter) → observed wire text, attribution surviving each hop.
  - **Sustained convergence**: paced corpus reconciled across three ledgers — receipts exact per event (every admitted event has exactly one sent receipt), canonical events exact (duplicates stay two), peer observation at a reported floor with listeners drained inside their windows; event scans page the whole ledger.

- **Matrix as a third transport** (`test_matrix_room_relay_three_transport`): a disposable Synapse homeserver (standalone starter — config generation, bot+peer registration, room provisioning, loud docker failures, container cleanup on failed provisioning) joins the runtime. Radio meshes relay into the room with contractual attribution; the independent peer user's room messages fan out to both radio meshes — fully automated, no human in the loop. Room-side observation is exact (durable server history). Over-budget truncation from the room (a source with no size limit) is asserted from receipt rendering evidence at both budgets.

- **LXMF as a fourth transport** (`test_lxmf_fourth_transport_relay`): the RNode pair via the lab RNS configs/identities; radio relays reach the native LXMF peer with attribution; the peer's direct-delivery messages fan out to both radio meshes; receipts exact per target.

- Platform ACK semantics stated precisely from firmware/SDK source: Meshtastic DMs carry recipient ACKs (routing `ERROR_NONE`, typed NAKs) and MeshCore DMs carry explicit ACK packets — what this harness relays is the unacknowledged traffic classes (Meshtastic channel broadcasts, where the firmware strips `want_ack` over the air, and MeshCore channel floods, which are never ACKed). MEDRE receipts mean acceptance by the local radio (`local_queue`/`local_transport`), never recipient confirmation.

## Testing

- Bench-validated during development: the matrix third-transport test passed a full run on hardware (room relay, both fan-out legs, per-target receipts); the sustained test passed a full volume run; MEDRE ledger assertions (receipts per event per target, canonical events, dedup, routing, rendering evidence) hold on every run.
- Later bench iterations surfaced hardware-state findings rather than pipeline defects: after hours of continuous traffic the Meshtastic node wedges (serial config handshake times out; a reboot restores live delivery), and runtime-relayed truncated frames are not dependably observable over RF on either mesh while identical direct sends deliver — recorded in the harness as a rested-bench follow-up. MEDRE-side ledgers stayed exact throughout.
- Default suite collects and deselects the harness (live/hardware-gated); the structure guard allowlists the starter's sync readiness poll and exempts live-marked files from the line-count boundary (they embed device maps and observation contracts that line budgets would sever from their tests).
- CI: Tests and Coverage + Docker Integration green at the review-fix push.

## Scope

- No production code changes; the harness exercises existing runtime behavior against real radios, a containerized homeserver, and an RNode pair.
- Known bench follow-ups: the truncated-long-frame RF observation anomaly, and a full rested-hardware validation pass across all six tests.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

This change adds opt-in live tests for message routing across Meshtastic, MeshCore, Matrix, and LXMF. It adds a Docker-based Synapse starter for Matrix tests and updates the test-suite structure checks for live and infrastructure-heavy test modules.

### Key changes

- **Features**
  - Add radio tests for route isolation, rendered messages and byte limits, provenance, and sustained traffic.
  - Add Matrix relay and fan-out tests using a provisioned Synapse instance.
  - Add an optional LXMF test for relay, attribution, fan-out, and receipts.
  - Add `start_synapse` and `stop_synapse` helpers to manage Synapse and provision test accounts and a room.

- **Test maintenance**
  - Allow a two-second interval in the bounded Synapse readiness-probe loop.
  - Exclude modules marked `live`, `soak`, `hardware`, or `docker` from the file-size check. Skip files that cannot be read or parsed.

author: matt17br
body:
## What changed

- A new `plain_frame_rows` helper selects rows of a plain `data.frame` exactly as `[.data.frame` does: the same columns, row names, row-name compaction and attribute order. R · base Sort Rows, Filter Rows, Drop Missing Rows and Drop Duplicates use it. `[.data.frame` hashes every row name to make repeated ones unique, but these steps never repeat a row, so the helper skips that hash. Frames with another class, or with matrix, array or data-frame columns, still use `[.data.frame`.
- After a row selection, a derived capture compares each clock and plain list column with the source column's selected rows. When they are identical, the existing `identical()` check skips rescanning the values. Any difference is still validated in full, and the source-row mapping is still checked after inspection. Positions outside the source rows skip the shortcut, so the mapping check reports them as before.
- R · base Pivot longer reads a plain captured frame directly instead of copying it first, because base R builds every result column as a new vector. Library helpers and data.table inputs still get a private copy.

Only live execution changed. Generated code and its embedded helpers are untouched.

## Why

On the 11.7-million-row Parquet file, R · base Sort Rows spent about 0.3 seconds hashing row names, and every library spent about 0.5 seconds rescanning the sorted timestamp column. R · base Pivot longer spent about 1 second copying the frame before reading it.

Main against this branch, previewing each step after Rename, alternating:

| Step | R · base | R · dplyr | R · data.table | R · collapse |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sort Rows | 4.37, 4.16, 4.11, 4.19 → 3.60, 3.66, 3.57, 3.34 s | 4.71, 4.56, 4.51 → 4.22, 4.15, 4.20 s | 4.78, 4.04, 4.12, 4.16 → 3.63, 4.17, 3.75, 3.61 s | 4.67, 3.97, 4.85, 4.42 → 3.71, 3.83, 3.97, 3.85 s |
| Pivot longer | 5.34, 5.11, 5.86, 5.52 → 4.12, 4.31, 4.29, 4.10 s | | | |

Drop Missing Rows, Filter Rows and Drop Duplicates keep fewer rows, and their times are within noise.

## Verification

- A frame contract test sorts a base R frame with automatic and character row names and a list column, with `class` stored before `row.names` as `data.frame()` stores them, and requires the result to be identical to `[.data.frame`, including attribute order. Keeping the source's attribute order makes it fail.
- A standalone check compared `plain_frame_rows` with `[.data.frame` over 35 cases (plain, data-frame column, 1-d array, matrix, named rows and custom attributes before or after the class, with permuted, partial, empty and full positions), including attribute order and row-name compaction.
- A new test sorts a frame with a nanosecond clock column in every R library, checks that the captured schema matches the source's, and requires a sorted frame with one corrupted clock field to fail with `invalid clock timestamp storage`. Skipping the `identical()` check makes it fail.
- The full R contract suite passes (all 26 phases), including the complete catalog's exact comparison of live and generated output.
- `npm run check` and `npm run docs:check` pass.

## User-facing docs or screenshots

CHANGELOG entry for faster Sort Rows in every R library and Pivot longer in R · base. `docs/architecture.md` records the clock and list comparison after row selection.

## Release or security impact

Results are identical to before. Every capture still validates each column that isn't identical to already validated values, and row mappings are checked in full. Generated code, protocol, settings, dependencies and package contents are unchanged.

- [x] I reviewed user-facing text using `docs/writing-style.md`, or this change has no user-facing text.
- [x] I updated the documents required by `AGENTS.md`.
- [x] This pull request is one reviewable change; if it is a release, all feature work was merged separately.

author: andrecamm
body: ## The issue When `GET /api/channels/:id/messages` failed, the channel showed its empty state: "Comece a conversa. As mensagens ficam salvas. Dá um oi." A channel with history looked like it had none. The only other sign was a thin red app banner with the raw server string, such as `x` or `database_unavailable`, and a "Dispensar" link. There was no retry. A 503 from the database breaker therefore made every channel opened during the blip look wiped until the next socket reconnect or a page reload. Found by the local E2E sweep and reproduced independently. ## Why it happened `openChannel` in `App.tsx` loads the history. On failure it only called `setAppError(error.message)`. It never told the message list that the load failed. `MessageList` saw zero messages and rendered the ordinary empty state. ## The fix - `App.tsx` records which channel's history failed (`historyFailedChannelId`) instead of setting the app banner. Opening a channel clears it. A successful reconnect refetch also clears it. - `MessageList` takes two optional props, `historyFailed` and `onRetryHistory`. With no messages, it shows an error state in place of the empty state: "Não deu pra carregar as mensagens", "Elas continuam salvas. Só não chegaram dessa vez.", and a "Tentar de novo" button. If live messages arrived after the failed load, they stay, and a short line above them says the earlier messages did not load, with the same retry. - The retry refetches only the newest page. It does not go through `openChannel`, so it does not close the thread panel, drop the reply target, or mark the channel read again. - The raw server string is no longer shown. The error text has `role="alert"`, because the message log itself is `aria-live="off"`. - New copy in pt-BR, en, and es under `chat.historyFailed.*`. The thread panel and the skeleton `MessageList` do not pass the new props and are unchanged. ## Screenshots Desktop, 1440px, pt-BR. The channel has three messages and the history request answers 503 `database_unavailable`. Look at the centre of the channel: | Before | After | |---|---| | | | After, once the request succeeds again and "Tentar de novo" is clicked. The three messages come back without a reload: ## How to check 1. Open a server text channel that has a few messages. 2. In DevTools, block the request URL pattern `*/api/channels/*/messages*` (Network, right-click, Block request URL). 3. Reload the page. 4. The channel shows "Não deu pra carregar as mensagens" with "Tentar de novo". It does not show "Comece a conversa", and there is no red banner with a raw error. 5. Unblock the request and click "Tentar de novo". The messages load in place. 6. Open another channel without blocking anything. It loads normally, and an empty channel still shows "Comece a conversa". ## Tests - New `client/e2e/messages-load-error.spec.ts`. It sends a message, answers the history request with 503, reloads, and asserts the error copy and retry button are visible and the empty state and raw server string are not. Then it removes the route, clicks retry, and asserts the message is back. It fails on `main` at the error-copy assertion and passes with the fix (run twice in a row). - The existing `message-context-menu` and `i18n-pt-br` specs pass. - Client typecheck, eslint on the changed files, `i18n:check`, and the chat component vitest all pass. Client-only. Does not restart the API.
